Synopsis: Altering the definition of "sexual abuse" for purposes relating to civil actions for child sexual abuse to include any act that involves an adult allowing or encouraging a child to engage in certain activities; establishing certain limitations on damages that may be awarded under the Act; repealing the statute of limitations in certain civil actions relating to child sexual abuse; repealing a statute of repose for certain civil actions relating to child sexual abuse; providing for the retroactive application of the Act; etc.
Title: Civil Actions - Child Sexual Abuse - Definition, Damages, and Statute of Limitations (The Child Victims Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Pornography -see also- Nudity and Sexual Displays; Obscenity
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Repeals the statute of limitations and statute of repose for civil actions arising from child sexual abuse. Authorizes victims of child sexual abuse to file civil actions for damages at any time. Revives previously time-barred claims retroactively unless the alleged victim is deceased when the action commences. Caps noneconomic damages for revived claims at $1,500,000 against a single defendant. Limits sexual abuse liability for the State, local governments, and county boards of education to $890,000 per claimant. Authorizes an interlocutory appeal if a circuit court denies a motion to dismiss challenging claim revival constitutionality.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland State Treasurer's Office
stakeholders: Victims and survivors of child sexual abuse, alleged perpetrators, the State of Maryland, local governments, county boards of education, and liability insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: Reimbursable fund expenditures for the State Treasurer's Office increase by $70,700 in FY 2024 and $96,096 by FY 2028 to hire a claims adjuster. Indeterminate expenditure increases for the State Insurance Trust Fund and affected State agencies due to higher litigation costs, claims payments, and insurance premiums. Indeterminate expenditure increases for local governments and county boards of education for litigation, claims, and liability insurance coverage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) and handles claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA). The bill revives time-barred child sexual abuse claims and increases the State's liability limit under MTCA to $890,000, creating direct financial and workload impacts on the Treasurer's Office, including the need for additional claims adjusters.

The bill eliminates the statute of limitations and statute of repose for child sexual abuse civil actions retroactively, permitting an influx of revived litigation in Maryland circuit courts and authorizing interlocutory appeals on certain motions to dismiss.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 4-105) to require the State Board of Education to establish updated standards for county school boards' comprehensive liability insurance policies, increasing the required minimum coverage for sexual abuse claims to $890,000.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State and its agencies in civil litigation, and will be tasked with defending State entities against revived and prospective tort claims filed under the expanded MTCA provisions.

Under the amended Education Article (§ 4-105(c)), the State Insurance Commissioner must adopt rules and regulations and review and approve the terms and conditions of county boards of education that elect to self-insure individually up to the updated $890,000 coverage requirement.

Synopsis: Allowing a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain union dues paid during the taxable year; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification - Union Dues

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for qualifying union dues paid during the taxable year. Applies to dues allowed as a deduction under Internal Revenue Code Section 162 before 2018. Permits the subtraction regardless of the two-percent limitation imposed under Internal Revenue Code Section 67. Caps the allowable subtraction modification at $250 for any taxable year. Takes effect July 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers who pay union dues and labor union members
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.88 million in FY 2024, growing to $11.56 million by FY 2028 due to subtraction claims. State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time Comptroller tax system modifications. Local income tax revenues decrease by $6.45 million in FY 2024 and $7.54 million by FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's income tax system. The bill creates a new income tax subtraction modification for union dues, directly requiring the Comptroller to update tax forms and systems, resulting in an estimated $50,000 administrative expenditure in FY 2024.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the Maryland State Police Gun Center to include the tracking, screening, and vetting of all firearms surrendered under final protective orders in the State; and requiring each law enforcement agency to report to the Center the number and type of firearms surrendered, the jurisdictions where the firearms were surrendered, and certain information regarding the individual who surrendered each firearm under final protective orders.
Title: Maryland State Police Gun Center – Firearms Surrendered Under Final Protective Orders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Expands the purpose of the Maryland State Police Gun Center to track, screen, and vet firearms surrendered under final protective orders. Requires the Center to create and maintain a statewide database tracking surrendered firearms. Mandates each law enforcement agency to report information on firearms surrendered under final protective orders in its jurisdiction. Requires reported details to include the number and type of firearms and demographic information of individuals surrendering them. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland State Police Gun Center
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, and individuals subject to final protective orders who surrender firearms
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources; revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland State Police and its Gun Center with expanding operations to create and maintain a statewide database to track, screen, and vet firearms surrendered under final protective orders.

Final protective orders under which firearms are ordered to be surrendered are issued and administered through the Maryland Judicial Branch, which coordinates protective order records across jurisdictions.

Synopsis: Repealing a certain prohibition on prosecuting a person for rape or a certain sexual offense against a victim who was the person's legal spouse at the time of the alleged rape or sexual offense.
Title: Criminal Law - Sexual Crimes - Repeal of Spousal Defense
bill_summary: Repeals the prohibition against prosecuting an individual for rape or a sexual offense committed against their legal spouse. Eliminates statutory requirements regarding separation agreements, living apart, or decrees of limited divorce to prosecute spousal sexual offenses. Allows prosecution for first-degree rape, second-degree rape, third-degree sexual offense, and fourth-degree sexual offense regardless of marital status. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Victims of spousal rape and sexual offenses; married individuals subject to prosecution for sexual crimes against their spouse
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund expenditures and local incarceration expenditures resulting from the expanded application of existing penalties; State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal liability by repealing the spousal defense for rape and sexual offenses, potentially increasing the caseload of indigent defendants requiring legal representation by OPD.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands prosecution and incarceration penalties for certain sexual offenses, resulting in an expected increase in commitments to State correctional facilities operated by DPSCS.
The bill allows criminal prosecution of spousal sexual offenses previously barred under law, impacting the volume and proceedings of criminal cases in the State court system.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services to establish and periodically update standards for State buildings to conserve energy and minimize adverse impacts on birds; requiring the Maryland Green Building Council to include the standards in certain requirements established for the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program; defining "State building" as one acquired, constructed, or renovated by the State or one for which 50% of the money for acquisition, construction, or renovation came from State funds; etc.
Title: Department of General Services - Energy-Conserving Standards (Maryland Sustainable Buildings Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to establish standards for State buildings to conserve energy and minimize adverse impacts on birds. Requires the Department to update the standards every five years while considering occupants' physical and mental health. Excludes public school construction, nonprofit capital grant projects, and public work contracts under $500,000. Requires shielding and minimizing building lighting from midnight to dawn during specified spring and fall periods. Requires the Maryland Green Building Council to include the standards in the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Green Building Council; Secretary of General Services
stakeholders: State agencies and departments occupying or acquiring State buildings; architects and contractors designing or constructing State buildings; State building occupants
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate effect on State construction and maintenance costs across all funds, though utility costs may decrease over time. Revenues and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including establishing and updating bird-safe and energy-conserving standards for State buildings every five years, reducing lighting in existing State facilities, and adopting regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Green Building Council (MGBC) is explicitly mandated under the bill to incorporate the newly established standards into the requirements for the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program for State buildings.

MDOT owns and operates a significant inventory of State buildings that are not managed by DGS, making its future capital construction, substantial alterations, and lighting operations subject to the bill's standards.

USM owns and maintains a substantial portion of State-owned facilities independent of DGS management, and its capital construction and building renovations exceeding statutory funding thresholds will be impacted by the new standards.

Synopsis: Requiring that equity be considered when State transportation plans, reports, and goals are developed; altering the membership of the advisory committee on State transportation goals; requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation to conduct transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and consult with certain communities before announcing or proposing any major service change or any reduction or cancellation of a certain capital expansion project in the construction program; etc.
Title: Equity in Transportation Sector - Guidelines and Analyses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Language -see also- Communication; Electronic Comm; Telecomm
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Transit Administration to evaluate equity in State transportation plans, goals, and reports. Expands the advisory committee on State transportation goals to include labor and civil rights representatives. Requires transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and community outreach before proposing major transit service changes. Prohibits implementing major service changes causing disparate impacts or disproportionate burdens unless substantial justification necessitates the change. Requires similar equity analyses and public reports before reducing or cancelling eligible capital expansion projects in the construction program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Transit riders in Maryland, including racial minority, low-income, disabled, transit-reliant, senior, and limited English proficiency riders, as well as transit contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $602,600 in FY 2025 to cover 3 new permanent staff positions, consultant support, and required transit equity and cost-benefit analyses, with ongoing costs reflecting inflation. State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including considering transportation equity in the Maryland Transportation Plan, evaluating performance indicators for racial/disability/low-income disparities, collaborating on transit equity and cost-benefit analyses, and staffing the expanded planning processes.

MTA is directly responsible for developing transit equity analysis policies, conducting transit equity and cost-benefit analyses prior to major service changes or capital project cancellations, conducting community outreach, publishing evaluations, and hiring additional staff and consultants.
The Maryland Department of Planning holds a designated statutory seat on the advisory committee that advises MDOT on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and equity indicators.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition, meeting requirements, and advisory scope of the advisory committee on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and indicators to include equity metrics and additional stakeholder representatives.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members and the chair to the advisory committee advising MDOT and receives the annual report on the attainment of State transportation goals and benchmarks.

The members of the Board of Public Works are mandated recipients of the transit equity analysis, cost-benefit analysis, and community outreach reports before major transit service changes or capital expansion project cancellations.

The Attorney General is a mandated statutory recipient of the final transit equity analysis and impact reports compiled by the MTA for major service changes or capital project reductions/cancellations.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain local detention center officers of Talbot County in the event Talbot County becomes a participating governmental unit in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System; and providing that certain local detention center officers who join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System and receive certain service credit shall no longer be members of the Employees' Pension System and shall have no further rights to any benefit in the Employees' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers’ Retirement System – Talbot County
bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for Talbot County detention center officers if the county becomes a participating unit. Grants qualifying officers eligibility and creditable service in the retirement system for prior employment with Talbot County. Terminates their membership and rights to any benefits in the Employees' Pension System upon transfer. Exempts the transfer of creditable service from standard statutory member contribution repayment requirements. Directs that existing statutory procedures govern the transfer and crediting of plan assets.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Talbot County
stakeholders: Talbot County local detention center officers and Talbot County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Talbot County elects to participate, county pension liabilities increase by $918,300, resulting in an ongoing annual increase of $94,000 in employer pension contributions for 25 years. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the transfer of Talbot County detention center officers from the Employees' Pension System to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System if the county elects to participate, requiring the Maryland State Retirement Agency to administer the membership changes, calculate service credits, and manage the transfer of assets and liabilities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, to identify additional standards for water quality testing; requiring the Department, subject to certain funding and in consultation with the Department of Information Technology, to utilize an online portal to receive and upload certain information and to provide public access to the information; requiring the Department of the Environment to consistently share the information collected with the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments; etc.
Title: Private Well Safety Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, establishing additional private well water testing standards. Directs the department, subject to available funding, to utilize an online portal providing public access to well testing information. Requires contracts for real property sales with private wells to include water quality testing as a condition of sale. Authorizes a purchaser to waive the water quality testing requirement in writing. Requires State-certified laboratories to submit well water testing results to the department within five business days. Mandates that the department study long-term funding options for groundwater monitoring and report by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Information Technology; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: buyers and sellers of real property with private or domestic water supply wells, State-certified water testing laboratories, residential tenants and landlords, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $186,800 in FY 2025 and reach $250,700 by FY 2029 to fund three staff positions at the Maryland Department of the Environment. If funded, online portal development could cost approximately $3.4 million over two years. Potential indeterminate impact on local health departments and MDH Laboratories Administration depending on testing standards developed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for administering the Act, including establishing private well water quality testing regulations, managing the online testing portal, receiving water testing data, conducting a groundwater funding study, and submitting required reports.
The bill statutorily requires MDE to consult with the Department of Information Technology regarding the planning, development, and utilization of the private well water quality online portal.

The bill mandates continuous information sharing between MDE and MDH regarding well water quality data. Additionally, the fiscal note highlights potential operational and staffing impacts on MDH's Laboratories Administration to conduct additional water quality testing.
MDE is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations regarding long-term funding options for groundwater monitoring and analysis directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

Synopsis: Repealing the authority of the Secretary of Transportation to designate transit-oriented development; establishing the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund to promote the equitable and inclusive development of transit-oriented developments; authorizing the Department of Transportation to use the Fund to provide financial assistance to local jurisdictions; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an amount sufficient to ensure a Fund balance of at least $5,000,000; etc.
Title: Equitable and Inclusive Transit-Oriented Development Enhancement Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund to finance local transit-oriented development projects. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Transportation to provide grants and loans for design plans, infrastructure, and gap funding. Expands the definition of transit-oriented development to include properties adjacent to planned or existing transit corridors. Transfers transit-oriented development designation authority from the Secretary of Transportation to the Smart Growth Subcabinet. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation ensuring a fund balance of at least $5,000,000. Directs the Secretary of Transportation to submit an annual progress report to the General Assembly by November 30.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Smart Growth Subcabinet; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: county and municipal governments; transit commuters; commercial and residential developers partnering on transit-oriented development projects; low-income and minority transit riders
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2024 (mandated beginning in FY 2025) to maintain the required fund balance, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $258,249 in FY 2024 for MDOT administrative staff and start-up IT consultant costs, with ongoing operational costs in future years. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local jurisdictions receive grants or revolving loans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for administering the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, publishing scoring standards, providing financial assistance to local jurisdictions, and submitting the annual report to the General Assembly.
DHCD is statutorily required to collaborate with MDOT to support recipients of awards from the fund by providing technical services for studies, plans, and code changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Smart Growth Subcabinet is given statutory responsibility to designate transit-oriented developments (TODs) and establish eligibility requirements and objective scoring standards for financial assistance applications under the fund.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and the bill establishes a mandated annual state budget appropriation of at least $5,000,000 to capitalize the new fund.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation sufficient to ensure a fund balance of at least $5,000,000 at the start of each fiscal year in the annual budget bill.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the new special, nonlapsing fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the newly established Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund and its interest earnings.

Synopsis: Providing that a person who is the victim of an act that would constitute a violation of certain hate crime laws may bring a civil action against the person or persons who committed the act in a court of competent jurisdiction; and authorizing the court to impose an injunction and award certain economic and noneconomic damages.
Title: Hate Crimes – Civil Remedy

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a victim of an act that would constitute a state hate crime violation to file a civil action. Permits the court to issue an injunction to prevent or restrain the prohibited act. Authorizes awards for economic damages, specified noneconomic damages, and reasonable attorney's fees and court costs. Excludes distress or anguish caused solely by property repair or replacement from recoverable noneconomic damages. Permits the court to award damages up to three times the amount of actual damages. Applies prospectively only to causes of action arising on or after October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Circuit Courts
stakeholders: victims of hate crimes and individuals sued for committing hate crime violations
fiscal_impact_summary: Any increase in District Court or circuit court proceedings can be handled using existing judicial resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a civil cause of action allowing victims of hate crimes to bring civil lawsuits in Maryland courts for injunctive relief and damages (including treble actual damages and attorney's fees), directly impacting District Court and circuit court caseloads and judicial administration.

Synopsis: Repealing the authority of the court to decree a limited divorce; and altering certain grounds for an absolute divorce.
Title: Family Law - Grounds for Divorce
bill_summary: Repeals the authority of a court to decree a limited divorce. Alters the statutory grounds required to obtain an absolute divorce. Establishes a six-month separation and irreconcilable differences as grounds for absolute divorce. Repeals prior grounds including adultery, desertion, criminal conviction, insanity, and cruelty of treatment. Deems parties living under the same roof as separated if they pursue separate lives.
responsible_party: Judiciary
stakeholders: individuals seeking a divorce or legal separation in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 only for computer programming changes. Operations and finances of the Judiciary and circuit court workloads are not otherwise materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the legal grounds and processes for granting divorces in Maryland circuit courts by repealing limited divorce and altering absolute divorce requirements. The Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts incurs a direct fiscal and operational impact to update court forms and case management programming.

Synopsis: Requiring each public school to provide information to students, faculty, staff, and parents regarding who serves as the Title IX coordinator for the school, the process in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint, and the support measures that are in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint and how to access the support measures.
Title: Primary and Secondary Education – Title IX – Notice (Hear Our Voices Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Requires each public school to provide Title IX information to students, faculty, staff, and parents. Mandates disclosure of the individual who serves as the Title IX coordinator for the school. Requires schools to explain the process in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint. Directs schools to detail available support measures for individuals filing complaints and how to access them. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland public schools
stakeholders: Public school students, faculty, staff, and parents in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local school systems can provide the required information using existing resources, resulting in no material impact on local expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public primary and secondary education system and sets educational standards and policies. MSDE provides policy guidance and oversight to ensure local public schools comply with Title IX regulations and state education requirements.

As a state agency operating public schools for deaf and hard-of-hearing students, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly subject to the bill's requirement to provide Title IX coordinator, complaint process, and support measures information to students, faculty, staff, and parents.

An independent unit within MSDE, the Center supports comprehensive school safety, supportive learning environments, and reporting systems for safety and misconduct concerns across public schools in Maryland.

Synopsis: Altering a certain statutory form for a general power of attorney by including certain provisions informing the principal and agent of certain matters, granting general authority with respect to tangible personal property and trusts and estates, authorizing the principal to grant the agent certain specific powers relating to successor agents, compensation, gifts, or transfers and opening joint accounts and beneficiary designations, and clarifying the force and effect of the form; etc.
Title: Maryland General and Limited Power of Attorney Act - Alterations
bill_summary: Alters the Maryland statutory forms for personal financial powers of attorney and limited powers of attorney. Authorizes agents to perform acts necessary to enable principals to qualify for governmental benefits or programs. Adds provisions granting agents general authority over tangible personal property, trust and estate matters, and disclaimers. Expands optional specific powers regarding gifts, joint accounts, beneficiary designations, and appointing successor agents. Incorporates warnings regarding asset risks for principals and specifies fiduciary duties of loyalty for agents.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Register of Wills
stakeholders: principals executing powers of attorney, designated agents and coagents, beneficiaries, and third parties relying on power of attorney documents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory power of attorney forms to include specific authority for agents to perform acts, transfer assets, or create special needs trusts to enable a principal to qualify for government benefit programs, specifically including Medicaid, which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill modifies statutory power of attorney forms that govern agent authority over trust and estate matters, demanding custody of wills, and making elective share elections subject to the Estates and Trusts Article, which intersect with estate administration overseen by the Registers of Wills.

The statutory power of attorney forms contain provisions concerning court litigation, guardian of the person and property nominations, and statutory elective share elections, which impact judicial branch proceedings supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to issue electronic licenses and registrations, except under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, on an applicant's request, to print a paper copy of the verification of licensure or registration and send it by first-class mail to the address on the application; repealing the requirement that the Board include certain information on each license and registration; and requiring the Board to send renewal notices by first-class mail under certain circumstances.
Title: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists - License and Registration Issuance and Renewals - Electronic Means

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to issue electronic licenses and registrations to qualifying applicants. Requires the Board, upon specific request, to mail a paper verification of licensure or registration to the applicant. Repeals requirements for the Board to include specific details, signatures, and its seal on licenses and registrations. Requires the Board to send renewal notices by electronic means at least 90 days before expiration. Directs the Board to send renewal notices by first-class mail if electronic transmissions fail or upon specific request.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: licensed psychologists, registered psychology associates, and applicants for psychology licensure or registration in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the operational changes are procedural in nature and do not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists operates within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) as a health occupations licensing board. MDH regulates health care professionals, and this bill directly alters the board's statutory licensing, registration, and renewal notification procedures.

Synopsis: Requiring that the holder of a certificate of sale include the e-mail address of certain persons in certain notices required to be sent to certain persons with an interest in a property that is sold at a tax sale; authorizing certain persons with an interest in owner-occupied property sold at a tax sale to request the current payoff amount to redeem the property; providing that the payoff amount to redeem the property provided by the holder of the certificate to the owner of the property is valid for 30 days; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Notices and Payoff Amount for Redemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: Requires holders of tax sale certificates to include email addresses in pre-foreclosure notices sent to interested parties. Authorizes owners, mortgagees, mortgage servicers, and deed of trust beneficiaries of owner-occupied residential property to request payoff amounts. Excludes owner-occupied residential property in Baltimore City from this specific payoff request process. Limits the payoff amount to expenses incurred before the certificate holder received the request. Deems the provided payoff amount valid for 30 days after the certificate holder provides it.
responsible_party: County Tax Collectors; Municipal Tax Collectors
stakeholders: Owners of owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sales, mortgage lenders and servicers, deed of trust beneficiaries, and holders of tax sale certificates of sale outside Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances, and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statutory requirements and prerequisites that must be satisfied before a certificate holder can file a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption in Maryland circuit courts. As the administrative support body for the Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts oversees court operations and case processing where these foreclosure actions are filed.

The bill impacts owner-occupied residential property retention and foreclosure prevention by establishing procedures for obtaining payoff redemption amounts. While the department has no direct administrative duties under the bill, it monitors residential property tax sale policies and programs related to homeownership preservation and foreclosure mitigation.

Synopsis: Altering requirements relating to relocation plans for mobile home parks to require a plan for park residents who will be dislocated as a result of the change in land use; requiring the owner, 60 days prior to entering into a contract to sell the community, to provide notice of the terms of the offer to homeowners in the community and provide them the opportunity to purchase the housing community; requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to list certain agencies to assist homeowners with the purchase of a community; etc.
Title: Mobile and Manufactured Homes - Relocation Plans and Sales of Communities (Manufactured Housing Modernization Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Alters relocation plan requirements when closing a mobile home park with more than 10 sites. Increases mandatory relocation assistance to 12 months of rent instead of 10 months. Conditions community purchase offers on filing an affidavit limiting lot rent increases and preserving park use. Requires community owners to notify homeowners and provide them an opportunity to purchase the property instead. Authorizes homeowners organizations to make purchase offers backed by 75% of member residents. Imposes $10,000 civil liability on community owners or purchasers who violate statutory requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Manufactured home owners, mobile home park residents, manufactured housing community owners, and prospective purchasers of manufactured housing communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected. The Department of Housing and Community Development and local housing agencies can receive notices and maintain web listings with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with receiving notices of conditionally accepted offers to sell manufactured housing communities and requires the department to maintain a public list on its website of organizations and county housing agencies that can assist homeowners with financing.

The bill creates civil liability provisions allowing homeowners organizations to seek $10,000 in statutory damages against community owners or purchasers for specific violations, which could result in civil actions handled by the state court system.

Synopsis: Requiring an individual, in order to be licensed as a psychologist by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, to have a doctoral degree in psychology from a certain school or university, to have received a postdoctoral respecialization certificate from a certain department of psychology that included a minimum of 1,750 hours in supervised internship, and to have completed at least 1,500 hours postcertification advanced training hours or precertification hours of service as a registered psychology associate; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Psychologists - Licensure Qualification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Alters the qualifications required for an individual to obtain a license as a psychologist. Expands the definition of a doctoral degree in psychology to include programs with recognized regional accreditation. Establishes a second licensure pathway for individuals who earn a postdoctoral respecialization certificate. Requires the respecialization program to include at least 1,750 hours in a supervised internship. Requires completing at least 1,500 hours of advanced training or psychology associate service. Mandates at least two years of board-approved professional, supervised experience in psychology.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: Applicants for psychologist licensure, including doctoral-level psychologists with nonclinical psychology degrees seeking clinical licensure
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the licensure requirements and qualifications overseen by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, which operates as a health occupations licensing board under the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals; clarifying and altering the distribution of certain fees and penalties; and clarifying the application of certain license requirements and penalties.
Title: Environment - On-Site Wastewater Services - Board, Fees, and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Alters the membership requirements and geographic composition of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals. Reduces the required number of on-site wastewater professional members on the Board from six to five. Clarifies that inspection license requirements and penalties apply only to inspections conducted for property transfers. Directs property transfer inspection license application fees into the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund. Redirects administrative penalties for property transfer inspection violations to the Maryland Clean Water Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals
stakeholders: On-site wastewater professionals, property transfer septic inspectors, and consumers purchasing or selling real property with on-site sewage disposal systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State finances, but results in a minimal shift in special fund administrative penalty revenue from the Bay Restoration Fund to the Maryland Clean Water Fund in fiscal years 2023 through 2025. No direct material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for issuing on-site wastewater property transfer inspection licenses, setting fees, collecting administrative penalties, and directing revenues into the Maryland Clean Water Fund and the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership composition, geographic representation requirements, and licensing prerequisites for the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals.

The bill modifies the statutory qualifications and geographic distribution criteria for the six board members appointed by the Governor to the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals, which directly impacts the vetting and recruitment process overseen by the Office of Appointments.

Synopsis: Establishing that the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is in the Office of Resilience in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management; and altering the process for electing a cochair of the Council.
Title: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Places the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council in the Office of Resilience within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. Requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to provide staff for the Council. Adds one representative of the seafood industry, appointed by the Secretary of Emergency Management, to the Council. Authorizes the Council to elect an annual cochair from among any of its members. Transfers Council appointment and administrative authorities from the Director to the Secretary of Emergency Management.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Office of Resilience; Maryland Food System Resiliency Council
stakeholders: Maryland seafood industry, local food council organizations, Maryland farmers, food businesses, and state food security agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The Department of Legislative Services determined the bill creates no new council duties or additional expenditures because the Maryland Department of Emergency Management already provides staff for the Council.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 32 establishes that the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in MDEM. The Secretary of Emergency Management cochairs the council, appoints numerous members, and MDEM is charged with providing staffing for the council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory placement, membership composition, and cochair election process of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Agriculture (or designee) is designated in statute as a member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated in statute as a member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

The Dean of the University of Maryland College of Agriculture and Natural Resources serves as a co-vice chair of the council. The bill also alters staffing provisions by removing the statutory requirement for the college to co-staff the council.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MARBIDCO (or designee) serves as a designated statutory member of the council.

Synopsis: Requiring, in certain actions to repossess residential rental property, a landlord to submit to the clerk of the court evidence of compliance with local rental property licensure requirements and demonstrate that the landlord is compliant with the licensure requirements.
Title: Real Property – Actions to Repossess – Proof of Rental Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires residential landlords in jurisdictions requiring rental licenses to plead and prove licensure status when filing repossession actions. Mandates that landlords state with supporting facts whether the property is licensed, exempt, or unlicensed for specified reasons. Excludes repossession actions for breach of lease involving clear and imminent danger from the initial pleading mandate. Requires landlords to demonstrate licensure compliance, exemption, or permitted unlicensed status at trial by a preponderance of the evidence. Authorizes landlords to provide electronic proof of licensure. Directs the court to grant one postponement if a party seeks additional evidence regarding licensure.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Judiciary
stakeholders: residential landlords and residential tenants in Maryland jurisdictions that require rental licensing
fiscal_impact_summary: The Judiciary can implement form revisions and computer programming changes with existing budgeted resources. No material effect on State or local government revenues or expenditures is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 36 directly affects District Court proceedings for residential repossession actions by requiring landlords to plead licensure compliance using a form prescribed by the Judiciary, prove compliance by a preponderance of the evidence, and requiring the court to grant a postponement under certain conditions. The Administrative Office of the Courts must revise court forms and update judicial case management systems.

The Office of the Attorney General, particularly through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces state consumer protection and tenant rights laws regarding residential leases and unlicensed rental properties. While not assigned direct procedural duties under the bill, it monitors and investigates unlawful landlord repossession practices.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from making certain telephone solicitations to a certain called party in a certain manner by restricting the methods, times, and identifying information that the person making the call may utilize; providing that the Act does not apply to certain entities and circumstances; and making a violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice that is subject to enforcement and penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
Title: Commercial Law - Consumer Protection - Telephone Solicitation (Stop the Spam Calls Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from making telephone solicitations using automated dialing systems or recorded messages without prior express written consent. Restricts telephone solicitations to the hours between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in the called party's time zone. Limits solicitations to no more than three times per 24-hour period on the same subject matter. Prohibits deliberately concealing caller identification information or altering caller voice to defraud or confuse the called party. Establishes violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: telephone solicitors and telephone subscribers receiving telephone solicitations in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations; minimal complaint processing costs for the Office of the Attorney General are expected to be absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of the bill's telephone solicitation provisions are designated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill provides an exemption for certain noncommercial telephone solicitations by nonprofits, conditioning that exemption on the organization being registered with the Secretary of State under Title 6 of the Business Regulation Article.

The bill defines telephone solicitations by cross-referencing Section 8-205 of the Public Utilities Article and specifies that it does not preclude the applicability of related Public Utilities Article provisions and Public Service Commission oversight.

Violations of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act may result in civil actions or misdemeanor criminal charges adjudicated in the state court system administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Exempting up to $500 in a deposit account or other accounts of a judgment debtor held by a depository institution from execution on the judgment without an election by the debtor to exempt the money; establishing procedures a depository institution is required to follow on receipt of a writ of garnishment or other levy or attachment under certain circumstances; establishing a $6,000 limit on the cumulative value of property and cash that may be exempted; etc.
Title: Courts - Judgments - Exemptions From Execution
bill_summary: Exempts up to $500 in a debtor's account held by a depository institution from execution without debtor election. Caps the cumulative value of cash and property exempted under this provision and election-based exemptions at $6,000. Requires writs of garnishment to instruct garnishees to garnish only amounts exceeding the exempted $500. Requires depository institutions receiving a writ of garnishment to answer stating whether debtor funds exceed $500. Authorizes depository institutions to determine how to apply the $500 exemption across multiple accounts. Shields depository institutions acting in good faith reliance on writ instructions from liability to judgment creditors.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: judgment debtors, judgment creditors, and depository institutions (including banks, credit unions, trust companies, savings banks, and savings and loan associations)
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. State and local debt collection practices rarely involve bank account garnishment, and any resulting revenue changes are anticipated to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court garnishment procedures by requiring writs of garnishment issued by Maryland courts to instruct depository institutions to exempt up to $500 in deposit accounts without debtor election. The Administrative Office of the Courts must update court forms, processes, and case management systems to reflect these statutory changes.

DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), the state's primary delinquent debt collector. The bill impacts state collections by automatically exempting the first $500 in debtor bank accounts from garnishment or execution, though the fiscal note anticipates minimal impact given CCU's collection practices.

Synopsis: Requiring each county to establish a process for a person entitled to  any balance over the amount required for the payment of taxes, interest, penalties, and costs of sale to claim the balance after a tax sale foreclosure; and requiring the collector of taxes for a county to notify the prior property owner, within 90 days after delivering a deed to a purchaser, of the amount of a certain balance and the process for claiming the balance.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Payment of Balance After Foreclosure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Requires each county to establish a uniform process to claim surplus balances following tax sale foreclosures. Prohibits the claim process from requiring a court order unless a dispute arises regarding payment. Requires county tax collectors to notify prior property owners of record within 90 days after delivering a deed. Specifies the notice must detail the surplus balance amount and the county process for claiming it.
responsible_party: County Governments; County Tax Collectors
stakeholders: Prior property owners of record whose properties are sold at tax sale foreclosure, tax sale purchasers, and county tax offices
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts judicial branch operations by specifying that a county's process for claiming surplus tax sale proceeds may not require a court order unless there is an active dispute regarding payment, thereby potentially reducing routine filings and petitions in circuit courts.

Synopsis: Repealing the Collaborative Care Pilot Program; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and provide reimbursement for services provided in accordance with the Collaborative Care Model under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program – Collaborative Care Model Services – Implementation and Reimbursement Expansion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Repeals the Collaborative Care Pilot Program and its associated reporting requirement. Removes the June 30, 2024 termination date for the program's original enabling statutes. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement and reimburse Collaborative Care Model services statewide. Covers somatic and behavioral health integration in primary care settings serving Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients. Clarifies that primary care providers may still refer patients to specialty behavioral health care providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, primary care practices, and behavioral health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by up to $15.7 million (61% federal funds, 39% general funds) in FY 2024 and $20.9 million annually beginning in FY 2025. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly by $9.6 million in FY 2024 and $12.8 million annually thereafter. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement and provide Medicaid reimbursement for somatic and behavioral health services provided under the Collaborative Care Model statewide in primary care settings, resulting in significant programmatic and fiscal impacts.

Synopsis: Codifying the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as an instrumentality of the State to submit, monitor, implement, and evaluate the State Plan under the federal Rehabilitation Act in conjunction with Centers for Independent Living in the State; and requiring the Attorney General to be the legal advisor to the Council.
Title: Human Services - Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Codifies the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as an instrumentality of the State. Requires the Council to work with Centers for Independent Living to submit, monitor, implement, and evaluate the State Plan. Directs the Governor to appoint Council members considering diversity and statewide geographic representation. Requires the Council to employ an executive director and authorizes the Council to hire staff. Designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the Council. Exempts the Council from State and local taxes and specified State procurement and personnel laws.
responsible_party: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council; Office of the Attorney General; Governor
stakeholders: individuals with disabilities in Maryland, Centers for Independent Living, and members and staff of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and federal fund revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 if additional legal staff is needed for the Office of the Attorney General, though exact costs cannot be reliably determined. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, and the fiscal note indicates a potential fiscal impact from additional staffing needed to advise the council.

MSDE houses the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which serves as the Designated State Entity under the federal Rehabilitation Act and State Plan for Independent Living, and is tasked with auditing the council's books and records.
The bill requires the Governor to appoint members to the council in compliance with federal guidelines and diversity criteria, as well as granting the authority to remove members for cause.

As the principal agency coordinating statewide policies and programs for individuals with disabilities, the department's mission directly intersects with the council's oversight of independent living programs and centers.
The office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment process for members of the newly codified council.
The bill explicitly subjects members and employees of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council to the Maryland Public Ethics Law administered by the commission.

Synopsis: Repealing certain limitations on the authority of certain local governments to set the time by which a property with taxes in arrears must be sold by the tax collector.
Title: Property Tax – Tax Sales – Requirement to Sell

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Repeals the statutory requirement that county tax collectors sell property with delinquent taxes within two years. Repeals the mandate that the Calvert County tax collector sell delinquent property after one year. Requires collectors to sell property with delinquent taxes at the time required by local law. Provides that failure to sell within that time does not affect the validity of taxes or sales. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: County tax collectors; local governing bodies
stakeholders: Property owners with delinquent property taxes, local governments, and tax sale purchasers
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local government revenues may be delayed beginning in fiscal 2024 if local governments allow longer periods before holding tax sales. Specific revenue figures cannot be reliably estimated. Expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill may cause a delay in Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues from state property taxes if local governments extend the time before conducting tax sales. The ABF is used to pay debt service on the State's general obligation bonds, which are overseen and managed by the State Treasurer's Office.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provided information on the bill, as tax sales and subsequent proceedings to foreclose the right of redemption involve filings and adjudications within the Maryland Judiciary's Circuit Courts.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for setting the annual State property tax rate to support the Annuity Bond Fund for debt service payments on general obligation bonds, the timing of which may be marginally affected by delayed property tax collections.

Synopsis: Establishing enhanced requirements under the Open Meetings Act for the State Ethics Commission; and requiring the Department of Information Technology to provide technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream the open meetings of the State Ethics Commission.
Title: Open Meetings Act - State Ethics Commission (Maryland State Agency Transparency Act of 2023)

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Subjects the State Ethics Commission to enhanced transparency requirements under the Open Meetings Act. Requires the Commission to post open meeting agendas and voting materials online at least 48 hours in advance. Mandates that the Commission provide live video streaming of each open session. Requires the Commission to maintain approved meeting minutes online for at least five years. Requires archived video recordings to remain available online for at least one year. Directs the Department of Information Technology to provide technical staff, support, and livestreaming equipment.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission; Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: State Ethics Commission and members of the public seeking access to State Ethics Commission open meetings
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,000 in FY 2024 only for the State Ethics Commission to reimburse the Department of Information Technology for video streaming equipment and support services. Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for the Department of Information Technology increase commensurately in FY 2024. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements to the State Ethics Commission, requiring it to livestream open meetings, post advance agendas and materials, and maintain video and minutes archives online, with an associated $10,000 fiscal expenditure in FY 2024.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Department of Information Technology provide the technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream open meetings of the State Ethics Commission.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal guidance on the Open Meetings Act and houses/staffs the Open Meetings Law Compliance Board, which handles complaints arising under the Act.

Synopsis: Prohibiting local jurisdictions from imposing any unreasonable limitations, including land use restrictions, on utility-designated pollinator areas maintained by a public service company under certain conditions; requiring certain public service companies to mow utility designated pollinator areas in a manner which minimizes disturbances to habitats; stating the intent of the General Assembly related to State and local laws regarding weed control and vegetation management by public service companies outside of pollinator areas; etc.
Title: Land Use - Public Service Companies - Pollinator-Friendly Vegetation Management and Utility-Designated Pollinator Areas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Prohibits local jurisdictions from imposing unreasonable limitations or land use restrictions on utility-designated pollinator areas. Applies the protection when an area meets a federal conservation agreement or statutory pollinator-friendly maintenance standards. Excludes utility property located on or below a trail overlap, a park overlap, or active farmland. Authorizes local land use restrictions that pertain to safe energy delivery or human health and safety. Requires participating public service companies to mow designated pollinator areas only within specified seasonal windows. Limits mowing of these pollinator areas to not more than once every other year.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; local governments
stakeholders: Public service companies maintaining utility-designated pollinator areas, local governments and zoning authorities, and native pollinator and wildlife populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes standards and protections for utility-designated pollinator areas and vegetation management performed by public service companies, which are regulated by the Public Service Commission pursuant to statewide service quality, reliability, and vegetation management standards.

The bill references plant listings maintained by the Department of Agriculture to define native plants and explicitly preserves existing State and local weed control laws under Title 9, Subtitle 4 of the Agriculture Article.

Synopsis: Altering the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Program to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program; expanding the purpose of the Program to include food from certified Chesapeake invasive species providers in the overall percentage goal of 20% of the unit's total dollar value for certain procurement contracts; and altering the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Food Aggregation Grant Fund to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Fund.
Title: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Renames the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Program to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program. Expands the State's 20% food procurement goal to include food from certified Chesapeake invasive species providers. Defines certified Chesapeake invasive species as high-priority finfish harvested from the Chesapeake Bay or its tributaries. Requires each State unit to structure food procurement procedures to try to achieve the combined 20% goal. Directs the Department of Agriculture to maintain a public directory and submit an annual consolidated implementation report.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
stakeholders: State procurement units, licensed seafood dealers and watermen providing Chesapeake invasive species, and certified local farms
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or expenditures. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement program expansion and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, with minimal expected impact on agency food procurement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture houses the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and is responsible for administering the program, certifying providers, adopting regulations, maintaining the provider directory, and submitting annual consolidated reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO administers the Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Fund and receives mandated general fund appropriations to provide grants and near-equity investments supporting aggregation sites and program participation.
The Board of Public Works receives annual reports regarding procurement goal waivers, must approve agency reporting guidelines, and submits waiver records annually to the General Assembly.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to the University System of Maryland.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to Morgan State University.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to St. Mary's College of Maryland.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding the definition of 'local' agricultural products for the Maryland Farm-to-School Meal Grant Pilot Program overseen by MSDE.
The criteria for certified Chesapeake invasive species rely on DNR's Maryland Aquatic Nuisance Species Management Plan and seafood dealer licensing under the Natural Resources Article.
As the state's central procurement authority, DGS manages state procurement standards and contracts that must adhere to the expanded food procurement goals.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of the service charge from $10 to $30 that may be imposed by a circuit court or the District Court for a dishonored check.
Title: Circuit Courts and District Court - Dishonored Checks - Service Charges

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Increases the service charge a circuit court clerk may impose for a dishonored check from $10 to $30. Authorizes the District Court to impose a $30 service charge for returned checks in motor vehicle, criminal, or civil cases. Applies when a check is returned for insufficient funds, a closed account, or a nonexistent account. Specifies that this service charge is in addition to any other penalty prescribed by law. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Circuit Courts; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Individuals who issue dishonored checks to pay circuit court charges or District Court fines and costs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by a minimum of $7,600 in fiscal 2024 and by a minimum of $10,100 annually thereafter due to higher service charges collected. Central Collection Unit special fund revenues may increase minimally. No material effect on State expenditures or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by authorizing clerks of the circuit courts and the District Court to increase the service charge assessed on dishonored checks from $10 to $30, resulting in increased general fund revenues collected by the courts.

DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which has a $30 minimum debt threshold. Increasing the fee to $30 enables the courts to refer delinquent check fees to CCU for collection, potentially generating minimal special fund fee revenues.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Transportation to implement all possible incremental near-term safety improvements as soon as practicable if a new approved pedestrian or bicycle safety construction or improvement project is projected to take more than 12 months to complete.
Title: Safe Access for All (SAFE) Roads Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to recommend and implement context-driven pedestrian and bicycle safety design elements. Applies this requirement during any construction, improvement, postconstruction, preservation, or maintenance project. Aligns these design elements with Federal Highway Administration Proven Safety Countermeasures. Mandates incremental, near-term safety improvements for approved pedestrian or bicycle projects projected to exceed 12 months. Requires implementation of these near-term improvements as soon as practicable. Maintains each project's priority ranking throughout implementation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Pedestrians and bicyclists using Maryland roadways, and highway contractors working on state transportation projects
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal redirection of Maryland Department of Transportation capital program funding beginning as early as fiscal 2023 to implement incremental safety improvements. No impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary department responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, specifically mandating that the Department implement incremental, near-term pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements whenever an approved safety project takes longer than 12 months.

As the modal agency within MDOT responsible for roadway planning, construction, and pedestrian/bicycle safety improvements across Maryland highways, SHA is directly responsible for carrying out the design and installation of the required near-term safety countermeasures.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "charitable contribution" to exclude an authorization for or a discount on the use of certain services or materials, equipment, or facilities for purposes of provisions of law regulating charitable organizations and charitable representatives; authorizing the Maryland Secretary of State to accept certain documentation in place of an audit or review in connection with a charitable organization's registration statement; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom

bill_summary: Alters the definition of charitable contribution under Maryland law regulating charitable organizations. Excludes certain donated property intended for free redistribution from the charitable contribution definition. Excludes discounts on or authorized use of services, materials, equipment, or facilities from the definition. Authorizes the Secretary of State to accept alternative documentation instead of an independent audit or review. Restricts this alternative option to qualifying charitable organizations that primarily solicit in-kind contributions.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
stakeholders: Charitable organizations operating or soliciting in Maryland and donors of in-kind property or discounted services
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in Maryland Secretary of State operational expenditures if additional staff are required to process waiver requests; revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 72 directly impacts the Secretary of State, which is the agency responsible for registering and overseeing charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill alters definitions regarding charitable contributions and authorizes the Secretary of State to review and accept alternative documentation in place of required audits or reviews for charitable registrations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Secretary of State on regulatory matters and assists in enforcing state laws related to charitable organizations and consumer protection.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education, before the start of the 2024-2025 school year, to adopt, implement, and publish guidelines in accordance with the State school health service guidelines to reduce the risk of exposure to anaphylactic major food allergens in classrooms and common areas; requiring each public school to develop a system to disclose the major food allergens contained in the foods served in the school; requiring each county board to make a good faith effort to adopt certain guidelines; etc.
