Title: Public Schools - Anaphylactic Food Allergies - Guidelines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt, implement, and publish guidelines reducing allergen exposure risks before the 2024–2025 school year. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health jointly to update school health guidelines by August 1, 2023. Directs each public school to develop a system to disclose served foods and their major food allergens in advance. Mandates that school principals monitor and implement local board guidelines for attending students with identified anaphylactic allergies. Prohibits requiring schools to dispose of certain pre-2023 food products lacking sesame labels before January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; county boards of education
stakeholders: public school students with anaphylactic food allergies, parents and guardians, public school educators and staff, and county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local revenues. The Maryland State Department of Education, the Maryland Department of Health, and local boards of education can implement the bill's guideline updates and disclosure requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 78 specifically requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to update the Maryland State School Health Services guidelines regarding anaphylactic food allergies and major food allergens, and oversees public school implementation.

HB 78 mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) jointly update the Maryland State School Health Services guidelines for anaphylaxis with MSDE. Additionally, local health departments and school health professionals under MDH's sphere have operational roles in school health services.

Synopsis: Requiring a tax collector to make certain attempts to contact a certain plaintiff or holder of a certificate of sale regarding certain expenses; and authorizing a collector to redeem certain property without a certain satisfaction letter if a plaintiff or holder of a certificate of sale fails to respond within 5 days after certain attempts by the collector to make contact.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Redemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires a tax collector to attempt contact with a tax sale certificate holder by phone and email. Triggers this requirement when the certificate holder fails to respond to an expense request for redemption. Applies to requests from the property owner, current mortgagee, assignee, mortgage servicer, or deed of trust beneficial interest holder. Authorizes the collector to redeem property without a satisfaction letter if the holder fails to respond within five business days.
responsible_party: Local Tax Collectors
stakeholders: Property owners whose property is sold at tax sale, mortgage lenders and mortgage servicers, holders of a beneficial interest in a deed of trust, and tax sale certificate holders
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts procedures surrounding property tax sales and the redemption process, which directly intersect with judicial actions to foreclose the right of redemption filed in the circuit courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted regarding court operations and proceedings related to these foreclosure actions.

Synopsis: Authorizing, subject to certain limitations, the disclosure of a business entity's federal employer identification number, name, physical address, mailing address, contact name, e-mail address, and phone number to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and its authorized contractors for the purposes of administering the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program and Trust.
Title: Disclosure of Tax Information – Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board – Authorization

bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to disclose specified tax information to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and its authorized contractors. Limits disclosures strictly to administering the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program and Trust. Permits disclosure of business identification numbers, names, addresses, and contact details received from State tax filings. Prohibits the disclosure of individual tax information and any information protected under federal law. Specifies that the Comptroller need not validate the tax information prior to disclosure. Requires recipients to use the information solely for purposes authorized by the Comptroller.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board
stakeholders: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, its authorized contractors, and Maryland business entities subject to retirement savings program requirements
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Comptroller's Office can handle the expanded disclosure authorization with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, which administers the MarylandSaves program, and its contractors to receive specific business tax information from the Comptroller to administer the program.

The bill amends Maryland tax disclosure statutes to authorize the Comptroller to disclose designated business entity tax information to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board under specified conditions and safeguards.

The State Treasurer's Office works closely with state savings initiatives and provided analysis regarding how accessing this tax information streamlines business registration and tracking for the program.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing bodies of counties and municipalities to adopt ordinances to regulate invasive bamboo, including by prohibiting a person from selling, planting, and allowing invasive bamboo to grow on the property of the person without proper upkeep and appropriate containment measures.
Title: Local Government - Regulatory Powers - Regulation of Invasive Bamboo

Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a county or municipality to regulate invasive bamboo by ordinance. Permits local ordinances to prohibit selling or planting invasive bamboo. Permits ordinances to prohibit growing invasive bamboo without proper upkeep and containment measures, including barriers or trenches. Authorizes local governing bodies to enforce ordinances by requiring mitigation of damages caused by invasive bamboo. Authorizes local governments to establish civil fines for violations.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of counties and municipalities
stakeholders: Property owners growing invasive bamboo, plant retailers and nurseries, landscaping businesses, and neighboring property owners
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. County and municipal governments can implement regulations using existing resources, with a potential indeterminate increase in local fine revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees the regulation and classification of invasive plant species (Tier 1 and Tier 2) and regulates plant nurseries and commercial sales statewide, which relates closely to local ordinances restricting the sale and planting of invasive bamboo.

The Department of Natural Resources manages invasive species impacts on Maryland natural habitats and public lands, maintains the statewide list of native plants, and served as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing that ground leases or amendments that are not posted on the State Department of Assessments and Taxation's website are not considered registered or amended; prohibiting a ground lease holder from collecting or attempting to collect rent, late fees, interest, collection costs, and other expenses related to a ground lease unless the ground lease is registered with the Department; etc.
Title: Ground Leases - Collection of Rent, Interest, Fees, and Other Expenses - Registration Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc

bill_summary: Establishes that ground leases and amendments are not registered until posted on the online state registry. Prohibits unregistered ground lease holders from collecting or attempting to collect ground rent, late fees, interest, or collection costs. Authorizes leasehold tenants to submit affidavits alleging unlawful collection to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Requires the Department to notify leaseholders, review responses, and issue decisions on alleged violations. Authorizes either party to file a circuit court action within 45 days of a final administrative decision. Requires the Department to void relevant ground lease registrations upon finding a violation or under court order.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: ground lease holders and leasehold tenants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State Department of Assessments and Taxation and Judiciary operations can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a right of action authorizing ground lease holders or leasehold tenants to file a de novo appeal in circuit court following a decision by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, requiring the courts to adjudicate these cases and issue orders regarding ground lease registrations.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition against a tenant who is seeking to redeem or extinguish ground rent providing certain documentation and payments to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation earlier than 90 days after an application for redemption or extinguishment has been posted on the Department's website.
Title: Residential Ground Leases - Redemption and Extinguishment - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc

bill_summary: Repeals a prohibition against leasehold tenants submitting redemption documentation and payments earlier than 90 days after website posting. Applies to tenants seeking to redeem or extinguish residential ground rents through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to submit required materials early for abandoned or distressed properties. Requires the Department to issue a certificate after notice has remained posted online for at least 90 days. Conditions certificate issuance on receipt of all required documentation, fees, redemption amounts, and past due ground rent.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: leasehold tenants of residential ground leases, ground lease holders, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: Likely generates operational efficiencies for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation but is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is identified as an information source in the fiscal note. The underlying statutory provisions governing ground rent redemption and extinguishment involve the circuit courts for interpleader actions and valuation disputes, although the bill's procedural timing changes primarily streamline the process before the State Department of Assessments and Taxation without imposing a significant operational impact on the courts.

Synopsis: Altering the types of elements and units for which a council of unit owners is required to maintain certain property insurance and altering certain requirements for the property insurance policy; and requiring owners of detached units to carry homeowners insurance on the entirety of the unit.
Title: Condominiums - Mandatory Insurance Coverage - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Alters mandatory property insurance requirements maintained by a condominium council of unit owners. Limits mandatory council property insurance coverage to common elements for detached condominium units. Maintains required council coverage on common elements and units for attached or multifamily dwelling units. Requires owners of residential, detached units to carry homeowners insurance on the entire unit. Restricts insurance proceeds disbursements for damaged units to condominiums with attached or multifamily units.
responsible_party: Council of Unit Owners
stakeholders: Condominium councils of unit owners, owners of detached condominium units, owners of attached or multifamily condominium units, and property insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters mandatory property insurance coverage requirements for condominium associations and establishes a statutory requirement for owners of detached condominium units to carry homeowners insurance, directly impacting the types and terms of property and casualty insurance policies regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The Secretary of State is the primary state entity responsible for the registration and oversight of condominium regimes in Maryland, which are directly governed by the condominium provisions modified by this bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provided information for the fiscal analysis and oversees the judicial branch, which adjudicates property dispute claims and disputes arising under the Maryland Condominium Act.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Agriculture to publish a fact sheet on the protection of pets in the event of an eviction or any other loss of possession of real property; requiring a landlord to provide a link to the fact sheet on the Department's website at the execution of a lease on or after November 1, 2023; requiring the Maryland Judiciary to provide a link to the fact sheet at certain times; requiring a sheriff or any other official to return a pet to a tenant or certain other person or to contact an animal shelter or rescue organization; etc.
Title: Real Property - Actions for Possession - Pet Protections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes pet protection procedures during evictions and real property repossession actions. Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture to publish a pet care eviction fact sheet by October 1, 2023. Requires landlords knowing a tenant has a pet to provide the fact sheet link at lease execution. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to include the fact sheet link with specified warrants. Mandates that executing officials inspect for pets and contact shelters if occupants are absent. Prohibits leaving a removed pet on public property or a public right-of-way.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Residential tenants with pets, residential landlords, property owners, sheriffs, constables, animal shelters, and animal rescue organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland Judiciary can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Agriculture develop, publish on its website, and regularly update a fact sheet providing information on how a person may care for and protect pets in the event of an eviction or loss of possession of real property.

The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to include a link to the Department of Agriculture's pet protection fact sheet on warrants issued for failure to pay rent, breach of lease, tenant holding over, and wrongful detainer actions.

Synopsis: Modifying the manner in which the chief executive officer of a municipality may fulfill certain notice requirements concerning proposed municipal charter amendments; and requiring the municipality to maintain certain records or receipts and make the records or receipts available to the public.
Title: Municipalities - Charter Amendments - Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes the chief executive officer of a municipality to provide notice of a proposed charter amendment through an alternative delivery method. Allows publishing a fair summary in a newspaper at least once and delivering a copy to every municipal residence. Permits delivery by hand, mail, or inclusion in a printed newsletter or regular municipal publication. Requires the municipality to maintain delivery records under its records retention schedule and make them publicly available. Extends the required posting duration for petition-initiated charter amendments from four weeks to at least 40 days before a referendum.
responsible_party: Chief executive officer of each Maryland municipality; Maryland municipal governments
stakeholders: Residents of Maryland municipalities and municipal officials
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Municipal expenditures and revenues are not materially affected.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025, to enroll individuals, based on certain eligibility, in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and the Maryland Children's Health Program; and requiring the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance to submit a final report to certain committees of the General Assembly by January 1, 2024, of its findings and recommendations, including recommended legislative and regulatory changes.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025. It enrolls individuals in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility. Prohibits the department from considering any other income or eligibility requirements. Requires the department to apply for federal Section 1115 waivers if needed to maximize eligible residents. Authorizes the department to implement express lane eligibility for renewals before initial enrollments. Requires the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance to submit a final report by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance
stakeholders: Low-income individuals and children receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits who are eligible for Medicaid or the Maryland Children's Health Program; low-income utility customers
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate impact on Maryland Department of Health revenues and expenditures to implement the Express Lane Eligibility Program, though new costs are subject to a 61% federal matching rate. The Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance can complete its final report using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 111 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025, to enroll individuals into Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility determinations, including applying for any necessary federal § 1115 waivers.

DHS administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), whose eligibility findings serve as the foundation for the Express Lane Eligibility Program, requiring DHS to enter into data use agreements with MDH. Additionally, DHS staffs the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, whose final reporting deadline is extended under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirement for the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, requiring it to submit a final report of study, findings, and recommendations by January 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing an Ocean City promoter's license in Worcester County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue the license to a for-profit organization to sell and serve beer, wine, and liquor at an entertainment event that is held on premises located within the corporate limits of the Town of Ocean City, owned by the Town of Ocean City, and approved in writing by the Ocean City Police Department; and authorizing a license fee of $5,000 per entertainment event.
Title: Worcester County - Alcoholic Beverages - Ocean City Promoter's License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes an Ocean City promoter’s license in Worcester County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue the license to a for-profit organization. Allows the licensee to sell and serve beer, wine, and liquor at entertainment events on specified town-owned premises. Requires event premises to be within Ocean City and designated and approved in writing by the Ocean City Police Department. Authorizes the board to adopt regulations restricting annual licenses and establishing health and safety standards. Sets the promoter's license fee at $5,000 per entertainment event.
responsible_party: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners; Ocean City Police Department
stakeholders: for-profit entertainment event promoters in Ocean City, the Town of Ocean City, and the Worcester County government
fiscal_impact_summary: Worcester County revenues increase by approximately $25,000 in fiscal 2024 from an estimated five licenses issued at $5,000 per event. Additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing county resources. No state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and administers state alcohol and sales taxes. While this bill specifically authorizes the local Worcester County Board of License Commissioners to issue promoter licenses for events in Ocean City with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to the regulation of alcoholic beverage sales in the state.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a leasehold tenant of an unregistered ground lease from being required to hold more than 3 years of ground rent in escrow; requiring a ground lease holder to mail certain notices or bills to a leasehold tenant in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to make available on its website the form a ground lease holder must use to provide a leasehold tenant bills or notices; etc.
Title: Ground Leases – Notices and Billing – Forms and Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits requiring leasehold tenants of unregistered ground leases to hold more than 3 years of ground rent in escrow. Requires ground lease holders to mail possession notices, installment bills, and transfer notices by first-class and certified mail. Prohibits ground lease holders from requiring leasehold tenants to reimburse costs incurred in providing required notices and bills. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to develop and publish mandatory forms for notices and bills. Requires transferees of ground leases to notify the department and tenants within 30 days of a transfer.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Ground lease holders, ground lease transferees, and leasehold tenants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no material impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes strict pre-filing notice, billing, and documentation requirements for ground lease holders seeking to file civil actions for possession in Maryland courts, directly impacting civil case filings and procedures administered by the judicial branch.

Synopsis: Requiring a treatment plan for an individual with a mental disorder admitted to a certain health care facility to include a discharge goal and an estimate of the probable length of the inpatient stay before the individual can be transferred to a certain setting; requiring certain facility staff to review and reassess a plan of treatment within certain time periods; requiring the Department of Health to report annually to the General Assembly on the Resident Grievance System and the grievances received related to State facilities; etc.
Title: Mental Health - Treatment Plans for Individuals in Facilities and Resident Grievance System

Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Requires mental health treatment plans in health care facilities to include a long-range discharge goal and estimated length of stay. Requires direct-care facility staff to reassess treatment plans every 15 days initially and every 60 days thereafter. Requires facilities to offer patients opportunities to authorize family members or other individuals to participate in treatment meetings. Authorizes patients or authorized individuals to request reviews of treatment plans and file grievances through the Resident Grievance System. Authorizes appeals of grievance reconsiderations to the Maryland Department of Health's Healthcare System Chief Medical Officer. Requires the Department to submit an annual report to the General Assembly on the Resident Grievance System starting in 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: individuals admitted to mental health facilities, their family members and designated representatives, facility treatment staff, and health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures for additional Maryland Department of Health staff to manage reviews, reconsiderations, and appeals, as well as potential costs for providing treatment outside State facilities. Specific dollar figures are unavailable. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) directly oversees State mental health facilities, administers the Resident Grievance System, is tasked with adopting regulations for the new appeals process to its Healthcare System's Chief Medical Officer, and must submit an annual report to the General Assembly on grievances received.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain plug-in electric drive vehicles for which a permit has been issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration to use high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes regardless of the number of passengers in the vehicles; requiring the Administration to charge a fee, not to exceed $20, for issuing the permit; and requiring, on or before January 1 each year, a report to be submitted to the Governor and the General Assembly on the effect of the use of the plug-in electric drive vehicle permits on the operation of HOV lanes.
Title: Vehicle Laws – HOV Lanes – Plug–In Electric Drive Vehicles

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles

bill_summary: Authorizes certain plug-in electric drive vehicles with permits to use high-occupancy vehicle lanes regardless of passenger occupancy. Applies only to plug-in electric drive vehicles capable of maximum speeds of at least 65 miles per hour. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to charge a permit fee not exceeding $20. Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to limit permit quantities upon recommendation of the State Highway Administration. Requires both administrations jointly to report annually by January 1 on the permit program's traffic effects. Terminates the authorization on September 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; State Highway Administration; Department of State Police
stakeholders: owners and drivers of plug-in electric drive vehicles capable of at least 65 miles per hour; Maryland motorists using high-occupancy vehicle lanes
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase through fiscal 2026 from permit fees capped at $20 (potentially up to $380,000 for roughly 19,000 projected permits). Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase minimally through fiscal 2026 by up to $26,220 to purchase decals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency tasked with issuing the plug-in electric vehicle HOV permits, collecting permit fees of up to $20, procuring decals, consulting on permit design, and submitting an annual report jointly with SHA.

SHA designates HOV lanes, may consult on permit design, provides recommendations to MVA to limit permit issuance to avoid operational degradation of HOV lanes, and co-authors the annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.
MDOT is the parent department of both MVA and SHA; the bill directly impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) through permit fee revenues and decal expenditures.
The Department of State Police is authorized to consult with MVA and SHA regarding the design of the HOV permit and enforces traffic regulations on state highways.
The Governor's Office receives the required annual report submitted jointly by MVA and SHA evaluating the effect of the permits on HOV lane operations.

bill_summary: Prohibits the District Court from ordering an individual to appear for an examination to enforce a small claims judgment. Prohibits the court from ordering an individual to answer interrogatories in aid of judgment execution. Limits post-judgment discovery methods available to creditors seeking to collect on small claims judgments. These statutory changes take effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Judgment debtors and judgment creditors in District Court small claims actions, including small businesses seeking debt collection
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on state or local finances. District Court operational adjustments, such as updating forms, brochures, and webpages, can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters procedures in the District Court by prohibiting judges from ordering individuals to appear for examinations or answer interrogatories in aid of enforcement of money judgments resulting from small claims actions. The Administrative Office of the Courts must implement these operational changes and update District Court forms, brochures, and webpages.

Synopsis: Converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage from an opt-in offering of coverage into an opt-out coverage option under provisions of law establishing requirements for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance; requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a study on the impact of converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage to an opt-out coverage option and report its findings to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2028; etc.
Title: Private Passenger Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance - Enhanced Underinsured Motorist Coverage - Opt-Out Option

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund

bill_summary: Converts enhanced underinsured motorist coverage from an opt-in option to an opt-out default for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance. Requires insurers to provide enhanced coverage on new policies issued on or after July 1, 2024, unless affirmatively waived in writing. Prohibits a waiver from taking effect unless the insurer first provides written notice of the coverage's nature, benefit, and cost. Requires waivers to be executed on a form required by the Insurance Commissioner. Directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to study the conversion's impact and submit reports by December 2026 and December 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Private passenger motor vehicle liability insurers and policyholders purchasing or renewing private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from the 2% insurance premium tax due to higher overall premiums. The Maryland Insurance Administration can conduct the study and complete required reports using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing the bill. It is responsible for prescribing the required waiver and offer forms, reviewing rate and form filings from insurers, and conducting a multi-year study with interim and final reports on the impact of moving EUIM coverage to an opt-out default.

MAIF issues private passenger motor vehicle liability policies as the insurer of last resort in Maryland, is subject to the statutory insurance requirements regarding underinsured motorist coverage, and is explicitly referenced in the bill's provisions regarding order of recovery priority.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is required to submit an interim report by December 31, 2026, and a final report by December 31, 2028, to the Governor detailing the findings and recommendations of the EUIM study.

Synopsis: Repealing the crime of unnatural or perverted sexual practice.
Title: Criminal Law – Unnatural or Perverted Sexual Practice – Repeal
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 796

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the criminal prohibition against unnatural or perverted sexual practices. Replaces statutory references to unnatural or perverted sexual practices with any other sexual conduct that is a crime. Retains prior convictions as qualifying offenses for human trafficking victims seeking to vacate judgments. Prohibits expungement of prior convictions committed without consent, with minors under age 16, or involving incapacitated individuals. Maintains Tier III sex offender registration requirements for prior offenses committed with force or threat of force. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals previously charged or convicted under prior unnatural or perverted sexual practice statutes, human trafficking victims, criminal justice entities, and sex offender registry officials
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal offense and modifies statutory provisions regarding criminal proceedings, motions to vacate judgments for human trafficking victims, and court record expungement petitions, directly impacting judicial administration and case tracking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities, community supervision, criminal history records, and sex offender registration requirements, which are modified under the bill's Tier III sex offender provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office represents indigent defendants charged with crimes, files motions to vacate convictions for human trafficking survivors, and assists clients with petitions for expungement affected by the repeal.

As the primary state law enforcement agency and repository for central criminal records, MSP is responsible for adjusting enforcement practices and complying with expungement orders for police records.

The bill amends the definition of sexual molestation and exploitation under Family Law and child welfare provisions governing Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and protective services administered by local social services departments.
The State Archives was consulted regarding the bill due to its role in maintaining permanent court and government records subject to statutory expungement provisions.

Synopsis: Altering certain qualifications for a journeyman license to provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration services to require having held an apprentice license for 4 rather than 3 years and having completed at least 6,000 rather than 1,875 hours of training under the direction and control of a licensed contractor.
Title: Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Services - Journeyman License - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Alters qualifications for a journeyman license to provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration services. Increases the required duration an applicant must hold an apprentice license from three years to four years. Raises the required training hours under a licensed contractor from at least 1,875 hours to 6,000 hours. Maintains the requirement that an applicant pass an examination administered by the Board.
responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) apprentices seeking journeyman licenses, licensed HVACR contractors, and businesses training apprentices
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund licensing revenues may be delayed if applicants spend more time in training before applying, but State finances and operations are not materially affected. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor directly regulates HVACR licensing through the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program within its Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. The bill alters statutory training hours and experience requirements for obtaining an HVACR journeyman license.

Synopsis: Limiting the percentage of the weekly benefits amount that the Secretary of Labor may deduct from weekly benefits payable to a claimant to recover certain overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits to 50% of the weekly benefit or 25% if the benefit is less than $100; and clarifying the circumstances under which the Secretary may use certain methods to recover overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits.
Title: Unemployment Insurance - Recovery of Benefits - Limitation and Methods

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Limits the amount the Secretary of Labor may deduct from future weekly benefits to recover nonfraud overpayments. Authorizes deductions of up to 50% of the weekly benefit amount from future weekly benefits payable. Restricts the deduction to up to 25% if the weekly benefit amount is $100 or less. Maintains existing alternative collection methods, including civil suits, assessments, and debt collection under State or federal law. Takes effect April 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Unemployment insurance claimants who received nonfraud benefit overpayments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, incurring a one-time administrative programming cost of $16,400 in fiscal 2024 funded by existing or additional federal funds. Nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund expenditures increase and revenues increase as alternative recovery methods are used; the net impact on the trust fund is unknown but expected to be negative. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Unemployment Insurance directly administers the State's unemployment insurance program. The bill restricts the Secretary of Labor's ability to recover non-fraud overpayments by capping weekly benefit deductions, requires the Secretary to adopt implementing regulations, and impacts the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Renaming the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs to be the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs; increasing the number of members of the Commission from 15 to 21; altering certain qualifications for members appointed to the Commission; staggering the terms of Commission members; and altering the duties of the Commission.
Title: State Government – Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs – Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Renames the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs in the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs. Expands the Commission's membership from 15 to 21 members appointed by the Governor with Senate advice and consent. Establishes staggered four-year terms for Commission members expiring in 2024, 2025, and 2026. Broadens appointment criteria to reflect additional forms of diversity including age, disability, and socioeconomic status. Directs the Commission to assess challenges, study best practices, and collect State agency data regarding LGBTQIA+ communities.
responsible_party: Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs; Governor's Office of Community Initiatives
stakeholders: LGBTQIA+ individuals and communities in Maryland, and members of the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for expense reimbursements for additional commission members can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs is explicitly housed as a unit within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives, which provides administrative support and oversight to the commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition, member qualifications, terms, and duties of the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs, an executive commission.

The bill increases the number of Commission members from 15 to 21, sets new qualification criteria, and establishes staggered terms, directly impacting the Office of Appointments' duties to recruit and vet gubernatorial appointees.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the 21 members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, and holds the authority to remove members for cause.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who fails to reactivate a real estate broker license on inactive status within 3 years to comply with specified requirements to obtain a license.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Inactive Licenses - Requirements After Expiration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Requires individuals whose inactive real estate licenses expire to satisfy initial licensing qualifications to obtain a new license. Applies when a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson fails to reactivate within three years. Mandates compliance with statutory application, examination, and prelicensing education requirements under state law. Retains existing reactivation procedures for inactive licensees who apply before the three-year expiration period ends. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons holding inactive licenses
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, as the Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement procedural changes using existing budgeted resources. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The department oversees professional licensing standards and will implement the procedural requirements for real estate brokers seeking licensure after inactive status expiration.

Synopsis: Exempting applications for changing certain resident agents from the requirement that the Board of License Commissioners for Howard County hold a public hearing on the applications; and authorizing the Board to hold a public hearing on certain applications if the Board determines there is good cause for the hearing.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Public Hearing Ho. Co. 13-23
bill_summary: Exempts certain applicants for a change of resident agent from public hearing requirements in Howard County. Applies to license holders seeking to become resident agents for their existing alcoholic beverages license. Requires that the applicant previously appeared and received approval at a nonviolation hearing for the same license. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to hold a hearing if it determines good cause exists. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Howard County
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders in Howard County seeking to become resident agents
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances or local revenues. Howard County expenditures decrease by up to approximately $14,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to reduced hearing costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation amends the Alcoholic Beverages Article, it specifically alters hearing notice and public hearing requirements administered by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners with no state-level regulatory or fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Altering the entity that must administer or approve an apprenticeship program for electricians; substituting the term "uninsured" for the term "inactive" in certain provisions of law relating to liability insurance requirements for certain electricians; prohibiting a certain electrician from contracting to provide electrical services unless the electrical work is covered by certain liability insurance; specifying who is authorized and required to purchase certain insurance; etc.
Title: Maryland Electricians Act - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Designates the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning to approve electrician apprenticeship programs. Replaces inactive licensing status with uninsured status throughout the Maryland Electricians Act. Prohibits contracting for electrical services unless covered by specified general liability and property damage insurance. Authorizes an uninsured master electrician to provide electrical services only as a journeyperson electrician in certain counties. Requires the State Board of Electricians to specify on each license whether the holder meets insurance requirements.
responsible_party: State Board of Electricians; Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning
stakeholders: licensed master electricians, journeyperson electricians, apprentice electricians, electrical inspectors, and electrical services businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues. The State Board of Electricians can implement the bill's administrative changes with existing resources. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor directly oversees professional licensing—including the State Board of Electricians—and houses the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning (DWDAL), which is designated under the bill as the approving entity for electrician apprenticeship programs and continuing education.

Synopsis: Establishing that adaptive reuse, retrofitting, and repurposing of existing buildings to develop new affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of certain financial assistance provided by the Department of Housing and Community Development; requiring the Department to notify applicants for certain financial assistance that adaptive reuse is an eligible use of funds; and providing that the notice requirement does not apply to individuals applying for loans from the Department that are not focused on housing.
Title: Housing and Community Development - Adaptive Reuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Establishes that adaptive reuse of existing buildings to develop affordable multifamily housing is an eligible loan use. Applies to any Department of Housing and Community Development program awarding loans for affordable multifamily housing development. Specifies that more specific program laws or regulations govern when they establish distinct adaptive reuse rules. Requires the Department to notify covered loan applicants that adaptive reuse is an eligible use of loan proceeds. Exempts loan applications under Department programs that do not focus on housing from the notice requirement.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: applicants for Department of Housing and Community Development housing loans, affordable housing developers, and individuals in need of affordable multifamily housing
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local operations or finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development already finances adaptive reuse projects and can notify loan applicants using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs loan programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), clarifying that adaptive reuse of existing buildings for affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of loan proceeds and requiring DHCD to notify loan applicants of this eligibility.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from including a certain term in a lease pertaining to electronic delivery of the notice of a rent increase; requiring a landlord to notify a tenant in writing before increasing the tenant's rent through first-class mail or, if elected by the tenant, electronic delivery; requiring a county or municipality that adopts a certain local law related to limitations on rent increases to report annually certain information on building permits issued for multifamily dwellings intended as rental housing; etc.
Title: Real Property - Residential Leases - Notification of Rent Increases

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires residential landlords to notify tenants in writing in advance of rent increases. Establishes advance notification timelines ranging from 7 to 90 days based on the length of the tenancy. Prohibits lease provisions requiring tenants to accept electronic delivery of rent increase notices. Prohibits landlords from conditioning lease application acceptance on electing electronic delivery. Requires local jurisdictions enacting rent increase limits to report bill details and multifamily rental building permit data to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly; local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities)
stakeholders: residential tenants, residential landlords, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local operations or finances, with minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Judiciary adjudicates landlord-tenant disputes and eviction proceedings, which may involve enforcement or defenses related to statutory lease requirements and rent increase notice periods.
The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces state consumer protection and fair housing laws, which encompass residential lease provisions and landlord-tenant practices.
The Department of Housing and Community Development monitors state housing policy, multifamily rental housing conditions, and regulations affecting residential rental communities.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose and contents of and the requirements and qualifications under the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund; requiring the Governor, in each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029, to include at least $100,000 for the Fund in the annual budget bill; establishing the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to recommend guidelines, policies, and practices for the implementation of the Grant Program; and requiring the Advisory Committee to report to certain committees of the General Assembly by December 30, 2023.
Title: Department of Agriculture - Urban Agriculture Grant Programs - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for grants under the Urban Agriculture Grant Program to agricultural producers, nonprofit organizations, and institutions of higher education. Broadens the definition of urban agricultural producer to include producers in any census-delineated urban area or municipal corporation. Requires the Governor to appropriate at least $100,000 annually to the Fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2029. Establishes the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to recommend grant guidelines, policies, and practices. Requires the committee to report annually to the Governor and designated legislative committees by December 30.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Urban agricultural producers, nonprofit organizations, and institutions of higher education in urban areas across Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2029 under a mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund increase correspondingly. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Urban Agriculture Grant Program, managing the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund, providing staff support to the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee, and determining applicant qualifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is statutorily designated to appoint one member to the newly established Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to advise on program guidelines, policies, and practices and to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.
DBM oversees the state budget and will be responsible for incorporating the bill's mandated annual appropriation of at least $100,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

The Governor is mandated to include an appropriation of at least $100,000 annually in the state budget for FY 2025 through 2029, and the Governor receives an annual report from the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund as a separate, nonlapsing special fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily responsible for accounting for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund.
Public institutions of higher education within USM are made eligible to apply for and receive grant funding and provide farmer training and technical assistance under the expanded program.
As a public institution of higher education, MSU is eligible to qualify for grant funds to provide agricultural training and technical assistance under the program.

Synopsis: Altering the voting rights of and the process for selecting a student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; prohibiting the student member from voting on matters before the board relating to personnel and collective bargaining decisions; establishing the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by April 1, 2024.
Title: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners - Student Members and Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the voting rights of the student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners. Requires the student member to be an enrolled high school junior or senior. Requires middle and high school students in the Baltimore City Public School System to elect the student member. Authorizes the student member to vote on budgets, school boundaries, and student disciplinary matters. Prohibits the student member from voting on personnel and collective bargaining decisions. Establishes a task force to study board compensation and adding a second student member.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; Office of the Mayor of Baltimore City; Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners
stakeholders: Middle and high school students in the Baltimore City Public School System, the student member, and members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal and absorbable impact on State expenditures for task force travel reimbursements. Baltimore City Public Schools and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office can implement the bill using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to examine board member compensation, evaluate adding a second student member, and submit recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Maryland State Department of Education exercises statewide oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 local school systems, and the bill amends the state Education Article regarding the governance, composition, and voting powers of the Baltimore City local school board.

The Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners is required by statute to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor by April 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Providing that a resident of the State meets certain residency requirements for an applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirements Ho. Co. 11-23
bill_summary: Allows an individual who resides anywhere in Maryland to satisfy residency requirements for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County. Extends this statewide residency qualification to applicants applying on behalf of partnerships, corporations, clubs, and limited liability companies. Alters petition of support provisions to verify Maryland residency instead of county residency. Removes requirements that continuing care retirement community license applicants be Howard County registered voters and taxpayers. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and license holders in Howard County, including partnerships, corporations, clubs, limited liability companies, and Maryland residents seeking county licenses
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Howard County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state and prescribes statewide alcoholic beverages application forms referenced under Article - Alcoholic Beverages § 4-108. However, because the bill specifically alters local residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Howard County, the direct impact on the Comptroller is minimal with no state fiscal effect.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority from issuing bonds beginning June 1, 2023; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to evaluate the Authority providing enough detail for the General Assembly to determine whether the Authority should continue in its current form; etc.
Title: Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority - Evaluation, Termination of Bond Authority, and Assumption of Functions, Employees, and Contracts (Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority Sunset Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Prohibits the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority from issuing bonds beginning June 1, 2023. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to evaluate the Authority and submit draft merger legislation by December 1, 2024. Directs the Maryland Environmental Service to review the Authority's contracts and employees by December 1, 2024. Requires the Maryland Environmental Service to temporarily assume the Authority's functions, employees, and contracts during any merger. Mandates that any entity assuming the Authority's operations establish a system to maintain stakeholder engagement.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Environmental Service; Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority
stakeholders: Member jurisdictions of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Harford, Howard, and Montgomery counties and Baltimore City), employees of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority, and entities contracting with the Authority
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted expenditures and matching revenues increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Environmental Service to conduct the required review. Potential indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures for the Department of Legislative Services in FY 2024 and FY 2025. Potential increase in local expenditures for member jurisdictions via Authority membership fees to cover study costs. Significant potential nonbudgeted expenditure and revenue impacts may occur in FY 2026 or later if the Maryland Environmental Service temporarily assumes Authority functions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 161 directly mandates that the Maryland Environmental Service review the functions, employees, and contracts of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (NMWDA) and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. MES is also required to temporarily assume all functions, employees, and active contracts of NMWDA during any merger, incurring estimated nonbudgeted expenditures of $100,000 in FY 2024.

The bill explicitly requires the evaluation of NMWDA to assess the impact that discontinuing the authority would have on the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and the pensions of NMWDA employees.
MDE regulates solid waste management and recycling under the Maryland Recycling Act, which is evaluated under the bill. MDE also served as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for certain local law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department under certain circumstances; providing that a certain individual is entitled to eligibility service and creditable service that was earned before the effective date of the Crisfield Police Department's participation in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System; providing for the transfer of creditable service for a certain individual; etc.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Crisfield Police Department

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for permanent full-time Crisfield police officers if the department participates. Grants transferred officers eligibility and creditable service for their prior employment with the Crisfield Police Department. Terminates their membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon joining the system. Exempts the service credit transfer from standard statutory contribution repayment requirements. Directs the transfer of assets and crediting of contributions under existing statutory procedures.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Crisfield Police Department
stakeholders: permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department and the City of Crisfield
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Contingent on the City of Crisfield electing to join the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System as a participating governmental unit, local employer pension contributions increase by approximately $120,700 annually and pension liabilities increase by $1.0 million. No effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). The bill directly impacts their administration by governing the membership, service credit transfer, and asset crediting for eligible Crisfield Police Department officers transferring into LEOPS.

Synopsis: Altering the list of crimes included within a certain definition of "crime of violence" to include sexual abuse of a minor if the offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under the age of 16 years; and requiring a sentence for certain persons convicted of certain sexual abuse crimes to include a term of lifetime sexual offender supervision.
Title: Sexual Offenses - Crime of Violence and Lifetime Supervision

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Harassment; Threats

bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of a crime of violence to include sexual abuse of a minor under specified conditions. Applies this classification when an offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under 16. Requires lifetime sexual offender supervision for adults convicted of child sexual abuse against victims under age 13. Mandates lifetime sexual offender supervision when an offender at least 21 years old abuses a victim under 16. Extends lifetime supervision mandates to adults convicted of specified second-degree sexual offenses occurring before October 1, 2017. Applies all changes prospectively to convictions occurring on or after October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Division of Parole and Probation
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual abuse of a minor or second-degree sexual offenses; victims of child sexual abuse; sex offender supervision agents
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in state general fund expenditures beginning in future years due to expanded incarceration and lifetime sexual offender supervision requirements. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS and its Division of Parole and Probation are directly responsible for conducting lifetime sexual offender supervision, managing incarceration and diminution credits for crimes of violence, and adopting regulations to administer the supervision requirements.

The Judiciary and sentencing courts are tasked with imposing the required lifetime supervision conditions at sentencing, reviewing presentence investigations, and adjudicating petitions for discharge from supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants facing criminal prosecution, sentencing enhancements, and lifetime supervision requirements expanded under the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to procure or provide for electricity customers energy efficiency and conservation programs and services designed to achieve certain target annual incremental gross energy savings for the 2024-2026 program cycle; establishing the Green and Healthy Task Force to develop policy and statutory recommendations to eliminate barriers to low-income households achieving, energy-efficient, affordable, and low-emissions housing; requiring an annual report beginning July 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Energy Efficiency and Conservation Programs - Energy Performance Targets and Low-Income Housing

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to procure or provide energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income electricity customers. Sets annual incremental gross energy savings targets of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026. Mandates approved contractors pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage and provide specified employee benefits. Establishes the Green and Healthy Task Force to coordinate housing resources for low-income communities. Directs the Department and task force to plan energy efficiency retrofits for all low-income households by 2031. Requires a disparity study evaluating remedial measures for minority- and women-owned businesses by December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Public Service Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation; Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
stakeholders: Low-income residential electricity customers and tenants; affordable housing owners and managers; electric companies; weatherization and energy efficiency contractors; minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development increase by an estimated $39.8 million in FY 2024, rising to $214.2 million by FY 2028 to meet statutory savings targets. These costs are funded by special fund revenues from EmPOWER Maryland surcharges collected on utility bills, ultimately increasing electricity rates for customers. Local housing authorities and weatherization agencies receive increased program and grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency under the bill, responsible for procuring and providing energy efficiency and conservation programs, achieving incremental gross energy savings targets, submitting triennial plans and biannual updates to the PSC, and staffing and chairing the newly established Green and Healthy Task Force.

PSC oversees the EmPOWER Maryland program, reviews and approves DHCD's triennial energy savings plans, establishes procedures for implementation, and reports annually to the General Assembly on low-income energy efficiency programs.

MEA is consulted on PSC's annual report, required to apply for all available federal funding to implement the bill, and serves as a designated member on the Green and Healthy Task Force, with potential special fund expenditure impacts.

As the State's designated MBE certification agency under the Board of Public Works, MDOT is tasked alongside GOSBA with conducting a disparity study regarding energy efficiency and conservation services by December 31, 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is mandated, in conjunction with the State's certification agency (MDOT), to initiate and submit a disparity study on minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency and conservation sector.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Green and Healthy Task Force to meet quarterly for three years to coordinate resources and develop policy recommendations for healthy, energy-efficient housing for low-income households.
DHCD is required to coordinate directly with DBM to identify additional funding sources to support whole-home energy efficiency and safety upgrade program expansions.
The Secretary of Human Services (or a designee) is designated by statute as a formal voting member of the Green and Healthy Task Force.
A representative from the Office of People's Counsel is designated to serve as a member of the Green and Healthy Task Force.
OAG must be consulted by MDOT and GOSBA during the execution of the required disparity study on energy efficiency contracting.
The Secretary of Health is designated as an official recipient of the annual findings and recommendations reported by the Green and Healthy Task Force.
The Secretary of the Environment is designated as an official recipient of the annual findings and recommendations reported by the Green and Healthy Task Force.

Title: Health Occupations - Licensed Athletic Trainers - Dry Needling Approval
