bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Physicians to approve licensed athletic trainers to perform dry needling as a specialized task. Requires applicants to complete at least 80 hours of approved continuing education instruction. Mandates at least 40 hours of didactic coursework and 40 hours of practical, hands-on instruction. Requires hands-on training under the guidance of a licensed practitioner with at least five years of dry needling experience. Subjects athletic trainers who perform dry needling without Board approval to disciplinary action.
responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Licensed athletic trainers and patients receiving athletic training services in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $31,893 in fiscal 2024 and $6,400 in fiscal 2025 for a part-time contractual analyst and one-time licensing software modifications. Special fund revenues may increase if the Board establishes an approval fee. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Board of Physicians, a licensing board within the Department of Health, by requiring it to establish an approval process, verify training requirements, handle specialized applications, and enforce disciplinary standards for licensed athletic trainers performing dry needling.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain assistant State's Attorney with knowledge of the case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior or the victim's representative within 20 days after receiving a request from the victim regarding a decision by the Office of the State's Attorney  not to file a charging document or to dismiss charges against an alleged suspect; requiring the assistant State's Attorney, at the meeting, to explain the justification for a certain decision; and establishing certain requirements for the meeting.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Victims of Sexually Assaultive Behavior
bill_summary: Requires an assistant State’s Attorney with knowledge of a case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior. The requirement also permits meeting with a representative designated by the victim. The meeting must take place within 20 days after receiving a request from the victim. The obligation applies when prosecutors decide not to file charges or dismiss charges against an alleged suspect. The assistant State’s Attorney must explain the justification for not filing charges or for dismissing charges. Participants may conduct the meeting in person, by telephone, or by other mutually agreed means.
responsible_party: Offices of the State's Attorney
stakeholders: victims of sexually assaultive behavior, designated victim representatives, and assistant State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local State's Attorneys' offices can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) serves as Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety and oversees statewide victim services policies and funding. The bill expands crime victims' rights by requiring prosecutors to meet with victims of sexually assaultive behavior when charges are dropped or declined.

Synopsis: Authorizing the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters; requiring certain members of the county board and the executive leadership of the Baltimore County public school system to develop a certain draft curriculum for budget training for student members of the county board and submit the draft curriculum to the county board for review; and requiring each student member of the board to complete the budget training within 2 months of the student's election to the board.
Title: Baltimore County Board of Education - Student Member - Voting and Training

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: Authorizes the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters. Requires each student member to complete budget training within two months of election to vote on budgetary matters. Requires a workgroup of board members and school executive leadership to develop a draft budget training curriculum. Mandates submission of the draft curriculum to the county board for review by December 31, 2023. Requires the training to focus on budget processes and be facilitated by the Division of Business Services.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education; Baltimore County Public School System
stakeholders: Student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education and Baltimore County public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore County Public Schools and the Baltimore County Board of Education can develop and implement the training curriculum using existing local resources, with no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school boards. While the bill specifically governs voting rights and budget training requirements for the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the statutory framework and governance of a local school system under the Education Article.

Synopsis: Designating Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the State spirit.
Title: State Designations – State Spirit – Maryland Rye

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: Designates Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the official State spirit. Adds the designation to the list of official State symbols in the General Provisions Article. Renumbers existing statutory sections within the subtitle to accommodate the addition. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland State Archives
stakeholders: Maryland distillers, rye farmers, and spirits producers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives maintains official state records, state symbols, and the Maryland Manual On-Line, and served as the informational source regarding official State symbols for this legislation.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time within which a person is required to file a Maryland estate tax return for the purpose of allowing a surviving spouse to take into account the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount to be consistent with the time for making a federal election; and applying the Act retroactively to any decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019.
Title: Maryland Estate Tax - Portability - Time Period for Election
bill_summary: Alters the deadline to file a Maryland estate tax return solely to elect deceased spousal unused exclusion portability. Replaces the former two-year deadline with the time period prescribed under federal estate tax law. Requires the Comptroller to adopt regulations ensuring the State and federal election deadlines are identical. Applies retroactively to affect decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Surviving spouses and personal representatives or executors of decedents' estates electing estate tax exclusion portability
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential general fund revenue decrease beginning in FY 2024 due to increased use of the deceased spousal unused exclusion election. Administrative costs for the Comptroller's Office to update forms and adopt regulations will be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Comptroller with administering the Maryland estate tax return deadlines for the deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) portability election, updating tax forms and instructions, and adopting regulations to align the state filing period with federal standards.

The Register of Wills administers probate estates and collects inheritance taxes; the statute references the registers' role in certifying inheritance tax paid to the Comptroller in relation to amended estate tax returns, and the agency was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for and the amount of a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for a taxpayer who adopts a child during the taxable year.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Adoption Expenses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- Parents and Guardians

bill_summary: Alters eligibility for and the amount of the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for adopting a child. Sets the subtraction modification at $12,000 for adopting a child with a special need. Sets the subtraction modification at $10,000 for adopting a child without a special need. Requires adoptions to occur through a private, nonprofit, licensed adoption agency or a public child welfare agency. Repeals prior limits based on whether the child is a State resident at adoption. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers adopting a child; adoptive parents; adopted children with or without special needs; private, nonprofit, licensed adoption agencies; public child welfare agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $91,000 annually beginning in FY 2024. State general fund expenditures increase by $43,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time tax system alterations by the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $54,000 annually beginning in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state income taxes and administering tax modifications. The bill alters the personal income tax subtraction modification for adoption expenses, requiring one-time computer system changes that will cost the Comptroller's Office $43,000 in FY 2024.

The Department of Human Services oversees Maryland's foster care and public adoption services, including public child welfare agencies and determining whether a child has special needs under the relevant federal Social Security Act standards cited in the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification to an unlawfully restrictive covenant for a property within the boundaries of the county or municipality after providing persons with an ownership interest in the property with 30 days' written notice; and providing that persons with an ownership interest in property that is subject to an unlawfully restrictive covenant may decline action by a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification.
Title: Real Property - Unlawfully Restrictive Covenants - Modification by Counties or Municipalities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification for property within its boundaries. Applies to recorded covenants or restrictions that unlawfully restrict ownership based on race, religious belief, or national origin. Requires the county or municipality to provide written notice by first-class mail to all property owners. Mandates that this notice be sent at least 30 days before executing and recording the modification. Allows a property owner to decline the modification by notifying the local government within 30 days after notice. Excludes unlawfully restrictive covenants in declarations, general schemes, or development plans of homeowners associations.
responsible_party: Counties and Municipalities; Clerks of the Circuit Court; County Attorneys; Administrative Office of the Courts
stakeholders: Property owners whose deeds or chains of title contain unlawfully restrictive covenants; Maryland counties and municipalities
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Local government expenditures and operational impacts are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill interacts directly with the land recording processes of the Circuit Court Clerks, and the restrictive covenant modifications must be accompanied by an intake sheet on a form provided and maintained by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain employee or certain exclusive representative to initiate a grievance procedure under certain provisions of law; requiring certain decision makers in a grievance procedure in certain higher education systems to award certain damages under certain circumstances; requiring certain employee grievance procedures to include certain redress for certain violations; requiring the Secretary of Transportation to be consistent with certain provisions of law and include redress for certain violations; etc.
Title: State Personnel - Education and Transportation - Grievance Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes employees of specified State higher education institutions and the Maryland Department of Transportation to initiate grievances for wage reporting failures. Allows exclusive representatives of covered employees to initiate these grievance procedures. Requires decision makers in grievance proceedings to award statutory damages when wages are improperly withheld. Mandates that employee grievance procedures for these entities provide redress and damages for wage reporting violations. Requires grievances to be initiated within 20 days after the failure to pay, or within six months if undiscovered. Caps damages at three times the amount of wage due that an appointing authority failed to report.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland; Baltimore City Community College
stakeholders: Employees and exclusive representatives of the Maryland Department of Transportation, University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate, but anticipated to be minimal, increase in Transportation Trust Fund and higher education expenditures for potential grievance filings and damage payments. Reimbursable expenditures and revenues for the Office of Administrative Hearings increase to the extent additional grievance cases are referred and adjudicated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the Transportation Article (§ 2-103.4) requiring MDOT to update its regulations and human resources management grievance procedures to include redress and damages for wage and payroll reporting violations.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 13-201 and § 13-203) governing USM employee grievances, expanding grievance definitions to include wage withholding violations and mandating that decision-makers award damages.
The bill amends the Education Article (§ 14-302) to require decision-makers in grievance procedures at Morgan State University to award damages for wage withholding violations.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 14-408) requiring the personnel system and grievance procedures of St. Mary's College of Maryland to provide redress and damage awards for wage payment violations.

The bill affects grievance appeal procedures that are referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings for adjudication, resulting in an increase in reimbursable expenditures and revenues per case heard.

As the state's principal personnel agency managing state employee systems and policies, DBM oversees general State Personnel Management System grievance frameworks and provided estimates on grievance hearing costs.
The Central Payroll Bureau operates under the Comptroller of Maryland, receiving reported payroll information and processing missing wages and damages following resolved grievances.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Education from issuing a certificate of approval to noncollegiate educational institutions that do not have a policy prohibiting the administration of corporal punishment; requiring regulations adopted by the State Board for the registration of family child care homes and large family child care homes and the licensing and operation of child care centers to prohibit corporal punishment; and requiring the State Board to identify certain methods in a certain overall plan.
Title: Nonpublic Schools and Child Care Providers - Corporal Punishment - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Education to identify methods to find and eliminate corporal punishment of students statewide. Prohibits the Board from issuing certificates of approval to noncollegiate educational institutions lacking corporal punishment prohibition policies. Excludes institutions operated by bona fide church organizations from the certificate of approval requirement. Requires regulations for family child care homes and large family child care homes to prohibit corporal punishment. Mandates that child care center licensing and operating regulations prohibit corporal punishment to discipline a child.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Noncollegiate educational institutions, family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and enrolled children and students
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 185 directly tasks the State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) with updating statewide plans to eliminate corporal punishment, conditioning certificates of approval for nonpublic educational institutions on corporal punishment prohibitions, and adopting regulations prohibiting physical discipline in registered and licensed child care facilities.

Synopsis: Providing for the stable funding and support of trauma-informed, high-quality programs and services for victims of crime; requiring the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to help support certain programs providing services for victims of crime; requiring the Office to consult with certain individuals and organizations regarding the allocation of certain funding; and requiring the Governor to include certain funding in the State budget.
Title: Victim Services Programs – Supplementing Federal Funding and Support (Victim Services Stabilization Act)

Elder Abuse and Neglect -see also- Vulnerable Adults
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to help support victim services programs statewide. Authorizes the office to award grants to public or private nonprofit organizations operating victim services programs. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation that, with prior-year federal funds, totals $60,000,000. Prohibits requiring programs to match state funds and prohibits using awarded funds for capital projects. Requires the Executive Director to submit an annual report to the General Assembly by December 31.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
stakeholders: Victims of crime, crime victim services programs, and public or private nonprofit organizations providing victim services
fiscal_impact_summary: Establishes a mandated aggregate appropriation of $60.0 million combining federal VOCA funds and State funds beginning in FY 2025. General fund expenditures are not anticipated to be affected assuming federal VOCA grants and current State funding levels remain steady. Local government revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (identified in the bill as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) is the primary administering agency responsible for supporting victim services programs, awarding grants, coordinating with federal VOCA funds, consulting stakeholder groups, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill that, in combination with federal VOCA awards from the prior year, totals $60.0 million for crime victim services programs.

As the principal agency responsible for formulating and executing the state budget, the Department of Budget and Management must incorporate and oversee the statutory mandated appropriation totaling $60.0 million in aggregate funding.

Synopsis: Increasing the membership of the Wildlife Advisory Commission; requiring the Governor to appoint a member to the Wildlife Advisory Commission who is an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, wildlife conservation, wildlife management, or ecology; and requiring the membership of the Commission to include representation from the farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities.
Title: Natural Resources - Wildlife Advisory Commission - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds

bill_summary: Expands the Wildlife Advisory Commission from nine to 10 members appointed by the Governor. Requires the Governor to appoint an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, conservation, management, or ecology. Mandates commission representation from the farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities. Establishes a four-year term for the new academic member beginning July 1, 2024. Prohibits altering the terms of commission members serving as of October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Governor; Department of Natural Resources; Wildlife Advisory Commission
stakeholders: Wildlife Advisory Commission members, academic researchers in wildlife sciences, farmers, hunters, wildlife preservation advocates, and passive wildlife recreationists
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Wildlife Advisory Commission is established within the Department of Natural Resources to advise on wildlife management, conservation, and recreational use policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory size, qualifications, terms, and stakeholder representation requirements of the Wildlife Advisory Commission.
The Governor is tasked with soliciting nominations and appointing the additional member who meets specific academic researcher criteria, as well as maintaining stakeholder balance on the commission.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages nominations and candidate selections for state boards and commissions on behalf of the Governor to fulfill the bill's new statutory appointment requirements.

Synopsis: Clarifying the language of provisions of law requiring the expungement of certain records maintained by the State or a political subdivision of the State relating to the charging of certain offenses under certain circumstances and notification of a certain right to expungement.
Title: Automatic Expungement - Clarification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Clarifies language governing automatic expungement of records for specified offenses with qualifying dispositions. Applies provisions to specified civil cannabis offenses and crimes other than non-appearance transportation violations. Requires expungement three years after disposition if charges result only in acquittal, dismissal, not guilty, or nolle prosequi. Mandates courts notify the Central Repository, relevant law enforcement agencies, and the defendant of the expungement date. Requires courts to notify eligible defendants of their right to expungement alongside a tort claim waiver form.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals charged with specified civil cannabis offenses or crimes other than non-appearance transportation violations whose charges result in favorable dispositions
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill clarifies existing statutory language without modifying government operations or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 189 directly impacts court processes by clarifying which court records are subject to automatic expungement and modifying the statutory notice requirements that the courts must send to defendants, the Central Repository, and law enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives notices of disposition from the courts and is responsible for expunging state criminal history records according to the clarified statutory criteria.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintains arrest and charging records that are subject to the automatic expungement provisions clarified under this bill.
The bill explicitly clarifies provisions concerning crimes and violations under the Transportation Article and the circumstances where an individual is or is not required to appear.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain persons subject to campaign finance regulation from making or accepting monetary contributions or monetary donations using any currency other than United States currency; prohibiting a campaign finance entity or a person acting on behalf of a campaign finance entity from making a monetary expenditure using any currency other than United States currency; authorizing the State Administrator of Elections or the Administrator's designee to investigate certain potential violations of the Act; etc.
Title: Currency - Campaign Finance Prohibitions - Disclosures by Financial Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Prohibits persons from making or accepting campaign contributions or donations using any currency other than United States currency. Prohibits campaign finance entities from making monetary expenditures using any currency other than United States currency. Authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to investigate potential violations and issue subpoenas for testimony and records. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to impose civil penalties or refer violations to the State Prosecutor. Expands the tax law definition of financial institution to include regulated virtual currency money transmitters. Authorizes the Comptroller to request tax enforcement information and assistance from virtual currency money transmitters.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; Maryland State Board of Elections; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: campaign finance entities, political donors, entities making independent expenditures or electioneering communications, and regulated virtual currency money transmitters
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in general fund revenues beginning in FY 2024 from tax liens satisfied through virtual currency accounts, and potential indeterminate increase in Fair Campaign Financing Fund revenues from civil and criminal penalties. Enforcement activities can be handled using existing agency resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns direct regulatory and enforcement authority to the State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections to investigate campaign finance violations involving non-U.S. currency, issue subpoenas, hold hearings, impose civil penalties, and adopt regulations.

The bill amends the Tax - General Article to authorize the Comptroller to request information and assistance from virtual currency money transmitters and direct them to seize or attach property subject to tax liens to enforce state tax laws.

The bill authorizes the State Board of Elections to refer potential willful and knowing criminal violations of campaign finance currency prohibitions to the State Prosecutor for investigation and prosecution.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to stay the entering of a conviction, defer further proceedings, and place a certain defendant on probation subject to reasonable conditions if the court finds facts justifying a finding of guilt; authorizing the State and a certain defendant to enter into a probation agreement under certain circumstances; providing that the entry of a probation agreement under the Act shall be considered a probation before judgment for all other purposes under State law; etc.
Title: Probation Before Judgment - Probation Agreements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Authorizes a court to defer entering a conviction and grant probation before judgment when a defendant pleads not guilty. Requires the State's consent, written consent from the defendant, and a finding serving public welfare. Mandates that the agreement provide the defendant admits no guilt and waives trial and appeal rights. Requires the court to find facts justifying guilt beyond a reasonable doubt while expressly withholding a finding of guilt. Authorizes the court to find guilt and impose the maximum statutory penalty if the probation terms are violated. Treats the resulting disposition as probation before judgment for all other purposes under State law.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Administrative Office of the Courts; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Criminal defendants pleading not guilty, State's Attorneys, District Court and Circuit Court judges
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $33,400 in FY 2024 only for Judiciary computer programming changes. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) is explicitly amended in statutory text regarding notification and records of approved treatment programs, and the Judiciary incurs a direct fiscal impact of $33,400 in FY 2024 for computer and case management programming changes to implement the new probation agreement procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants who will directly utilize and negotiate these new not-guilty probation before judgment agreements to avoid federal immigration and collateral consequences.

The bill amends provisions in the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Department of Health's responsibility to approve, monitor, and report alcoholism and substance abuse education and treatment programs utilized as probation conditions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services oversees the Division of Parole and Probation, which is responsible for supervising individuals placed on probation before judgment and monitoring compliance with court-ordered conditions.

Synopsis: Making the proposed appropriations contained in the State Budget for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, in accordance with Article III, Section 52 of the Maryland Constitution; etc.
Title: Budget Bill (Fiscal Year 2024)
bill_summary: Appropriates funds for the operating and capital expenses of Maryland State government for fiscal 2024. Funds public education, healthcare programs, transportation infrastructure, environmental initiatives, and public safety operations statewide. Authorizes cost-of-living adjustments, salary increments, and benefit enhancements for qualifying State employees. Provides state aid to local governments, including disparity grants and public school funding formulas. Allocates dedicated resources to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund and the State Reserve Fund. Enacts deficiency appropriations across multiple State agencies to address budgetary needs for fiscal 2023.

Synopsis: Authorizing the creation of a State Debt in the amount of $1,218,639,000, the proceeds to be used for certain necessary building, construction, demolition, planning, renovation, conversion, replacement, and capital equipment purchases of the State, for acquiring certain real estate in connection therewith, and for grants to certain subdivisions and other organizations for certain development and improvement purposes; etc.
Title: Creation of a State Debt – Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023, and the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loans of 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022
bill_summary: Authorizes the creation of State debt to fund the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023. Sets the total 2023 general obligation bond authorization at $1,218,639,000 for statewide capital improvements. Allocates bond proceeds for State facilities, higher education, public school construction, and local grants. Reduces prior State debt authorizations from previous bond loan acts by $13,639,000. Preauthorizes future capital bond loans for fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026. Alters annual reporting deadlines and balance restrictions for the Construction Contingency Fund.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer; Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, local boards of education, public higher education institutions, local governments, non-profit grant recipients, and Maryland property taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: Authorizes $1,218,639,000 in State general obligation bonds, offset by $13,639,000 in cancellations of prior authorizations, for a net new debt total of $1,205,000,000. Debt service principal and interest payments are financed by the statewide property tax.

Synopsis: Authorizing or altering the distribution of certain revenue; repealing a certain required appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account; altering the areas in which certain faculty must specialize to be assigned to provide clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center; reducing the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024; etc.
Title: Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: Alters state budget appropriations, revenue distributions, and statutory mandates to finance state and local government operations. Reduces the required Medicaid Deficit Assessment for hospitals to $244,825,000 for fiscal year 2024 only. Eliminates the required fiscal year 2024 surplus appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account. Extends the Bainbridge Development Corporation land transfer deadline to the Department of Natural Resources to June 1, 2025. Reduces the fiscal year 2023 appropriation for the Department of Human Services Assistance Payments Program by $7,500,000. Authorizes the Maryland Energy Administration to use $9,250,000 in merger funds to repair existing natural gas infrastructure.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department_of Human Services; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; University of Maryland Medical System
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, public assistance recipients, Washington Gas customers, Baltimore County library users, Bainbridge Development Corporation, and patients of University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2023, State general fund expenditures decrease by $0.2 million. In FY 2024, special fund revenues decrease by $50.0 million, special fund expenditures decrease by $40.8 million, and general fund expenditures increase by $49.5 million, reflecting hospital assessment reductions and contingent fund swaps. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary fiscal and budget agency for the State, DBM oversees state spending, manages the budget, and prepares the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act (BRFA) to balance the state operating budget and implement budget-related statutory changes.

The bill explicitly alters the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024, lowering it by $50 million, and tasks MDH alongside HSCRC to adopt policies preserving the State's Medicare waiver.

HSCRC regulates hospital revenues and is directed alongside MDH to adopt policies regarding hospital assessment and remittance revenue and to reduce the Medicaid Deficit Assessment while preserving the Medicare waiver.

The bill authorizes MEA to use $9.25 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (derived from the AltaGas/WGL merger) to support repairs of natural gas infrastructure in the Washington Gas service territory.
The bill directly reduces the fiscal year 2023 general fund appropriation for the Assistance Payments Program within DHS by $7.5 million.

The bill alters statutory requirements governing the University of Maryland School of Medicine regarding the clinical faculty specializations assigned to provide care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center.
The bill extends the statutory deadline by which the Bainbridge Development Corporation must transfer 120 to 150 acres of the Bainbridge Naval Training Center site to DNR for a state park.
The bill authorizes the transfer of unexpended capital grant appropriations budgeted under DGS (Miscellaneous Grants - Capital Appropriation H00H01.03) to Baltimore County library projects.

The bill repeals the requirement to repay the Local Reserve Account (administered by the Comptroller for local income tax reserves) over 15 years for refunds of recalculated homeowners' property tax credits.

The elimination of the fiscal 2024 Revenue Stabilization Account transfer results in $500 million being redirected to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, directly impacting long-term public education funding overseen by MSDE.
The bill is an Administration bill establishing budget reconciliation provisions, altering mandated executive budget appropriations and authorizing executive budget amendments.
The bill details surplus formula allocations under State Finance and Procurement § 7-311, including statutory funding for the Maryland Equity Investment Fund administered by TEDCO.

The bill references statutory distributions of state general fund surplus allocations under State Finance and Procurement § 7-311 directed to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System.

Synopsis: Altering the eligibility requirements for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program and publicly funded prekindergarten programs to include certain operational requirements, staff credentials, and student-to-staff ratios; requiring Montessori schools and programs to maintain a student-to-classroom personnel ratio of no more than 10 to 1, with a maximum of 20 students if all the students are under the age of 5 years; requiring a classroom teacher to hold a bachelor's degree and be certified by certain organizations; etc.
Title: Early Childhood Education - Prekindergarten Programs - Montessori Schools and Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.

bill_summary: Alters eligibility requirements for Montessori schools and programs participating in State prekindergarten programs. Requires Montessori classroom teachers to hold a bachelor’s degree in any field and an approved Montessori credential. Recognizes credentials from Association Montessori Internationale, American Montessori Society, or Montessori Accreditation Council for Teacher Education accredited programs. Establishes a student-to-classroom personnel ratio of 10 to 1 for students under age 5. Sets a maximum class size of 20 students when all students are under age 5. Permits a ratio of 14 to 1 and 28 students when some are at least 5.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Montessori schools and programs, prekindergarten teachers and staff, and enrolled prekindergarten students and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as altering eligibility requirements is not anticipated to materially affect State funding under the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant program or the publicly funded full-day prekindergarten program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees early childhood education, approves prekindergarten providers, and administers the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program, which is directly altered by the bill to accommodate Montessori credentials and ratios.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions governing the issuance of stock, convertible securities, and scrip; clarifying the authority of corporations to hold annual meetings by remote communication; clarifying the application of certain provisions of law to the conversion of a corporation; requiring a real estate investment trust that voluntarily dissolves to file a notice of termination with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation; etc.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: Prohibits corporations and limited liability companies from issuing stock certificates, scrip certificates, or membership certificates in bearer form. Exempts stock and convertible security issuances from certain board resolution requirements when executed during a conversion. Requires unanimous stockholder approval for the conversion of a close corporation. Clarifies that corporations may hold stockholder meetings partially by remote communication. Requires dissolving real estate investment trusts to file a notice of termination with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Applies the Maryland Control Share Acquisition Act to certain statutory trusts operating as closed-end investment companies.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, close corporations, nonstock corporations, limited liability companies, real estate investment trusts, closed-end statutory trusts, and their stockholders and members
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the authority of the Attorney General to institute proceedings to dissolve a real estate investment trust (REIT) that has abused, misused, or failed to use its powers. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General's Securities Division regulates securities and provided information on the corporate and securities law revisions.

Synopsis: Requiring the seven elected members of the Baltimore County Board of Education to be elected in gubernatorial election years; requiring the four appointed members of the Board to be appointed in presidential election years; providing for the termination of the terms of certain appointed members of the Board in 2024; and providing for the  appointment of certain members of the Board in 2028.
Title: Baltimore County - Board of Education - Member Elections and Appointments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: Staggers the election and appointment of members of the Baltimore County Board of Education. Requires the seven elected members to be elected in gubernatorial election years. Requires the Governor to appoint the four at-large members in presidential election years. Terminates the terms of the four appointed members on December 1, 2028, rather than December 1, 2026. Directs the Governor to appoint four members in 2028 to serve four-year terms beginning December 2, 2028.
responsible_party: Governor; Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission; Baltimore County Board of Education
stakeholders: Appointed and elected members of the Baltimore County Board of Education, candidates for the board, and registered voters in Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact as the bill is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the statutory authority of the Governor to appoint four members to the Baltimore County Board of Education, altering the appointment schedule to presidential election years and extending incumbent appointed terms to December 2028.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing appointments to state and local boards, including the gubernatorial appointees to the Baltimore County Board of Education affected by this legislation.

The Maryland State Department of Education exercises general supervision over the state's public education system and the statutory governance structures of local school boards under the Education Article.

The State Board of Elections oversees election administration in Maryland, and the bill codifies that the seven elected members of the Baltimore County Board of Education are elected at general elections in gubernatorial election years.

Title: Commission on Public Health - Establishment

Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Public Health to recommend improvements to foundational public health services. Requires the Commission to assess capabilities of the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments. Directs the Commission to establish workgroups and hold at least three public meetings across the State. Requires the Commission to make draft recommendations available for 30 days of public comment. Requires submission of an interim report by December 1, 2023, and a final report by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Commission on Public Health; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, local health departments, State academic institutions, and Maryland residents receiving public health services
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures may increase in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to provide staff support, though costs can likely be absorbed with existing resources. Maryland Department of Health and local health department impacts can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Commission on Public Health within the Health - General Article to assess the foundational public health capabilities of the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments. Several department officials (Deputy Secretary for Public Health, Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health, and Director of the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities) serve on the commission, and the department must provide data, interviews, and address recommendations for reform.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes a temporary, independent advisory body—the Commission on Public Health—along with multiple thematic workgroups to assess and recommend systemic reforms to the State's public health delivery.

The bill requires a faculty member from a public health program at a historically Black college or university to be appointed as a member and co-chair of the commission. Academic institutions represented by co-chairs must provide staff support for the commission, which may impact Morgan State University's expenditures as identified in the fiscal note.

The bill mandates that representatives from State academic institutions with expertise in public health systems serve on and co-chair the commission, requiring the represented institutions to provide staff support to the commission and potentially increasing higher education expenditures.
The Governor is responsible for appointing numerous members to the Commission, designating co-chairs, and receiving the Commission's interim and final reports on public health reform.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the newly created Commission on Public Health, including local health officers, academic experts, and public members.
The bill specifically directs the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Maryland Health Care Commission as appropriate and necessary in performing its duties.

The bill specifically directs the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Health Services Cost Review Commission as appropriate and necessary in conducting its assessments and formulating recommendations.
The bill specifically mandates consultation with the Department of Budget and Management, particularly regarding public health funding, workforce, and organizational capabilities.
The bill mandates that the Commission consult with the Department of General Services, particularly as recommendations are formulated concerning state procurement and oversight of contractors.
The bill explicitly requires the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Maryland Department of Disabilities in performing its duties and assessments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from using a lease or form of lease that contains a provision that limits a tenant's ability to summon, or penalizes a tenant or another individual solely for summoning, the assistance of law enforcement or emergency services; prohibiting a landlord from taking certain retaliatory actions because a tenant or another individual summons the assistance of law enforcement or emergency services for certain purposes; prohibiting a local jurisdiction from enacting certain laws; etc.
Title: Real Property - Limitations on Summoning Law Enforcement or Emergency Services - Prohibition
