bill_summary: Prohibits landlords from using lease provisions that penalize tenants or limit their ability to summon emergency services. Prohibits landlords from taking retaliatory actions solely because an individual summoned law enforcement or emergency services. Prohibits counties and municipalities from establishing emergency call thresholds to designate residential properties as nuisances. Prohibits local governments from penalizing property operators, owners, owner-occupants, or tenants for summoning emergency assistance. Authorizes affected operators, owners, owner-occupants, and tenants to seek damages, attorney's fees, and rental license reinstatement.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; governing bodies of counties and municipalities
stakeholders: residential tenants, residential landlords, residential property owners, owner-occupants, property operators, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local operations or finances. Small business effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates statutory affirmative defenses and civil causes of action for damages, attorney's fees, and other relief in court proceedings concerning prohibited lease provisions, retaliatory landlord actions, and local nuisance enforcement.
The Office of the Attorney General, particularly its Consumer Protection Division, oversees compliance with consumer protection and landlord-tenant statutory protections in residential leasing.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that an application for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County include certain petitions of support signed by at least three residents who are owners of real property and registered voters in the district where the business is to be conducted.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Repeal of Petition of Support Requirement Ho. Co. 12-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that an alcoholic beverages license applicant in Howard County submit a petition of support. Excludes Howard County from statewide petition of support requirements. Retains the Howard County Board of License Commissioners' authority to waive the county residency requirement. Authorizes the waiver if the applicant purchased a business already in operation. Authorizes the waiver if the applicant owned the premises for at least two years immediately preceding the application. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license applicants and business owners in Howard County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Howard County can implement the changes to the license application process with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and oversight of the alcoholic beverages industry. While this bill solely alters local application requirements for retail alcoholic beverages licenses handled by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework of the state's Alcoholic Beverages Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the St. Mary's County Board of County Commissioners to produce a report recommending and describing the areas of St. Mary's County that the County Board considers appropriate for the operation of unregistered golf carts on public highways, subject to certain standards; and requiring the County Board to submit the report to certain committees of the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
Title: St. Mary's County - Golf Carts on Public Highways - Report

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires the St. Mary’s County Board of County Commissioners to report on areas appropriate for unregistered golf cart operation. Establishes criteria for candidate areas, including isolated island or peninsula locations bordering the Chesapeake Bay. Requires candidate areas to feature public or private docking facilities and viable tourist attractions for boaters. Specifies that candidate areas should preferably contain no State highways or roads exceeding 30 miles per hour. Mandates a detailed map delineating all public highways within the recommended areas. Directs the Board to submit the report to specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: St. Mary’s County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Golf cart owners, boaters, tourists, and motorists in St. Mary’s County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. St. Mary's County can produce and submit the required report using existing resources, resulting in no local revenue or expenditure impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires a study on permitting unregistered golf carts on public roadways and near docking facilities in St. Mary's County, which relates directly to the state's transportation network and highway safety policies overseen by MDOT.

MVA administers vehicle registration and driver licensing under the Maryland Vehicle Law. The study evaluates potential future exemptions to motor vehicle registration requirements for golf carts operating on public highways.
SHA maintains state roadways outside Baltimore City. The reporting criteria specify that recommended areas for golf cart operation should preferably contain no State highways.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "person in a position of authority" applicable to sexual offense in the fourth degree; altering a certain prohibition against a certain person in a position of authority engaging in certain conduct to prohibit a person in a position of authority from engaging in a sexual act, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with a minor who is enrolled at a school or participating in a certain program for which the person in authority works; authorizing the imposition of a certain sentence;  etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Person in a Position of Authority - Sexual Offenses With a Minor

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the definition of a person in a position of authority under the fourth-degree sexual offense statute. Prohibits qualifying school workers and volunteers from engaging in sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with enrolled students. Prohibits qualifying youth program workers and volunteers from engaging in sexual conduct with minors at least six years younger. Bars treating fourth-degree sexual offenses as lesser included crimes of other offenses unless specifically charged by the State. Authorizes sentences under this statute to run consecutive to or concurrent with sentences for related crimes.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: minors attending schools or youth programs; employees and volunteers at schools, child care facilities, sports, camps, and youth-serving programs
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures due to the expanded application of existing monetary fines and incarceration penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of criminal acts categorized as fourth-degree sexual offenses, which may result in increased commitments to State correctional facilities and reimbursement payments to local detention facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the criteria under which individuals can be prosecuted for sexual offenses against minors, potentially increasing the agency's caseload and legal representation responsibilities for indigent defendants.
The bill alters criminal penalties and definitions under fourth-degree sexual offenses, impacting District and Circuit Court caseloads, trial proceedings, and fine collection.

The bill specifically addresses personnel, contractors, and volunteers in public and private elementary and secondary schools, establishing criminal liability for persons in positions of authority who engage in sexual misconduct with students.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates allegations of criminal sexual offenses and enforces state criminal law provisions.
The department is concerned with child welfare and youth supervision and provided information on the potential impacts of criminal statutes involving offenses against minors.

Synopsis: Requiring the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to release certain personal information of a minor who has a work permit to employers and apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards that have requested and have registered with the Maryland Department of Labor for the purpose of receiving the information, if a parent or legal guardian of the minor or the minor elects to allow the sharing of the information.
Title: Employment for Minors - Opportunities for Work

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to release contact information of certain minors with work permits. Applies to minors who are at least 16 years old. Directs release to registered employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs, educational institutions, and qualifying local workforce development boards. Authorizes release only if the minor or a parent or guardian elects to allow information sharing. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt regulations implementing the opt-in process.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Minors at least 16 years old holding work permits, parents and guardians of minors, employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Department of Labor can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor and its Commissioner of Labor and Industry are the primary administrators responsible for implementing the bill, including registering eligible entities, processing opt-in consent, releasing minor work permit contact information, and promulgating the necessary regulations.

The bill facilitates workforce pipeline connections by authorizing the release of minor work permit data to local workforce development boards, employers, and apprenticeship sponsors, which intersects with the board's statewide workforce development strategies and oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations on or before December 1, 2023, establishing requirements for the sale of new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles in the State; defining a "heavy-duty vehicle" as one with a gross vehicle weight rating equal to or greater than 14,001 pounds; requiring the Department, in consultation with certain units of State government, to prepare and submit to the General Assembly a certain needs assessment and deployment plan by December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Department of the Environment - Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles - Regulations (Clean Trucks Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations establishing requirements for selling new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. Incorporates California's Advanced Clean Trucks regulations by reference, taking effect starting with model year 2027. Directs the department to submit a needs assessment and deployment plan to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. Authorizes the department to delay implementation by model years if assessment criteria demonstrate it is not feasible. Alters the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to cover up to 75% of incremental equipment costs. Mandates an annual $10,000,000 appropriation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for grants from fiscal 2024 through 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: commercial and industrial vehicle fleet owners, medium- and heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers and dealers, local governments, and entities operating in overburdened or underserved communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,200 in FY 2024 for staffing and contractual costs, with ongoing operational costs in future years. Strategic Energy Investment Fund expenditures increase by $5.25 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for vehicle and equipment grants. Local governments face indeterminate expenditure changes when replacing municipal fleet vehicles, potentially offset by higher grant amounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for promulgating regulations incorporating California's Advanced Clean Trucks regulations, preparing the zero-emission needs assessment and deployment plan, and determining any potential delays in implementation.

MEA administers the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, receives an increased mandated annual appropriation of $10 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, must implement new grant preferences, and is a required statutory partner on the needs assessment.

MDOT is explicitly named as a consulting agency required to collaborate with MDE on developing the needs assessment and deployment plan and determining whether to delay implementation of the regulations.

DGS oversees state-owned facilities and fleet management and is statutorily required to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan, particularly regarding transitioning the State vehicle fleet to zero-emission vehicles.
PSC is statutorily required to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan, specifically assessing electric grid capacity, transmission, distribution demands, and feasibility.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $10 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027.
DBM oversees the development of the state budget and must incorporate the bill's mandated annual appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

Synopsis: Providing that the use of cannabis by a parent or certain other individuals who care for a child does not qualify as neglect except in certain circumstances for purposes of provisions of law relating to children in need of assistance.
Title: Child in Need of Assistance – Neglect – Cannabis Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Alters the definition of neglect within statutory provisions governing child in need of assistance proceedings. Excludes cannabis use by any parent or individual with care, custody, or supervision of a child from constituting neglect. Authorizes a finding of neglect if cannabis use harms or places the child's health or welfare at substantial risk. Permits a neglect finding if cannabis use causes mental injury or substantial risk of mental injury. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Parents and caretakers who use cannabis, and children involved in Child in Need of Assistance proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees Child Protective Services and local social services departments responsible for investigating child abuse and neglect allegations and initiating Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) petitions. Modifying the statutory definition of neglect regarding parental cannabis use directly impacts DHS child welfare policies and investigations.

CINA proceedings are adjudicated in Maryland's juvenile courts under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch in managing and hearing these proceedings, and was an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to indigent parents and guardians facing allegations of neglect in CINA and parental defense proceedings.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to take disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee for failing to comply with a Board order; authorizing the Board to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting a Board order from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to reinstate a suspended or revoked license only in accordance with the terms and conditions of the order or an order of reinstatement issued by the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners - Disciplinary Actions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to discipline an applicant or licensee for failing to comply with any Board order. Permits disciplinary actions including license denial, reprimand, probation, suspension, revocation, or any combination thereof. Prohibits a Board order from being stayed pending judicial review. Authorizes the Board to grant a stay of enforcement in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act. Authorizes the Board to appeal a decision that reverses or modifies its order. Permits license reinstatement only under the terms of the disciplinary order or a Board reinstatement order.
responsible_party: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners
stakeholders: chiropractic applicants and licensed chiropractors in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Chiropractic Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the Board's regulatory and disciplinary authority over licensees and applicants.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state licensing boards, including the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners, and represents the Board in court proceedings and appeals authorized under the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a holder of a certificate of sale from filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption for owner-occupied residential property until 9 months from the date of sale; prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a certain notice from being sent to certain persons with an interest in owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sale until 7 months after the date of sale; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Owner-Occupied Property - Foreclosure, Notice, and Reimbursement of Expenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Prohibits tax sale certificate holders statewide from filing a foreclosure complaint on owner-occupied residential property until nine months post-sale. Bars sending the first required pre-foreclosure notice on owner-occupied residential property until seven months after the sale. Delays expense reimbursement eligibility for certificate holders regarding owner-occupied residential property until seven months post-sale. Extends the general expense reimbursement waiting period for redeemed property from four to six months in twenty-three jurisdictions. Applies all provisions to tax sale certificates issued on or after January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: County Tax Collectors; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Homeowners with owner-occupied residential property facing tax sale foreclosure; tax sale certificate purchasers; mortgage holders and lienholders
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory timelines governing when a certificate holder may file a civil complaint in court to foreclose the right of redemption on owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sale, impacting the scheduling and intake of foreclosure actions within the Maryland court system.

Synopsis: Expressing the intent of the General Assembly that at least 2% of the balance in the Homeowner Protection Fund be spent each year to conduct outreach in a certain manner to homeowners in tax sale to encourage the homeowners to enroll in the Homeowner Protection Program; authorizing the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct outreach using State employees and resources or to contract with a private vendor; requiring that certain State and local government agencies provide certain information to facilitate outreach efforts; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protection Program - Outreach

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Expresses legislative intent that at least 2% of the Homeowner Protection Fund balance be spent annually on outreach to homeowners in tax sale. Directs that outreach prioritize live telephone calls or non-mail contact methods promptly after dwellings are sold. Authorizes the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct outreach using State employees or through a private vendor contract. Requires local tax collectors, the Comptroller, and other agencies to provide homeowner contact details upon request. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to summarize homeowner outreach in its annual report.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners whose dwellings are sold at tax sale
fiscal_impact_summary: Homeowner Protection Fund special fund expenditures may increase by up to $204,200 in FY 2024, reflecting staffing, vendor contracting, phone research, and Comptroller system programming. Ongoing annual special fund expenditures range from $187,100 to $202,100 through FY 2028. Special fund revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2025 because unrecoverable outreach costs reduce funds otherwise used to purchase recoverable liens. Local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller, upon request of the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, to provide telephone numbers of homeowners that were included on tax returns filed with the Comptroller's Office. According to the fiscal note, this creates an estimated $30,000 IT programming expenditure for the Comptroller's Office to query and extract phone numbers from its database.

Synopsis: Extending, until July 1, 2036, the termination date applicable to an exemption from the sales and use tax for certain construction material or warehousing equipment purchased for use in a certain target redevelopment area in Baltimore County.
Title: Sales and Use Tax Exemption - Redevelopment Areas in Baltimore County - Sunset Extension
bill_summary: Extends the termination date of a sales and use tax exemption for redevelopment areas in Baltimore County from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2036. Applies the exemption to sales of construction material or warehousing equipment purchased solely for use in a target redevelopment area. Defines the target area as Baltimore County real property previously owned by Bethlehem Steel Corporation or its subsidiaries. Requires the target property to have had an approved Voluntary Cleanup Program application as of January 1, 2016. Requires buyers to provide vendors with evidence of eligibility issued by the Comptroller.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Businesses purchasing construction materials or warehousing equipment for redevelopment in eligible former Bethlehem Steel property in Baltimore County, material and equipment vendors, and competing businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues continue to decrease through fiscal 2036, with the exact amount depending on the value of eligible purchases. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's sales and use tax, collects tax revenues, and is specifically responsible for issuing evidence of eligibility for this tax exemption to buyers in the designated redevelopment area.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting an order of the Board from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to appeal a decision that reverses or modifies its order; altering the grounds for disciplining massage therapists and procedures related to the discipline of massage therapists, including appeals procedures and reinstatement procedures; etc.
Title: Massage Therapy - Discipline

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Alters disciplinary grounds and enforcement procedures for licensed massage therapists and registered massage practitioners. Authorizes the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to discipline individuals who fail to comply with board orders. Authorizes the Board to grant a stay of enforcement of its own orders under the Administrative Procedure Act. Prohibits staying a Board order pending judicial review and authorizes the Board to appeal reversals or modifications. Repeals the requirement to publish revocation or suspension notices in the Maryland Register within 24 hours. Exempts individuals whose license or registration expired fewer than six months prior from specified criminal misdemeanor penalties.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and applicants for massage therapy licensure or registration
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners operates within the Maryland Department of Health, which is responsible for regulating health care professionals and occupations across the state. This bill alters the Board's disciplinary procedures, licensing reinstatement rules, and regulatory enforcement authorities.

Synopsis: Establishing the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force to survey and document a representative sampling of the variety of ordinances, laws, codes, and policies regarding the development and operation of accessory dwelling units in areas zoned for single-family residential use; and requiring the Task Force to report to the Governor and General Assembly on its activities on or before November 1, 2023, and its findings and recommendations on or before June 1, 2024.
Title: Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 798

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Establishes the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force staffed by the Maryland Department of Planning. Directs the Task Force to survey State and local codes regarding accessory dwelling units. Requires the Task Force to study best practices for streamlining accessory dwelling unit permitting. Mandates policy recommendations addressing development on single-family zoned land and local housing impacts. Requires interim activity reporting by November 1, 2023, and final recommendations by June 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force; Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: single-family residential property owners, local governments, residential builders, and housing advocates
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in fiscal 2024 for the Maryland Department of Planning to hire a consultant. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Planning to provide staff for the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force, designates the Secretary of Planning as a member, and results in a $50,000 fiscal expenditure for the department in FY 2024 to hire a consultant.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a formal member of the Task Force, and the subject matter directly concerns residential development and housing policies.
The Governor is responsible for appointing eleven members of the Task Force, designating the chair, and receiving interim and final reports on findings and recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force as a temporary advisory body to study state and local policies and recommend best practices.
The office assists the Governor in vetting and processing the appointments of the diverse stakeholder representatives mandated for the newly formed Task Force.

Synopsis: Authorizing an application for special death benefits to be made for the death of certain members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Special Death Benefits - Applicability

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Authorizes the surviving spouse of certain deceased correctional officers to apply for a special death benefit by December 31, 2023. Applies to Correctional Officers' Retirement System members who died by duty-related homicide on or after June 1, 2001. Requires the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to administer approved benefits. Includes a retroactive lump sum payment with 4% annual compound interest from the date of death. Reduces the retroactive payment by previously awarded earnable compensation death benefits and accrued interest. Prohibits duplicate distributions of previously paid accumulated contributions.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of Correctional Officers' Retirement System members who died by duty-related homicide on or after June 1, 2001
fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or employer contributions, as the bill applies to only one individual. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System, administered by the Maryland State Retirement Agency, to process and award an adjusted special death benefit to an eligible surviving spouse of a deceased member of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill addresses special death benefits for the surviving spouse of a correctional officer who died in the line of duty while employed at a state correctional facility under the department.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "massage therapy"; altering the date after which the option to be registered by the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to practice massage therapy in a setting that is not a health care setting will no longer be available; and repealing a provision of law that provides that certain provisions of law do not require a nonprofit health insurance plan, an insurer, a health maintenance organization, or a person acting as a third party administrator to reimburse certain individuals for services rendered.
Title: Massage Therapy - Definition, Registration, and Reimbursement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: Alters the definition of massage therapy by removing the treatment of illness, disease, or injury from excluded practices. Extends through September 30, 2024, the period during which an applicant may qualify for practitioner registration. Prohibits the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners from issuing initial registrations beginning October 1, 2024. Requires the Board to adopt related regulations on or before October 1, 2024. Repeals provisions stating health insurers and health maintenance organizations are not required to reimburse massage practitioners.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, applicants for massage practitioner registration, and health insurance carriers and third-party administrators
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article governing the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, which operates within the Maryland Department of Health. The department and board are responsible for licensing, registration, and adopting the regulations required under the bill.

The bill repeals a statutory provision specifying that insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and third-party administrators are not required to reimburse licensed massage therapists or registered massage practitioners, which falls under the regulatory purview of health insurance oversight administered by the MIA.

Synopsis: Transferring the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency;  requiring program grant applicants to include the distribution of books to children in low-income zip codes within the applicants' areas of service; requiring the Governor to include $350,000 in the annual budget bill for the Program; requiring the State Library Board, beginning December 1, 2024, to report every other year to the General Assembly on the effectiveness of the Program; etc.
Title: Baltimore City Young Readers Program and Young Readers Matching Grant Program - Alterations (Young Readers Program Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Transfers the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency. Requires the State Librarian to administer both programs in partnership with an early reader organization. Authorizes public libraries to apply for grants under the Young Readers Matching Grant Program. Requires grant applicants to prioritize gifting books to children in low-income zip codes within their service area. Increases the annual mandated appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program from $250,000 to $350,000. Mandates biennial reports by the State Library Board to the General Assembly starting by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; State Librarian; State Library Board
stakeholders: public libraries, affiliated book-gifting services, early reader organizations, and children and families in Maryland, particularly in low-income zip codes
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to reflect the higher mandated appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program. Local revenues and expenditures increase for local public library systems and counties that apply for and receive matching grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers both the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency, requiring the State Librarian to administer the programs and the State Library Board to report biennially to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the programs away from this office (formerly known as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services), relinquishing its previous administrative oversight and budget funding.

The bill alters statutory mandated appropriations that must be included in the annual state budget bill, increasing the required annual appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to $350,000.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations in the annual budget bill for both programs ($200,000 for the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and $350,000 for the Matching Grant Program).

Synopsis: Requiring a register of wills to accept certain documents filed electronically through a system established by the register of wills; and prohibiting a register of wills from refusing to accept a document based on the manner in which it was signed.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Registers of Wills - Electronic Filing and Signatures
bill_summary: Requires each register of wills to accept any document filed electronically through a system established by the register. Excludes original wills from the electronic filing requirement. Mandates that electronic filings comply with the Maryland Rules. Prohibits a register from refusing to accept a document based on the manner of its signature. Clarifies that the law does not prohibit filing documents in paper form.
responsible_party: Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Individuals filing estate or probate documents, estate planning attorneys, personal representatives, and registers of wills across Maryland's 24 jurisdictions
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in state general fund revenues beginning in FY 2024 due to reduced administrative costs for paper filings. State expenditures and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 244 directly applies to the Registers of Wills, requiring them to accept documents filed electronically through an established system (with the exception of original wills) and prohibiting them from rejecting documents based on the manner in which they were signed.

The bill requires electronic filings with the registers of wills to be in accordance with the Maryland Rules adopted by the judiciary, which the Administrative Office of the Courts supports, and registers also serve as clerks to the Orphans' Courts.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to include an attestation that all units required to report are represented in its annual report beginning December 31, 2023; requiring the Office to conduct a certain periodic audit to ensure the accuracy of the attestation; requiring a certain annual report to be submitted to the Joint Committee on Fair Practices and State Personnel Oversight; etc.
Title: Minority Business Enterprise Program - Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to include a reporting attestation in its annual report. Requires the attestation to confirm all units required to report are represented in the annual report. Requires the Office to audit the Executive Branch every three years starting by December 31, 2023. Adds the Joint Committee on Fair Practices and State Personnel Oversight as a recipient of the annual report. Requires the Office of State Procurement to maintain a list of units required to report.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Office of State Procurement in the Department of General Services
stakeholders: Executive Branch procurement units; certified minority business enterprises
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs and the Department of General Services can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary implementing agency responsible for including an attestation in its annual MBE report that all required executive branch units are represented, conducting a triennial audit of the executive branch to determine which entities meet the definition of a 'unit', and submitting the report to the designated committees.

The bill statutorily requires the Office of State Procurement within the Department of General Services to maintain the official list of executive branch units required to submit annual MBE procurement reports.
The Board of Public Works receives GOSBA's annual MBE summary report and attestation, and retains authority over the approval of reporting formats and regulations related to the MBE program.

Synopsis: Extending to October 1, 2028, the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to impose a transfer tax on certain instruments of writing.
Title: St. Mary's County - Transfer Tax - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Extends the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to impose a local transfer tax. Delays the termination date of this taxing authority from October 1, 2024, to October 1, 2028. Applies to instruments of writing recorded with the Circuit Court Clerk or filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County; Clerk of the Circuit Court for St. Mary's County; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Property buyers and sellers in St. Mary's County; St. Mary's County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. St. Mary's County maintains approximately $8.0 million annually in transfer tax revenues for its capital improvement fund through FY 2028, with approximately $2.0 million collected in FY 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the sunset for St. Mary's County's transfer tax on instruments of writing, which are recorded by the Clerk of the Circuit Court for St. Mary's County. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, operational, and financial support to the circuit court clerks who process these documents and collect associated taxes.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County to issue a Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) license for use at certain Towson University events.
Title: Baltimore County - Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) License - Towson University

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class B–ECF/DS beer, wine, and liquor license for Towson University. Allows the license holder to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption at catered university-related events. Directs all retail sales profits into Towson University's auxiliary services account. Requires the university to report catered events selling or serving alcohol to the Board at least five days in advance. Sets the annual license fee at $2,000.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Towson University; campus dining services contractors; attendees of Towson University catered events
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Baltimore County revenues increase by $2,500 in FY 2024 from application and license fees, and by $2,000 annually thereafter from license renewal fees. Baltimore County can monitor and enforce license provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Towson University and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County are constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (USM). The bill authorizes Towson University to obtain a Class B-ECF/DS alcoholic beverages license for campus-related catered events and deposit sales profits into its auxiliary services account.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person who applies for certain property tax exemptions for real property in Baltimore City to request that the exemption be applied retroactively for up to 3 taxable years, subject to certain requirements; requiring Baltimore City and the State to pay a refund of excess real property taxes paid due to a retroactive exemption that is granted; and requiring the Baltimore City Department of Finance to submit a report on the number of requests made and the amounts refunded by December 1 each year from 2023 to 2027.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - Retroactive Exemption
bill_summary: Authorizes persons applying for specified property tax exemptions in Baltimore City to request retroactive exemption for up to three taxable years. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to grant the retroactive exemption upon good cause shown. Conditions approval on the review and consent of the Baltimore City Solicitor and Baltimore City Department of Finance. Requires Baltimore City and the State to refund excess real property taxes paid. Mandates annual reporting by the Baltimore City Department of Finance through December 1, 2027. Terminates the retroactive exemption provisions on December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Baltimore City Department of Finance; Baltimore City Solicitor
stakeholders: Nonprofit, charitable, and religious property owners in Baltimore City seeking retroactive property tax exemptions; Baltimore City government
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease by approximately $14,200 annually in fiscal 2023 through 2027. Baltimore City property tax revenues decrease by approximately $285,000 annually from fiscal 2023 through 2027 due to required refunds of excess taxes paid.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Baltimore City Department of Finance to submit an annual report to the Governor (from 2023 through 2027) on the number of retroactive exemption requests received and approved, as well as amounts refunded.
The bill mandates that the State pay refunds for excess property taxes paid due to approved retroactive exemptions, which affects State tax revenue and requires State disbursement of tax refunds.
The bill results in a reduction of State real property tax revenues deposited into the Annuity Bond Fund, which the Treasurer's Office utilizes for debt service on State general obligation bonds.

Synopsis: Repealing certain geographic and temporal restrictions on the issuance of Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Class A-7 Licenses
bill_summary: Repeals geographic and temporal restrictions on issuing Class A–7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City. Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue Class A–7 licenses in the 43rd legislative district. Removes the July 1, 2022 deadline prohibiting subsequent issuances of Class A–7 licenses. Allows eligible Class B–D–7 license holders to apply to exchange their licenses with Baltimore City Council approval. Maintains the $1,500 annual license fee and off-premises sales authorization from 10 a.m. to midnight daily.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners; Baltimore City Council
stakeholders: Holders of Class B–D–7 alcoholic beverages licenses seeking conversion, applicants for Class A–7 licenses, and retail alcohol businesses in Baltimore City, including the 43rd legislative district
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license and application fees ($600 application fee plus $1,500 annual license fee, or a net $780 initial and $180 annual increase per exchanged license). Baltimore City can implement the bill with existing resources. No effect on State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically governs local retail licenses administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and carries no direct state fiscal effect, it amends Maryland's Alcoholic Beverages Article governing alcoholic beverage regulations.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations to exempt an on-farm composting facility from the requirement to obtain a permit if the on-farm composting facility uses 10,000 square feet of area or less for active food scrap composting, composts only certain materials, records the amount and source of off-site type 2 organics composted and the date and time the off-site type 2 organics arrived on the farm, retains the records for 5 years, provides records on request, and meets any other condition for a permit exemption; etc.
Title: Environment - On-Farm Composting Facilities - Permit Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations exempting certain on-farm composting facilities from permit requirements. Applies the exemption to facilities using 10,000 square feet or less of area for active food scrap composting. Restricts composting feedstocks to specified on-site materials, Type 1 feedstock, and eligible Type 2 feedstock. Requires facility operators to maintain certain feedstock records for five years and provide them upon request. Mandates operators provide written notice to the Department before conducting on-farm composting without a permit. Directs the Department to submit an impact report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Maryland farmers and on-farm composting facility operators
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can adopt regulations, implement the exemption, and prepare the report with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) with adopting regulations to establish a permit exemption for certain on-farm composting facilities, receiving required notices from farm operators, inspecting records, and submitting a comprehensive report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.

The bill regulates on-farm composting operations that intersect directly with agricultural operations and references compliance with nutrient management plans under COMAR 15.20.07 and soil conservation and water quality plans overseen and supported by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

Synopsis: Requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Caroline County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county; and requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Queen Anne's County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county.
Title: Caroline and Queen Anne's Counties - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirement
bill_summary: Alters residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Caroline County and Queen Anne's County. Requires at least one applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Caroline County to reside in Maryland. Establishes that an alcoholic beverages license remains valid only while at least one applicant resides in Maryland. Removes county residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Queen Anne's County. Exempts Caroline County license applications from general petition of support requirements. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners; Queen Anne's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: applicants for and holders of alcoholic beverages licenses in Caroline County and Queen Anne's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Local operations and finances in Caroline County and Queen Anne's County are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is tasked with regulating the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically adjusts local residency requirements for alcoholic beverage license applicants in Caroline and Queen Anne's counties with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework of alcoholic beverage administration and licensing forms overseen by the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Establishing a licensing and regulatory system for sign language interpreters under the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters in the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing; establishing the Sign Language Interpreters Fund to be used exclusively to cover the documented direct and indirect costs of fulfilling the Board's duties, including development of programs to assist licensure of marginalized interpreters, development of certain mentorship programs, and financial assistance for certain applicants; etc.
Title: Maryland Sign Language Interpreters Act

bill_summary: Establishes the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing. Requires individuals providing sign language interpretation services in the State to hold a license starting January 1, 2025. Creates the Sign Language Interpreters Fund to support board operations using licensing fees and other revenue. Directs the board to publish licensing requirements for all interpreting settings by July 1, 2024. Mandates an appropriation of $100,000 in general funds in fiscal year 2025 for board implementation. Sunsets the regulatory program and its regulations on July 1, 2033.
responsible_party: State Board of Sign Language Interpreters; Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Sign language interpreters, deaf and hard of hearing individuals, state and local court systems, and interpreting service agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $253,800 in FY 2024, including $94,300 in one-time general fund Judiciary programming costs and $159,500 in ODHH personnel expenses. FY 2025 expenditures increase by $374,000, supported partly by a mandated $100,000 general fund appropriation and an estimated $90,000 in special fund fee revenues. Local circuit courts may experience operational delays or increased costs to secure qualified interpreters.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH), requires ODHH to provide staff support and administer the Sign Language Interpreters Fund, and requires annual reporting on the board's activities.

The bill places a mandatory reporting requirement on the Maryland Judiciary regarding sign language interpreter usage, delays, and emergency unlicensed use in court proceedings, necessitating $94,300 in IT programming expenditures and potentially affecting court operations.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the newly created State Board of Sign Language Interpreters, exercising general executive authority over the board, and mandating a $100,000 appropriation in the fiscal year 2025 budget bill.
The bill requires the Board to pay all collected fees to the Comptroller, who must distribute them to the newly established Sign Language Interpreters Fund and account for the fund.
The bill establishes the Sign Language Interpreters Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund and statutorily tasks the State Treasurer with holding and investing the fund's moneys.

The fiscal note specifically identifies the Maryland School for the Deaf as an entity likely impacted if new interpreter licensing requirements reduce the availability or raise the cost of sign language interpreters for student instruction and support.

Synopsis: Requiring producers of any cement or concrete mixture used in the construction of an eligible project to submit environmental product declarations to the Department of General Services by December 31, 2024; requiring the Department to establish a maximum acceptable global warming potential for certain categories of eligible materials by January 1, 2026; establishing an Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund to support the development of certain environmental product declarations; etc.
Title: Eligible Projects - Procurement of Construction Materials (Buy Clean Maryland Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to establish maximum acceptable global warming potential limits for cement and concrete mixtures in eligible projects. Requires producers of eligible materials to submit environmental product declarations to the Department by December 31, 2024. Prohibits contractors from installing eligible materials on an eligible project until submitting a facility-specific environmental product declaration. Authorizes the Department of General Services to waive requirements under specified circumstances, including technical infeasibility or significant cost increases. Establishes an Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund administered by the Department of Commerce to award grants to eligible producers.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Department of Commerce; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: producers of cement and concrete mixtures, construction contractors bidding on State and community college capital projects, and Maryland community colleges
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2024 to capitalize the Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund, $50,000 in FY 2025 for consultant services, and $217,900 in FY 2026 for DGS staffing. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2024. Construction costs for State and local community college capital projects likely increase, though total capital spending caps remain unchanged.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency of the Buy Clean Maryland Act. It is tasked with collecting and analyzing environmental product declarations (EPDs), establishing and periodically reviewing maximum acceptable global warming potential (GWP) benchmarks for cement and concrete, managing contractor compliance and waiver requests, and submitting annual progress reports.

The bill establishes the Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund and explicitly designates the Department of Commerce to administer the fund and award grants to producers of eligible construction materials.
The bill explicitly requires DGS to consult with the Maryland Department of Transportation when establishing the maximum acceptable global warming potential for eligible materials.

DBM oversees the state capital budget and jointly administers the high-performance building requirements under § 3-602.1 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which defines which capital projects are eligible under this Act.

The bill defines greenhouse gases by direct reference to the Environment Article and targets statewide carbon reduction from building materials, aligning with MDE's environmental protection and climate mandates.

Synopsis: Authorizing a police department that takes an abandoned vehicle into custody to notify any secured party electronically if that form of notice is agreed to by the police department, the tower, and the secured party in a certain manner; and altering the application of a provision of law authorizing a police department to provide certain alternative public notice of custody of an abandoned vehicle to include circumstances where electronic notice is unacknowledged or undeliverable.
Title: Abandoned Vehicles - Secured Parties - Electronic Notification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a police department taking an abandoned vehicle into custody to notify any secured party electronically. Requires mutual agreement in writing or by electronic communication among the police department, tower, and secured party. Expands alternative circuit court notice posting requirements to include circumstances where electronic notice is unacknowledged or returned undeliverable. Maintains existing certified mail notice requirements for the last known registered owner. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; local police departments
stakeholders: Secured parties holding vehicle liens, towing companies, law enforcement agencies, and owners of abandoned vehicles
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations, though minimal cost savings and operational efficiencies may be realized from electronic notices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police frequently takes abandoned vehicles into custody and is directly authorized by this bill to use electronic notifications for secured parties in lieu of certified mail, creating operational efficiencies.

The bill references secured parties as shown on the records of the Administration (MVA), which maintains vehicle titling, registration, and lienholder data utilized by law enforcement during abandoned vehicle procedures.
MDOT oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and transportation network operations, and its modal administrations encounter abandoned vehicles and enforce transportation article provisions.

The bill expands the circumstances under which a police department must post public notices in the circuit court of the county where an abandoned vehicle was found, which relates to courthouse administration under the Judiciary.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain senior activity center to conduct gaming events, bunco games, and card games in St. Mary's County; prohibiting a senior activity center in St. Mary's County from awarding prize money in excess of $50 to a winner in each session or charging a participant more than $25 to play one session; requiring any money that remains after prizes are awarded to be used to support future programming at the senior activity center; etc.
Title: St. Mary's County - Gaming - Senior Activity Centers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles

bill_summary: Authorizes senior activity centers in St. Mary’s County to conduct gaming events, bunco games, and card games. Defines a senior activity center as a community facility providing diverse services to senior citizens and their spouses. Prohibits centers from charging a participant more than $25 to play one session. Prohibits centers from awarding a money prize exceeding $50 to a winner in each session. Requires any remaining money after awarding prizes to support future programming at the center.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Government
stakeholders: Senior activity centers, senior citizens, and their spouses in St. Mary's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances, as lottery and casino revenues are not materially affected. St. Mary's County local finances experience a negligible fiscal impact with no substantial changes to revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and lottery operations in Maryland. While the bill expands localized gaming events to senior activity centers in St. Mary's County without materially altering state gaming revenues, the agency served as an information source for the legislation.

The Department of Aging oversees programs and supports for older adults and local Area Agencies on Aging. The bill specifically authorizes senior activity centers in St. Mary's County to conduct certain gaming events to generate funds for future center programming.

Under county gaming provisions in the Criminal Law Article, the Maryland State Police has authority to examine gaming records upon request; however, the fiscal note confirms operations are not substantially affected.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to order child abduction prevention measures if the court finds there is a credible risk of abduction of the child; authorizing certain parties to petition the court for child abduction prevention measures; requiring a petition to be verified, include a copy of any existing child custody determination, and specify the risk factors for abduction; requiring the court to consider certain evidence of a credible risk of abduction; establishing requirements for an abduction prevention order; etc.
Title: Family Law - Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes a court to order child abduction prevention measures on its own motion or upon petition during child custody proceedings. Permits parties to child custody determinations, prosecutors, or authorized public authorities to petition for abduction prevention relief. Requires courts to evaluate specified risk factors when determining whether a credible risk of child abduction exists. Authorizes courts to impose travel restrictions, require passport surrender, order supervised visitation, or mandate financial bonds. Empowers courts to issue ex parte warrants directing law enforcement officers to take immediate physical custody of endangered children.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Circuit Courts
stakeholders: parents and legal guardians in child custody proceedings, minor children at risk of abduction, prosecutors, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: Not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. Creates potential operational impacts for the Judiciary and local circuit courts due to requirements to hold hearings on the next business day following the execution of an ex parte warrant. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 267 creates the Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act, enacting new judicial procedures, evidentiary standards, abduction prevention orders, and ex parte warrants for physical custody of children in custody proceedings. The fiscal note explicitly notes an operational impact on the Judiciary to handle expedited next-business-day hearings following the execution of an ex parte warrant.

The bill authorizes courts to issue ex parte warrants directing law enforcement officers to immediately take physical custody of a child and authorizes law enforcement to enter private property or make forcible entry under exigent circumstances to locate and recover the child.

As the state's primary agency for child welfare and family stability, DHS often intersects with child custody proceedings involving allegations of child abuse, neglect, and domestic violence, which are key risk factors evaluated under this Act. DHS was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2025 an appropriation of $12,000,000 to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund for the purpose of designating and maintaining 9-8-8 as the universal telephone number for a national suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline and for developing and implementing a statewide initiative for the coordination and delivery of behavioral health crisis response services in the State.
Title: 9–8–8 Trust Fund – Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $12,000,000 appropriation to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund in the fiscal 2025 budget bill. Supports maintaining 9-8-8 as the universal telephone number for suicide prevention and mental health crises. Directs funding toward crisis call centers, mobile crisis teams, and crisis stabilization centers. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to administer the nonlapsing special fund. Specifies that the Act takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: individuals experiencing behavioral health crises, operators of crisis call centers, mobile crisis teams, crisis stabilization centers, and acute behavioral health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures and special fund revenues increase by $12.0 million in FY 2025 due to the mandated appropriation. Special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2025 to support crisis response services and MDH personnel costs ($94,023 in FY 2025 for one administrator). Local revenues and expenditures may increase significantly for jurisdictions providing behavioral health crisis response services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the 9-8-8 Trust Fund and is responsible for implementing the statewide behavioral health crisis hotline, awarding funding for crisis response services, and managing personnel supported by the fund.
The bill legally mandates that the Governor include a $12.0 million appropriation to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund in the fiscal year 2025 annual budget bill.

As the principal agency responsible for preparing and supervising the executive state budget, the Department of Budget and Management must implement the $12.0 million mandated appropriation for fiscal year 2025.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the 9-8-8 Trust Fund separately and invest the money in the fund.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily required to account for the 9-8-8 Trust Fund.
The 9-8-8 Trust Fund is statutorily subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

Synopsis: Altering the education requirements for an applicant for licensure as an environmental health specialist; altering the grounds for which the Board may take disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee to include misfeasance and malfeasance while performing the duties of an environmental health specialist; etc.

bill_summary: Alters educational and experience requirements for licensure as an environmental health specialist. Reduces required science semester credit hours for baccalaureate degree applicants from 60 to 30. Replaces statutory laboratory course requirements with laboratory coursework required under Board regulations. Repeals an alternative licensing pathway requiring 24 months of in-training experience. Expands disciplinary grounds to include misfeasance and malfeasance committed while performing specialist duties. Repeals statutory reexamination application and fee mandates.
responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
stakeholders: applicants for environmental health specialist licensure and licensed environmental health specialists in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local governmental finances, as the bill's changes are largely technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which regulates environmental health specialists and oversees licensure, examination, and disciplinary requirements.

The Department of the Environment employs and collaborates extensively with environmental health specialists across environmental protection and public health programs, and was consulted as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Providing certain funding for each county public library system for fiscal year 2028 and each fiscal year thereafter.
Title: Education - Libraries - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Provides per-resident funding of $19.10 for county public library systems for fiscal year 2027 and each subsequent fiscal year. Continues the minimum library program funding allocation for operating and capital expenses. Requires the State and participating counties to share the capital and operating costs of the minimum library program. Maintains the State share at approximately 40 percent and county funding at approximately 60 percent statewide.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: county public library systems, county governments, Baltimore City, and county public library employees
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing funding levels for local library systems established under prior legislation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the primary state entity responsible for providing funding, leadership, and coordination to Maryland's 24 public library systems, which are the direct subjects of the statutory library aid funding formula in this bill.
The Department of Budget and Management develops and oversees the state budget, which incorporates the state share of mandated funding formulas for local library systems.

Synopsis: Providing that the restriction on holding or having a financial interest in other retail alcoholic beverages licenses for holders of a Class 7 micro-brewery license does not apply to a holder of a Class B-BWL (clubhouse/lodge) license in Montgomery County who is issued a Class 7 micro-brewery license.
Title: Montgomery County – Alcoholic Beverages – Holders of Class B–BWL (Clubhouse/Lodge) License and Class 7 Micro–Brewery License MC 16–23
bill_summary: Exempts Montgomery County Class B-BWL clubhouse or lodge license holders from a retail license limitation on micro-breweries. The exemption applies when the license holder is issued a Class 7 micro-brewery license. General law restricts micro-brewery licensees from holding a financial interest in more than one separate retail license. Class B-BWL licenses are issued for Montgomery County Revenue Authority multiuse facilities accommodating golf courses. The act takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: Montgomery County Class B–BWL (clubhouse/lodge) license holders, including the Montgomery County Revenue Authority, and Class 7 micro-brewery operators
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State operations or finances and is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees statutory provisions related to alcoholic beverages and manufacturer licenses referenced in the bill.

Synopsis: Defining "clinical nurse specialist" and "practice as a clinical nurse specialist" for the purpose of authorizing clinical nurse specialists to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment under regulations adopted by the State Board of Nursing; designating a clinical nurse specialist as an "authorized prescriber" under the Maryland Pharmacy Act; and authorizing a licensed physician to personally prepare and dispense a prescription written by a clinical nurse specialist.
Title: Health Occupations - Clinical Nurse Specialists - Prescribing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes clinical nurse specialists to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment under State Board of Nursing regulations. Defines clinical nurse specialists and practice as a clinical nurse specialist under the Health Occupations Article. Permits clinical nurse specialists to order diagnostic and laboratory tests, home health care, and hospice care. Designates clinical nurse specialists as authorized prescribers under the Maryland Pharmacy Act. Authorizes licensed physicians to prepare and dispense prescriptions written by advanced practice registered nurses in their office.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: clinical nurse specialists, advanced practice registered nurses, licensed physicians, and patients receiving complex care
fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive impact on State or local governmental operations or finances. The Maryland Board of Nursing can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.
