agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Nursing, which is tasked with certifying clinical nurse specialists, regulating their expanded scope of practice, and adopting regulations governing their authority to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment.

Synopsis: Reestablishing the requirement that the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, under certain circumstances, draft a plan of action for implementing a process to set upper payment limits for certain prescription drug products; reestablishing the authority of the Board to set upper payments limits, under certain circumstances, for prescription drug products that are purchased or paid for by or through certain State or local government entities, plans, or programs; etc.
Title: Prescription Drug Affordability Board - Upper Payment Limits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Reestablishes authority for the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to draft an action plan for setting upper payment limits. Applies the process to prescription drug products determined to have led or will lead to affordability challenges. Requires approval of the plan by the Legislative Policy Committee or both the Governor and the Attorney General. Authorizes payment limits on drugs purchased or paid through State and local entities, employee plans, or Medicaid. Prohibits applying upper payment limits to drugs on the federal Food and Drug Administration drug shortage list. Requires a report by December 1, 2026, on expanding payment limits to all purchases statewide.
responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
stakeholders: State and local government entities, public employee health benefit plans, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, prescription drug manufacturers, and health care payors
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and local government health care expenditures decrease to the extent that upper payment limits are implemented and reduce prescription drug costs. State and local revenues are not affected. Specific savings figures are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes upper payment limits for prescription drugs purchased or paid for by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and state hospitals, both of which are administered and operated by the Maryland Department of Health.

If the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve the Prescription Drug Affordability Board's plan of action, the plan must be submitted to the Governor and the Attorney General for joint approval before upper payment limits may be set.
The Attorney General is given joint statutory authority with the Governor to approve the plan of action for setting upper payment limits if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve it.

As the agency administering the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is directly impacted because upper payment limits apply to prescription drugs paid for through State health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly applies upper payment limits to prescription drugs purchased or paid for by State correctional facilities operated by DPSCS.
Upper payment limits apply to prescription drug products purchased or paid for by health clinics at State institutions of higher education.

The agency regulates commercial health benefit plans in Maryland and provided information for the bill's fiscal note regarding the application and impact of drug payment limits on health benefit plans.
Decisions by the Board regarding upper payment limits may be contested and appealed under the Administrative Procedure Act, which involves the administrative hearings framework.

The bill provides that any person aggrieved by a final decision of the Board regarding an upper payment limit may petition for judicial review in the State courts under the Administrative Procedure Act.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on January 1, 2024, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide gender-affirming treatment in a nondiscriminatory manner; requiring that the gender-affirming treatment be assessed according to nondiscriminatory criteria that are consistent with current clinical standards; prohibiting the issuance of an adverse benefit determination related to gender-affirming treatment unless a certain experienced health care provider has reviewed and confirmed the appropriateness of the determination; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Gender-Affirming Treatment (Trans Health Equity Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, beginning January 1, 2024, to cover medically necessary gender-affirming treatment in a nondiscriminatory manner. Prohibits the Program from excluding treatments as cosmetic services or establishing categorical exclusions for particular gender-affirming procedures. Prohibits issuing an adverse benefit determination unless an experienced provider reviews and confirms the determination's appropriateness. Requires Medicaid managed care organizations to submit annual reports identifying contracted providers offering gender-affirming care who consent to inclusion. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Health publish an annual geographic access report on its website beginning January 1, 2025. Requires the Department and managed care organizations to include participating gender-affirming treatment providers in their provider directories.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients seeking gender-affirming care (including transgender, nonbinary, intersex, two-spirit, and other gender diverse individuals), Medicaid managed care organizations, and health care providers offering gender-affirming treatment
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but likely significant amount beginning in fiscal 2024, with federal matching fund revenues increasing accordingly. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is required by this bill to cover medically necessary gender-affirming care, establish review standards for adverse benefit determinations, compile annual geographic access reports, and maintain updated provider directories.

Synopsis: Requiring the owners and operators of grocery stores with annual gross incomes greater than $10,000,000 or restaurants with annual gross incomes of more than $1,000,000, beginning on January 1, 2024, to place an automated external defibrillator in a prominent, accessible area and maintain the functionality of the defibrillator; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems jointly to adopt certain regulations.
Title: Grocery Stores and Restaurants - Automated External Defibrillator Program (Joe Sheya Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Requires owners and operators of certain grocery stores and restaurants to place and maintain an automated external defibrillator. Exempts grocery stores that have an annual gross income of $10,000,000 or less. Exempts restaurants with seating under 100 individuals or annual gross income of $1,000,000 or less, excluding off-premises sales. Excludes covered grocery stores and restaurants from the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program but requires MIEMSS registration. Grants civil liability immunity to grocery stores, restaurants, and individuals rendering aid in good faith without compensation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to adopt regulations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
stakeholders: Owners and operators of grocery stores and restaurants; customers and employees of grocery stores and restaurants; individuals experiencing sudden cardiac arrest
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund increase by at least $41,371 in FY 2024 for MIEMSS to employ a part-time administrator and oversee registration. Annual operating costs range between $46,000 and $53,100 from FY 2025 through FY 2028. State revenues are not affected. Local health department expenditures may increase minimally if required to conduct AED inspections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is the primary regulatory and administrative agency tasked with implementing the AED program for qualifying grocery stores and restaurants. The agency must jointly adopt regulations with MDH, maintain the registration system, provide maintenance/recall notices, and complete two evaluation reports for the General Assembly, resulting in direct fiscal impacts on the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund.

MDH is statutorily required to jointly adopt regulations with MIEMSS establishing guidelines for AED periodic inspections, annual maintenance, and assistance to facility owners. Additionally, local health departments under MDH oversight may inspect or monitor AED requirements during food service and grocery inspections.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Forestry Education Fund to expand and enhance the Maryland Forestry Foundation's capacity to provide certain education and resources to forest landowners, the ability of district forestry boards and the knowledge of local governments to achieve healthy and sustainable forests, and the ability of businesses to test innovative best management practices in forestry; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill $250,000 for the Fund in fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
Title: Maryland Forestry Education Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Forestry Education Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Forestry Foundation. Directs the Fund to support forestry education, outreach, sustainability programs, and grants for testing innovative best management practices. Allocates resources to forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and businesses. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 to the Fund in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Exempts the Fund from general fund interest accrual and credits interest earnings directly to the Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Forestry Foundation; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and forestry businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026 due to the mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly as funds are received and disbursed. Local government grant revenues and expenditures likely increase in FY 2025 and FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is codified under the Natural Resources Article and directly impacts forestry in Maryland, providing resources and education to district forestry boards established under the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and supporting programs aligned with DNR's Forest Service mission.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Maryland Forestry Education Fund separately and investing its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Forestry Education Fund.
The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $250,000 for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, which impacts state budget formulation and fiscal planning managed by DBM.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $250,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 for the Maryland Forestry Education Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the Maryland Dent-Care Program; establishing a requirement regarding the reimbursement of dental-related services under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; establishing requirements on the Maryland Department of Health regarding the creation and distribution of plain language materials related to dental services; requiring the State Board of Dental Examiners to publish a searchable list of licensed providers who provide mobile dental services or portable dental services in the State; etc.
Title: Public Health - Dental Services - Access

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Expands the Maryland Dent-Care Program to include licensed dental hygienists. Sets loan assistance grants of at least $50,000 annually for dentists and up to $10,000 for dental hygienists. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to annually evaluate Medicaid reimbursement rates for dental services. Directs the department to create plain language dental health materials and distribute them to dental practices. Requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to maintain a searchable directory of mobile and portable dental providers. Mandates studies on provider participation, community health worker reimbursement, and opening dental practices in underserved areas.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Higher Education Commission; State Board of Dental Examiners
stakeholders: Dentists, dental hygienists, Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, and mobile or portable dental service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $186,400 in FY 2024 ($136,400 general funds, $50,000 federal funds) and $20,000 in FY 2025 ($10,000 general funds, $10,000 federal funds) for contractual studies, educational materials, and system updates. Federal fund revenues increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 and $10,000 in FY 2025 from Medicaid matching funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency. The bill tasks MDH with evaluating Medicaid dental reimbursement rates, assisting with the Maryland Dent-Care Program via the Office of Oral Health, developing and distributing plain language dental health materials, conducting studies on dental provider participation and community health worker reimbursement, and overseeing the State Board of Dental Examiners' new reporting and directory requirements for mobile/portable dental providers.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program. The bill alters program eligibility to include dental hygienists and establishes statutory grant award parameters, requiring updates to MHEC's Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).

The Higher Education Commission administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, which must update program systems and grant amounts to accommodate dental hygienists and revised award amounts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the establishment of a stakeholder workgroup to study the creation of a grant or no-interest loan program for dental providers in underserved areas and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Altering the educational requirements that individuals must meet to be licensed as clinical or graduate alcohol and drug counselors.
Title: Health Occupations - Clinical and Graduate Alcohol and Drug Counselors - Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Alters educational requirements for licensing clinical alcohol and drug counselors and graduate alcohol and drug counselors. Requires qualifying master's or doctoral degrees to be in a professional counseling field instead of health and human services. Permits qualifying degrees from accredited institutions rather than specifying regionally accredited institutions. Repeals the alternative educational pathway for clinical alcohol and drug counselor licensure. Removes specific statutory coursework credit-hour requirements to practice as a licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselor.
responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors
stakeholders: applicants for licensure as clinical alcohol and drug counselors and licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselors
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The procedural changes to educational qualifications do not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, which regulates and administers licenses for clinical and graduate alcohol and drug counselors impacted by this bill.

Synopsis: Exempting certain family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers that serve only dependent children of military personnel and are located on a military base or federal property or are certified as a family child care provider by a branch of the U.S. Department of Defense or the Coast Guard from certain registration and licensing requirements; authorizing certain entities to assume responsibility for approving or determining which children may be served by exempted child care providers; etc.
Title: Child Care Providers - Registration and Licensing - Exemptions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Exempts certain family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers from State registration and licensing requirements. Applies to providers that serve only dependent children of military personnel. Requires providers to be on a military base or federal property, or certified by defense authorities. Authorizes the U.S. Department of Defense, the U.S. Coast Guard, or their agents to approve children served. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Military personnel and their dependent children, and operators of military-associated family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. Qualifying child care providers that are small businesses may benefit from the elimination of duplicative State and federal licensing and registration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) regulates and licenses child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes across the state. This bill directly amends the Education Article to exempt qualifying military-affiliated child care providers from MSDE licensing and registration requirements.

The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, which was consulted on the legislation. The bill establishes exemptions for child care providers operating on military installations or certified by military branches serving dependents of military personnel.

The department is tasked with advocating for and supporting active-duty service members, military personnel, and their families, who are the direct beneficiaries of the military child care facilities addressed by the bill.

Synopsis: Altering procedures that a law enforcement officer and a court are required to follow when the law enforcement officer or court has reason to believe that a child who has been detained is a victim of sex trafficking or a victim of human trafficking; providing that a minor may not be criminally prosecuted or proceeded against under certain provisions of law for a certain offense if the minor committed the offense as a direct result of being a victim of sex trafficking or being a victim of human trafficking; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Victims of Child Sex Trafficking and Human Trafficking - Safe Harbor and Service Response

NarrowSubjects.Name: Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians
Controlled Dangerous Substances -see also- Drugs; Subst Abus
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund
Nudity and Sexual Displays -see also- Obscenity; Pornography

bill_summary: Prohibits criminal prosecution of a minor for qualifying offenses committed as a direct result of being a trafficking victim. Requires law enforcement officers to notify a regional navigator and child welfare agency upon detaining a suspected child victim. Prohibits detaining a suspected child trafficking victim in a juvenile detention facility for a qualifying offense. Requires juvenile courts to stay proceedings and dismiss charges upon determining the offense resulted directly from trafficking. Adds unauthorized use of a motor vehicle and prostitution solicitation to offenses eligible for vacated judgments.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Minors who are victims of sex trafficking or human trafficking, law enforcement officers, and individuals seeking to vacate qualifying convictions
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected; any workload changes can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters juvenile and criminal court procedures, requiring courts to stay proceedings, schedule hearings within specified timelines, refer children to regional navigators, determine victim status, dismiss certain charges, and adjudicate motions to vacate judgments.
Law enforcement and courts are required to notify DHS and report suspected victims to local child welfare agencies, which may also receive custody of youth when return to parents/guardians is unsafe.

The bill explicitly prohibits law enforcement from detaining a suspected child victim of human or sex trafficking in a juvenile detention facility for qualifying offenses, directly affecting DJS intake and detention facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent juveniles and indigent individuals charged with qualifying offenses and will utilize the safe harbor protections to file motions staying proceedings, dismissing charges, or vacating prior judgments.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP troopers must adhere to altered mandatory procedures when detaining children suspected of being human trafficking victims, including regional navigator notification and child welfare placement protocols.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP oversees statewide victim services funding, juvenile justice policy, and public safety initiatives, making the implementation of human trafficking safe harbor provisions directly relevant to its coordination role.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The expansion of qualifying offenses eligible for motions to vacate judgments under Criminal Procedure § 8-302 impacts adult criminal records and correctional or supervision caseloads managed by DPSCS.

Synopsis: Establishing the Rare Disease Advisory Council to study and make recommendations on matters relating to individuals with rare diseases in the State; requiring the Council to convene public hearings, make inquiries, and solicit comments from the public on the needs of rare disease patients, caregivers, and health care providers; requiring the Council to report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1 each year beginning in 2024 and to provide recommendations on ways to address the needs of persons with rare diseases in the State; etc.
Title: Public Health - Rare Disease Advisory Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Rare Disease Advisory Council to study matters relating to individuals with rare diseases. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide staff for the council. Directs the council to survey the needs of rare disease patients, caregivers, and health care providers. Mandates policy recommendations regarding healthcare coverage, diagnostics, timely treatment, and provider educational resources. Requires an annual activities and recommendations report to the Governor and General Assembly beginning December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Rare Disease Advisory Council
stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with rare diseases, caregivers of rare disease patients, health care providers treating rare diseases, and health insurance carriers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected as the Maryland Department of Health can staff the council using existing budgeted resources. Potential indeterminate increase in federal fund revenues and expenditures if the council secures federal grants. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds the Rare Disease Advisory Council under the Health - General Article and requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to provide staff support for the council. Furthermore, the Secretary of Health, representatives from Maryland Medicaid, and the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities serve on the council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes a new, ongoing state advisory body—the Rare Disease Advisory Council—charged with studying and formulating policy recommendations regarding individuals living with rare diseases in Maryland.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must designate a representative from the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve on the advisory council, which is tasked with researching insurance utilization management procedures and coverage of prescription drugs for rare diseases.

The Governor is responsible for appointing 14 members of the advisory council, designating the initial council chair, and receiving the council's annual reports on rare disease findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing applications, and facilitating the appointment of 14 diverse stakeholders and experts to the newly created council.

Synopsis: Authorizing an applicant for State employment or a State employee to file a complaint alleging harassment by an employer within 2 years after the alleged violation that is the basis of the complaint; and increasing, from 30 days to 1 year, the period of time for an applicant or employee to file a complaint alleging certain prohibited personnel actions.
Title: State Employee Rights and Protections - Personnel Actions and Harassment - Complaints

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes an applicant or State employee to file a written complaint alleging employer harassment with the principal unit head. Requires harassment complaints to be filed within two years after the alleged violation occurred. Increases the deadline to file complaints alleging prohibited personnel actions from 30 days to one year. Starts the one-year period when the complainant first knew or reasonably should have known of the violation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Heads of principal units of State government; Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State Executive Branch employees, applicants for employment in Executive Branch agencies, and Executive Branch employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to investigate and manage additional complaints, but the exact cost cannot be reliably estimated. Local governments and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees Executive Branch personnel policies, rules, and equal employment opportunity complaint processes. The bill directly impacts the administration of state employee complaints regarding prohibited personnel actions and workplace harassment.

MCCR investigates and enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws, including workplace harassment under § 20-606 of the State Government Article. The bill specifically references these violations and alters the complaint processes and timelines available to state employees.
OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases, including state personnel and employment grievances that proceed through the appeals process following agency decisions.

Synopsis: Establishing a certain income tax checkoff for voluntary contributions to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund; requiring the Comptroller to include certain information in each individual income tax return package; etc.
Title: Income Tax Checkoff - Maryland Veterans Trust Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes an individual income tax checkoff for voluntary contributions to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund. Requires the Comptroller to include the checkoff on individual income tax return forms. Requires the Comptroller to describe the purposes of the Fund within income tax return packages. Directs the Comptroller to deduct administrative costs and distribute remaining proceeds to the Fund. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Maryland individual income taxpayers, Maryland veterans and their families, and public and private programs supporting veterans
fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal impact in FY 2024 or FY 2025. In FY 2026, general fund expenditures increase by $150,598 ($79,000 for one-time Comptroller tax system modifications and $71,598 for one Department of Veterans Affairs grants specialist), with ongoing department personnel costs of $90,500 in FY 2027 and $95,300 in FY 2028. Maryland Veterans Trust Fund nonbudgeted revenues increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2026, while revenues to other income tax checkoffs may potentially decrease. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is directly responsible for implementing the bill by modifying the individual income tax return form and tax packages to include the checkoff, collecting contributions, deducting administrative costs, and distributing net proceeds to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund, requiring $79,000 in FY 2026 for tax system changes.

The department (formerly the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs) houses and staffs the Maryland Veterans Trust, which maintains the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund. Increased checkoff revenues will directly support the fund's grants and require an additional grants specialist position starting in FY 2026.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account to the State Treasurer for checkoff contribution moneys collected and deposited.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Agriculture, in consultation with certain State and federal agencies, to study the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in pesticides in the State; and requiring the Department to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment, and the House Health and Government Operations Committee on or before November 1, 2023.
Title: Pesticides - PFAS Testing - Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to study the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances in pesticides in Maryland. Mandates consultation with the Department of the Environment, the Maryland Department of Health, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Directs the study to analyze health and environmental impacts and identify pesticide testing methods. Requires updates on federal testing method certifications and state and federal regulatory efforts. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to the Governor and designated legislative committees by November 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: pesticide manufacturers, pesticide distributors, agricultural producers, and public health and environmental advocates
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Agriculture and consulting agencies can complete the study and report using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing agency directed to conduct the study on the use of PFAS in pesticides and report its findings and recommendations.

The bill statutorily requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment in studying the environmental impacts, testing methods, and regulation of PFAS in pesticides.
The bill statutorily requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to analyze the health impacts associated with PFAS in pesticides.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the final study report and recommendations submitted by the Department of Agriculture.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student data" for purposes of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System to include student disability data by specific disability category.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System - Definition of Student Data - Alteration
bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of student data within the Maryland Longitudinal Data System. Adds student disability data by specific disability category to the system's inventory. Maintains the general statutory exclusion of medical and health records from student data. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: students with disabilities in Maryland public schools, education policymakers, and academic researchers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center and the Maryland State Department of Education can incorporate and transfer the data using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory definition of student data collected, analyzed, and maintained by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to include student disability data by specific disability category.
The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) collects student disability data by category and must coordinate with the MLDS Center to provide and transfer this data for inclusion in the system.

As the principal state agency coordinating services and policy for residents with disabilities, including education and youth transitioning to adulthood, the department has an interest in longitudinal data tracking outcomes for students with disabilities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Cigarette Restitution Fund to include a separate account consisting of payments received by the State from certain enforcement actions related to the sale and marketing of electronic smoking devices; and providing that distributions from the separate account may be used, consistent with any other State law, to supplement General Fund appropriations designated for certain programs with the purpose of reducing the use of tobacco products by individuals under 21 years of age.
Title: Cigarette Restitution Fund - Payments for Sale and Marketing of Electronic Smoking Devices - Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Smoking and Vaping -see also- Cannabis; Cigarettes

bill_summary: Requires the Cigarette Restitution Fund to include a separate account for electronic smoking device enforcement payments. Captures payments from any judgment, settlement, penalty, offer of compromise, or other enforcement action. Limits account distributions to supplementing General Fund appropriations for programs reducing tobacco product use under age 21. Mandates that all distributions remain consistent with any other provision of State law. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Individuals under age 21; manufacturers and retailers of electronic smoking devices; tobacco use prevention and cessation program providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No significant net effect on overall State finances, but redirects future spending. Settlement and enforcement revenues related to electronic smoking devices (such as Maryland's anticipated $13.0 million share from the JUUL Labs settlement) will be deposited into a separate account to supplement General Fund appropriations for youth tobacco prevention programs rather than following standard statutory distributions. Any administrative costs are handled using existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the State's tobacco use prevention, cessation, and public health programs. It is directly impacted as funds from the new separate account will supplement appropriations for its programs targeting youth tobacco reduction, likely increasing program funding and staffing needs.

The OAG investigates, prosecutes, and enters into settlements regarding electronic smoking device manufacturers' sales and marketing practices (such as the JUUL Labs settlement), which generate the revenues credited to this separate account.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, including supervising how Cigarette Restitution Fund revenues are allocated and ensuring compliance with the statutory distribution requirements for the new separate account.

The bill impacts executive budgeting requirements, and statute requires the Governor to develop key goals and performance indicators for funded activities and submit an annual report to the General Assembly on fund expenditures and outcomes.

As the state's chief financial officer and accounting agency, the Comptroller maintains the state's accounting records and manages fund and account structures, including establishing and maintaining the separate account within the Cigarette Restitution Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and provide reimbursement for intensive in-home services, case management, and wraparound services; requiring, beginning in fiscal year 2024, the Behavioral Health Administration to fund 100 slots in the mental health case management program for children or youth at risk of out-of-home placement who are not eligible for program services; requiring the Governor to include funding in the annual budget bill for customized goods and services for certain youth; etc.
Title: Public Health - Home- and Community-Based Services for Children and Youth

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and reimburse specified wraparound and intensive in-home services. Directs the Behavioral Health Administration to fund 100 case management slots for youth at risk of out-of-home placement. Mandates budget appropriations of $150,000 in fiscal 2025, $250,000 in 2026, and $350,000 thereafter for customized youth goods and services. Requires the Department to reimburse at least one pilot program utilizing value-based purchasing for case management services. Directs the Department to submit annual enrollment reports and review eligibility criteria and provider reimbursement rates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration
stakeholders: Children and youth with intensive behavioral health needs, children at risk of out-of-home placement, their families, and behavioral health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $3,496,500 in FY 2024 for three new positions, consultant contracts, and additional case management slots. Indeterminate additional expenditures and matching federal revenues will occur for service reimbursements. Mandated general fund appropriations provide $150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 for customized goods and services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH and its Behavioral Health Administration are directly responsible for implementing the bill, including providing reimbursements for wraparound and in-home services, funding 100 case management slots, establishing a value-based purchasing pilot, and conducting required stakeholder reviews and annual reports.

The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include specific funding allocations in the annual operating budget bill beginning in FY 2025 ($150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 annually thereafter) for customized goods and services.
DBM is the principal agency responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and it must incorporate and manage the bill's mandated annual operating budget appropriations starting in FY 2025.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of Home Energy Programs to enroll households, based on certain eligibility, in any fuel and utility assistance program; and altering the eligibility requirements for the electric universal service program to provide assistance to customers with annual incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.
Title: Social Services Programs - Eligibility and Enrollment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Requires the Office of Home Energy Programs to enroll qualifying households in any fuel and utility assistance program. Covers households containing an individual eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program or Temporary Assistance for Needy Families. Covers households containing an individual eligible for Supplemental Security Income or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits. Expands electric universal service program eligibility to all customers with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Takes effect January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Office of Home Energy Programs; Department of Human Services; Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Low-income households, electric utility customers with household incomes up to 200% of the federal poverty level, and recipients of SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits
fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Human Services special fund expenditures increase by at least $15,024,000 in FY 2024 and by $30,048,000 annually thereafter for bill payment assistance and auto-enrollment in the Electric Universal Service Program. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), a unit within DHS, with enrolling eligible households receiving SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits into fuel and utility assistance programs. The bill also has a significant fiscal impact on DHS special fund expenditures of at least $15 million in FY 2024 and $30 million annually thereafter.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article governing the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), which the Public Service Commission is statutorily required to establish, expanding customer income eligibility up to 200% of the federal poverty level.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to issue a license to an animal control facility to administer rabies vaccines; requiring the Board to establish an expedited process to authorize a veterinary practitioner who holds a current, valid license to practice veterinary medicine in another state or jurisdiction to become licensed to practice veterinary medicine in the State; requiring the Secretary of Health to allow certain veterinary technicians or other clinical staff to administer rabies vaccines; etc.
Title: Provision of Veterinary Services - Practice of Veterinary Medicine and Rabies Vaccines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinary practitioners. Authorizes the Board to license animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines. Requires the Secretary of Health to allow veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal facilities to administer rabies vaccines. Restricts these rabies vaccinations to animals under the custody or control of the shelter or facility. Mandates training verification and identification of the administering individual on the rabies certificate. Requires the Board to report on the expedited process status and funding needs by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Out-of-state veterinary practitioners, veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal shelters and animal control facilities, animal shelters, and animal control facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 only to update the SBVME licensing portal. Special fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 from application and license fees. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners (SBVME) is housed within the Department of Agriculture. The bill requires SBVME to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinarians, expands the board's licensing authority for animal control facilities regarding rabies vaccines, incurs IT portal modification expenses, and requires reporting to the General Assembly.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Secretary of Health to allow registered veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal shelters or animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines under certain conditions, and requires consultation on regulations with the Department of Agriculture.

Synopsis: Establishing invoicing and prompt payment requirements for certain State grants; requiring the State to make payment under certain grant agreements within 37 days of the payment becoming due under the agreement or after receiving a proper invoice; and authorizing interest accrual at the rate of 9% per year on any amount that is due and payable but remains unpaid after a certain time.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - Grants - Prompt Payment Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes prompt payment and invoicing standards for State grant agreements with 501(c) nonprofit organizations. Sets a State policy to pay proper invoices within 37 days of receipt or due date. Requires grant-making entities to review invoices within five business days and report defects within two business days. Directs the Comptroller to disburse payment within five business days after receiving an approved invoice. Assesses a 9% annual interest penalty starting on the 38th day on qualifying late payments. Mandates payment of accrued interest from an agency's operating budget rather than grant appropriations.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; State grant-making entities
stakeholders: 501(c) nonprofit organizations receiving State grants; State grant-making agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures may increase by up to $8,100 in FY 2023 and up to $97,100 annually thereafter to pay interest on late grant disbursements. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is statutory responsible for issuing payments within five business days once a proper invoice is submitted by a grant-making entity and coordinates the state's accounting and payment processing under the bill.

MDH administers a very high volume of operating grants to nonprofit health organizations and is specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as being substantially impacted by invoice turnaround deadlines, interest liability, and potential staffing needs.

DNR awards a significant volume of grants to nonprofits and is specifically cited in the fiscal note regarding the operational and fiscal impact of adhering to the strict invoice review and prompt payment timelines.

The Governor's Grants Office assists state agencies with grant management practices, training, and compliance, making the new statewide prompt payment rules for grants directly relevant to its advisory and coordination mission.
DBM oversees executive agency operating budgets, from which any 9% interest penalties incurred by grant-making agencies for late payments must be paid.
MDOT is explicitly noted in the fiscal note regarding how prompt payment timelines interact with agency-specific grant reporting and performance milestones required before payments can be dispersed.
MSDE awards and manages substantial grant funding to educational and community nonprofit entities that will be subject to the 37-day prompt payment timetable and interest penalty provisions.

DHCD regularly administers operational grants to nonprofit community development and housing organizations, making its invoice processing subject to the new review schedule and potential late interest liabilities.
DHS contracts and provides grant funding to numerous nonprofit social service providers across Maryland, directly subjecting its grant administration workflow to the bill's prompt payment rules.
The bill explicitly carves out and exempts grants funded from general fund capital appropriations made to the Board of Public Works.
Commerce provides state financial assistance and economic development grants to nonprofit organizations that will be governed by the bill's prompt payment mandates.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements related to the reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs paid by certain hospital patients who were eligible for free care, including requirements related to the consideration of data and the reporting and disclosure of certain information; authorizing the Commission to impose a fine of up to $50,000 per violation if a hospital fails to provide refunds to qualifying patients; making a violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; etc.
Title: Hospitals - Financial Assistance - Medical Bill Reimbursement Process

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices

bill_summary: Modifies the process for identifying and reimbursing hospital patients who paid out-of-pocket costs and qualified for free care. Requires implementation of Option 3 from the Health Services Cost Review Commission's December 2022 refund process report. Directs State agencies to share tax and public assistance benefits data as de facto evidence of patient eligibility. Requires each hospital to reimburse participating State agencies for the costs incurred in implementing the refund process. Authorizes civil fines up to $50,000 per violation and classifies hospital violations as unfair trade practices.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission; Office of the Comptroller; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services; Maryland State Department of Education; Health Education and Advocacy Unit in the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Hospital patients who paid more than $25 out of pocket for hospital care between 2017 and 2021 while eligible for free care; hospitals in Maryland; local education agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase in FY 2024 and FY 2025 for affected agencies to conduct data matching and patient assistance, including approximately $28,000 annually for the Comptroller's Office. State revenues increase correspondingly because hospitals must reimburse State entities for all implementation costs, resulting in generally no net effect on State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is the primary regulatory body charged with developing, modifying, and overseeing the hospital financial assistance refund process, coordinating with other agencies, calculating hospital cost reimbursements to state entities, reporting to the General Assembly, and levying civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation.

The Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) within the Office of the Attorney General is specifically tasked with assisting patients in obtaining refunds, requesting and receiving patient data, and receiving cost reimbursement from hospitals. In addition, violations of the Act are enforceable by the OAG as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

The Comptroller's Office is required to match hospital patient data with state tax records to identify patients with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, share confidential tax information as authorized, and receive reimbursement from hospitals for incurred costs.

The Maryland Department of Health is required to coordinate with HSCRC, match patient data against public health assistance program enrollment data (such as WIC), share information with hospitals and state entities, and receive cost reimbursement from hospitals.

The Department of Human Services coordinates in developing the refund process, matches patient records against benefit programs including SNAP and the State energy assistance program for presumptive eligibility, shares relevant data, and receives reimbursement from hospitals for expenses incurred.

The Maryland State Department of Education is added as a coordinating entity to match patient information against enrollment data for the free and reduced-cost meal program, disclose necessary data, report to HSCRC, and obtain reimbursement from hospitals for operational costs.

Synopsis: Extending the time for the submission of the final report of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission to December 1, 2025; and extending the termination date for the Commission to June 30, 2026.
Title: Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission - Reporting and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission to June 30, 2026. Delays the required submission date for the Commission's final report to December 1, 2025. Requires the Commission to deliver its final findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly. Continues the statutory operations and authority of the Commission for an additional two years.
responsible_party: Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission
stakeholders: Families and communities affected by racially motivated lynchings in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues. The Commission can continue operations with existing resources through its extended termination date.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the operational sunset date and final reporting deadline for the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

Bowie State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, provides primary staffing and administrative support for the Commission, and this operational commitment is extended under the bill.
The Office of the Attorney General is statutorily required to provide dedicated staff to assist the Commission and exercise subpoena authority on its behalf throughout its extended duration.
The Commission is mandated to submit its final report of findings and restorative justice recommendations directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County to include a designee of the Director of the Services and a designee of the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police.
Title: Montgomery County - Alcohol Beverage Services - Advisory Board MC 04-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County. Authorizes the Director of Alcohol Beverage Services to designate an alternate representative to the board. Permits the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police to send a designee. Maintains the existing seats for the Board of License Commissioners Chair and five appointed county residents.
responsible_party: Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County; Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services; Montgomery County Department of Police
stakeholders: Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County, Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services leadership, and Montgomery County Department of Police leadership
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law requiring the Comptroller to distribute a certain amount of certain abandoned property funds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund which provides grants to the University of Maryland School of Law, the University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service to operate tax clinics for low-income Maryland residents.
Title: Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders - Funding - Repeal of Sunset

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Repeals the termination date for funding the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund. Requires the Comptroller to distribute $250,000 annually from abandoned property funds to the fund. Distributes fund grants equally to the University of Maryland School of Law and University of Baltimore School of Law. Distributes one-third of the grant funds to the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service. Supports legal clinics that assist low-income Maryland residents with tax disputes.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents facing tax disputes, University of Maryland School of Law, University of Baltimore School of Law, and Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to the permanent distribution from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund (TCLIM). In FY 2024, TCLIM special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $250,000, and higher education revenues and expenditures increase by $166,700. Starting in FY 2025, general fund expenditures are assumed to decrease by $250,000 annually, resulting in no net state fiscal effect. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers both the unclaimed/abandoned property funds and the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, and is responsible for making the permanent $250,000 annual distribution to the Fund.

Two constituent institutions (the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law) each receive a mandatory one-third distribution of grant funds to operate tax clinics for low-income residents.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill permanently diverts $250,000 annually from General Fund revenues and directly impacts state budget formulations and assumptions regarding appropriations.
The statute specifically references the Governor's discretionary authority to include an annual budget appropriation to the Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission to hold a public hearing on the selection of a nominee for a single vacancy on the Baltimore County Board of Education in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the Commission to make publicly available on its website live video streaming of certain public hearings and certain archived video recordings; and authorizing the Commission to retain and reactivate the applications of certain candidates for certain vacancies on the county board.
Title: Baltimore County - School Board Nominating Commission - Vacancy Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Alters public hearing requirements for the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission when filling school board vacancies. Requires at least one public meeting in the councilmanic district or at administrative offices for single vacancies. Mandates website publication of live video streams and complete unedited archived recordings of each public meeting. Authorizes the Commission to retain and reactivate candidate applications for up to two years with applicant consent. Sets 14-day deadlines for requesting and receiving consent to reactivate an application after a new vacancy occurs.
responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission; Baltimore County Public Schools
stakeholders: applicants and nominees for the Baltimore County Board of Education, Baltimore County Public Schools, and Baltimore County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Baltimore County can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Baltimore County Board of Education from the list of nominees submitted by the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, whose vacancy and nomination procedures are modified by the bill.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing appointments to state and local boards, including gubernatorial appointments to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date on the eligibility of the Maryland School for the Blind for funding under the Public School Construction Program.
Title: Maryland School for the Blind - Public School Construction Program - Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Repeals the termination date on the Maryland School for the Blind's eligibility for Public School Construction Program funding. Maintains the school's eligibility for state capital improvement and construction funding beyond fiscal 2028. Directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to adopt regulations for funding projects at the school. Applies statutory requirements governing construction and capital improvement projects funded for county boards of education. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
stakeholders: Maryland School for the Blind; local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on total State revenues or expenditures, as Public School Construction Program funding is determined annually through the capital budget process. Beginning in fiscal 2029, Public School Construction Program funds awarded to the Maryland School for the Blind may decrease funding available for local school systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) with adopting regulations for school construction and capital improvements at the Maryland School for the Blind, and permanently extends the school's eligibility for funding administered by the IAC under the Public School Construction Program.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day in recognition of the service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II.
Title: 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Governor annually to proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day. Recognizes the wartime service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II. Renumbers existing statutory sections within the General Provisions Article to codify the commemoration. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: women veterans, families and descendants of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Governor annually proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day.

As the primary state department dedicated to recognizing and supporting military veterans and their history, the department has an interest in and may participate in commemorations honoring the World War II service of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion.

Synopsis: Altering the threshold amount for certain indemnity mortgage transactions that are exempt from the recordation tax from less than $3,000,000 to less than $12,500,000; and applying the Act to instruments of writing recorded on or after July 1, 2024.
Title: Recordation Tax - Indemnity Mortgage Exemption - Threshold Amount
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 800

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Increases the threshold for indemnity mortgage transactions exempt from recordation tax from $3,000,000 to less than $15,000,000. Applies the exemption to mortgages securing repayment of a loan or series of qualifying loans. Requires county tax collectors or circuit court clerks to submit an annual report starting July 1, 2025. Directs reports to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and House Ways and Means Committee. Requires reports to detail exempt mortgage counts, secured debt amounts, and forgone recordation tax revenue. Takes effect July 1, 2024, applying to instruments of writing recorded on or after that date.
responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court; County Tax Collectors
stakeholders: Commercial borrowers, loan guarantors, commercial lenders, and Maryland counties and Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant decrease in local recordation tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2025. State general fund revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 from reduced collection commissions remitted by clerks of the circuit court. State expenditures are unaffected, and local reporting requirements can be absorbed with existing resources; exact revenue loss figures are unavailable because transaction volume and values cannot be reliably predicted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: In 10 Maryland counties, the Clerks of the Circuit Court (supported operationally and administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts) collect local recordation taxes and retain a percentage commission that is remitted to the State General Fund. Under this bill, circuit court clerks in these jurisdictions are responsible for implementing the altered exemption threshold, will see a decrease in collected commissions, and are mandated to compile and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding the exempt mortgages and forgone tax revenue.

Synopsis: Altering the name of the Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship to be the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship.
Title: Higher Education – Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship – Altering Name of Scholarship

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Renames the Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship to the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship. Alters the name of the associated nonlapsing scholarship fund accordingly. Maintains fund administration and annual reporting requirements under the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: veterans and active-duty members of the U.S. Armed Forces who served in the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts, activated reserve and Maryland National Guard members, and their eligible spouses, children, and stepchildren
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC administers the Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship and its associated fund, and will be responsible for implementing the name change across its systems (such as the Maryland College Aid Processing System) and reporting.
The Commission directly oversees and administers the scholarship program and scholarship fund being renamed by this legislation.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly renamed Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund separately and receive deposits for the fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Health to adopt regulations for pharmacy benefits managers that contract with managed care organizations that establish requirements for conducting audits of pharmacies or pharmacists; establishing requirements and prohibitions regarding audits by certain pharmacy benefits managers, including provisions related to audit limits, acceptance of certain documents as proof, recoupment of funds or charging of fees for prescriptions of unbreakable package sizes, and access to financial documentation; etc.
Title: Health Insurance – Pharmacy Benefits Managers – Audits of Pharmacies and Pharmacists

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Regulates audits of pharmacies and pharmacists conducted by pharmacy benefits managers and authorized auditing entities. Requires the Secretary of Health to adopt pharmacy audit regulations for pharmacy benefits managers contracting with managed care organizations. Prohibits pharmacy benefits managers from auditing more than 125 prescriptions during a desk or site audit. Bars managers from recouping funds for incorrect days-of-supply calculations when package sizes are unbreakable. Requires managers to accept completed cash register transactions as proof of pickup unless contradictory information exists. Mandates managers respond to audit inquiries within three business days and provide secure electronic document submission mechanisms.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Pharmacies, pharmacists, pharmacy benefits managers, auditing entities, Medicaid managed care organizations, and health benefit plan purchasers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate expenditure increase for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and Medicaid managed care organizations if pharmacy benefits managers pass increased administrative costs to purchasers, with an indeterminate increase in federal matching revenues. Local government expenditures for fully insured health plans may also increase. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Health to adopt regulations establishing audit standards for pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs) contracting with Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs), which may also result in an increase in Medicaid expenditures.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-1629, which is regulated and enforced by the Maryland Insurance Administration, granting the Insurance Commissioner regulatory authority over PBM audit standards and procedures.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which contracts with PBMs; any additional administrative costs incurred by PBMs complying with the new audit restrictions may be passed along to the State Plan.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, except under certain circumstances, insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations that provide coverage for diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations from imposing a copayment, coinsurance, or deductible requirement for the examination; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to study and report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by October 1, 2023 on the financial impact of eliminating cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided biopsies for breast cancer.
Title: Health Insurance - Diagnostic and Supplemental Examinations and Biopsies for Breast Cancer - Cost-Sharing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing cost-sharing for diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations. Authorizes carriers to apply deductible requirements to these examinations for enrollees covered under high-deductible health plans. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study eliminating cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided breast cancer biopsies. Directs the commission to submit its report to the Governor and legislative committees by October 1, 2023. Applies the cost-sharing prohibition to health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, individuals receiving diagnostic or supplemental breast cancer examinations, and local governments purchasing health plans
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues in FY 2024 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Form reviews and the Maryland Health Care Commission study will be conducted within existing budgeted resources. Local government expenditures may increase to the extent that fully insured employee health plans face higher premium costs, but exact figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Section 2 of the bill directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission study and submit a report to the Governor and legislative committees on the financial impact of eliminating health insurance cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided biopsies for breast cancer.

As the state's insurance regulator, MIA is responsible for enforcing compliance with the new coverage and cost-sharing prohibitions under the Insurance Article, as well as reviewing carriers' rate and form filings.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which may experience an indeterminate fiscal impact from prohibiting cost-sharing on diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations.
MHBE oversees qualified health plans offered on the individual and small group exchange in Maryland, which are subject to state insurance coverage mandates and cost-sharing requirements.

Synopsis: Increasing the threshold amount above which the Friendship Heights Village Council is prohibited from entering into a certain contract without a competitive bidding process; and authorizing the village council, by majority vote, to enter into a certain contract that exceeds the $20,000 threshold amount without a competitive bidding process if the procurement is in response to an emergency.
Title: Montgomery County - Village of Friendship Heights Special Taxing District - Procurement MC 15-23
