Special fund expenditures for the State Board of Nursing increase by up to $100,000 in fiscal 2024 for one-time programming costs, alongside potential additional personnel costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the state's health occupations boards. The bill directly impacts these boards by prohibiting them from requiring proof of lawful presence or a Social Security number/ITIN as a condition of licensure, modifying application intake processes, and resulting in operational and fiscal impacts on licensing boards (such as the Board of Nursing).

The Department of Human Services oversees the Child Support Administration, which coordinates with professional licensing authorities under the Family Law Article to identify child support obligors in arrears using identification numbers and licensing data.

Synopsis: Altering the authority of the Ocean Downs Race Course to use certain Purse Dedication Account funds generated from video lottery terminal proceeds for operating loss assistance to support a certain minimum number of live racing days at the racecourse.
Title: Video Lottery Terminal Proceeds - Purse Dedication Account - Ocean Downs Race Course Operating Loss Assistance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Alters the authorized use of Purse Dedication Account funds by Ocean Downs Race Course for operating loss assistance. Removes the calendar year 2024 sunset date, making the operating loss assistance permanent. Replaces the $1,200,000 annual limit with an amount equal to up to $30,000 per live racing day held. Requires the assistance to cover operating losses incurred during that calendar year under generally accepted accounting principles. Maintains the requirement to support a minimum of 40 annual live racing days unless prevented by uncontrollable circumstances.
responsible_party: State Racing Commission
stakeholders: Ocean Downs Race Course, standardbred horse owners and trainers, and Maryland standardbred racetracks
fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on State revenues or total special fund expenditures. Purse Dedication Account funds are redirected to Ocean Downs Race Course, increasing its allocation by approximately $210,000 annually in calendar 2023 and 2024 and by roughly $1.41 million annually thereafter, correspondingly reducing funds available for standardbred track purses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Racing Commission, which administers and holds statutory authority over the Purse Dedication Account and allocates funds to horse racing venues, is housed within the Department of Labor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and video lottery terminals in Maryland, the proceeds of which directly fund the Purse Dedication Account.
The Comptroller is responsible for the collection and distribution of state revenues and special fund allocations, including distributions derived from video lottery terminal proceeds.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations necessary to ensure that individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled have appropriate access to prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides; requiring the Board to give visually impaired individuals an opportunity to comment on the regulations; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report by December 1, 2023, to the General Assembly on the implementation process for providing accessible labels for visually impaired persons.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Accessible Prescription Labels, Bag Tags, and Medical Guides for Blind, Visually Impaired, and Print Disabled Individuals - Regulations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations ensuring accessible prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides. Guarantees access at no additional cost to individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled. Directs the Board to allow visually impaired individuals an opportunity to provide input on the regulations. Mandates that the Board adopt the regulations on or before January 1, 2025. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to report on potential enhanced dispensing fees by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled; pharmacies
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Pharmacy and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on local government finances. Small business pharmacies may incur additional compliance costs depending on the regulations adopted by the Board.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the State Board of Pharmacy (housed within MDH) to adopt regulations ensuring accessible prescription labels for blind, visually impaired, or print-disabled individuals, and requires MDH to submit a report to the General Assembly evaluating the costs and process of implementing enhanced dispensing fees.

The bill establishes accessibility requirements for individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled, which aligns with the Department of Disabilities' mandate to coordinate accessible services and advocate for accommodations across state programs and healthcare settings.

Synopsis: Repealing the School Safety Grant Program and the Aging Schools Program as of June 30, 2026; altering provisions relating to school construction approvals by the State Superintendent of Schools; altering provisions related to a public-private partnership agreement in Prince George's County; establishing that the Interagency Commission on School Construction is an independent unit of State government; repealing the requirement for the Board of Public Works to approve grants awarded under a certain capital grant program; etc.
Title: Public School Construction - Programs, Approvals, and Administration - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Interagency Commission on School Construction as an independent unit of State government. Repeals the School Safety Grant Program and the Aging Schools Program effective June 30, 2026. Raises project cost thresholds requiring State Superintendent approval for school building remodeling and change orders. Requires county boards of education to evaluate 50-year life cycle costs and alternative energy systems during design development. Increases annual statutory transfers to Prince George's County public-private partnership school construction to $27,000,000 starting in fiscal 2025.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Stadium Authority; Department of General Services
stakeholders: local school boards; Prince George's County Board of Education; public school students and educators
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $123,300 in FY 2024 for an Interagency Commission human resources administrator, and by approximately $2.1 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to backfill $2.0 million in Education Trust Fund revenues redirected to the Prince George's County public-private partnership. Beginning in FY 2027, $16.1 million formerly mandated for the Aging Schools and School Safety Grant programs is assumed redirected to the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund. Prince George's County Public Schools revenues increase by $2.0 million annually starting in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 458 establishes the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) as an independent unit of State government, alters member removal provisions, repeals certain grant programs under its purview, assigns it administration of the Prince George's County P3 Fund, and requires it to develop life cycle cost analysis standards and submit annual reports.

The bill formally separates the IAC from functioning within the Maryland State Department of Education, alters approval thresholds for school construction and remodeling for the State Superintendent of Schools, and requires coordination on life cycle cost analysis standards.

The bill alters funding streams managed by the Authority under the Built to Learn Program, increases its required transfers from the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund to the Prince George's County P3 Fund to $27 million annually, and requires joint progress reporting.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of General Services to coordinate with the IAC and the State Department of Education to develop life cycle cost analysis standards. In addition, the Secretary of General Services serves as an ex officio member of the IAC.

The bill removes the requirement that the Board of Public Works approve grants awarded by the IAC under the Capital Grant Program for Local School Systems With Significant Enrollment Growth or Relocatable Classrooms.

The Comptroller is mandated to deposit specified amounts from the Education Trust Fund into the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund and is responsible for accounting for the Prince George's County Public–Private Partnership Fund.

The State Treasurer is required to hold, manage, and invest the monies of both the Prince George's County Public–Private Partnership Fund and the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund.

The Governor retains appointment and removal powers over appointed members of the newly independent IAC, jointly selects the commission chair, receives annual evaluations and reports regarding P3 agreements, and is authorized to process a budget amendment transferring $25 million.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

The bill impacts state budget allocations, requiring adjustments to the general fund to backfill revenue shifted from the Education Trust Fund, and involves personnel and budget adjustments associated with establishing IAC as an independent agency.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Architects in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2028, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Architects - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Continues the State Board of Architects in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Extends the termination date for the board's statutory and regulatory authority to July 1, 2028. Maintains the licensing and regulation of individual architects in the State. Preserves the board's authority to issue licenses, permits, and disciplinary penalties. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Board of Architects; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Licensed architects, architectural business permit holders, applicants for architectural licensure, and consumers of architectural services in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Architects are maintained through fiscal 2028. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill extends the termination date of the Board to July 1, 2028, directly allowing the Department to continue licensing and regulating architects and maintaining related special fund revenues and expenditures.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual under the age of 16 years to use a collapsible trap, net ring, handline, or dip net when catching or attempting to catch crabs in the waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries without a recreational crabbing license.
Title: Natural Resources - Recreational Crabbing Gear - Individuals Under the Age of 16 Years

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes an individual under the age of 16 years to use specified gear without a recreational crabbing license. Applies to catching or attempting to catch crabs in the waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries. Permits the youth to use a collapsible trap, net ring, handline, or dip net. Requires the authorized gear to match descriptions established by the Department of Natural Resources in regulations. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: individuals under the age of 16 years catching crabs recreationally in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, with any potential decrease in recreational crabbing license fee revenues expected to be negligible. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to allow individuals under 16 years of age to use specified recreational crabbing gear in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries without a license, as described by the Department in regulations. The Department of Natural Resources manages the state's fisheries, recreational crabbing licensing, and related regulations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt game birds and game mammals on a Sunday, subject to certain time restrictions, during the open season for that game bird or game mammal; authorizing the Department to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt on public land designated for hunting on Sundays, subject to certain time restrictions; and altering the safety zone from 150 to 50 yards from certain buildings occupied by human beings within which archery hunting may not take place.
Title: Worcester County - Natural Resources - Hunting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to permit Sunday hunting of game birds and mammals in Worcester County. Allows this hunting on private property and designated public land during open seasons. Restricts Sunday hunting hours generally from 30 minutes before sunrise until 10:30 a.m. Lifts the morning time restriction during deer firearms season and designated deer bow hunting Sundays. Reduces the archery hunting safety zone around occupied buildings in Worcester County from 150 yards to 50 yards.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, landowners, and outdoor-related businesses in Worcester County
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to authorize the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to permit Sunday hunting for game birds and mammals in Worcester County on private and designated public lands, as well as alters the archery hunting safety zone in the county.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the setting on fire or burning of oriented strand board for certain fire-fighting training; and establishing an administrative penalty not exceeding $500 for a first violation of the Act and a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation of the Act.
Title: Environment - Fire-Fighting Training - Oriented Strand Board - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from setting on fire or burning oriented strand board for fire-fighting training purposes. Excludes the manufacture, sale, use, or distribution of oriented strand board for purposes outside fire-fighting training. Establishes an administrative penalty not exceeding $500 for a first violation. Subjects a violator to a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: fire departments, public and private fire-fighting training academies, and emergency personnel conducting fire training
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $57,100 in FY 2024 for MDE enforcement and outreach staffing, continuing through FY 2026. Local government expenditures may increase to dispose of existing oriented strand board and purchase alternative training materials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Environment Article and assigns regulatory oversight to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). MDE incurs a direct fiscal impact to hire a contractual environmental compliance specialist to conduct outreach, investigate complaints, and enforce the prohibition against burning oriented strand board in fire-fighting training.

The Maryland State Police (which includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal) oversees fire safety and fire service regulations, and was evaluated as an entity that conducts or oversees fire-fighting training, though it reported no current use of oriented strand board.

The agency conducts specialized aircraft rescue and fire-fighting training at state-owned airports (BWI and Martin State) and was evaluated for potential operational impacts or material replacements under the bill.
DNR's Maryland Forest Service conducts wildfire suppression and wildland fire-fighting training, making it subject to review regarding the materials used in fire training operations.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time that an area may be designated as a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) zone from 5 to 10 years; increasing the number of RISE zones that the Secretary of Commerce may approve in Baltimore City to not more than four; extending the termination date of the RISE Program to January 1, 2030; and authorizing a political subdivision to pledge certain revenues to secure the payment of obligations to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation for infrastructure improvements located in a RISE zone.
Title: Economic Development – Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone Program – Alterations and Financing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Extends the initial designation period of a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) zone from 5 years to 10 years. Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to approve up to four RISE zones in Baltimore City. Extends the termination date of the RISE Zone Program and associated benefits to January 1, 2030. Includes RISE zones in the statutory definition of Maryland Economic Development Corporation infrastructure financing obligations. Authorizes political subdivisions to pledge local tax revenues to secure debt service on those obligations. Requires the Department of Commerce to study program effectiveness and report recommendations by December 15, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation
stakeholders: businesses located in RISE zones, qualified higher education institutions, regional higher education centers, and local governments including Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected through FY 2028, but extending the program may increase rental assistance matching grant expenditures in FY 2029 and FY 2030. MEDCO nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2024. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to extensions of legacy property tax credits, while local expenditures and matching revenues for rental assistance and infrastructure obligations may increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the RISE Zone Program. The bill extends the program's sunset date, lengthens zone designations from 5 to 10 years, increases the number of allowable zones in Baltimore City, and mandates that the Department conduct a study on program effectiveness and report to the General Assembly.

The bill amends statutory provisions regarding MEDCO obligations to explicitly include infrastructure improvements located in or supporting a RISE zone and authorizes political subdivisions to pledge special fund and tax revenues to secure MEDCO obligations, directly impacting MEDCO's financing activities and operations.

The bill extends the termination date for the RISE Zone Program and its authorized tax credits and benefits through January 1, 2030, impacting tax incentives administered and collected by the Comptroller's Office.

Public four-year higher education institutions within USM serve as qualified institutions anchoring RISE zones, can sponsor rental assistance programs for businesses in the zones, and are key stakeholders consulted in Commerce's mandated study.

As a public research university located in Baltimore City, Morgan State qualifies as an institutional anchor for RISE zones and could be directly impacted by the bill's increase in the cap on allowable RISE zones in Baltimore City from three to four.

Synopsis: Requiring, on or before August 1, 2024, certain public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan to provide at the institution or to refer students to a comprehensive range of reproductive health services; requiring the University of Baltimore, in lieu of developing and implementing a reproductive health services plan, to provide students with access to over-the-counter contraception through certain on-campus means; etc.
Title: Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Reproductive Health Services Plans - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: Requires certain public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan. Sets a deadline of August 1, 2024, for plan implementation and mandates annual updates. Requires plans to provide or refer students to comprehensive contraception, sexually transmitted infection treatment, and abortion care. Mandates 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception on campus through health centers, retail establishments, or vending machines. Authorizes the University of Baltimore to provide over-the-counter contraception in lieu of developing a plan. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to assist institutions upon request.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
stakeholders: Students enrolled at public senior higher education institutions in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Higher education expenditures increase for some institutions, particularly for one-time setup costs in fiscal 2024, which may be offset by student fees. The Maryland Department of Health can likely provide required assistance using existing budgeted resources. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland develop, implement, and annually update a reproductive health services plan, or in the case of the University of Baltimore, provide 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception.

Morgan State University is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution required to develop, implement, and annually update a comprehensive reproductive health services plan for students.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution required to develop, implement, and annually update a comprehensive reproductive health services plan for students.

The Maryland Department of Health is statutorily required to provide technical assistance and clinical guidance upon request to public senior higher education institutions developing their reproductive health services plans.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to bury the eligible spouse or dependent of a veteran in a State veterans' cemetery without charge.
Title: Department of Veterans Affairs - Burial in State Veterans' Cemeteries - Spouses and Dependents

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to bury an eligible spouse or dependent of a veteran without charge. Mandates that the Department provide a grave liner at no cost for an eligible spouse or dependent. Prohibits the Department from charging for opening and closing the plot for an eligible spouse or dependent. Defines eligible spouses and dependents based on federal national veterans' cemetery eligibility standards. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Eligible spouses and dependents of qualifying military veterans seeking burial in Maryland State veterans' cemeteries
fiscal_impact_summary: MDVA special fund revenues decrease, likely by a significant amount, beginning in FY 2024 due to eliminated interment fees and grave liner charges. General fund expenditures increase accordingly to backfill the lost fee revenue and maintain the Cemetery Program, illustratively estimated at $1.24 million annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Veterans Affairs (now Department of Veterans & Military Families) bury eligible spouses and dependents of veterans in State veterans' cemeteries at no charge and provide grave liners at no cost, which eliminates fee revenue and directly impacts the operations and funding of its Cemetery Program.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain previous convictions for drunk or drugged operation of a vehicle or vessel and grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel under certain provisions of law constitute prior convictions for the purpose of determining certain enhanced subsequent offender penalties.
Title: Grossly Negligent or Drunk or Drugged Operation of Vehicle or Vessel - Prior Convictions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes that prior convictions for drunk or drugged driving constitute prior convictions when calculating subsequent vessel operating penalties. Treats prior convictions for operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired as prior convictions for driving offenses. Applies enhanced penalties to repeat driving offenders previously convicted of grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel. Counts equivalent violations committed in other states or under federal law as prior convictions. Imposes misdemeanor penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both for specified repeat violations.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Natural Resources; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: individuals convicted of driving or operating a vessel while under the influence of alcohol, impaired by alcohol or drugs, or convicted of grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from District Court fines and potential minimal increase in State correctional expenditures due to longer sentences. Potential minimal increase in local revenues from circuit court fines and potential minimal decrease in local incarceration expenditures as individuals shift to State facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article (§ 8-738) concerning the operation of vessels while under the influence or impaired, which is enforced and administered by the Department of Natural Resources and its Natural Resources Police.

The bill amends § 21-902 of the Transportation Article governing penalties for driving under the influence or impaired by alcohol or drugs, establishing cross-applicability with vessel operating convictions.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for driver records, driver licensing, and traffic safety compliance, the MVA tracks vehicle convictions and sanctions related to § 21-902 violations.

The Judiciary (District and Circuit courts) adjudicates motor vehicle and vessel impairment offenses, determines subsequent offender status based on prior convictions, and imposes enhanced statutory penalties and fines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Attorneys with the Office of the Public Defender represent indigent clients charged with criminal driving or boating offenses who face enhanced criminal subsequent-offender penalties and longer potential terms of imprisonment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages State correctional facilities, which may experience a minimal fiscal impact and increased commitment lengths if defendants receive higher terms of incarceration under subsequent offender provisions.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle laws and impaired driving statutes, MSP investigates and charges individuals under § 21-902 of the Transportation Article.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation to collect information from each local board of education on nonpublic school student busing programs other than for the transportation of students in special education; and requiring the Task Force to report by December 15, 2023, to certain committees of the General Assembly any recommendations as to how the State may support a reduction in the use of passenger vehicles for nonpublic school students and policies for certain busing programs.
Title: Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to chair and provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to collect data from local school boards regarding nonpublic student busing programs. Mandates evaluation of traffic congestion, fiscal impacts, and nonpublic busing models adopted by other states. Requires the Task Force to report findings and recommendations to specified legislative committees by December 15, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation
stakeholders: nonpublic school students and administrators, local boards of education, school bus drivers, and county departments
fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements and staffing costs for the Maryland State Department of Education can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local school boards and county governments can provide required information using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to provide staff for the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation. Additionally, the Director of the Office of Pupil Transportation and Emergency Management within MSDE chairs the task force, another MSDE director serves as a member, and MSDE is responsible for designating several other members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation, to examine nonpublic student busing programs, evaluate potential policies and programs, and submit findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Transportation, or the Secretary's designee, is named as a member of the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation.

The task force is required to consult with the Comptroller when evaluating the impact on State revenues and expenditures of potential credits against the State income tax for student bus transportation expenses or other financial support.

Synopsis: Altering the number of years that a school vehicle may be operated in Anne Arundel County from 12 years to 15 years.
Title: Anne Arundel County - School Vehicles - Duration of Operation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes school vehicles in Anne Arundel County to operate for up to 15 years instead of 12 years. Requires vehicles operating past 12 years to meet applicable school bus and motor vehicle safety standards. Mandates compliance with a preventive maintenance plan approved by state authorities. Requires an inspection at the end of the twelfth year and at least two inspections each year thereafter. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Department of State Police; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Public Schools, school vehicle contractors, bus drivers, and public school students in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or Anne Arundel County Public School System finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the operational life of school vehicles in Anne Arundel County and affects oversight and waiver policies administered under the State Superintendent of Schools and the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill directly involves the Motor Vehicle Administration, which inspects school vehicles operating beyond standard limits and approves preventive maintenance plans and structural repair certifications pursuant to Section 7-804 of the Education Article.

The Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Department of State Police is statutorily tasked under Section 7-804 with jointly approving preventive maintenance plans for extended-use school vehicles.
The Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and general vehicle safety regulations and school bus standards in Maryland.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Department of Education from increasing the copayment levels, reducing the reimbursement rates, reducing the income eligibility requirements, or implementing an enrollment freeze for the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect as of January 1, 2023, unless certain conditions are met.
Title: Early Childhood Development - Child Care Scholarship Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Prohibits the State Department of Education from altering the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect January 1, 2023. Prohibits increasing copayment levels, reducing reimbursement rates, reducing income eligibility requirements, or implementing enrollment freezes. Authorizes these alterations if the department notifies four specified General Assembly committees. Prohibits implementing notified alterations until the completion of the immediately following regular legislative session. Authorizes alterations during the fiscal year if the Board of Public Works approves program budget reductions.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Low-income families participating in or eligible for the Child Care Scholarship Program and participating child care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact in fiscal 2024. Future-year general fund expenditure impacts are indeterminate, but restricting the Maryland State Department of Education's ability to freeze enrollment, raise copayments, or reduce subsidy rates and eligibility may significantly limit cost-saving measures when federal funds expire. No effect on local finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE administers the Child Care Scholarship Program. The bill directly restricts MSDE from increasing copayment levels, lowering reimbursement rates, lowering income eligibility thresholds, or implementing enrollment freezes without submitting advance legislative notification or receiving Board of Public Works budget reduction approval.

The bill explicitly establishes that if the Board of Public Works approves budget reductions for the program under § 7-213 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, MSDE may make alterations (such as rate cuts, copay increases, eligibility reductions, or freezes) at any time during that fiscal year.

DBM oversees statewide budget execution, long-term fiscal planning, and the formulation of § 7-213 budget reduction proposals submitted to the Board of Public Works. The bill restricts fiscal flexibility and could significantly impact general fund expenditures in future fiscal years.

The bill reenacts provisions governing the program's payment process, under which the Comptroller is statutory tasked with disbursing payments to child care providers within 5 days of receiving notice from MSDE.

Synopsis: Repealing the provisions of law establishing and governing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation in the State budget for fiscal year 2024 and each fiscal year thereafter to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
Title: Rural Health Collaborative Pilot Repeal and Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition Funding

bill_summary: Repeals the statutory provisions establishing and governing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2024. Directs the mandated funding to support operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. Eliminates statutory procedures and governance structures for establishing rural health complexes. Supports regional health collaboration across Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne’s, and Talbot counties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: Residents, healthcare providers, and local health departments in Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne’s, and Talbot counties, and the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures of $150,000 annually are maintained beyond fiscal 2023 but shift from the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot to the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. State revenues are unaffected. Local revenues and expenditures shift accordingly from the Kent County Health Department to the regional coalition.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot, which was established as an independent unit within the Department of Health, and mandates funding for the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition to address regional public health priorities.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation in the State budget starting in fiscal year 2024 to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
As the principal agency responsible for preparing and supervising the annual State budget, DBM must incorporate and administer the statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $150,000 annually.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, for meetings held on or after October 1, 2024, to allow members of the public to submit certain public comments electronically except under certain circumstances; requiring public comments to be included in certain meeting materials and posted and retained online; and requiring an additional staff position at the Board to carry out requirements of the Act.
Title: Board of Public Works Public Comment Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works to allow the public to electronically submit comments on meeting agenda items. Applies this requirement to board meetings held on or after October 1, 2024. Directs the board to include submitted comments in meeting packets and post them online. Mandates the retention of public comments online through the board's website. Excludes discussion items not subject to open meetings requirements from public comment. Requires the board to employ at least one additional staff position beyond fiscal 2023 authorized levels.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Members of the public participating in Board of Public Works proceedings, and Board of Public Works staff and members.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $227,400 in FY 2024 to hire one computer operator manager and develop an online public comment web portal, and by $92,200 in FY 2025 for ongoing personnel and operating expenses. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Board of Public Works establish an electronic public comment submission process for its agenda items, include comments in meeting packets, post and retain them online, and hire an additional staff member to carry out these requirements.

As noted in the fiscal note, the Department of Information Technology provides IT services to the Board of Public Works on a fee-for-service basis and is anticipated to administer the new web portal required to receive, post, and store public comments.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Human Services to restore to a beneficiary any benefits lost due to theft; authorizing certain households to request a hearing within 90 days after a certain determination; requiring the State to give preference to certain vendors in the procurement process for electronic benefits distribution or administration; authorizing the Department to restore certain benefits; requiring the Department to take certain actions to reduce the vulnerability of Electronic Benefits Transfer cards to theft; etc.
Title: Department of Human Services - Electronic Benefits Transfer Cards - Theft of Benefits (Prevent Electronic Benefits Theft Act of 2023)

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to automatically restore public assistance benefits lost due to theft. Requires the department to decide, restore stolen benefits, and issue a replacement card within 10 days. Prohibits the department from requiring a police report as a condition of benefit restoration. Authorizes households to request an administrative hearing within 90 days to dispute restoration decisions. Authorizes the department to restore benefits lost to theft between January 1, 2021, and October 1, 2022. Requires the State to give procurement preference to electronic benefit distribution vendors offering identity fraud protections.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cardholders, recipients of public assistance benefits, and electronic benefits distribution vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by up to $1.9 million in FY 2023, $6.2 million in FY 2024, and $4.2 million annually thereafter for benefit restorations. Federal fund revenues offset SNAP benefit reimbursements through FY 2025. Local law enforcement agencies can handle reporting consultation duties using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) programs, investigating benefit theft, automatically restoring stolen benefits, issuing new cards, enhancing EBT security features, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

As the State's central procurement authority, DGS is impacted by the bill's procurement preferences for EBT distribution and administration vendors and must establish procurement templates, guidelines, and training for DHS solicitations.

bill_summary: Establishes the Greenspace Equity Program and Advisory Board within the Department of Natural Resources. Authorizes grants to eligible land trusts, nongovernmental organizations, counties, and municipalities for community greenspace projects. Targets projects located in or adjacent to overburdened communities and underserved communities. Redirects Program Open Space funds up to $5,000,000 in fiscal 2025, rising to $10,000,000 annually by fiscal 2027. Requires recommended grant applications to undergo State Clearinghouse review and receive Board of Public Works approval.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Board of Public Works; Greenspace Equity Advisory Board; Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: residents of overburdened communities and underserved communities, land trusts, nongovernmental organizations, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,000 in FY 2024 and $365,700 in FY 2025 for agency administration. Special fund allocations under Program Open Space of up to $5.0 million in FY 2025, $7.0 million in FY 2026, and $10.0 million annually thereafter are redirected to grants, causing no net change to special fund expenditures. Local revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local governments receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and requires the Department of Natural Resources to administer the Greenspace Equity Program, provide staff for the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board, develop grant applications and regulations, and award grants funded through redirected Program Open Space funds.
Each grant application recommended for an award under the Greenspace Equity Program is statutorily subject to final review and approval by the Board of Public Works.

Grant applications recommended for award must be submitted to the Maryland State Clearinghouse for Intergovernmental Assistance (housed within MDP) for review and comment. Additionally, the Secretary of Planning must approve any proposed conversion of land acquired under the program to another use.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must provide prior written approval before any land acquired through the program can be converted from outdoor public recreation or open space to any other use.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board as an advisory body to consult with and advise the Department of Natural Resources on program implementation and grant application review.
The Governor is tasked with appointing multiple members to the newly created Greenspace Equity Advisory Board and designating the chair of the board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of gubernatorial appointees to the newly established Greenspace Equity Advisory Board.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government with the authority to conduct and support advocacy, systems change, and capacity-building efforts to promote inclusive communities and equity in services for individuals with disabilities in the State, research best practices and provide related training and technical assistance to communities in the State, and inform State and local leaders about disability issues.
Title: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council - Establishment

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government. Requires the Council to operate and receive funding under the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act. Mandates that the Council develop, implement, and annually evaluate a five-year strategic plan. Requires the Governor to appoint members, with at least 60% representing individuals with developmental disabilities and families. Prohibits State entities from interfering with Council advocacy, budget, personnel, or plan implementation.
responsible_party: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council; Governor
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities, their parents, guardians, and immediate relatives, and disability service providers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact beyond minimal, absorbable operational costs for the Maryland Department of Aging. The Council is an existing entity fully funded under federal law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Disabilities (or a designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council, and the Council's advocacy directly aligns with the Department's core mission.

The bill mandates three representatives from units within the Department of Health to serve on the Council: the Deputy Secretary of the Developmental Disabilities Administration, a representative of the Prevention and Health Promotion Administration, and a representative of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
The bill establishes that the Secretary of Aging (or a designee) will serve as a member of the Council, adding MDoA representation where it previously was not included.
The State Superintendent of Schools and the Assistant State Superintendent of the Division of Rehabilitation Services (both within MSDE) are mandated members of the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies into State law the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council to advise government leadership, evaluate State plans, and conduct advocacy and capacity-building activities.
The Governor appoints all members of the Council, and the Council is tasked with advising the Governor on policies and programs affecting individuals with developmental disabilities.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the Council to meet specific statutory composition requirements.

Synopsis: Establishing that an elevator installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling on or after October 1, 2023, is subject to certain inspection and registration requirements; prohibiting the Commissioner of Labor and Industry from disclosing to the public any information regarding a registered elevator unit installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling; and requiring the Commissioner to delete certain registration information on the completion of the final acceptance inspection on a certain unit.
Title: Elevator Safety - Privately Owned Single-Family Residential Elevators - Inspection and Registration Requirements
bill_summary: Subjects elevator units installed in privately owned single-family residential dwellings on or after October 1, 2023, to registration and inspection requirements. Requires owners or lessees to register the unit at least 60 days before planned completion and placement in service. Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to conduct a final acceptance inspection before the elevator enters service. Prohibits the Commissioner from disclosing unit registration information to the public. Requires the Commissioner to delete the registration upon completion of the final acceptance inspection. Exempts these residential elevator units from statutory reregistration requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
stakeholders: Owners and lessees of privately owned single-family residential dwellings with newly installed elevators, elevator contractors and mechanics, and state elevator inspectors
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor increase by $171,900 in FY 2024 to hire two elevator inspectors, increasing to $235,500 by FY 2028. State special fund revenues to the Elevator Safety Review Board Fund increase by $109,700 in FY 2024 and approximately $146,300 annually thereafter from inspection fees. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Commissioner of Labor and Industry administers elevator safety laws and oversees the Elevator Safety Inspection Unit. The bill directly requires the Commissioner to handle registrations, conduct final acceptance inspections for newly installed residential elevators, and hire additional safety inspectors, resulting in notable fiscal impacts on department expenditures and revenues.

The Maryland Department of Labor's Elevator Safety Inspection Unit is funded through an annual appropriation from the Workers' Compensation Commission. Consequently, the addition of new elevator inspection staff and related operating costs impacts the commission's funding stream and could theoretically influence employer assessment rates.

Synopsis: Requiring a county or municipal corporation to define, by law, who is a law enforcement officer or rescue worker; altering eligibility for the tax credit to include certain disabled law enforcement officers or rescue workers who were domiciled in the State as, or any time within the 5 years before the officer or worker died or was determined to be disabled; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.

bill_summary: Requires each county or municipal corporation to define by law who is a law enforcement officer or rescue worker. Expands eligibility for local property tax credits granted on qualifying dwellings. Covers officers or rescue workers domiciled in Maryland within five years before being adjudged disabled or dying. Authorizes the credit for eligible surviving spouses and cohabitants meeting the five-year domicile standard. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing body of each county or municipal corporation
stakeholders: disabled law enforcement officers, disabled rescue workers, surviving spouses, cohabitants, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2024 to the extent local credits are authorized and additional taxpayers qualify. The specific revenue decrease cannot be reliably estimated. Local expenditures and State finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals and resolves disputes regarding property valuations, tax exemptions, and property tax credits. Clarifications and expansions to eligibility criteria for local property tax credits may occasionally lead to administrative appeals brought before the local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body for reviewing property tax disputes and appeals arising from decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards, including determinations regarding property tax credit eligibility.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results on its website immediately after a municipality submits its election results; and requiring, within 30 days after the results of a municipal election are certified, the municipality to submit to the State Board an electronic copy of the election results for each office or question voted on at the election.
Title: State Board of Elections - Municipal Elections - Publication of Results on Website

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results immediately on its website upon submission. Mandates organizing the published results by election year and the name of the municipality. Requires municipalities to submit certified election results to the State Board within 30 days after certification. Requires vote totals for each office or question reported separately by voting method, if applicable. Includes in-person early voting, mail-in voting or vote-by-mail, provisional voting, and in-person election day voting. Mandates reporting candidate party affiliation if the municipality conducts partisan elections.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal election officials, municipal candidates, and municipal voters
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 509 directly requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results submitted by municipalities on its website, organized by election year and municipality.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce prevailing wage requirements for contractors on investor-owned utility underground infrastructure projects. Specifies that prevailing wage rates are determined solely by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry. Requires covered contractors and subcontractors to request wage determinations from the Department by October 1, 2023. Directs the Commissioner to determine initial wage rates by hand survey by December 1, 2023, if no rates apply. Requires the Commissioner to waive civil penalties for noncompliant contractors who achieve compliance by March 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
stakeholders: Investor-owned gas and electric companies, contractors and subcontractors performing underground utility work and related traffic control, and utility construction workers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Assuming general compliance by contractors and subcontractors, State revenues are not materially affected. There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to enforce prevailing wage requirements on underground utility infrastructure projects, issue wage determinations, provide guidance to contractors, and conduct wage surveys if needed.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article concerning investor-owned gas and electric utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission, clarifying that prevailing wage enforcement rests with the Department of Labor rather than the Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the date from February 1, 2020 and each February 1 thereafter, to July 1 each year, on which the Department of Agriculture must submit to the General Assembly a certain annual report regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry to the General Assembly.

bill_summary: Alters the annual deadline for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit a report on antimicrobial drug use. Moves the reporting date to the General Assembly from February 1 to July 1 each year. Retains the February 1 deadline for licensed veterinarians to submit drug records and animal accounting to the department. Governs reported data on medically important antimicrobial drugs administered to cattle, swine, and poultry.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: licensed veterinarians who prescribe antimicrobial drugs for food-producing animals, and owners and operators of cattle, swine, and poultry farm operations
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The reporting date change is procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 516 directly alters the statutory annual deadline from February 1 to July 1 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit its report to the General Assembly regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry.

Synopsis: Establishing an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption to a nonprofit organization primarily engaged in certain arts-related activities; and providing for a license fee of $1,000.

bill_summary: Establishes an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to qualifying nonprofit organizations. Restricts eligibility to nonprofits primarily engaged in art display, art instruction, or live performances. Prohibits licenses for organizations that sell mass-produced art or lack a dedicated artistic corporate purpose. Authorizes license holders to sell or serve beer and wine at retail for on-premises consumption. Sets the annual license fee at $1,000 and prohibits transferring the license to another location.
responsible_party: City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: nonprofit art organizations in the City of Annapolis
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. City of Annapolis revenues decrease to the extent that the new annual art establishment licenses replace multiple single-use event licenses. City of Annapolis expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the regulation of the alcohol industry in the state. While HB 520 specifically authorizes the local City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners to issue art establishment beer and wine licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's broader alcoholic beverages statutory framework under the Comptroller's general regulatory domain.

bill_summary: Establishes the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund within the Maryland Stadium Authority. Establishes the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within the Maryland Department of Transportation to provide grants to eligible local grantees. Alters the required annual distributions of State Lottery Fund proceeds across stadium financing funds and bus rapid transit grants. Expands the Maryland Stadium Authority membership from 9 to 11 members, adding appointments by the Governor and the Prince George's County Executive. Alters the boundary definition for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor and specifies that corridor facilities do not include sports facilities. Requires Montgomery County to receive at least $20,000,000 annually in bus rapid transit grants when eligible and multiple grantees qualify.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Maryland Department of Transportation; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Montgomery County; Prince George's County; Maryland Stadium Authority; Baltimore sports franchises; local governments operating or developing bus rapid transit systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues increase by $14.2 million in FY 2024 due to modified lottery distribution triggers, while Maryland Department of Transportation special fund revenues and expenditures decrease correspondingly by $14.2 million. Local revenues and expenditures for Montgomery County decrease by $14.2 million in FY 2024, with potential reallocation of transit grant funding among local governments in FY 2025 and later.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 524 directly impacts MSA by expanding its board membership and establishing two new nonlapsing funds—the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund—which MSA is tasked with administering to manage debt service and facility expenses.

The bill creates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within MDOT, tasks the department with administering the fund, and modifies statutory formulas and eligibility criteria for MDOT's distribution of bus rapid transit system grants.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the newly established funds and adjusting monthly distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the stadium facilities funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly established Camden Yards sports facility supplemental financing funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund separately and invest their moneys in the same manner as other State funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory distributions of State Lottery Fund proceeds and requires agency regulations to apportion lottery money in accordance with the amended statutory schedule.
The bill expands the Maryland Stadium Authority membership, increasing the number of members appointed by the Governor from six to seven.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, including the newly added gubernatorial seat on the Maryland Stadium Authority.

bill_summary: Establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program in the Maryland State Department of Education. Requires the department to license outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs. Directs the department to select between five and 10 participating programs for the initial school year. Mandates the adoption of licensing regulations governing health, safety, and operating standards in outdoor classrooms. Requires the department to submit interim implementation reports and a final findings report by December 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care providers, licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, enrolled preschool children, and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pilot program and comply with reporting requirements using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), requiring the department to administer the program, adopt regulations, select participating programs, convene an advisory group, and submit progress reports.
The bill references programs licensed as camps by the Maryland Department of Health, establishing priority selection for these entities to participate in the pilot program.
The Maryland State Department of Education is required to submit interim and final implementation and evaluation reports on the pilot program directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Transferring all the functions, powers, and duties of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County and certain personnel to the Child Support Administration of the Department of Human Services.

bill_summary: Transfers all child support enforcement functions and personnel from the St. Mary's County State's Attorney's Office to the Child Support Administration. Requires the Department of Budget and Management to create State positions for transferred personnel within the Department of Human Services. Grants transferred employees credit for county employment toward State seniority, leave accumulation, and layoff rights without reducing compensation. Requires St. Mary's County to pay transferred employees any salary compensation due upon termination of county employment. Directs the transfer of county employer pension contributions and interest from the municipal pool to the State pool.
responsible_party: Child Support Administration; Department of Human Services; Department of Budget and Management; Office of the Attorney General; Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Employees of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County, child support recipients and obligors in St. Mary's County, and St. Mary's County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $236,300 in FY 2024 (and $251,900 to $289,300 annually thereafter) to absorb operating costs and personnel, while federal fund expenditures increase by $38,400 in FY 2024. State general fund revenues decrease by $24,200 in FY 2024 and $32,300 annually from the loss of the county administrative fee. St. Mary's County expenditures decrease by an estimated $249,200 in FY 2024 and at least $332,300 annually thereafter.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the functions, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County to the Child Support Administration within the Department of Human Services, resulting in notable operational and expenditure impacts.

The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Budget and Management to create and establish new State Position Identification Numbers (PINs) allocated to the Department of Human Services for the transferred employees.

The bill authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to appoint legal personnel (an Assistant State's Attorney) transitioning from county service to continue providing child support legal services as a State employee.

The bill requires employer contributions and interest for transferred employees to be shifted from the municipal pool to the State pool within the State Employees' Pension System, requiring actuarial valuation oversight designated by the system's Board of Trustees.
