Makes certain transferred members eligible to receive retirement creditable service for unused sick leave accrued in prior systems. Extends unused sick leave credit adjustments to specified Department of Juvenile Services positions transferred on or after July 1, 2022. Requires earlier transfer of service credit if an eligible individual applies to retire before June 30, 2024.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Current members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System transferred from the Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System, including specified Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and Department of Juvenile Services personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities and contributions increase minimally across all funds beginning in fiscal 2025, but a precise estimate is not feasible. There is no effect on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is directly responsible for executing the transfer of service credit from ERS/EPS to CORS, providing the opt-out election forms to members, and recalculating creditable service for unused sick leave.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects DPSCS employees transferred into CORS under prior enactments (including case management specialists, parole and probation agents, and maintenance officers) regarding the transfer of their pension service credit.

The bill directly impacts DJS staff (including detention officers, resident advisors, case management specialists, and group life managers) concerning the transfer of their pension service credit and eligibility for unused sick leave credits.

Synopsis: Altering the distribution of certain funds from local impact grants to Baltimore City; and altering the appointment process for certain members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority.
Title: Gaming - Video Lottery Terminals - Local Impact Grants and Pimlico Community Development Authority Membership - Baltimore City

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles

bill_summary: Alters the distribution of video lottery terminal local impact grants within Baltimore City for fiscal years 2024 through 2032. Increases the portion dedicated to capital projects consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan from 75% to 85%. Reduces the share dedicated to other specified Baltimore City neighborhoods surrounding Pimlico Race Course from 25% to 15%. Requires Senate advice and consent for ten Pimlico Community Development Authority members appointed by the Mayor of Baltimore City. Repeals the requirement that the Mayor consult with General Assembly members representing legislative districts 40 and 41.
responsible_party: Mayor of Baltimore City; Pimlico Community Development Authority; Senate of Maryland
stakeholders: residents, business owners, and community service providers in the Park Heights Corridor and surrounding Baltimore City neighborhoods near Pimlico Race Course
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Total annual local impact grants distributed to Baltimore City remain unchanged, but the bill reallocates grant funding within the city. Funding for Park Heights Master Plan projects increases by $363,500 in FY 2024 (growing to $424,200 by FY 2028), with an equal reduction in funding for other specified nearby Baltimore City neighborhoods.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the membership appointment process for the Pimlico Community Development Authority by requiring the advice and consent of the Senate for certain mayoral appointments. It also alters the formula for video lottery terminal local impact grants that the Authority oversees and advises on for neighborhood revitalization.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and video lottery terminal operations in Maryland, which generate the local impact grant revenues distributed under this legislation.
The Comptroller receives statutorily required reports from the Legislative Policy Committee regarding the continuation of video lottery terminal fund distributions.

Synopsis: Requiring a local board of elections to send, not later than 43 days before an election, a ballot to voters who have made a request and qualify to vote by absentee ballot; altering the procedures for the canvassing of and curing of errors on absentee and provisional ballots; prohibiting the tabulation of absentee ballot vote totals before the polls close; requiring that the statewide primary election and the primary election for the municipal offices of Baltimore City in 2024 be held on the second Tuesday in May; etc.
Title: Election Law - Ballot Issuance, Processing, and Reporting Procedures and 2024 Primary Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: Requires local boards of elections to begin processing absentee ballots eight business days before early voting. Mandates sending absentee ballots at least 43 days before an election to voters requesting them early. Establishes procedures allowing voters to cure missing signatures on absentee ballot envelopes up to ten days post-election. Directs election boards receiving multiple ballots from one voter to count only the first legally sufficient ballot. Requires the State Board of Elections to report precinct results including early, absentee, and provisional votes. Moves Maryland's 2024 statewide and Baltimore City municipal primary elections to the second Tuesday in May.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, absentee and provisional ballot voters, candidates in the 2024 primary election, and local election officials
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $84,100 in FY 2024 and ongoing amounts exceeding $100,000 annually thereafter for an IT programmer and related system costs. Local board of elections expenditures increase beginning in FY 2024 due to additional personnel for early canvassing, flash drives, scanners, and shared contractual software costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 535 directly governs Maryland election administration by altering absentee ballot issuance timelines, canvassing procedures, ballot signature curing processes, and election result reporting requirements. The State Board of Elections is required to adopt regulations, oversee local election board implementation, manage waiver requests, update reporting formats, and hire additional IT personnel and acquire technology solutions to implement ballot curing systems.

Synopsis: Specifying that the definition of "earnable compensation" does not include certain payments requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to pay a nonvested former member's accumulated contributions to the nonvested former member's designated beneficiary or estate if the nonvested former member dies before withdrawing the member's contributions; and providing a list of individuals who immediately vest on taking certain offices.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Earnable Compensation, Nonvested Former Members, and Immediate Vesting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Excludes retroactive lump sum salary payments from the definition of earnable compensation in the State Retirement and Pension System. Applies this exclusion retroactively to July 1, 2022, while exempting qualifying Maryland Department of Transportation payments. Requires the Board of Trustees to pay accumulated contributions of a deceased nonvested former member to their beneficiary or estate. Specifies twenty-one appointed State agency heads, commissioners, and officials who vest immediately upon taking office.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Nonvested former members of the State Retirement and Pension System, beneficiaries and estates of deceased members, specified appointed State agency heads and officials, and State employees receiving retroactive lump sum salary payments
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the vesting provisions clarify existing law, payment of deceased nonvested members' contributions codifies current practice, and earnable compensation exclusions produce at most a negligible liability reduction.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), SRA is the primary implementing agency responsible for executing the definition of earnable compensation, disbursing accumulated contributions of deceased nonvested members, and administering immediate vesting provisions.

The bill explicitly carves out retroactive salary increase lump-sum payments made by the Maryland Department of Transportation between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2023, from the retroactive exclusion from earnable compensation.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Adjutant General upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (now GOCPP) upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of Homeland Security upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of Performance Improvement upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Maryland Energy Administration upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Insurance Commissioner upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the State Archivist upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the State Board of Contract Appeals upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chief Administrative Law Judge of the Office of Administrative Hearings upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the State Prosecutor upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the Public Service Commission upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the Workers' Compensation Commission upon taking office.

Synopsis: Increasing certain dollar thresholds of spending for the purposes of defining "small procurement" for State procurement contracts.
Title: State Procurement - Small Procurement - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement

bill_summary: Increases the general State small procurement spending threshold from $50,000 to $100,000. Raises the small procurement ceiling for specified revenue-generating service contracts from $50,000 to $100,000. Doubles the small procurement limit to $200,000 for Department of General Services and Maryland Department of Transportation construction contracts. Increases the threshold to $200,000 for Department of Natural Resources capital projects or maintenance contracts. Raises the spending ceiling to $100,000 for State Retirement Agency independent medical evaluation and testimony expenses.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Natural Resources; State Retirement Agency; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State procurement agencies and contractors, vendors, and small businesses bidding on State contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances, though State agencies may experience administrative efficiencies by using small procurement methods for higher-value purchases. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly increases the small procurement dollar threshold for construction contracts sought by the Department of General Services from $100,000 to $200,000, and as the state's central procurement authority, DGS is directly affected by changes to state small procurement thresholds.
The bill explicitly alters the small procurement definition to raise the maximum contract value for construction procurements sought by the Department of Transportation from $100,000 to $200,000.
The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for contracts sought by the Department of Natural Resources for capital projects or maintenance from $100,000 to $200,000.

The bill explicitly doubles the small procurement threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 for expenditures by the State Retirement Agency regarding independent medical evaluations and related physician hearing testimony.

The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement and is statutory tasked under this section with reviewing labor and material costs every three years to recommend adjustments to small procurement thresholds to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the percentage of the federal earned income tax credit used for determining the amount that an individual may claim as a refund under the Maryland earned income tax credit under certain circumstances; repealing a certain limitation on the amount certain individuals may claim as a refund under the credit; altering the definition of "qualified child" and income eligibility requirements for purposes of qualifying for a certain credit against the State income tax for certain dependent children; etc.
Title: Family Prosperity Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Permanently extends and expands the refundable Maryland earned income tax credit and State child tax credit. Maintains the refundable earned income credit at 45% of the federal credit for eligible residents. Eliminates the $530 cap on the 100% refundable earned income credit for individuals without qualifying children. Expands child tax credit eligibility to resident taxpayers with federal adjusted gross income of $15,000 or less. Includes all qualifying dependents under age six and repeals the credit reduction for federal child tax credits claimed.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Low-to-moderate-income Maryland resident taxpayers, low-income workers without qualifying children, and low-income parents or guardians of dependents under age 6 or dependents under age 17 with disabilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $172.3 million in FY 2024, increasing to $186.5 million by FY 2028. General fund expenditures increase by $36,533 in FY 2024 and approximately $60,000 to $70,000 annually thereafter for one revenue examiner in the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $6.1 million in FY 2024 and similar amounts annually thereafter, while Montgomery County expenditures for its local supplement program may increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for tax administration and collection. The bill alters the State earned income tax credit and child tax credit, requiring the Comptroller's Office to adjust tax forms, validate claims, and hire additional personnel to process the anticipated increase in credit claims.
This is an Administration bill ('By Request - Administration') championed as a key executive policy initiative (Family Prosperity Act of 2023) to support low-income families and combat poverty.

The bill results in a significant reduction in State general fund revenues exceeding $170 million annually, which directly affects the State budget development, revenue estimates, and long-term fiscal planning managed by DBM.

The office is tasked with coordinating efforts to promote child well-being and reduce child poverty in Maryland, which aligns directly with the bill's permanent expansion of the child tax credit and earned income tax credit for low-income families.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State for purposes of developing opportunities for banking institutions and credit unions to better serve the needs of low- to moderate-income tracts; providing for certain assessment offset credits for certain banking institutions and credit unions in certain areas; authorizing the use of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Financial Regulation - Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund - Establishment (Access to Banking Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State using public and private funds. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to provide an initial equity investment of up to $2,500,000. Authorizes the Commissioner to use up to $250,000 from the regulatory fund for startup and administrative expenses. Authorizes eligible banking institutions and credit unions to request assessment offset credits for branches in low- to moderate-income tracts. Authorizes the Commissioner to match qualifying institutional investments in the venture fund through June 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: State-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and businesses located in low- to moderate-income census tracts
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund increase by $2,838,500 in fiscal 2024 for initial capital investment, administrative setup costs, and matching expenditures. Special fund revenues decrease by $171,000 in fiscal 2024 and by $310,000 in fiscal 2028 due to assessment offset credits claimed by eligible depository institutions. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Commissioner is the primary official tasked with establishing and governing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, authorizing investments, administering assessment offset credits, and regulating banking institutions and credit unions.

The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund, receiving and depositing revenues and managing the fund from which initial capital and administrative expenditures for the new venture fund are drawn.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state budget processes, including budget amendment procedures under § 7-209 of the State Finance and Procurement Article applicable to expenditures from the special fund.
This is an Administration priority bill ('Access to Banking Act') sponsored by request of the Governor to improve capital access and banking services in low- to moderate-income communities.

Synopsis: Altering the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Program by extending the duration of the Program through fiscal year 2026, repealing the rebates that may be issued to retail service station dealers, and increasing the limitation on the total amount of rebates that the Maryland Energy Administration may issue in each fiscal year; altering the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program by altering the definition of "grant"; etc.
Title: Maryland Energy Administration – Energy Programs – Modifications (Clean Transportation and Energy Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Modifies clean transportation and energy programs administered by the Maryland Energy Administration. Extends the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program through fiscal year 2026. Increases the annual rebate cap to $2,500,000 and raises maximum rebate amounts for individuals and businesses. Alters the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to cover up to 75% of incremental costs. Limits vehicle grants to commercial or industrial uses and requires preference for overburdened or underserved communities. Raises the administrative expense cap for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to $7,500,000.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Purchasers and installers of electric vehicle recharging equipment, commercial and industrial fleet operators, local governments, and residents of overburdened or underserved communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund increase by $7.75 million in FY 2024, $7.5 million annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026, $5.0 million in FY 2027, and an indeterminate amount in FY 2028. Revenues are unaffected. Local governments may benefit from increased grant and rebate availability.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary administering agency for the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program, the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which are all amended by this bill.
DBM oversees the development of the executive budget, including monitoring statutory mandated appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and reviewing SEIF budget amendments.
The legislation was introduced as an Administration bill and modifies requirements governing the Governor's annual budget bill appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

The bill references statutory definitions under the Environment Article for overburdened and underserved communities to prioritize grants and rebates, and impacts programs funded by carbon allowance proceeds under the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI).
The bill alters the authorized uses of Alternative Compliance Payments (ACPs) paid by electricity suppliers under Maryland's Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard, which is regulated by the PSC.

The bill reenacts provisions governing the distribution of RGGI proceeds within the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which includes designated allocations to DHS for the Electric Universal Service Program and electricity assistance.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study as to how the State can incentivize broadband service providers to expand broadband infrastructure to communities that are unserved or underserved; and requiring the Office to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Office of Statewide Broadband - Study of Broadband Expansion Incentives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Office of Statewide Broadband to study incentives for expanding broadband infrastructure to unserved and underserved communities. Directs the study to evaluate regulatory and financial incentives for broadband service providers. Requires the Office to examine how other states encourage private investment in broadband networks. Directs the Office to identify ways to deploy federal broadband infrastructure grants effectively. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Office of Statewide Broadband; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: broadband service providers and Maryland residents in unserved or underserved communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources, though general fund expenditures could potentially increase by a limited amount in FY 2024 if contractual consulting costs cannot be absorbed. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 551 specifically tasks the Office of Statewide Broadband, which is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), with conducting a comprehensive study on incentives for expanding broadband infrastructure and submitting findings and recommendations.

The bill was introduced as an Administration initiative and requires the Office of Statewide Broadband to submit its final report, findings, and recommendations directly to the Governor by January 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce to provide funding for certain costs for infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors; requiring certain grantees to provide matching funds and to demonstrate certain abilities; and requiring the Department to report to the Governor and the General Assembly on the projects funded through and the economic impact of the Program by July 1, 2026.
Title: Economic Development - Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund (Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund in the Department of Commerce. Authorizes the department to award up to $2,000,000 per fiscal year for innovation infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors. Permits grants to private companies, nonprofit entities, local governments, and colleges and universities in the State. Requires matching funds of at least 200% for grants up to $1,000,000 and 400% for larger grants. Caps awards to colleges and universities at 50% of the fund's annual appropriation. Terminates the program and abrogates the act on June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Private companies, nonprofit entities, local governments, and colleges and universities in Maryland pursuing innovation infrastructure projects
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2027 to capitalize the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly for grants and administrative costs. Local government and higher education revenues and expenditures increase to the extent they receive grants and provide required matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Commerce as the primary administering agency for the newly created Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and the Build Our Future Grant Fund, including awarding grants, adopting regulations, and submitting program evaluation reports.

Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland are directly eligible to receive grant funding (up to 50% of total fund appropriations) for technology infrastructure projects and must provide matching funds.
As a public university in Maryland, Morgan State University is eligible to receive grants under the program for qualifying technology and innovation infrastructure projects.
As a public higher education institution in the State, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible applicant for grant funding for eligible technology infrastructure initiatives.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Build Our Future Grant Fund separately and invest its moneys, with interest credited directly to the fund.
The bill explicitly mandates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Build Our Future Grant Fund.
DBM is responsible for supervising state budget execution and fiscal planning associated with the bill's annual $10 million general fund appropriation into the special fund.
The legislation is an Administration bill, and the Department of Commerce must report to the Governor by July 1, 2026, regarding the program's projects and economic impact.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of a certain subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain military retirement income received by individuals under the age of 55 years to $12,500 and individuals at least 55 years of age to $20,000 during the taxable year for certain military service; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Military Retirement Income (Keep Our Heroes Home Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans

bill_summary: Increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for eligible military retirement income. Repeals the prior age-based distinction that restricted subtraction amounts by age. Sets the subtraction at the first $25,000 of military retirement income for tax year 2023. Increases the subtraction to the first $40,000 of military retirement income starting in tax year 2024. Covers retirement and death benefits from active, reserve, Maryland National Guard, and specified commissioned corps service.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Military retirees and beneficiaries of military death benefits in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $11.2 million in FY 2024, growing to $13.1 million in FY 2028 due to increased subtraction modifications. Local income tax revenues decrease by $7.3 million in FY 2024 and by $8.6 million by FY 2028. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary tax administrator responsible for collecting state income taxes and implementing income tax subtraction modifications, forms, and reporting rules affected by this bill.

The Department is the state's lead agency advocating for and serving veterans and military retirees, who are the direct beneficiaries of the increased income tax subtraction for military retirement pay.
The bill causes a notable reduction in State General Fund revenues (over $11 million annually), directly impacting state revenue estimates and executive budget planning overseen by DBM.
Service in the Maryland National Guard is explicitly enumerated in the bill as qualifying military service for the military retirement income tax subtraction modification.

Synopsis: Increasing the number of resident judges of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County from 20 to 21.
Title: Baltimore County - Circuit Court Judgeships
bill_summary: Increases the number of resident judges of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County from 20 to 21. Adds one new circuit court judgeship to address critical judicial resource needs. Provides support for associated judicial staff, including a courtroom clerk and a law clerk. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Circuit Court for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Baltimore County Circuit Court judges and court staff; litigants in Baltimore County; Baltimore County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $365,916 in fiscal 2024 and by $486,000 in fiscal 2025 for one additional judge, a courtroom clerk, and a law clerk. Baltimore County expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to fund an administrative assistant and related operating costs. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an additional circuit court judgeship in Baltimore County. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational, financial, and technological support to the Maryland Judiciary, and the bill has a direct state fiscal impact on the Judiciary's budget for the new judge, associated staff, and operating costs.
The Governor is responsible for appointing judges to newly created circuit court positions.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor by recruiting, vetting, and processing candidates to fill judicial vacancies and new judicial seats.

Synopsis: Renaming the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission to be the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; establishing the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government; establishing a regulatory and licensing system for adult-use cannabis; imposing a sales and use tax of 9% on the sale of cannabis; requiring the Administration, by July 1, 2023, to convert medical cannabis licenses to licenses to operate a medical and adult-use cannabis business; etc.
Title: Cannabis Reform

bill_summary: Establishes a comprehensive regulatory, licensing, and taxation framework for adult-use and medical cannabis in Maryland. Renames the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission. Creates the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government to regulate cannabis businesses. Imposes a 9% sales and use tax on retail sales of adult-use cannabis beginning in fiscal 2024. Establishes the Office of Social Equity and the Social Equity Partnership Grant Program to support qualifying applicants. Distributes cannabis tax revenues among dedicated special funds, counties, municipalities, and the General Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Department of General Services
stakeholders: Adult-use cannabis consumers, qualifying medical cannabis patients and caregivers, cannabis business license applicants, medical cannabis growers, processors, and dispensaries, social equity applicants, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State sales and use tax revenues from adult-use cannabis generate an estimated $36.0 million in FY 2024, rising to $146.6 million by FY 2027. Special fund revenues from fees and tax distributions increase by $67.95 million in FY 2024. Net General Fund revenues increase by $18.0 million in FY 2024. State expenditures increase for administration operations and grant programs, including an annual $5.0 million mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2025. Local government revenues increase through a 5% direct tax share and distributions from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 556 creates the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government and the successor to the Maryland Medical Cannabis Commission, tasked with the comprehensive licensing, regulation, and enforcement of medical and adult-use cannabis in Maryland.

Administers and collects the 9% adult-use cannabis sales and use tax, distributes the revenues to mandated special funds and local jurisdictions, and accounts for and administers the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund and Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

Administers the expanded Cannabis Business Assistance Fund providing grants and loans to small, minority-owned, and women-owned cannabis businesses, and establishes and operates the new Capital Access Program to stimulate financing for social equity licensees.

Transfers medical cannabis regulatory oversight and personnel out of MDH, administers the Cannabis Public Health Fund, and is authorized to explore an MOU with the Cannabis Administration to co-locate testing at state health laboratories.

Required to conduct a study identifying potential incubator space locations across four specified regions, and to acquire, construct, or refurbish at least one facility for use as a cannabis incubator space.

Responsible for appointing the Director of the Maryland Cannabis Administration, the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, and members of the Advisory Board on Medical and Adult-Use Cannabis, as well as authorizing budget transfers.

bill_summary: Grants urban renewal authority to the Town of Mount Airy in Carroll County and Frederick County. bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee to establish specifications for purchasing compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate. Requires each unit of State government purchasing these materials to include the specifications in procurements. Applies this requirement only when qualifying products are readily available, competitively priced, and of satisfactory quality.
responsible_party: Maryland Green Purchasing Committee
stakeholders: State agencies purchasing landscaping and aggregate materials, vendors and producers of recycled or organic soil and aggregate products, and local governments managing municipal solid waste
fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative costs can be absorbed with existing resources, but overall procurement cost impacts cannot be reliably estimated due to uncertain product pricing and availability. agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee—a statutory state committee—to establish, publish, and maintain online specifications for purchasing compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate made from recycled or organic materials.

MDOT oversees major capital and maintenance projects across the state that require extensive procurement of aggregate, crushed stone, sand, and soil amendments, making the bill's procurement specifications directly applicable to its contracting operations.

As the agency responsible for maintaining thousands of lane miles of highways and roadside land, SHA is one of the state's largest purchasers of aggregate, mulch, and soil amendments for roadwork, erosion control, and landscaping.

DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks where compost and soil amendments are utilized, and the fiscal note highlights specific agency concerns regarding contaminant risks in solid waste and organic materials applied to state lands.

MDE regulates solid waste management, food waste diversion, sludge, and dredged material beneficial reuse, which form the source materials for the compost and aggregate specifications governed by this bill.

MES operates composting, recycling, dredged material containment, and solid waste facilities across the state, making it directly connected to the supply and production of recycled soil amendments and aggregates purchased by state units.

bill_summary: Prohibits housing discrimination against an individual with a disability who has, obtains, or retains a service dog or guide dog. Authorizes an individual to retain a former service dog or guide dog as a pet for its life after retirement. Exempts qualifying individuals from lease provisions prohibiting dogs and bars landlords from charging additional rent or fees. Holds the individual liable for any damage done to the premises by the service dog or former service dog. Excludes from the definition of service dog animals meant to deter crime or provide only emotional support or companionship.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities who have, obtain, or retain service dogs or guide dogs; housing providers, residential property sellers, and landlords
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary enforcement agency responsible for investigating and resolving complaints of discriminatory housing practices under Title 20 of the State Government Article.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts administrative hearings for contested housing discrimination claims referred by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts, where individuals alleging housing discrimination under these provisions may file civil actions.
The Maryland Department of Disabilities coordinates state policies and initiatives to advance accessible housing and protect the rights of individuals with disabilities.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Nursing in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; altering the exceptions to the registered nurse and licensed practical nurse licensure requirements; providing that, for a certain period of time, the Secretary of Health, rather than the Board, has authority over the infrastructure operations of the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Nursing – Sunset Extension, Licensure Exceptions, and Board Operations and Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Nursing to July 1, 2025. Transfers temporary authority over Board infrastructure operations and staff employment to the Secretary of Health through June 30, 2025. Prohibits using the Board of Nursing Fund for infrastructure operations during that period. Terminates the terms of Board members in office across two staggered dates in 2023. Authorizes applicants who fail the licensing exam once within 120 days of application to practice while pending. Requires the Board to hire an external consultant to evaluate operations and create an action plan.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, applicants for nursing licensure, and members of the State Board of Nursing
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase from fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2025 to cover Board infrastructure operations, including $8.0 million allocated in the fiscal 2024 budget. Special fund expenditures from the Board of Nursing Fund correspondingly decrease for infrastructure but increase by at least $150,000 to hire an external consultant. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing is a health occupations board within the Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date, temporarily transfers authority over the Board's infrastructure operations to the Secretary of Health, authorizes the Secretary to employ staff and set compensation, and directs millions in general fund expenditures to MDH for these operations.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of Health to determine the board positions for which compensation may be set independently, and DBM is mandated to partner in developing the comprehensive action plan addressing Board staffing and infrastructure needs.
The bill mandates that the Board's independent action plan be developed in partnership with DoIT to address immediate infrastructure and operational technology needs.

The bill terminates the terms of all 14 existing Board of Nursing members on staggered dates, requiring gubernatorial appointment and reappointment actions, and requires the Board to submit specified reports directly to the Governor.

Because the terms of all 14 current Board members end on an expedited, staggered schedule under the bill, the Office of Appointments will be responsible for processing, vetting, and administering the appointments and reappointments to the Board.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Aging to oversee long-term care and train the staff of long-term care and dementia care navigation programs; requiring each area agency to establish a long-term care and dementia care navigation program; and requiring the Department to submit a report by October 1, 2024, and each year thereafter, to the Governor, the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House, and certain committees of the General Assembly about the services provided by the program and to publish the report on its website.
Title: Department of Aging - Long-Term Care and Dementia Care Navigation Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes

bill_summary: Requires each area agency on aging to develop a long-term care and dementia care navigation program. Tasks programs with providing cognitive screening, caregiver support, and referrals to long-term care and chronic disease services. Requires the Maryland Department of Aging to oversee and train program staff and collect interaction data. Mandates an annual report on program services submitted to state officials and published online by October 1. Mandates an annual state appropriation of $2,400,000 beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund statewide management and local programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Area Agencies on Aging
stakeholders: individuals experiencing cognitive changes or symptoms of dementia, family caregivers, and area agencies on aging
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $79,733 in FY 2024 for personnel and operating expenses. General fund expenditures increase by $2,400,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to a mandated appropriation. Local area agencies on aging that are units of local government see matching increases in revenues and expenditures beginning in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to oversee and train navigation program staff, disseminate best practices, collect interaction data, distribute $2.4 million in annual mandated funding proportionally to Area Agencies on Aging, and submit an annual report on program outcomes.

The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $2,400,000 starting in fiscal year 2025, which directly impacts state budget planning and execution overseen by the Department of Budget and Management.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a $2,400,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025 and requires the Department of Aging to submit an annual report on navigation services directly to the Governor.

The work of the navigation programs must be guided by recommendations from the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council (established under the Health - General Article), and the programs must establish relationships with health care providers and make referrals to chronic disease services.

Synopsis: Extending the reporting and termination dates, to July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025, respectively, for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals.
Title: Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals - Extension of Dates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Extends deadlines for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals. Requires the Workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by July 1, 2024. Extends the Workgroup's termination date to June 30, 2025. Directs the Workgroup to study shortages and recommend incentives to increase underrepresented behavioral health professionals. Maintains joint staffing support from the University System of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Health.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and other underrepresented behavioral health professionals and students; patients in underserved communities
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal and absorbable increase in State expenditures within existing budgeted resources for the University System of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Health for staffing and workgroup travel reimbursements. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health jointly staffs the Workgroup with the University System of Maryland, and the Secretary of Health designates the chair and appoints several members to the Workgroup.

The University System of Maryland jointly provides staff for the Workgroup, and the presidents of three constituent USM institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore) serve as members.
The President of Morgan State University, or the President's designee, is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the reporting and termination deadlines for a state-established advisory workgroup examining diversity within behavioral health professions.
The Workgroup is statutorily required to submit its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor by the extended reporting deadline.

Synopsis: Establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in the Department of Commerce to provide grants to certain small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises to assist those manufacturers with implementing new Industry 4.0 technology or related infrastructure for certain purposes; establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; and requiring the Governor to include in the budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 an appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Fund.
Title: Economic Development - Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in the Department of Commerce. Authorizes competitive grants between $25,000 and $500,000 to qualifying small and medium-sized enterprise manufacturers. Requires grant recipients to provide matching funds under a sliding scale formula based on employee count. Directs the Department to reserve at least 20% of annual grant funds for manufacturers employing 50 or fewer employees. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $1,000,000 to the program fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Small and medium-sized enterprise manufacturers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $1,123,176 in FY 2025 and approximately $1.1 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2028 to fund grants and department administrative costs. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 as mandated appropriations are received and awarded as grants. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund within the Department of Commerce, tasking the department with program administration, regulation adoption, application evaluation, and grant distribution.

The bill authorizes the Department of Commerce to enter into a memorandum of understanding with a State-chartered corporation under Title 10 to administer the program, and the fiscal note explicitly identifies TEDCO as a potential administrator.

The bill allows Commerce to partner via MOU with a State-chartered corporation under Title 10 to administer the grant program, with MEDCO specifically identified in the fiscal note as an eligible entity.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund in the state budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and development, which must incorporate the statutorily mandated $1.0 million annual appropriation to the Fund from fiscal 2025 through 2028 along with associated administrative costs.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established special fund separately and to invest the fund's moneys.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund.

Synopsis: Expanding the forms of financial assistance available under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program; altering eligibility requirements for projects that may receive financial assistance under the Program; altering the time period when applications may be submitted under the Program; repealing certain restrictions on the amount of financial assistance that may be provided under the Program; etc.
Title: Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development. Expands allowable financial assistance to include loans, grants, interest reductions, prepayments, assurances, guarantees, and credit enhancements. Permits developers to apply for financial assistance when a qualified project is proposed rather than completed. Repeals statutory limits on the amount of financial assistance DHCD may provide. Adds infrastructure and other expenses determined by the Secretary to eligible construction expenses. Requires qualified projects receiving financial assistance to comply with local development and land use plans.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Affordable housing developers and homebuyers in low-income census tracts and sustainable communities
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State operations or finances because funding for the program has not been budgeted since its enactment. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 625 alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The bill expands the types of financial assistance DHCD may provide, alters application timelines, requires DHCD to develop regulations for the application process and distribution of assistance, and authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to determine eligible construction expenses.

Synopsis: Establishing the Human-Relevant Research Fund under the administration of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to provide grants and loans to promote State-funded research intended to develop human-relevant alternatives to using nonhuman animals in medical and product testing and research; requiring, beginning January 15, 2024, research facilities that engage in animal testing or research to pay a contribution, based on a certain number of animals, to the Secretary of Health; providing a civil penalty for a violation of the Act; etc.
Title: Animal Testing and Research - Human-Relevant Research Funding and Animal Testing and Research Contributions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Human–Relevant Research Fund under the administration of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Requires the Corporation to establish a grant and loan program promoting human–relevant alternatives to animal testing. Requires Maryland research facilities that submit federal APHIS Form 7023 to pay an annual contribution to the Department of Health. Sets annual contribution tiers between $5,000 and $75,000 based on the total number of animals reported. Subjects research facilities that fail to pay the required contribution to a civil penalty up to $1,000 per day.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Research facilities in Maryland conducting animal testing or research; public and private entities researching human-relevant animal testing alternatives; public higher education institutions; Community College of Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Human-Relevant Research Fund increase by up to $915,000 annually beginning in FY 2024. State higher education expenditures increase by $120,000 annually across four public universities to pay mandatory contributions. Local expenditures increase by $5,000 annually for the Community College of Baltimore County.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly established Human-Relevant Research Fund, creating and operating the grant and loan program, contracting with an independent review board, adopting regulations, and reporting annually.

The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for collecting the mandatory annual contributions from animal testing research facilities based on federal APHIS Form 7023 filings, assessing civil penalties for failure to pay, and transferring collected funds to TEDCO.

Four USM member institutions (University of Maryland, College Park; University of Maryland, Baltimore; Towson University; and Frostburg State University) conduct animal research subject to the bill and are directly impacted by paying an estimated combined $120,000 annually in required contributions.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Human-Relevant Research Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund and invest fund monies, with interest credited to the Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

The Governor's Office receives the required annual progress report regarding research funded by the program and has discretionary authority to include an appropriation to the Fund in the annual state budget.

Synopsis: Specifying that a certain surviving spouse of a member of the armed forces is eligible to apply for a scholarship under the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program if the service member died, suffered a service connected disability, or was declared to be a prisoner of war or missing in action under certain circumstances.
Title: Higher Education – Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program – Surviving Spouses of Service Members

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to include certain surviving spouses of service members. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the service member died from military service after December 7, 1941. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the service member suffered a service-connected 100% permanent disability. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the member was declared a prisoner of war or missing in action. Requires applicants to be Maryland residents at application or at the disabling or fatal event.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of deceased, disabled, or POW/MIA U.S. armed forces members; eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $7,700 per award annually, but the total fiscal impact cannot be reliably determined because the number of new recipients is unknown.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary state agency responsible for overseeing and administering the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program, updating program regulations, and allocating scholarship funds to postsecondary institutions for eligible recipients.
As the state's postsecondary coordinating body, it oversees financial aid administration including the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and allocates funds to participating institutions.

USM constituent institutions verify eligibility and award Conroy scholarships to enrolled students; additionally, the statutory cap on scholarship award amounts is directly benchmarked to the highest resident undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees within USM.
As an eligible public four-year university, Morgan State processes applications, verifies eligibility, and disburses scholarship awards to qualifying students under the expanded eligibility rules.

The department advocates for and provides outreach to military families and surviving dependents regarding available state educational assistance benefits, including expanded eligibility for surviving spouses under this program.

Synopsis: Authorizing an account holder who is the victim of abuse to terminate, and requiring a utility to allow for the termination of, the account holder's future liability under a utility contract if the account holder provides the utility with certain written notice requesting termination of the account holder's future liability under the contract; requiring a utility to allow an account holder who terminates a utility contract under the Act to open a new utility account notwithstanding a certain account balance or arrearage; etc.
Title: Utility Account Holders - Victims of Abuse - Protections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Authorizes a utility account holder who is a victim of abuse to terminate future liability under a utility contract. Requires a covered utility to allow termination upon written notice by first-class mail or hand delivery. Requires the notice to include an eligible protective order, peace order, or qualified third-party report. Limits the terminating account holder's liability to charges incurred through the billing cycle when notice is submitted. Requires the utility to allow the account holder to open a new account regardless of past arrearages.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Utility account holders who are victims of abuse, and utilities including electric companies, electricity suppliers, gas companies, gas suppliers, sewage disposal companies, and water companies
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and local utilities can implement the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources, resulting in no material impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body overseeing electric, gas, water, and sewage disposal companies in Maryland, which are directly subject to the utility account termination and customer protection mandates established by the bill.

The Office of the People's Counsel advocates on behalf of residential utility consumers regarding utility service practices, consumer rights, and billing protections, aligning directly with the bill's protections for abuse victims holding utility accounts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy coordinates victim services and public safety policy across Maryland and provided information for the evaluation of this bill regarding protections for domestic violence and abuse survivors.

Synopsis: Requiring that the credential reappointment process for physician staff included in certain minimum standards for hospitals licensed in the State be conducted in accordance with standards of the accreditation body that accredits a hospital, rather than every 2 years.
Title: Hospital Credentialing - Reappointment Process for Physician Staff - Modification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Modifies the physician credentialing reappointment process required for hospital licensure in the State. Replaces the mandate to conduct reappointments at least every two years with a requirement to follow accreditation body standards. Retains requirements to document a physician's pattern of performance by analyzing clinical skills, claims, and other performance data. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Secretary of Health
stakeholders: licensed hospitals in Maryland and physicians employed by or holding staff privileges at Maryland hospitals
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources with no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), through the Secretary of Health, licenses hospitals in the state, establishes minimum regulatory standards for hospital credentialing processes, and enforces compliance through penalties or delicensure.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "personal information" for purposes of certain provisions of the Public Information Act to include an individual's personal e-mail address; requiring certain custodians to deny inspection of certain records of personal e-mail addresses and telephone numbers except under certain circumstances; and requiring certain custodians to allow inspection of certain records of business e-mail addresses under the same circumstances as inspection of certain records of business addresses and telephone numbers.
Title: Public Information Act - Inspection of E-Mail Addresses and Telephone Numbers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Alters the definition of personal information under the Maryland Public Information Act to include an individual's e-mail address. Requires custodians to deny inspection of school district records regarding a student's personal e-mail address, with specified exceptions. Requires custodians to deny inspection of personal telephone numbers and personal e-mail addresses of State and local government employees. Directs custodians to allow inspection of a notary public's business e-mail address or fallback personal e-mail address. Requires custodians to allow inspection of an occupational or professional licensee's business e-mail address when identified as such.
responsible_party: Custodians of public records in Maryland State and local government units
stakeholders: Public school students, State and local government employees, notaries public, occupational and professional licensees, and Public Information Act applicants
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends § 4–332 of the General Provisions Article concerning Public Information Act disclosures of notary public applications, commissions, and contact information, which are maintained and administered by the Secretary of State.

The bill explicitly references the Maryland Higher Education Commission in § 4–313, governing its ability to inspect student contact information (including personal email addresses) and prohibiting commercial use or redisclosure of such records.

The bill amends § 4–333 regarding the inspection and disclosure of occupational and professional licensing records, specifically establishing guidelines for releasing licensee business email addresses, an area directly overseen by the Department of Labor.
The bill updates public record disclosure protections for student records across school districts in § 4–313 to include students' personal email addresses and telephone numbers.
The Office of the Attorney General advises state agencies on Maryland Public Information Act compliance and publishes the state's official Public Information Act Manual.
The department licenses numerous health care occupations and professions and serves as the custodian of those licensing records governed by the amended disclosure rules in § 4–333.

Synopsis: Altering the grounds on which a deputy sheriff having a rank of major or below in Washington County may be discharged after 2 years of continuous employment; providing that a special deputy sheriff in Washington County is not a State employee for certain purposes; authorizing sworn deputy sheriffs at the rank of sergeant and below and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below to engage in collective bargaining with the Washington County Sheriff and the County Administrator; etc.
Title: Washington County - Deputy Sheriffs and Correctional Deputies - Employment Conditions and Collective Bargaining

NarrowSubjects.Name: Termination of Employment -see also- Work, Labor, and Employ
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes Washington County sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below to bargain collectively. Subjects any additional funding required by a negotiated agreement to approval by the County Commissioners. Limits the discharge of tenured deputy sheriffs at the rank of major or below strictly to police misconduct. Prohibits covered deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies from engaging in strikes. Specifies that special deputy sheriffs are not State employees for employment security or employee benefits. Establishes that collective bargaining agreements must extend between one and four years.
responsible_party: Washington County Sheriff; Washington County Administrator; County Commissioners of Washington County
stakeholders: Full-time sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below in the Washington County Sheriff's Office, special deputy sheriffs in Washington County, and the Washington County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Washington County expenditures may increase minimally from potential third-party neutral arbitration costs or negotiated agreements, though any funding impact is subject to County Commissioner approval; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly clarifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not considered State employees for the purpose of employee benefits, which are overseen and managed centrally by DBM.

The bill clarifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not State employees for the purpose of employment security (unemployment insurance), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B-GSF (golf simulator facility) license to a golf simulator facility under certain circumstances; authorizing the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption under certain circumstances; requiring the license holder to submit an annual gross sales report to the Board before a license may be renewed; and establishing an annual license fee of $1,500.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Golf Simulator Facility
bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B–GSF license to golf simulator facilities. Requires qualifying facilities to be open to the public and have at least five simulator bays with dedicated seating. Authorizes license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption when food is offered on-premises. Caps annual gross sales of alcohol at 35% while requiring at least 50% from bay rentals and 15% from food. Requires licensees to submit an annual gross sales report to the Board before license renewal. Sets the annual license fee at $1,500.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
stakeholders: golf simulator facility operators and patrons in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by $2,250 in fiscal 2024 for each new license issued (comprising a $750 application fee and $1,500 annual fee) and $1,500 annually thereafter for each renewal. Local enforcement can be handled with existing resources. No state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland and oversees state sales tax collections. While this bill is local to Frederick County and administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing within the state.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $8 to $10, the auctioneer's fee for the tax sale of property in Garrett County for each property sold.
Title: Garrett County - Tax Sales - Auctioneer Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Increases the auctioneer fee allowed as an expense in Garrett County property tax sales. Raises the fee from $8 to $10 for each property sold. Establishes that the fee remains a lien on the property sold at tax sale. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Garrett County Collector of Taxes
stakeholders: Auctioneers and property purchasers participating in tax sales in Garrett County, as well as Garrett County property owners subject to tax sales
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Garrett County finances are not materially affected because the auctioneer fee is included in the property sale price and paid by purchasers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts serves as an information source for the legislation. While the bill specifically adjusts the allowable auctioneer fee for local property tax sales in Garrett County with no state fiscal effect, matters relating to property tax sales and the foreclosure of rights of redemption fall within the jurisdiction of Maryland's court system.

Synopsis: Updating certain provisions of law regarding Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts to refer to the Legislative Districting Plan of 2022; and requiring the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to grant a certain exemption to certain persons under certain circumstances.
Title: Baltimore City – Alcoholic Beverages Districts – Legislative Districting Plan References
bill_summary: Updates references defining Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts to align with the Legislative Districting Plan of 2022. Applies updated boundaries to license issuance, license transfers, tasting licenses, and after-hours operational exemptions. Requires the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to exempt certain license holders from the act. Limits exemptions to holders conducting activities approved by the board on or before February 1, 2022. Mandates that qualifying license holders must have owned the licensed premises continuously since February 1, 2022.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and license applicants in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. Minimal local fiscal impact, as the change is technical and does not directly affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry.
