While the bill specifically updates local legislative districting plan references for Baltimore City's alcoholic beverages districts administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it touches the broader alcoholic beverages regulatory framework.

Synopsis: Altering the timing of the annual election of the officers of the Talbot County Board of Education to be at its last meeting at the end of each calendar year, or at the meeting in December each year.
Title: Talbot County - Board of Education - Election of Officers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: Alters the timing of the annual election of officers for the Talbot County Board of Education. Requires the board to elect a president and a vice president from among its members. Mandates the election occur at the last meeting at the end of each calendar year or in December. Repeals the requirement to elect officers at the first meeting at the beginning of each calendar year.
responsible_party: Talbot County Board of Education
stakeholders: Talbot County Board of Education members
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the change is procedural in nature and does not affect Talbot County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the internal election timing of officers for the Talbot County Board of Education. While MSDE provides statewide oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 local school systems, this procedural change has minimal impact and no fiscal effect on the department.

Synopsis: Altering the requirements for the subject matter of continuing education courses for licensees issued an initial license by the Real Estate Commission.
Title: Real Estate Brokers, Salespersons, and Associate Brokers - Continuing Education Courses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Alters continuing education requirements for real estate brokers, salespersons, and associate brokers holding an initial license. Requires these initial licensees to complete four 3-clock-hour courses across specified real estate topics. Mandates instruction in contract writing, brokerage disclosures, real estate practice principles, and landlord and tenant laws. Requires at least one 1.5-clock-hour course each in real estate financing and professional ethics. Maintains current continuing education curriculum requirements for licensees holding renewal certificates.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: individuals initially licensed as real estate brokers, salespersons, or associate brokers in Maryland, and real estate education course providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State Real Estate Commission special fund expenditures increase by approximately $42,600 in FY 2024 for IT programming and consulting, followed by ongoing consulting expenditures of $2,200 to $2,500 annually through FY 2028. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill alters continuing education curriculum requirements for newly licensed real estate professionals and results in special fund expenditures for the department to update IT tracking systems and engage curriculum consultants.

Synopsis: Requiring the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to confer to identify ways the Comptroller could collaborate with the Department to enhance access to certain property tax benefits administered by the Department; and requiring the Comptroller and the Department to submit a joint report of their findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Comptroller and State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Enhancing Access to Property Tax Benefits - Report
bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to confer during the 2023 legislative interim. Directs both agencies to identify collaboration methods to enhance access to and raise awareness of Department-administered property tax benefits. Seeks to simplify application processes by reducing or eliminating redundant income reporting for homeowners' and renters' tax credits. Requires a joint report of findings and recommendations to two legislative committees by December 1, 2023. Mandates that the report detail required funding amounts and implementation timelines for any recommended changes.
responsible_party: Comptroller; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, renters, disabled veterans, disabled active duty service members, and surviving spouses
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to hire a consultant for the required report. Comptroller operations are handled with existing resources. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly directs the Comptroller to confer with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) during the 2023 legislative interim to identify methods to enhance access, raise awareness, and streamline the application process for state property tax benefits, and to submit a joint report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for a real estate appraisal license and for a certificate for residential or general real estate appraisal to include completion of certain criteria in the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal program.
Title: Real Estate Appraisers - Licensing and Certification - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Establishes an alternative pathway to qualify for a real estate appraisal license or certificate. Allows applicants to complete the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal program criteria. Substitutes the program for the required 1,000 or 1,500 hours of supervised trainee experience. Applies to applicants seeking a real estate appraisal license or residential or general real estate certification. Maintains existing requirements including minimum age, examination passage, and good character.
responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors
stakeholders: Applicants for real estate appraiser licenses and residential or general appraisal certificates, real estate appraiser trainees, and certified real estate appraisers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors likely increase due to additional applicants, but a reliable estimate is not feasible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters licensing and certification qualification pathways for real estate appraisers, directly impacting the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, which operates under the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The department will experience operational and fiscal impacts from reviewing alternative credentials, issuing licenses/certifications, and managing related regulatory oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County to meet at least twice a month; authorizing the Board to hold public meetings in person or through live video streaming; and prohibiting the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings without a formal declaration of a state of emergency.
Title: Garrett County - Board of County Commissioners - Meetings
bill_summary: Requires the Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County to meet in public session at least twice a month. Authorizes the Board to hold public meetings in person or through live video streaming. Prohibits the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings. Waives this prohibition only under a formal declaration of a state of emergency.
responsible_party: Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County
stakeholders: Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County and Garrett County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or Garrett County finances.

Synopsis: Repealing certain requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration increase fares for certain transit services according to the Consumer Price Index; and repealing certain provisions prohibiting the Administration from increasing fares under certain circumstances.
Title: Maryland Transit Administration – Fare Price Requirements – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Repeals requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration increase transit fares every two or five years based on the Consumer Price Index. Eliminates statutory restrictions on fare increases, including caps and conditions tied to inflation declines. Subjects any future fare modifications to existing public hearing requirements. Retains the prohibition against reducing transit service levels to achieve a specific farebox recovery ratio. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: mass transit riders and commuters using Maryland Transit Administration services
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by up to $6.9 million in FY 2024, $7.1 million in FY 2025, $18.1 million in FY 2026, $17.6 million in FY 2027, and $19.8 million in FY 2028 due to foregone mandated fare increases. MTA may mitigate revenue losses by exercising its general authority to raise fares after public hearings. Expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Maryland Transit Administration by repealing statutory requirements that mandated CPI-based increases to its transit fares every two and five years, restoring discretionary fare adjustment authority subject to public hearing requirements.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees transit operations and relies on the Transportation Trust Fund, which will experience a direct revenue reduction of up to tens of millions of dollars annually due to the repealed mandated fare increases.

Synopsis: Altering the uses of the Historic Preservation Loan Fund; and authorizing the Maryland Historic Trust to transfer funds from the Fund to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization to pay for the acquisition, restoration, or rehabilitation of certain historic properties, to provide loans for the acquisition, rehabilitation, restoration, or refinancing of certain properties, and for necessary administrative and programmatic expenses.
Title: Maryland Historic Trust - Historic Preservation Loan Fund - Qualified Cooperating Nonprofit Organizations - Transfers

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Historical Trust to transfer money from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization. Defines qualifying organizations as Maryland-based statewide nonprofits experienced in rehabilitating historic structures, managing preservation funds, and holding preservation easements. Limits the use of transferred funds to acquiring or restoring historic properties, issuing specified loans, and covering administrative costs. Requires recipient organizations to develop a competitive award process and publish program guidelines online. Mandates that recipient organizations submit an annual report to the Trust by June 30 detailing all funds received.
responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
stakeholders: Qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations, historic property owners, and entities or individuals seeking financing to acquire, restore, or rehabilitate historic properties.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures may increase and special fund revenues from loan repayments may decrease in FY 2024 and future years due to transfers from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund; exact amounts cannot be reliably determined.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is a unit within the Maryland Department of Planning. The bill alters the authorized uses of MHT's Historic Preservation Loan Fund to allow transfers to qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations and requires MHT coordination and oversight.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the Historic Preservation Loan Fund, which will be impacted by changes in fund balance and expenditure flows authorized by the bill.
The Board of Public Works has statutory oversight and approval authority over certain expenditures and loans from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund financed through general obligation bonds.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland to study the adequacy of trauma center funding across the State for operating, capital, and workforce costs; and requiring the Commission to reports its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
Title: Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland. Directs the Commission to study the adequacy of State trauma center funding for operating, capital, and workforce costs. Requires the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems and the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide joint staff. Requires the Commission to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and terminates at the end of June 30, 2024.
responsible_party: Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland trauma centers, trauma physicians and clinical staff, trauma patients, Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems, and the Maryland Health Care Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational costs are absorbable within existing budgeted resources of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems and the Maryland Health Care Commission. Commission travel expense reimbursements are assumed to be minimal. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS's Executive Director serves as co-chair of the newly created Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland, and the agency is required to jointly provide staff and expertise for the commission.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission serves as co-chair, the agency jointly provides staff for the Commission, and its members and administrative role with the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund are central to the study.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) serves as a member of the Commission and is tasked with appointing several key commission members representing various health and trauma stakeholder groups.
HSCRC is designated a representative on the Commission and co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, which is a major focus of the Commission's review.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study commission within the State to analyze and report on trauma center operating, capital, and workforce funding adequacy.
The Commission is mandated to report its findings and recommendations regarding trauma center funding to the Governor on or before December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Making certain provisions of law governing cemeteries applicable to pet cemeteries; providing that a certain registered cemeterian, registered crematory operator, or permit holder who sells or offers to sell to the public certain services for pet remains owes a duty of perpetual care for the cemetery in which certain pet remains are interred; and requiring the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt regulations to enforce certain provisions of the Act.
Title: Cemeteries - Interment - Pet Remains
bill_summary: Expands State cemetery oversight laws to cover pet remains and pet interments. Defines pet remains to include whole bodies, body parts, and cremated remains of deceased pets. Imposes a duty of perpetual care on cemetery operators and permit holders offering pet burial or cremation services. Requires preneed burial contracts to include the name of the pet, if applicable. Requires the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt regulations to enforce these provisions.
responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: registered cemeterians, registered crematory operators, cemetery and burial goods permit holders, and pet owners purchasing burial or cremation services
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal impact on the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which can adopt regulations and enforce provisions using existing budgeted resources; special fund revenues may increase minimally if pet cemeteries register, though specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly impacts the OCO by redefining interment to include pet remains, imposing perpetual care requirements, and requiring the Director of the OCO to promulgate regulations and oversee compliance.

Synopsis: Extending until fiscal year 2028 the appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund that the Governor is required to include in the annual budget bill for the operation of the replica sailing vessel known as the Pride of Baltimore II.
Title: Pride of Baltimore II - Appropriations - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Extends the mandated annual budget appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund for operating the Pride of Baltimore II through fiscal 2028. Requires any entity receiving these funds to submit an annual report by December 1. Directs the recipient to submit the report to the Maryland Department of Transportation and specified legislative committees. Requires the report to include expenditure accountings, vessel itineraries, and a multi-year strategic business plan. Extends the termination date of the funding authorization to June 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: operators of the replica sailing vessel Pride of Baltimore II, maritime history educators, and Maryland tourists
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from fiscal 2024 through fiscal 2028 for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II. Revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) from FY 2024 through FY 2028 for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II and requires the fund recipient to submit annual expenditure reports and strategic plans directly to the department.

As the agency responsible for formulating and managing the state budget, DBM is responsible for incorporating and executing the mandated annual appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund into the state budget.
The bill places a statutory requirement on the Governor to include the annual appropriation for the Pride of Baltimore II in the annual State budget.

Synopsis: Requiring in Frederick County a license holder to frame and conspicuously display an alcoholic beverages license on the licensed premises.
Title: Frederick County – Alcoholic Beverages Licenses – Display of License
bill_summary: Alters the license display requirements for alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County. Requires a license holder to frame the license and display it conspicuously in the licensed premises. Removes the statewide requirement that the framed license be under glass within the county. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Frederick County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. Although this legislation specifically affects local retail license display requirements in Frederick County without state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader regulation and governance of alcoholic beverage licenses in the state.

Synopsis: Increasing the total amount of credits against the State income tax that the Maryland Higher Education Commission may approve in a taxable year for certain individuals with certain student loan debt amounts; requiring the Commission to reserve a certain amount of the tax credits that the Commission is authorized to approve for certain graduates; extending, from 2 years to 3 years, the period of time that an individual who claims the credit has to prove that they used the credit to repay the individual's student loan debt; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: Increases the annual cap for the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit from $9 million to $18 million. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to reserve $9 million of authorized credits for State employees. Establishes priority for State employees graduating from Maryland institutions where at least 40% of attendees receive federal Pell Grants. Extends the period to prove student loan repayment from two years to three years to avoid credit recapture. Mandates an outreach and marketing plan and an annual report on credit applicants and recipients. Requires the Office of Student Financial Assistance to inform scholarship recipients about the credit.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
stakeholders: Qualified taxpayers with student loan debt, particularly State employees and graduates of Maryland higher education institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.0 million annually beginning in FY 2024 due to additional personal income tax credits claimed. Expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for reviewing applications, certifying up to $18 million in student loan debt relief tax credits annually, reserving $9 million for qualified state employees, prioritizing applicants, executing outreach campaigns, and submitting an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the state's coordinating board for higher education and administrator of financial assistance programs, the Commission is directly responsible for certifying the tax credits, prioritizing eligible applicants, conducting outreach to institutions of higher education, and reporting annual program metrics.

The Comptroller administers the State income tax system against which this credit is claimed. The office processes the tax returns, handles refundable credits, manages recapture provisions, and accounts for an estimated $9 million annual decrease in State general fund revenues.
The bill mandates that MHEC submit an annual comprehensive report to the Governor by January 1 each year regarding application volume, credit awards, and demographic breakdowns of recipients.

The bill requires MHEC to encourage Maryland institutions of higher education to advise new graduates about the credit, especially those entering public service, and creates priority categories for state employees and graduates of Maryland higher education institutions.

As a public institution of higher education in Maryland with high Pell Grant recipient representation, its graduates and employees are directly impacted and targeted for outreach under the bill's prioritization criteria.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to issue an apprentice hunting license to a person under the age of 17 years who has previously been issued an apprentice hunting license under certain circumstances.
Title: Natural Resources – Apprentice Hunting License – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue an apprentice hunting license to a person under age 17. Allows eligible youth to obtain a license even if previously issued an apprentice hunting license. Requires applicants for a second or subsequent apprentice license to repeat an approved hunter safety course. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters under the age of 17 seeking an apprentice hunting license and supervising adult hunters
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal potential impact on State hunting license fee revenues, with no material effect on State operations or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's wildlife conservation and hunting laws. This bill directly authorizes DNR to issue second or subsequent apprentice hunting licenses to youth under the age of 17 and requires DNR to ensure applicants repeat the approved course in firearm competency and hunter safety.

Synopsis: Eliminating requirements for collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions to maintain separate licenses for branch locations and authorizing them to conduct business at multiple licensed locations under a single license; and altering certain other requirements and provisions governing the licensing and regulation of collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions, including applications, assessments, and bond requirements.
Title: Financial Regulation - Modernizing Licensing of Non-Depository Institutions and Elimination of Branch License Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Eliminates separate branch license requirements for collection agencies and specified non-depository financial institutions. Authorizes licensees to conduct business at multiple locations under a single license recorded in NMLS. Requires licensees to maintain and update additional business locations and trade names in NMLS. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to levy annual assessments on licensees to support the Non-depository Special Fund. Alters surety bond amounts and calculation factors across regulated non-depository license categories.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; State Collection Agency Licensing Board
stakeholders: non-depository financial institutions, collection agencies, mortgage lenders, check cashers, money transmitters, debt management services providers, consumer lenders, sales finance companies, and Maryland consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Non-depository Special Fund decrease by approximately $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to the elimination of branch licensing requirements and associated fees. Special fund expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR) is a major unit within the Department of Labor. OCFR is the primary regulatory and implementing body for this bill, modernizing the licensing, assessments, and oversight of non-depository financial institutions and managing the Non-Depository Special Fund.

The State Treasurer is statutorily designated as the custodian of the Non-Depository Special Fund created/re-established under Section 2-120 of the Financial Institutions Article, responsible for holding, investing, and depositing revenues collected for the fund.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for interest earnings on special funds under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article (amended by the bill to exempt the Non-Depository Special Fund) and receives fines and penalties collected under the title into the General Fund.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and enforcement support to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the Collection Agency Licensing Board, and its Consumer Protection Division was consulted in the fiscal note analysis.

Synopsis: Establishing rules governing the exercise of the decanting power to distribute the property of a first trust to one or more second trusts or to modify the terms of a first trust; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Trusts - Decanting (Maryland Trust Decanting Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Trust Decanting Act governing an authorized fiduciary's power to distribute trust property or modify trust terms. Applies retroactively to express trusts administered in Maryland or governed under Maryland law. Permits fiduciaries to exercise decanting powers without court approval after providing 60 days' advance notice to specified parties. Prohibits decanting that reduces vested interests, diminishes charitable interests, or violates express restrictions in the trust instrument. Authorizes special needs fiduciaries to decant trust property into special needs trusts for beneficiaries with disabilities. Grants the Attorney General the rights of a qualified beneficiary when a trust contains a determinable charitable interest.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Settlors, trustees, authorized fiduciaries, current and remainder trust beneficiaries, individuals with disabilities, and charitable organizations holding trust interests
fiscal_impact_summary: No material direct effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Office of the Attorney General the rights of a qualified beneficiary to represent and bind determinable charitable interests, requiring fiduciaries to give notice to the Attorney General prior to decanting and giving the Attorney General authority to consent or object to trust administration changes.

The bill establishes judicial procedures and authorizes courts with trust jurisdiction to review decanting actions, instruct fiduciaries, appoint special fiduciaries, and determine the validity of decanting exercises under the Act.

While the Register of Wills primarily oversees probate of estates and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court, the agency is consulted on changes to the Estates and Trusts Article concerning fiduciary standards and potential overlaps with testamentary trusts.

Synopsis: Requiring that each memorandum of understanding establishing a school in the Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) School Program ensures that each P-TECH student receives a high school diploma immediately following completion of high school graduation requirements.
Title: Pathways in Technology Early College High (P–TECH) School Program – High School Diplomas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires memoranda of understanding establishing P-TECH schools to guarantee students receive high school diplomas immediately upon completing graduation requirements. Directs the local county board of education to award the diploma. Applies the requirement regardless of whether the student completes a full six-year pathway sequence. Prohibits construing the change to alter education funding formulas for public schools or community colleges. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) students, local school systems, community college partners, and industry partners
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $14,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland State Department of Education to update its student accountability system. Local school system expenditures may increase minimally for system updates. State and local revenues and education formula funding are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public secondary school policy and graduation requirements. The bill requires P-TECH students to receive high school diplomas immediately upon completing graduation requirements, necessitating that MSDE update its student accountability tracking system at an estimated cost of $14,000 in FY 2024.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission coordinates postsecondary education policies in the state, including policies impacting community college partners participating in P-TECH programs, though the bill does not alter community college funding formulas.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation.
Title: Maryland African American Museum Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation. Reduces total board membership from 37 members to 25 members. Adds two appointees selected respectively by the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House. Reduces governor-appointed members with specialized expertise or community representation from 28 to 19. Decreases representatives of African American historical or cultural institutions from four to one. Replaces three previous commission representatives with one member approved by the Commission on African American History and Culture.
responsible_party: Maryland African American Museum Corporation
stakeholders: Members and trustees of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, the Commission on African American History and Culture, Morgan State University, and Maryland African American historical and cultural organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 690 directly alters the composition and structure of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, reducing the total membership from 37 to 25.
The bill alters the Governor's statutory appointment authority regarding the Corporation's Board of Directors, reducing the number of gubernatorial appointees from 36 to 22.
The bill explicitly requires that one member of the Corporation's Board of Directors be a representative of Morgan State University, approved by the university's Board of Regents.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing appointments to state boards, including the gubernatorial appointees to this reconstituted board.

Synopsis: Establishing that a county or a municipal corporation has the authority to approve or deny any local permit required under a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued by the Public Service Commission for generating stations, transmission lines, and qualified generator lead lines; requiring a county or municipal corporation to approve or deny the local permits in a certain manner; prohibiting a county or municipal corporation from conditioning the approval of the local permits on certain approvals; etc.
Title: Public Service Commission – Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity – Local Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to approve or deny local permits required under a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Requires a county or municipal corporation to approve or deny these permits within a reasonable time. Requires permit decisions to follow local laws to the extent state law does not preempt them. Prohibits conditioning permit approval on conditional use, special exception, or floating zone approvals. Affirms judicial precedent concerning state preemption of local zoning over certificate-approved energy projects.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: electric generating station and transmission line developers; county and municipal governments in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances or operations. Local government operations and finances may be affected by the requirement to process certificate-related permits within a reasonable timeframe and without certain zoning conditions, though the fiscal impact on any individual local government is likely minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary state regulator responsible for issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) for generating stations and transmission lines under the Public Utilities Article, which this bill directly amends.

DNR administers the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), which evaluates the environmental and siting impacts of projects during the PSC's CPCN review process, and was consulted as an information source on the bill.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Board of Pharmacy to include a registered pharmacy technician; authorizing a licensed pharmacist, under certain circumstances, to delegate the entry of certain data into databases or patient charts to be performed at a remote location to a registered pharmacy technician and a registered pharmacy intern; prohibiting registered pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees from making decisions requiring the professional judgment of a pharmacist; etc.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Board Membership, Delegated Pharmacy Acts, and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Adds a registered pharmacy technician to the State Board of Pharmacy, increasing total board membership to 13. Authorizes licensed pharmacists to delegate remote prescription-related data entry to registered pharmacy technicians or registered pharmacy interns under specified conditions. Prohibits registered pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees from making decisions requiring the professional judgment of a pharmacist. Authorizes registered pharmacy technicians to administer specified vaccines to individuals meeting age thresholds, while prohibiting trainees from administering vaccinations. Extends the termination date of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: registered pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technician trainees, registered pharmacy interns, licensed pharmacists, and pharmacy patients
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy are maintained through fiscal 2025. Special fund expenditures may increase minimally for per diem and expenses for the additional board member. Local operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Pharmacy operates within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date under the sunset act, alters board membership, and modifies statutory provisions regarding delegated pharmacy acts and vaccinations.
The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint a newly created registered pharmacy technician member to the State Board of Pharmacy from lists submitted by designated professional associations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing nominations and appointments for vacancies on state boards, including the newly added seat on the State Board of Pharmacy.

Synopsis: Authorizing the allocation of grants from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund for certain business and workforce development activities.
Title: Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund - Allocation of Grants (Rural Communities Improvement Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the allowable uses of grant disbursements from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund. Adds agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development to the rural entrepreneurship grant category. Defines cooperative development to include feasibility, industry, and market studies, as well as business entity establishment. Defines workforce development to include worker skills training and support for local workforce training organizations. Awards competitive grants to promote economic growth and employment opportunities in rural communities.
responsible_party: Rural Maryland Council; Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Board
stakeholders: Rural businesses, agricultural cooperatives, rural workers seeking job training, community colleges, career and technical education centers, and local workforce boards in Maryland rural communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected overall, though grant disbursements from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund may be reallocated among eligible recipients, including institutions of higher education. Local community colleges may experience a minimal increase in grant funding for workforce development programs. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Rural Maryland Council directly administers the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF). The bill modifies the allowable uses and categories of RMPIF grant distributions to include agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development.

The Rural Maryland Council is administratively housed within the Department of Agriculture, and the legislation expands allowable grant allocations under RMPIF to specifically include agricultural development.

The bill explicitly expands grant eligibility to include workforce development programs and activities designed to train workers for local employers, intersecting with the Department of Labor's role in workforce training and adult learning.

The legislation modifies grant funding criteria for rural entrepreneurship, small business feasibility, and cooperative business development, which aligns with the Department of Commerce's focus on statewide business development.

Synopsis: Establishing the Black Bass Conservation Fund in the Department of Natural Resources to further black bass management; requiring the Department to administer the Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring interest earnings of the Fund to be credited to the Fund; and requiring the Department to establish a process through which an individual who purchases a certain license online to make a voluntary donation to the Black Bass Conservation Fund.
Title: Natural Resources - Black Bass Conservation Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Black Bass Conservation Fund within the Department of Natural Resources to further black bass management. Requires the Department to allow purchasers of an angler's license or Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license to donate. Restricts voluntary donations to individuals purchasing directly through the electronic system rather than authorized vendors. Authorizes fund monies for stocking black bass, enhancing aquatic habitats, and supporting responsible tournaments. Authorizes expenditures for scientific research related to black bass conservation.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Recreational anglers purchasing Maryland fishing licenses, black bass tournament organizers, and the Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 from voluntary donations, interest earnings, and black bass management expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Black Bass Conservation Fund within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and requires DNR to administer the fund, integrate voluntary donation options into its electronic licensing system, collect donations, and expend fund revenues on bass stocking, habitat enhancement, tournaments, and research.
The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold the Black Bass Conservation Fund separately and invest its moneys, with net interest retained in the fund rather than accruing to the General Fund.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Black Bass Conservation Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the placement and use of a speed monitoring system at the intersection of Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue in Talbot County, subject to placement and signage requirements; requiring the fines collected by the Town of Oxford as a result of the speed monitoring system to be used to assist in covering the cost of roadway and pedestrian safety improvements in and around the intersection; etc.
Title: Talbot County – Speed Monitoring Systems – Intersection of Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Authorizes placement of one speed monitoring system at Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue in Talbot County. Requires warning signage and a proximate device displaying real-time driver traveling speed before activating the system. Allows the Town of Oxford to recover system implementation and administration costs from collected violation fines. Requires remaining fine balances to be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration. Directs the State Highway Administration to use funds solely for roadway and pedestrian safety improvements near the intersection. Abrogates the statutory authority on September 30, 2028.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) in Talbot County; Town of Oxford; pedestrians near the intersection of Maryland Route 333 and Bonfield Avenue
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures increase from FY 2024 through FY 2029 to the extent the speed camera is installed, with net revenues dedicated to local roadway and pedestrian safety improvements. General fund revenues may increase negligibly from contested citations in District Court. Local revenues and expenditures increase for system implementation and cost recovery.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT SHA is specifically designated to receive remitted speed monitoring system net revenues distributed via the Comptroller and is required to use those funds solely to cover the costs of roadway and pedestrian safety improvements at the intersection of MD Route 333 and Bonfield Avenue. The bill also references SHA traffic control device standards for signage.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration. The bill directly impacts Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures, which increase as fine balances are collected and expended for safety improvements on a state route.

The bill mandates that remaining fine revenues collected by the Town of Oxford be remitted to the Comptroller, who is then responsible for distributing those funds to the State Highway Administration.

The District Court prescribes the uniform citation form and penalty amounts for speed camera violations, and handles any contested citations resulting from the newly authorized speed monitoring system.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, in consultation with the Secretary of Health, to set the compensation of certain Commission employees; requiring the Secretary of Budget and Management, in consultation with the Secretary of Health, to determine the positions for which the Commission may set compensation; and authorizing the Comptroller, the Treasurer, and the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scale of certain positions in their offices.
Title: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and Offices of the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General - Compensation and Pay Scales of Employees
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 801

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission to set compensation for certain unique staff positions. Authorizes the Comptroller, the Treasurer, and the Attorney General to set pay scales for specific unique positions. Requires consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management to set pay scales and determine eligible positions. Requires eligible positions to be unique to each agency and require specific skills or experience. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer; Office of the Attorney General; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Employees in qualifying unique positions within the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, Office of the Comptroller, Office of the State Treasurer, and Office of the Attorney General
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase for the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and general fund expenditures increase for the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General beginning as early as fiscal 2024. Exact fiscal amounts are indeterminate because they depend on determinations of eligible positions and salary adjustments made by agency leadership and the Secretary of Budget and Management. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Comptroller, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scales of positions unique to the Office of the Comptroller, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact.

The bill grants statutory authority to the State Treasurer, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scale for positions unique to the Office of the Treasurer, directly impacting agency expenditures and personnel administration.

The bill authorizes the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to establish pay scales for positions unique to the Office of the Attorney General, leading to direct personnel and fiscal impacts.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is tasked with consulting with the Comptroller, Treasurer, Attorney General, and the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission to determine eligible positions and consult on pay scales.

The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (MCHRC) operates within MDH, and the Secretary of Health is statutorily required to consult with the Commission on determining job classifications, grades, and employee compensation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide certain information regarding the acquisition of a nursing home to the Office of Health Care Quality; requiring the Secretary of Health to consider the information before taking action regarding licensure to operate a nursing home; and requiring the Commission, in consultation with certain stakeholders, to study and make recommendations regarding the expansion of the certificate of need program over acquisitions of nursing homes and report by December 1, 2023.
Title: Health Care Facilities - Nursing Homes - Acquisitions and Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide written findings and recommendations to the Office of Health Care Quality. Applies this mandate when evaluating notices of acquisition or transfer of interest of a nursing home. Requires the Secretary of Health to consider those findings before approving, denying, conditioning, or revoking a license. Mandates inclusion of purchaser quality ratings, three-year compliance surveys, corrective action plans, and patient lawsuits. Directs the Commission to study expanding the Certificate of Need program over nursing home acquisitions by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Office of Health Care Quality; Secretary of Health
stakeholders: nursing home owners, operators, prospective purchasers of nursing homes, and nursing home residents
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected, as the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission can implement the requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks MHCC with evaluating notices of acquisition or transfer of interest in nursing homes, compiling detailed findings and recommendations on facility quality and performance, transmitting them to the Office of Health Care Quality, and conducting a study regarding the expansion of the Certificate of Need program over nursing home acquisitions.

The bill requires the Secretary of Health to consider MHCC's findings and recommendations before approving, denying, conditioning, or revoking a nursing home operating license. Additionally, units within MDH (the Office of Health Care Quality and the Medicaid Administration) receive these findings and are named as key consulting stakeholders for the required study.

Synopsis: Establishing that every person, as a central component of an individual's rights to liberty and equality, has the fundamental right to reproductive freedom; and prohibiting the State from, directly or indirectly, denying, burdening, or abridging the right unless justified by a compelling State interest achieved by the least restrictive means.
Title: Declaration of Rights - Right to Reproductive Freedom
Status: Approved by the Governor, assigned a chapter number, enactment subject to constitutional referendum - Chapter 245

NarrowSubjects.Name: Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution establishing a fundamental right to reproductive freedom. Protects an individual's ability to make and effectuate decisions to prevent, continue, or end a pregnancy. Prohibits the State from denying, burdening, or abridging this right directly or indirectly. Permits restrictions only if justified by a compelling State interest achieved by the least restrictive means. Submits the proposed constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2024 general election.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Governor
stakeholders: Maryland voters, individuals making reproductive and pregnancy decisions, and licensed healthcare providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires a proposed constitutional amendment on reproductive freedom to be submitted to Maryland voters at the November 2024 general election, which the State Board of Elections must prepare, certify, and place on ballots statewide.

As the State's chief legal counsel, the Office of the Attorney General provided information for the bill's analysis and is responsible for defending and interpreting state constitutional provisions, including the proposed standard of strict scrutiny regarding reproductive freedom.

The Department of Health regulates health care providers and reproductive healthcare services in Maryland, and constitutionalizing the right to reproductive freedom impacts the regulatory framework and state limits surrounding reproductive healthcare and pregnancy.

Pursuant to the bill and Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution, the official election returns regarding the adoption or rejection of the constitutional amendment are formally reported to the Governor.

Synopsis: Establishing the Business Facade Improvement Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development to assist qualified businesses located in sustainable communities with improving the outside appearance of the qualified businesses' buildings or facilities; requiring the Department to develop an application process for political subdivisions seeking to participate in the Program; and requiring the Governor, beginning in fiscal year 2025, to include $5,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the Program.
Title: Community Development - Sustainable Communities - Business Facade Improvement Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Business Facade Improvement Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires the Department to distribute program funds to political subdivisions that have at least one sustainable community. Requires participating political subdivisions to distribute grants to qualified businesses improving their facilities' outside appearance. Requires both the Department and participating political subdivisions to develop application processes and award criteria. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $5,000,000 to the program beginning in fiscal year 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Qualified businesses in sustainable communities, counties, and municipal corporations in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $1.5 million in bond funds in FY 2024 and by $5.0 million in general funds annually beginning in FY 2025 under a statutory mandate. Local revenues and expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2024 and approximately $4.9 million annually thereafter from grant distribution.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Business Facade Improvement Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). DHCD is the primary agency responsible for administering the program, developing application processes and rating criteria, distributing funds to political subdivisions, and adopting regulations.
The bill explicitly mandates that for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter, the Governor must include an appropriation of $5,000,000 to the program in the annual state budget bill.

As the principal fiscal and budget agency for the state, DBM oversees budget formulation and must account for the $5,000,000 annual mandated general fund appropriation to the program starting in FY 2025.

Synopsis: Establishing the Taxpayer Advocate Division in the Office of the Comptroller to assist taxpayers and their representatives in resolving certain taxpayer problems and complaints and represent taxpayers' interests in a certain manner.
Title: Office of the Comptroller - Taxpayer Advocate Division

NarrowSubjects.Name: Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division in the Office of the Comptroller. Places the division under the administrative control of a Taxpayer Advocate supervised by the Comptroller. Requires a minimum of six division employees, including the Taxpayer Advocate and an information technology webmaster. Directs the division to assist taxpayers and their representatives in resolving tax and debt collection problems. Mandates the division establish a website portal, conduct annual taxpayer surveys, and compile complaint data. Requires the division to propose administrative, legislative, or regulatory changes to resolve systemic taxpayer issues.
responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers and their representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $294,700 in FY 2024 to hire four staff members and cover operating expenses, increasing to $401,600 by FY 2028. Revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division within the Office of the Comptroller, requiring the Comptroller to appoint staff, oversee the division, establish an electronic taxpayer portal, and absorb personnel and operational expenditures.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Budget and Management, in coordination with the Comptroller's Office, to make appropriate personnel allocations and provide the ability to reclassify positions for the new division.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of the Comptroller, the Office of the State Treasurer, the Department of Budget and Management, the Department of Information Technology, and the Department of General Services, in consultation with a representative of the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission, to develop, implement, manage, and oversee the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise; and requiring the Office of the Comptroller to periodically report to the General Assembly on the status of the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise.
Title: Modernization of State Financial Systems - 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires five State departments to develop and oversee the cloud-based 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise. Mandates consultation with a designated representative from the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission. Directs the departments to standardize State financial management by requiring all State agencies to participate. Authorizes the departments to collaborate with consultants, assign resources, and establish working groups as needed. Requires the Office of the Comptroller to submit semiannual progress reports through January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Office of the State Treasurer; Department of Budget and Management; Department of Information Technology; Department of General Services
stakeholders: All Maryland State agencies, State accounting personnel, and users of State financial management information systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Comptroller as a primary implementing partner to develop, manage, and oversee the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise, and requires the Comptroller's Office to submit semi-annual status reports to the General Assembly through 2027.
The bill explicitly designates DBM as one of the primary departments required to develop, implement, manage, and oversee the modernization of the State's financial management infrastructure.
The bill explicitly designates DGS as one of the partner departments responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing the new financial management systems enterprise.
The bill explicitly designates DoIT as one of the core departments responsible for setting technology policies and overseeing the cloud-based IT infrastructure transformation.
The bill explicitly names the Treasurer's Office as one of the key departments tasked with overseeing and implementing the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires the partner departments to consult with a designated representative from the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission (MMOC) in planning and implementing the enterprise.

MDOT operates a separate version of the Financial Management and Information System (FMIS) and is undergoing its own modernization effort, making the bill's mandate to standardize financial management across all state agencies directly impactful to their systems.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law authorizing the use of speed monitoring systems in certain residential districts apply in Anne Arundel County.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Residential Districts

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Authorizes the placement of speed monitoring systems on highways in residential districts in Anne Arundel County. Restricts placement to highways with a maximum posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour. Requires the speed limit to be established using generally accepted traffic engineering practices. Prohibits system use unless authorized by local law enacted after reasonable notice and a public hearing. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Motorists driving in Anne Arundel County, residents of Anne Arundel County residential districts, Anne Arundel County government, and municipal governments in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues likely increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 due to contested citations in District Court, with no material expenditure impact. Local revenues increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2024 from citation fines, while local expenditures increase for system procurement, installation, and maintenance, with net balances dedicated to public safety purposes. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Contested speed camera citations issued under the authorization in Anne Arundel County will be adjudicated in the District Court, impacting court caseloads and generating fine revenues paid into the State general fund.

The bill amends Title 21 of the Transportation Article regarding speed monitoring system authorization on highways in residential districts, affecting transportation safety regulation and state road infrastructure.
The State Highway Administration establishes traffic engineering standards, regulates speed limits, and adopts standards for required signage proximate to speed monitoring systems.
Under statutory provisions governing speed monitoring systems, if a local jurisdiction's net camera revenues exceed 10% of its total revenues, the excess balance must be remitted to the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Altering the information that must be included in a written statement provided by a managed care organization to a health care provider when retroactively denying reimbursement as a result of coordination of benefits.
Title: Managed Care Organizations - Retroactive Denial of Reimbursement - Information in Written Statement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: Alters the information required in written statements from managed care organizations retroactively denying reimbursement. Applies when a managed care organization retroactively denies provider reimbursement due to coordination of benefits. Requires the statement to include the name and address of the entity identified as responsible for payment. Exempts managed care organizations from obtaining an acknowledgment of responsibility before denying a claim. Maintains the acknowledgment requirement for carriers that are not managed care organizations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Medicaid managed care organizations, health care providers, and health insurance carriers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the state's Medicaid program, under which Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) operate. This bill amends provisions in the Health-General Article governing MCO procedures for retroactive denial of reimbursement to health care providers.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance carriers and enforces the Insurance Article, including § 15-1008 which governs retroactive denials of reimbursement and coordination of benefits requirements for health insurance carriers.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which contracts with health insurance carriers subject to state insurance statutory standards regarding claims and reimbursement denials.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Nursing to appoint peer advisory committees to provide advice related to midwifery; authorizing registered nurses certified as nurse-midwives and licensed certified midwives to personally prepare and dispense a starter dosage of certain drugs under certain circumstances; altering the exceptions to the certified midwifery licensure requirement and the qualifications required for a license; etc.
Title: State Board of Nursing - Peer Advisory Committees, Scopes of Practice, and Licensure Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes licensed certified midwives and nurse-midwives to personally prepare and dispense starter dosages of certain drugs. Permits licensed certified midwives to delegate technical tasks to trained assistants under direct, on-site supervision. Expands definitions of certified medication technicians and certified nursing assistants to include tasks delegated by midwives. Repeals the prerequisite health and science coursework requirement for certified midwife licensure. Authorizes the State Board of Nursing to appoint peer advisory committees regarding certified midwifery practice. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to recommend strategies expanding birthing center access by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed certified midwives, licensed registered nurses certified as nurse-midwives, certified medication technicians, certified nursing assistants, birthing centers, and maternity patients
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Nursing and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Board of Nursing, a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), altering licensure standards, scope of practice, and delegation authorities for nurse-midwives and certified midwives. In addition, Section 2 of the bill specifically requires MDH, in consultation with stakeholders, to develop recommendations and submit a report on expanding access to birthing services in birthing centers across the State.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "qualified conservation" for purposes of provisions of law related to forest mitigation banks; altering certain  methods of calculating forest afforestation, reforestation, and preservation requirements; authorizing local jurisdictions to adopt certain alternative afforestation, reforestation, and preservation requirements; requiring the Department of Natural Resources to establish a workgroup to evaluate and recommend incentives for private landowners to conserve forest; etc.
Title: Natural Resources – Forest Preservation and Retention

NarrowSubjects.Name: Clean Energy Credits -see also- Renewable Energy Sources
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees

bill_summary: Modifies the State forest preservation policy to increase statewide forest land and tree canopy acreage every four years. Replaces conservation thresholds with a standard reforestation ratio of one acre planted for each acre cleared. Establishes a reduced reforestation ratio of one-half acre per cleared acre in designated priority funding areas. Exempts transit-oriented developments and specified multifamily housing projects subject to mandatory reforestation or preservation mitigation. Authorizes local jurisdictions to adopt alternative forest conservation requirements approved by the Department of Natural Resources. Extends the deadline for the Department of Natural Resources to expend Forest Conservation Fund deposits to five years.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: private landowners, residential and commercial developers, local governments, forest mitigation bank operators, and commercial landscaping and nursery contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in State PAYGO general fund expenditures and local capital expenditures beginning in FY 2025 for public construction projects clearing forest land. Indeterminate net effect on State and local forest conservation fund fee-in-lieu revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Forest Conservation Act (FCA). The bill requires DNR to update the State Forest Conservation Technical Manual, review and approve local alternative forest conservation programs, administer the State Forest Conservation Fund with updated expenditure timelines, and establish a workgroup to recommend incentives for private landowner forest conservation.

The bill incorporates MDE-identified Tier II and Tier III high-quality watersheds into priority forest retention criteria and cross-references MDE environmental site design and stormwater management standards for reforestation mitigation credits.

The bill alters exemptions from the Forest Conservation Act regarding electric generating stations and solar photovoltaic facilities licensed via Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) issued by the Commission.

State transportation and infrastructure projects are subject to the Forest Conservation Act's updated reforestation ratios and buffer requirements. The bill also establishes specific reforestation and mitigation ratios for transit-oriented developments defined under the Transportation Article.

The bill defines procedures, timeframes (30-day petition deadline), and evidentiary scopes (limited to the agency record) for judicial review of approved forest conservation plans and priority clearing determinations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation requires the creation of a temporary workgroup to evaluate and recommend incentives for private landowners to conserve forest lands.

Synopsis: Requiring, unless the child's family requests that the child be removed, that a child on the registry for the Autism Waiver remain on the registry if the child's family relocates out of the State for military service; and providing that if a child on the registry for the Waiver becomes eligible for services while the child's family is out of the State for military service, the child shall be eligible for services through the Waiver if the family relocates to the State.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Autism Waiver - Military Families

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
