bill_summary: Requires a child on the Autism Waiver registry to remain on the registry during out-of-state military relocations. Allows removal from the registry only upon request by the child's family. Restores eligibility for waiver services if the family relocates back to Maryland after qualifying while out of State. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: military families with children on the Autism Waiver registry
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies current practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, maintains and manages the Autism Waiver registry, conducts eligibility verifications, and will need to pursue any required federal Medicaid waiver amendments.

The Maryland State Department of Education directly administers the Autism Waiver, monitors military family participants relocating out of state, and implements placement on the waiver registry upon their return to Maryland.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families advocates for and assists active-duty service members and their families in navigating and securing state benefits and healthcare services in Maryland.
The Maryland Department of Disabilities coordinates statewide policies and service delivery for individuals with developmental disabilities and works with MSDE and MDH on disability support programs.

Synopsis: Approving certain projects for the acquisition, development, and improvement of certain academic facilities for the University System of Maryland; approving the issuance of bonds by the University System of Maryland in a total principal amount of $25,000,000 for financing the projects; providing that the bonds are not a debt or obligation of the State or any of its subdivisions; and authorizing the Board of Regents to approve the use of money received from the sale of certain property for operating expenses at certain campuses.
Title: University System of Maryland - Facilities - Bonding Authority and Sale

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee

bill_summary: Approves $30,000,000 in academic facilities bond authority for the University System of Maryland. Allocates $5,000,000 to finance an infrastructure project at the University of Maryland, College Park. Allocates $25,000,000 for systemwide capital facilities renewal projects across constituent institutions and centers. Specifies that issued bonds do not constitute debt or an obligation of the State. Authorizes nonresidential campuses to use property sale proceeds for operating expenses with Board of Regents approval.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland; Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, students, faculty, and nonresidential campuses including University of Maryland Global Campus

Nonresidential campus revenues and operating expenditures may increase from expanded authorized uses of property sale proceeds. No local fiscal impact.

Under the statute amended by the bill, the Board of Public Works approves the sale or exchange of real properties by the USM Board of Regents and the standard uses of property sale proceeds.

bill_summary: Prohibits reporting a known false emergency or crime to a governmental emergency report recipient with reckless disregard of bodily harm. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to three years imprisonment and a $2,000 fine for violations. Elevates the offense to a felony if the response proximately causes serious physical injury, severe emotional distress, or death. Subjects felony violators to maximum penalties of 10 years imprisonment and a $20,000 fine. Classifies a minor's first violation as a civil offense and prohibits Department of Juvenile Services out-of-home placement. Makes violators civilly liable to any individual injured as a result of the violation.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Individuals who report emergencies or crimes, victims of swatting incidents, emergency responders, and juvenile offenders
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected. Potential minimal increases in expenditures may occur for the Office of the Public Defender and the Judiciary due to additional caseloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends statutory provisions governing the Department of Juvenile Services by prohibiting a child from being committed to DJS for out-of-home placement if the most serious offense is a first-time violation of the antiswatting provisions.

The bill creates new criminal offenses (misdemeanor and felony), juvenile civil procedures, and a civil cause of action, directly impacting court caseloads, filings, and judicial proceedings managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender will be required to provide legal defense representation to indigent individuals and juveniles charged with the new misdemeanor, felony, and juvenile offenses established by the bill.

As the primary state law enforcement agency and a governmental emergency report recipient, the Maryland State Police is directly affected through responding to emergency reports, investigating swatting incidents, and enforcing the new criminal statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees incarceration in state correctional facilities and community supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation for individuals convicted of misdemeanor or felony violations under the bill.

The bill specifically encompasses false reports made to public safety answering points (PSAPs), which are overseen and coordinated through the Maryland 9-1-1 Board housed within the Department of Emergency Management.

bill_summary: Establishes concurrent jurisdiction of Maryland juvenile courts with federal courts over certain offenses committed on military installations. Applies to proceedings where a child commits a federal law violation on a U.S. Department of Defense installation. Requires the federal court to waive exclusive jurisdiction and the violation to constitute a crime under State law. Authorizes the Governor to enter agreements establishing concurrent jurisdiction over federal land regardless of prior statutory cessions. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: juveniles alleged to have committed offenses on U.S. Department of Defense military installations in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Procedural measure not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the statutory jurisdiction of the State's juvenile courts to exercise concurrent jurisdiction with federal courts over certain offenses committed by juveniles on federal Department of Defense military installations.

The Department of Juvenile Services oversees, assesses, and provides services to youths adjudicated within the Maryland juvenile court system, which may now include children processed under concurrent state jurisdiction for offenses on military installations.

The bill amends General Provisions § 6-202 to expressly authorize the Governor to enter into agreements with the United States to establish full or partial concurrent jurisdiction over any land in the State held by the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to eligible juveniles in delinquency proceedings and could be assigned to represent youths charged under state juvenile court jurisdiction for incidents occurring on military installations.

bill_summary: Establishes the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund. Requires the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the Fund. Dedicates grants to Mental Health First Aid for Public Safety training and Critical Incident Stress Management peer support training. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the Fund in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2025. Requires recipient law enforcement agencies to submit expenditure and performance data within 90 days after each grant cycle. Requires the Executive Director to submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
stakeholders: State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies, sheriffs' offices, and police officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $27,800 in FY 2024 for administrative staffing, and by approximately $1.1 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize and administer the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by an assumed $1.0 million annually starting in FY 2025 for grant awards. Local law enforcement grant revenues and expenditures likely increase beginning as early as FY 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is designated as the primary administrative agency responsible for managing the newly established Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund, reviewing grant applications, monitoring grantee performance, and reporting annually to the Governor and General Assembly.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund as a separate, nonlapsing special fund.
The statute specifically requires the Comptroller, in conjunction with the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, to account for the new grant fund.

The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the fund in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025 and requires annual reports on fund usage to be submitted to the Governor.
As the state's budget agency, DBM is involved in coordinating discretionary appropriations and general fund expenditures to capitalize the fund and support administrative staffing costs.

Because the definition of eligible law enforcement agencies encompasses state-level law enforcement organizations that enforce general criminal laws, MSP is potentially eligible to receive grant funding for officer mental health and crisis peer support training.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for the storage and preservation of sexual assault evidence collection kits; requiring sexual assault evidence collection kits collected before January 1, 2000, to be retained and transferred in a certain manner; and requiring the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee, by December 1, 2023, to issue a report to the Governor and the General Assembly on certain recommendations, in consultation with the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

bill_summary: Extends from 20 to 75 years the minimum retention period for sexual assault evidence collection kits and related evidence. Prohibits law enforcement agencies, health care providers, and hospitals from destroying kits within 75 years of collection. Requires hospitals and child advocacy centers to transfer kits and self-administered kits to law enforcement agencies within 30 days. Requires kits collected before January 1, 2000, to be transferred to law enforcement agencies for testing. Directs the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee to submit recommendations by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: victims of sexual assault, law enforcement agencies, hospitals, child advocacy centers, and qualified health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No material near-term impact on State or local finances. State general fund expenditures and local expenditures may increase in future years should the Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies need to acquire additional long-term storage facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Attorney General to adopt regulations for uniform statewide implementation of sexual assault evidence kit requirements, authorizes the office to direct the transfer of certain pre-2000 kits, and tasks its Consumer Protection Division with consulting on consumer education regarding self-administered kits.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Department of State Police investigates sexual assault cases, receives and maintains custody of evidence collection kits, and will be required to preserve and store kits for 75 years instead of 20 years, with potential long-term fiscal impacts on evidence storage capacity.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee is tasked with reporting to the Governor and General Assembly with recommendations on transfer guidelines, guidance on self-administered kits, and victim education resources.
The bill directly amends retention, notice, and storage requirements for healthcare providers and hospitals that perform sexual assault evidence collection exams and store kits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates state policies, initiatives, and grant funding related to crime prevention, public safety, and victim services, including sexual assault response.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated recommendations report from the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee by December 1, 2023.

Allows victims and victim representatives to track the location, status, and chain of custody of their kits. Requires law enforcement agencies, health care providers, forensic laboratories, and State's Attorneys possessing kits to submit tracking information. Authorizes the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund to cover kits collected before or after the fund's establishment.

Kit tracking software procurement is funded through existing federal grant awards. Local governments, forensic laboratories, and State's Attorneys can implement reporting requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the office (referenced as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to establish and administer the statewide sexual assault evidence collection kit tracking and reporting program, adopt necessary regulations, and administer the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund.

As a primary law enforcement agency operating the state crime laboratory, the Maryland State Police must report kit location, status, and chain of custody data into the reporting program and comply with all program regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the administering agency to develop regulations for the reporting program in consultation with the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee.

fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local expenditures or revenues. Existing administrative appropriations within the Senator George C. Edwards Fund accommodate the Executive Director salary of up to $75,000 and minimal board reimbursements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership, voting structure, officers, and administrative oversight of the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, including establishing an Executive Director position.

The board is required to submit an annual implementation report to the Governor detailing funding, completed projects, and economic metrics, and the Governor oversees executive budget appropriations for the associated fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Senator George C. Edwards Fund, which supports the program and covers the salary of the newly established Executive Director.
The State Treasurer is tasked with holding and investing the monies of the special, nonlapsing Senator George C. Edwards Fund governed by the legislation.

Authorizes Tier II children with disabilities or non-English home backgrounds to enroll in full-day prekindergarten for the 2023–2024 school year. Requires assistant principals on the career ladder to participate in direct classroom student interactions rather than formal classroom teaching. Delays county board selection of curriculum-writing experts until July 1, 2026, conditioned on career ladder establishment. Prohibits requiring schools to collect the alternative income eligibility form until the year after the Department adopts it. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for administering public education funding formulas, regulating early childhood and prekindergarten programs, developing and adopting the alternative income eligibility form, and implementing career ladder guidelines for educators under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory composition and terms of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports by adding a certified school counselor designated by the Maryland School Counselor Association.

The Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports is administratively housed within the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission under the Department of Health, and its membership is expanded by this bill.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Health or Office of Health Care Quality to investigate unlicensed assisted living programs. Requires the investigation to determine whether residents suffered neglect, exploitation, or abuse. Subjects operators to immediate prosecution upon credible allegations or findings of neglect, exploitation, or abuse, or upon noncooperation. Authorizes the Department, Attorney General, State's Attorneys, or local health officers to petition for injunctive relief. Repeals consideration of a facility's ability to pay when the State recommends criminal penalties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of Health Care Quality
stakeholders: Residents and operators of unlicensed assisted living programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Imposition of existing penalty provisions and injunctive relief authority are not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health and its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) investigate unlicensed assisted living programs for abuse, neglect, and exploitation, enforce licensure compliance, and authorize petitions for injunctive relief.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General, authorizes the Attorney General to petition circuit courts for injunctive relief against unlicensed assisted living facilities, and classifies operating without a license as a violation of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces.
The Department of Aging oversees long-term care advocacy and the protection of rights and welfare for older adults residing in care facilities across Maryland.
The Department of Human Services oversees adult protective services aimed at protecting vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

The bill establishes provisions allowing state entities to petition circuit courts for injunctive relief and modifies statutory factors in criminal felony prosecutions concerning unlicensed assisted living programs.

bill_summary: Prohibits selling or offering essential goods or services designated by the Governor at prices 15% or more above pre-emergency levels. Prohibits charging 15% or more above average prices for emergency cleanup repair or reconstruction services during and 90 days post-emergency. Permits price increases directly attributable to increased supplier costs, labor, materials, or documented three-year seasonal pricing. Establishes violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act civilly. Requires the Secretary of State to establish an electronic notification system for emergency declarations and covered goods. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide 20 days' advance notice before filing an enforcement action.
responsible_party: Secretary of State; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Consumers and businesses purchasing essential goods or services; merchants, retailers, and contractors selling essential goods, services, and emergency repair or reconstruction services during declared states of emergency
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 for the Secretary of State to implement the electronic notification system, followed by minimal ongoing annual licensing costs. The Office of the Attorney General can enforce the bill using existing resources. The bill has no material fiscal effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 775 statutorily requires the Secretary of State to establish and maintain an electronic notification system for individuals to register and receive notices regarding declared states of emergency, price gouging protections, and covered essential goods and services, with an estimated fiscal impact of $25,000 in FY 2024.

The bill designates price gouging as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division, and explicitly requires OAG to provide at least 20 days' pre-action notice to potential violators.

The bill's price protections are triggered by a state of emergency declared by the Governor and apply to specific categories of essential goods and services designated by the Governor via declaration or executive order.
The bill authorizes civil enforcement actions and private causes of action for damages under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which are adjudicated in the Maryland court system.

Permits a court to strike a foreclosure judgment and vest title in local government after 105 days of purchaser nonpayment. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies judicial procedures in tax sale foreclosure actions, requiring circuit courts to adjudicate motions to assign certificates of sale, issue show-cause orders to certificate holders, strike final judgments, and direct tax collectors regarding deed execution.

The bill relates to local government acquisition and demolition of vacant, unsafe, and blighted structures for redevelopment, which intersects with DHCD's community revitalization, blight elimination, and housing policies.

bill_summary: Establishes the Equitech Growth Fund and the Equitech Growth Commission within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Requires the corporation to award financial assistance to public, nonprofit, or private entities for workforce development and infrastructure. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $5,000,000 for fund awards from fiscal year 2025 through 2033. responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
stakeholders: Emerging and advanced industry businesses, workforce trainees, public and private entities, and institutions of higher education in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million in FY 2024 and by $5.6 million annually from FY 2025 through 2033 to provide $5.0 million in mandated award funding and $0.6 million for administrative expenses. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the fund increase correspondingly. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local entities, including community colleges, receive grants and provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the Equitech Growth Fund, adopting program regulations, awarding financial assistance, staffing the Equitech Growth Commission, and submitting annual reports.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Equitech Growth Commission, aligning with the department's role in statewide economic growth and business attraction.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Equitech Growth Commission to help guide workforce development initiatives targeted by the fund.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) serves as a member of the Equitech Growth Commission to advise on workforce pathways and education strategies for the innovation economy.
The Executive Director of MEDCO (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the Equitech Growth Commission to assist in strategic planning and infrastructure development.
The USM Chancellor (or designee) is a statutory member of the commission; USM institutions are also eligible recipients for financial assistance and workforce development awards from the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state commission, the Equitech Growth Commission, tasked with developing a 10-year strategic plan for growing Maryland's innovation economy.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Equitech Growth Commission, is mandated to include specific appropriations in the annual budget bill, and receives reports and strategic plans required by the bill.
DBM oversees the state budget execution, which includes the mandated general fund appropriation of $5.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2033 for the fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the newly created Equitech Growth Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Equitech Growth Fund.

Morgan State University is explicitly identified in the statute as one of the eligible HBCUs from which the Governor may appoint an institutional president to serve on the Commission, and is also an eligible recipient of fund awards.

fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. The bill has no material fiscal effect on Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission finances, as the commission can continue operating its existing minority business enterprise program within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill aligns the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission's (WSSC) Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) definition, standards, and criteria directly with the State's MBE program under Title 14, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which is monitored and coordinated by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs.

The Maryland Department of Transportation acts as the State's official MBE certification agency under § 14-303(b) of the State Finance and Procurement Article. Under the bill, WSSC's MBE program directly incorporates and recognizes MDOT's certifications and certification standards.

bill_summary: Authorizes Class B and specified Class C licensees in Prince George's County to sell beverages by the glass or bottle. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup to Study Best Practices for Safe Event Promotion and the Leveraging of Alcoholic Beverages Licenses in Prince George's County to study event promotion and local alcohol licensing practices and report findings to local and state officials.

The bill explicitly references written reports of violations forwarded by uniformed officers of the State Police as a basis for the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to inspect licensed premises and take appropriate action.

bill_summary: Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to establish a step therapy exception process. Mandates granting an exception request under specified clinical circumstances, including contraindication, expected ineffectiveness, or prior patient stability. Prohibits carriers and pharmacy benefits managers from requiring multiple prior authorizations for different dosages of the same drug. Excludes non-partial-agonist opioids from the single prior authorization restriction. Requires private review agents to decide electronic authorization requests in real time or within one business day.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Insured individuals and enrollees with prescription drug coverage; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; pharmacy benefits managers; health care prescribers; private review agents
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Indeterminate but potentially significant cost increase for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program due to reduced step therapy utilization. No material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers, nonprofit health service plans, HMOs, and private review agents in Maryland. It is responsible for reviewing policy and contract form filings for compliance with the bill's new step therapy and prior authorization requirements and collects associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The program provides prescription drug coverage through a pharmacy benefits manager (PBM) that is subject to the bill's mandates, potentially leading to significant fiscal impacts on state health benefit expenditures.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates the state's health insurance marketplace, where qualified health plans issued by commercial carriers must adhere to Maryland insurance laws, including step therapy and prior authorization protocols.

The Department of Health oversees public health policy and healthcare financing, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal note; however, Medicaid managed care organizations are explicitly exempt from the prior authorization provisions in § 15-854.

stakeholders: paid emergency medical technicians and participating governmental units, including counties and municipal corporations

Grants eligibility and creditable service for prior employment with the department upon joining the system. Terminates an officer's membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon transfer. Exempts transferring officers from paying member contribution rate differences under Title 37.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Frostburg City Police Department
stakeholders: Permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Frostburg City Police Department and the City of Frostburg
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Contingent on the City of Frostburg joining the system, local employer pension contributions increase by approximately $130,300 annually due to higher contribution rates net of an amortized new entrant credit. No impact on local revenues or other participating governmental units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). This bill directly governs the transfer of service credit, member accounts, and asset liabilities between EPS and LEOPS if the Frostburg City Police Department joins LEOPS as a participating governmental unit.

stakeholders: Transit riders, business communities, and transit labor union employees in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Howard County, as well as the Maryland Transit Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $431,300 in FY 2024 and by $575,000 annually thereafter to fund three planner positions at the Baltimore Metropolitan Council. Local governments can participate using existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission specifically to oversee, review, and comment on MTA transit operations, budgets, and plans in the Baltimore region. In addition, MTA is required to directly fund the commission's operational and staffing expenses via the Transportation Trust Fund.

MDOT is the parent department of MTA, and the Secretary of Transportation (or designee) serves as an ex officio member with tie-breaking voting authority. The commission also reviews Consolidated Transportation Program priorities and utilizes Transportation Trust Fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new regional transit oversight and advisory body, the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission, within state law.
The Governor is responsible for appointing seven members across four jurisdictions to the newly created commission and receives an annual report of the commission's findings and recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the seven gubernatorial seats on the newly established commission.

Defines net recovery after deducting attorney's fees, expenses, medical bills, and satisfaction of liens or subrogation claims. stakeholders: parents owed child support arrearages, individuals owing child support arrearages who receive workers' compensation benefits, and workers' compensation insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services oversees the Child Support Administration, which enforces child support orders and collects arrearages. This bill allows up to 25% of net recovery from workers' compensation indemnity benefits to be subject to execution for child support arrearages.

The bill alters statutory exemptions from execution on a judgment within the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, affecting garnishment and enforcement proceedings overseen by the Maryland court system.
The Commission adjudicates workers' compensation claims and oversees awards and settlements, which are directly subject to the execution for child support arrearages under this legislation.

Bars contracts if the institution receives commissions, bonuses, or incentive payments for securing student wagering participation. Prohibits institutions from contracting with sports marketing entities if either entity receives incentives for student wagering. Permits other contracts between institutions of higher education and regulated gaming entities or sports marketing entities. Subjects permitted contracts formed by public institutions of higher education to inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act. Protects existing obligations and contract rights from impairment under the Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Institutions of Higher Education
stakeholders: Maryland institutions of higher education, college students, regulated gaming entities, and sports marketing entities
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill does not affect gaming revenues or expenditures in the State and does not affect State funding of institutions of higher education.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restricts public institutions of higher education, including USM constituent universities, from entering into certain sports wagering contracts or promotional partnerships that incentivize student betting, and subjects permissible contracts to the Maryland Public Information Act.

As an independent public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is directly prohibited from entering into sports wagering incentive contracts and must make allowable contracts available under the Maryland Public Information Act.

As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the prohibition against entering into contracts with gaming or marketing entities that provide compensation based on student sports wagering participation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency licenses and regulates the mobile sports wagering licensees, sports wagering licensees, and online sports wagering operators defined and affected by the contracting prohibitions in this bill.

MHEC is the coordinating board responsible for postsecondary education policy and governance across Maryland's public, private nonprofit, and for-profit institutions of higher education, all of which fall under the scope of this legislation.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating body for public and private postsecondary institutions, the commission oversees policy compliance for institutions impacted by the prohibition on sports wagering contracts.

bill_summary: Alters the calculation and remittance process for administrative fees paid to the State Retirement and Pension System. Defines administrative fees as actual operating expenses incurred as of June 30 of the second prior fiscal year. Requires the Board of Trustees to certify the payable amount to each local employer by October 1. Directs local employers to pay 25 percent of the certified amount across four quarterly dates each year. Requires reimbursement of administrative fees to system accumulation funds on or before June 30 each year.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Participating employers in the State Retirement and Pension System, including State agencies, local school boards, community colleges, and participating governmental units
fiscal_impact_summary: Largely procedural in nature with no material effect on State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the funding of administrative and operational expenses for the State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System, altering the timing and formula used to calculate and collect administrative fees.

The Board of Trustees must certify membership percentages and provide official notice of local employer fee estimates and certifications to the Secretary of Budget and Management for state budget integration.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to execute the right of setoff against funds owed to local participating employers if they become delinquent in remitting their required administrative fees to the retirement system.

The bill mandates that the Governor include in the annual budget bill an appropriation to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System equal to the authorized administrative fees.

Synopsis: Altering the amortization periods to be used for certain unfunded liabilities or surpluses of the State Retirement and Pension System.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Amortization of Unfunded Liabilities and Surpluses
bill_summary: Alters amortization periods for certain unfunded liabilities and surpluses of the State Retirement and Pension System. Continues amortizing existing liabilities or surpluses accrued as of June 30, 2023, until June 30, 2039. Amortizes annual experience gains and losses over 15 years and actuarial assumption changes over 25 years. Amortizes new legislation effects over 10 to 15 years and early retirement incentives over five years. Authorizes the Board of Trustees to adjust amortization periods to mitigate tail volatility in contribution rates. Prohibits the Board from certifying contribution rates below the actuary-determined normal cost.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members, retirees, and participating employers of the State Retirement and Pension System, and Maryland State government employees
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State pension liabilities beginning in fiscal 2024, but not expected to have a discernible effect on State pension contributions. No effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly modifies how the SRPS Board of Trustees calculates amortization periods for unfunded liabilities and surpluses, sets contribution rates, and works with the system's actuary.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state budget, fiscal planning, and state employee benefits. Adjustments to the amortization schedule and contribution rate volatility for the State Retirement and Pension System impact long-term state pension funding obligations within the executive budget.

bill_summary: Authorizes an autonomous vehicle converter to sell, transfer, lease, offer for sale, or resell a converted autonomous vehicle. Restricts these authorizations solely to motor vehicles intended for commercial or industrial use. Excludes autonomous vehicle converters from statutory definitions of vehicle dealers, distributors, factory branches, and manufacturers. responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: autonomous vehicle converters and commercial or industrial motor vehicle operators
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and does not directly affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) regulates automotive businesses, including motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches under Title 15 of the Transportation Article. HB 806 explicitly excludes autonomous vehicle converters from these licensing categories and permits them to sell, lease, and transfer converted autonomous vehicles without obtaining dealer or manufacturer licenses from the MVA.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and houses the Motor Vehicle Administration, which administers vehicle laws under the Transportation Article amended by this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a judge from requiring a person to give certain testimony or a statement or to produce evidence for a case involving an alleged violation of the criminal law of another state relating to health care that is legally protected in the State; prohibiting a judge from issuing an ex parte order to intercept certain communication for the purpose of investigating or recovering evidence related to legally protected health care, subject to a certain exception; etc.
Title: Reproductive Health Protection Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Protects individuals and health care practitioners from out-of-state legal actions and investigations relating to legally protected health care. Prohibits judges from compelling witness testimony or evidence and issuing wiretap orders for out-of-state investigations of lawful reproductive care. Bars the Governor from surrendering individuals under out-of-state extradition demands for lawful reproductive health care activities. Forbids State and local agencies from expending resources or assisting interstate investigations into legally protected health care. Prohibits health occupations boards and medical liability insurers from taking disciplinary or adverse actions against practitioners providing protected care. Exempts high-deductible health plans from abortion coverage mandates if excluded from federal preventive care safe harbor rules.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Health Occupations Boards; Maryland Insurance Administration; Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Health care practitioners providing reproductive health services, patients receiving reproductive health care, medical professional liability insurers, State and local government employees, and individuals facing out-of-state investigations regarding reproductive health care.
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The Department of Legislative Services determined that the bill's provisions are procedural in nature and will not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly restricts the Governor's authority under the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act, prohibiting the surrender of any individual demanded by another state if the alleged violation relates to providing, procuring, or aiding in legally protected reproductive health care that is lawful in Maryland.

The bill establishes statutory restrictions and procedures for Maryland courts, prohibiting judges from compelling witness attendance in out-of-state prosecutions, barring ex parte wiretap orders for reproductive health investigations, requiring sworn statements for foreign subpoenas, and restricting the filing of foreign judgments.

The bill directly prohibits health occupations boards (which operate under and in coordination with the Department of Health) from revoking, suspending, or taking adverse disciplinary actions against licensed health care practitioners for providing legally protected reproductive health care.

The bill tasks the Insurance Commissioner with making determinations regarding high-deductible plan safe harbor exemptions under the Internal Revenue Code and prohibits medical professional liability insurers from taking adverse actions against health care practitioners providing legally protected health care.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and personnel administration, directly aligning with the bill's enactment of § 2-312 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article prohibiting State employees and agencies from expending time, money, or resources on interstate investigations of legally protected health care.

The Secretary of State processes extraditions on behalf of the Governor, an administrative function directly affected by the bill's prohibition on extraditing individuals facing out-of-state charges relating to legally protected health care.

The bill limits the Attorney General's ability to seek ex parte wiretap and electronic surveillance orders relating to legally protected health care and involves legal defense guidance for state agencies regarding interstate subpoenas and investigations.

The bill specifically limits the State Prosecutor's authority to apply for ex parte wiretap and electronic communication interception orders when investigating matters related to legally protected health care.

Synopsis: Altering to July 1, 2025, the termination date for certain provisions of law governing the Minority Business Enterprise Program and its application to offshore wind projects and video lottery terminals; and altering the date by which certain reports, studies, and guidelines must be submitted.
Title: State Procurement – Minority Business Enterprise Program – Extension and Reports

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Minority Business Enterprise Program to July 1, 2025. Continues Minority Business Enterprise participation requirements for offshore wind projects and video lottery terminal operations through July 1, 2025. Postpones the submission deadline for the comprehensive disparity study and related analyses to late 2024. Extends the deadline for establishing capital project minority business enterprise policies and guidelines to July 1, 2025. Requires reports on brokerage and investment management services and capital project subgoals by December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Maryland Department of Transportation; Board of Public Works; Office of the Attorney General; Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Certified minority business enterprises; State procurement prime contractors and subcontractors; offshore wind project applicants; video lottery facility applicants and licensees
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances. Extending due dates for the disparity study, related analyses, and program termination dates does not affect the total cost of the studies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is directly responsible for administering the MBE program, establishing implementation guidelines, and completing multiple required reports and studies regarding MBE subgoals, disparity analyses, and race/gender-neutral approaches.

MDOT serves as the State's official MBE certification agency and is required to conduct and submit the disparity study and related analyses for offshore wind projects and P3s under the extended deadlines.

The bill mandates that the MBE certification agency and GOSBA consult with the Attorney General when analyzing disparity studies, establishing implementation policies and guidelines, and evaluating constitutional compliance.
The Board designates the state certification agency, adopts regulations regarding data collection for disparity studies, and oversees MBE goal requirements for public-private partnerships.
The bill extends the statutory termination date for MBE participation requirements and progress reporting associated with offshore wind energy projects approved by the PSC.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters and extends the termination date for statutory MBE participation goals applied to video lottery terminal licensees and facility operations.
As the State's central procurement authority, DGS is directly impacted by the one-year extension of the statutory MBE program across state contracts.

The bill extends the reporting deadline for the study evaluating MBE participation and race/gender-neutral approaches in brokerage and investment management services used by the State Retirement and Pension System.

Synopsis: Requiring a hospital to include testing for fentanyl as part of a urine drug screening; and requiring the hospital, if a urine drug screening detects fentanyl, to report the deidentified test results  to the Maryland Department of Health through the State-designated health information exchange.
Title: Hospitals - Testing for Fentanyl (The Josh Siems Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Controlled Dangerous Substances -see also- Drugs; Subst Abus
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Requires hospitals to include fentanyl testing whenever conducting a diagnostic urine drug screening on an individual. Mandates that hospitals report deidentified positive fentanyl test results to the Maryland Department of Health. Directs hospitals to submit these reports through the State-designated health information exchange. Exempts any hospital that does not have chemical analyzer equipment. Preserves existing statutory civil and criminal immunity for individuals seeking or receiving emergency medical assistance. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, hospital patients undergoing diagnostic urine drug screening, and individuals experiencing or reporting drug overdoses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires hospitals that detect fentanyl during urine drug screenings to report deidentified test results to the Maryland Department of Health through the State-designated health information exchange.

The Commission oversees and designated the Chesapeake Regional Information System for Our Patients (CRISP) as Maryland's State-designated health information exchange, which is the platform mandated by the bill for reporting positive fentanyl test results.

Synopsis: Regulating the disclosure of certain information related to legally protected health care by custodians of public records, health information exchanges, and electronic health networks; requiring that the regulations adopted by the Maryland Health Care Commission regarding clinical information to be exchanged through the State-designated exchange restrict data of patients who have obtained legally protected health care; establishing the Protected Health Care Commission; etc.
Title: Health - Reproductive Health Services - Protected Information and Insurance Requirements

Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: Prohibits health information exchanges and electronic health networks from disclosing mifepristone data and sensitive health service codes without authorization. Restricts disclosures of abortion care records except for claims adjudication or with specific written patient consent. Establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to recommend sensitive health services designated as legally protected health care. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to adopt regulations shielding patient data related to legally protected health care. Shields identifying information of ambulatory surgical and abortion facilities and investigated licensees under the Public Information Act. Clarifies that health insurers providing labor and delivery coverage must cover abortion care services without cost-sharing.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Secretary of Health; Protected Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Patients seeking abortion and reproductive health services, licensed health care providers, health information exchanges, electronic health networks, and health insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2024 only for contractual services to develop confidentiality policies and standards. General fund fine revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 812 directly expands the purpose of MHCC to establish policies and standards protecting the confidentiality of legally protected health care information. MHCC is required to adopt emergency regulations restricting data exchange through health information exchanges and electronic health networks, and to submit quarterly implementation reports to legislative committees. The fiscal note also identifies a $100,000 expenditure in FY 2024 for MHCC contractual services.

The Secretary of Health is tasked with identifying and regulating procedure, diagnosis, medication, and related codes for legally protected health care, adopting emergency regulations, and responding to semiannual reports. In addition, the Department of Health is required to provide staff for the newly created Protected Health Care Commission.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-857 to clarify requirements for health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs offering labor and delivery coverage to cover abortion care services without cost-sharing notwithstanding grandfathered plan exceptions, subject to exemptions granted by the Insurance Commissioner.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to advise and issue semiannual recommendations to the Secretary of Health regarding sensitive health services that should be classified as legally protected health care.
The Attorney General (or their designee) is designated as an ex officio statutory member of the newly established Protected Health Care Commission.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date of certain provisions of law that establish and govern the funding for the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program; and requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Administration, to conduct a study on available federal and State subsidies and report its findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2024.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Extends the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program through June 30, 2026. Authorizes the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to designate funds providing up to $20,000,000 in annual subsidies. Requires the Exchange to establish subsidy eligibility and payment parameters for calendar years 2022 through 2025. Requires the Exchange, in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Administration, to study available subsidies and waiver options. Requires the Exchange to report its study findings and recommendations to legislative committees by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Young adults in Maryland purchasing individual market health benefit plans
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund special fund expenditures increase by up to $10.0 million in FY 2024, up to $20.0 million in FY 2025, and up to $10.0 million in FY 2026 to fund subsidies. General fund revenues decrease only to the extent that unspent premium tax reversions are reduced. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary agency responsible for administering the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program. The bill extends the program's sunset date through FY 2026, authorizes up to $20 million annually in subsidies from the MHBE Fund, requires data tracking, and mandates that MHBE conduct a study and report on subsidy availability and the State's 1332 waiver.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Administration are statutorily consulted by MHBE in establishing subsidy eligibility and payment parameters, as well as in conducting the mandated study and report regarding federal and State health insurance subsidies and the 1332 waiver.

Synopsis: Requiring insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for certain lung cancer diagnostic imaging and limiting the copayment, coinsurance, or deductible that the entities can require for lung cancer screening and diagnosis; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an assessment on certain outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening and report the results to the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Cancer Screening - Health Insurance and Assessment of Outreach, Education, and Health Disparities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: Requires health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover recommended follow-up diagnostic imaging for lung cancer. Mandates coverage of diagnostic ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and image-guided biopsy. Limits cost-sharing for lung cancer screening and diagnosis to amounts no greater than those for breast cancer screening. Permits high-deductible health plans to subject follow-up diagnostic lung imaging to plan deductibles. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to assess cancer screening outreach, education, and health disparities. Requires the department to establish an advisory stakeholder workgroup and report findings by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, individuals recommended for lung cancer screening, and communities affected by cancer health disparities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,900 in fiscal 2024 only for contractual staff at the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the assessment and convene the workgroup. Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration from form filing fees. Potential increase in local government expenditures to the extent insurance premiums rise for fully insured employee plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that MDH conduct an assessment on outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening, convene a stakeholder workgroup to provide recommendations, and report findings to the General Assembly, requiring additional general fund expenditures in FY 2024.

MIA regulates the commercial health insurance market in Maryland and is responsible for overseeing compliance with the new coverage mandates and cost-sharing limits for lung cancer screening, as well as reviewing policy form filings.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which may experience an indeterminate fiscal impact from the mandated coverage of follow-up lung cancer diagnostic imaging.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a cancer screening stakeholder workgroup convened by MDH to advise on cancer screening disparities and develop outreach recommendations.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard to evaluate units of State government on the units' performance toward meeting certain participation goals under the Minority Business Enterprise Program and the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise Program; establishing a certain grading scale for the scorecard; and requiring grades achieved by each unit to be published each year on the Office's website.
Title: Procurement - Minority Business Enterprises and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises - Participation Goal Scorecard

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Requires the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard evaluating State government units. Directs the scorecard to evaluate unit performance toward meeting statewide Minority Business Enterprise and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise goals. Requires the Office to develop a grading scale as a weighted system reflecting each unit's contribution toward the goals. Mandates annual publication of each unit's achieved grades on the Office's website. Requires the Office to submit the published information to the General Assembly within 30 days of website publication.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
stakeholders: State procurement agencies and units of State government, certified Minority Business Enterprises, and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises.
fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no net impact on state expenditures or revenues. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard and weighted grading scale evaluating State agencies on their MBE and VSBE participation goals, publish the grades annually on its website, and submit the results to the General Assembly.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch operations, and the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs is a coordinating office within the Executive Department responsible for statewide procurement equity initiatives.

Synopsis: Requiring the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent issues of the Maryland Register available to the public for online searching; altering the requirements for a unit of State government to submit certain proposed or emergency regulations, work plans, and evaluation reports to the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review, the Department of Legislative Services, and the Administrator of the Division of State Documents; etc.
Title: State Government - Regulation Procedures and the Maryland Register

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent Maryland Register issues searchable online. Directs promulgating units altering proposed regulations before publication to notify reviewing entities and follow specified withdrawal or certification procedures. Extends the review period after an administrative hold override notice from 30 days to 60 days. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to adopt procedures for submitting proposed regulations, emergency regulations, work plans, and evaluation reports. Mandates that the Administrator develop and maintain a comprehensive electronic filing and tracking system by October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Division of State Documents; Department of Legislative Services; Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review
stakeholders: State agencies and units promulgating regulations; subscribers to the Maryland Register; members of the public seeking regulatory information
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $124,200 in FY 2024 and $122,700 in FY 2025 for DSD contractual staff and operating support, with ongoing general fund spending of $39,000 annually. Special fund revenues and expenditures decrease by $29,300 in FY 2024 and $39,000 annually thereafter due to reduced Maryland Register subscriptions. Electronic filing system modifications could also create significant additional costs. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of State Documents (DSD), which is administratively housed within the Office of the Secretary of State, is directly responsible for administering the bill's provisions. DSD must make recent issues of the Maryland Register freely searchable online, develop and maintain a new electronic filing system (ELF 2.0) for regulations, and handle revised submission workflows, resulting in direct fiscal impacts from lost subscription revenues and additional operational expenditures.

The bill and fiscal analysis directly involve DoIT in consulting and collaborating with the Division of State Documents on the development, functionality, server hosting, and security of the electronic filing system (ELF 2.0) used by state units to submit and track regulations.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for a violation of the prohibition on wearing, carrying, or transporting a handgun; requiring the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy to annually report certain information to the Governor and General Assembly; requiring the Department of State Police to transmit a certain summary of certain laws relating to firearms to certain persons; requiring the Secretary of State Police, in consultation with the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Health, to develop a certain curriculum; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Regulated Firearms - Possession and Permits to Carry, Wear, and Transport a Handgun

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc

Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Alters qualifications, disqualifiers, and application fees for possessing regulated firearms and obtaining handgun carry permits. Increases the maximum incarceration penalty from 3 to 5 years for first-time handgun carry violations. Raises the minimum age to obtain a handgun permit to 21 years old, with military exceptions. Increases maximum permit fees to $125 for initial applications and $75 for renewals. Requires the Secretary of State Police to regularly review active permit holders and revoke noncompliant permits. Directs the Department of State Police to email summaries of statutory firearms changes to firearm registrants.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy; Office of Administrative Hearings; Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: handgun wear, carry, and transport permit applicants and holders; regulated firearm owners; State-certified firearms instructors; individuals convicted of specified criminal violations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by an estimated $5,294,200 in FY 2024 from increased permit application and renewal fees. General fund expenditures increase by at least $2,402,200 in FY 2024 to support 26 positions at the Department of State Police and one position at the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy. Incarceration costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and local detention centers increase minimally due to longer sentences.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of State Police is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. The bill alters permit qualifications, fee structures, revocation procedures, and mandates regular review of active permit holders, curriculum development, email notifications, and annual reporting.

OAH is statutorily designated to conduct de novo administrative hearings for individuals appealing handgun permit denials, renewals, revocations, or limitations, issue written findings of fact and decisions within 90 days, and submit annual statistical reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS maintains the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository required to be regularly reviewed for active permit holder qualifications, and its correctional facilities may experience a fiscal impact due to increased maximum incarceration penalties for certain firearm violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy (MSCCSP) is explicitly mandated by the bill to produce an annual report disaggregated by jurisdiction, race, and gender on charges, convictions, and sentences, requiring an additional researcher position and ongoing operational funds.
OAG is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of State Police in the development, publication, update, and distribution of the classroom curriculum for firearms training courses.
MDH is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of State Police in developing training curriculum topics, specifically suicide prevention, conflict de-escalation, and anger management.

The Maryland Judiciary is affected by judicial appeals arising from OAH decisions regarding handgun permits and the adjudication and sentencing of expanded firearm possession prohibitions and increased penalties.
The Governor is designated as a recipient of mandatory annual reports from the Maryland State Police, the Office of Administrative Hearings, and the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy.

Synopsis: Granting the Town of Forest Heights in Prince George's County the authority to exercise urban renewal powers in areas zoned for commercial use for blight clearance and redevelopment under Article III, Section 61 of the Maryland Constitution; and authorizing the municipality to levy certain taxes and issue general obligation bonds and revenue bonds to carry out urban renewal powers.
Title: Town of Forest Heights (Prince George's County) - Urban Renewal Authority for Blight Clearance PG 410-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Grants the Town of Forest Heights urban renewal powers for blight clearance in areas zoned for commercial use. Requires the municipal legislative body to adopt a resolution defining the blighted area before initiating any project. Authorizes the municipality to acquire property through eminent domain with just compensation and transfer property to private persons. Authorizes the town to levy taxes, make appropriations, and issue general obligation bonds and revenue bonds. Permits the town to establish a separate public body or agency to carry out urban renewal activities.
responsible_party: Town of Forest Heights
stakeholders: Commercial property owners, businesses, and redevelopers in blighted commercial areas in the Town of Forest Heights
fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues may experience a minimal increase with no effect on expenditures. Town of Forest Heights expenditures may increase for land acquisition, legal fees, and urban renewal projects, potentially offset by revenues from property sales and expanded municipal and county tax bases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is responsible for community revitalization and redevelopment initiatives across Maryland communities. While the bill directly grants urban renewal and blight clearance authority to the Town of Forest Heights, DHCD coordinates and supports local revitalization efforts and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

MDP provides technical assistance, data analysis, and guidance to local governments regarding comprehensive land use planning and sustainable redevelopment. The bill requires urban renewal plans to conform substantially to municipal master planning, and MDP served as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority in Prince George's County to support and develop a certain neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with certain residents; and requiring the Authority to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly on or before October 31, 2025.
Title: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority - Established
