Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority in Prince George's County. Requires the Authority to support the development and approval of a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan for six target municipalities. Authorizes the Authority to manage appropriated funds from target municipalities, Prince George's County, and the State. Authorizes the Authority to receive donated consultant services and manage staff and consultants. Requires the Authority to report its revitalization strategy to the Governor and designated legislative committees by October 31, 2025. Abrogates the Act after September 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and local governments in the Prince George's County target area, including the City of Mount Rainier, Town of Brentwood, Town of Cottage City, City of Bladensburg, Town of Colmar Manor, and Town of North Brentwood.
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State or local fiscal effect. State and local authority members are assumed to provide staffing and expense reimbursements within existing resources. The bill authorizes the Authority to manage appropriated funds from the State, Prince George's County, and municipalities, but does not mandate any appropriations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the newly established Prince George's Gateway Development Authority under the Economic Development Article.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as an ex-officio member of the Authority, which is tasked with creating a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization and housing plan.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, a temporary statutory authority charged with formulating a neighborhood revitalization strategy and reporting to state leadership before sunsetting in 2028.
The Authority is statutorily required to submit its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report to the Governor on or before October 31, 2025.

Synopsis: Establishing and altering certain requirements related to the installation of equipment for the charging of electric vehicles during the construction of certain housing units; clarifying that a county or municipal corporation may require a greater number of electric vehicle parking spaces; requiring the Maryland Energy Administration to study certain issues related to the installation of electric vehicle parking spaces at multifamily residential buildings and submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2023; etc.
Title: Residential Construction - Electric Vehicle Charging

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires new residential construction of single-family detached houses, duplexes, and townhouses to include electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Mandates that each new unit with a garage, carport, or driveway feature one EVSE-installed or EV-ready parking space. Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to require a greater number of electric vehicle parking spaces. Directs the Maryland Energy Administration to study the costs of electric vehicle parking at multifamily residential buildings. Requires the Administration, in consultation with the Department of the Environment, to report findings by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Residential home builders, purchasers of newly constructed single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by up to $250,000 in FY 2024 only for the Maryland Energy Administration to hire a consultant for the required multifamily building study. State revenues are unaffected. Local governments can enforce the requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is tasked with conducting a comprehensive study on the costs, emissions impacts, and payment mechanisms associated with electric vehicle charging infrastructure at multifamily residential buildings, with a dedicated special fund expenditure of up to $250,000 to complete the required analysis and report.

MDE is statutorily required to consult with the Maryland Energy Administration on the required study to project the number of electric vehicles on Maryland roads from 2024 through 2050 under the Advanced Clean Cars II standards.

The Governor is a required recipient of the final study and policy recommendations regarding multifamily residential electric vehicle charging infrastructure submitted by the Maryland Energy Administration.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to expand the EV Pilot Program to allow participating electric companies to install EV charging stations in multifamily dwellings in underserved communities; requiring the Commission to terminate the expansion of the EV Pilot Program on December 31, 2025; requiring an electric company operating an EV charging network to ensure the EV charging stations in the EV charging network maintain certain uptime standards, subject to certain exceptions; etc.
Title: Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure - Requirements (Electric Vehicle Charging Reliability Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Directs the Public Service Commission to expand the EV Pilot Program to new and existing multifamily dwellings in underserved communities. Requires the Commission to terminate this expansion on December 31, 2025. Requires electric companies operating public charging networks to maintain federal or Commission-approved uptime standards. Requires participating electric companies to maintain adequate staff to monitor, assess, and repair charging stations. Mandates quarterly submission of detailed charging station operational, uptime, and cost data to the Commission. Authorizes the Commission to impose civil penalties or take remedial action for uptime noncompliance.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: electric companies operating public EV charging networks, electric vehicle owners, and residents of multifamily dwellings in underserved communities
fiscal_impact_summary: No material direct impact on state or local finances; the Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Electricity rates paid by all electric customers, including state and local governments, may experience a limited increase through utility cost recovery.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 834 directly mandates the Public Service Commission (PSC) to expand and oversee the EV Pilot Program for multifamily dwellings in underserved communities, establish and monitor charging station uptime and reporting requirements, evaluate utility compliance, and assess civil penalties or remedial actions for noncompliance.

The bill impacts utility rate recovery, service reliability, and electric vehicle charging program parameters before the Public Service Commission. The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential consumers in PSC proceedings concerning utility service quality, reliability, and the rate impacts associated with utility capital expenditures and pilot program costs.

Synopsis: Establishing the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study approaches to water and wastewater governance in the Baltimore region; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Mayor of Baltimore City, the County Executive of Baltimore County, the Governor, and the General Assembly on or before January 30, 2024.
Title: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force

bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study approaches to regional water and wastewater governance. Directs the task force to review prior utility business studies and evaluate alternative regional governance and financing models. Requires the task force to analyze fiscal implications, efficiencies, transition costs, and customer rate stability for each model. Mandates consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Environmental Service. Requires the task force to report its findings and legislative recommendations by January 30, 2024.
responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force; Mayor of Baltimore City; County Executive of Baltimore County; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Environmental Service
stakeholders: Water and wastewater customers, ratepayers, and local governments in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, and Howard County
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal local expenditure impact for Baltimore City and Baltimore County to provide task force staffing and member expense reimbursements, absorbable within existing resources. State consultation costs for the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Environmental Service are absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force as a temporary public body to study, assess, and make recommendations on water and wastewater governance models in the Baltimore region.
The bill statutorily requires the Task Force to consult with the Department of the Environment in developing its recommendations and final report concerning regional water and wastewater systems.
The bill statutorily requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Environmental Service in developing its recommendations and final report regarding water supply and wastewater governance.
The Governor is tasked with appointing two members to the Task Force and will receive the Task Force's final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the appointment of the two Task Force members designated to be appointed by the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish and maintain a website that provides certain information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals living in a common ownership community.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish and maintain a common ownership community website. Directs the website to provide information on the current rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities. Requires the website to include a hyperlink to each local common ownership community program in Maryland. Mandates the annual posting of information and General Assembly website hyperlinks for relevant statewide legislation enacted in the prior session. Requires the department to post this legislative update on or before June 1 each year.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents and unit owners of condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations, as well as local common ownership community programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 in FY 2024 to develop the website, with indeterminate annual increases in subsequent years for maintenance and updates. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 844 directly requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish, host, and annually maintain a website providing information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities (COCs), resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $90,000 in FY 2024 and ongoing maintenance costs.

bill_summary: Establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment. Authorizes the department to issue permits regulating reclaimed water use as a source for drinking water facilities. Requires the department to accept permit applications from July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024. Mandates advanced treatment including reverse osmosis, ultraviolet disinfection, and storage in an environmental buffer for at least 180 days. Authorizes the department to renew qualifying potable reuse permits on or after July 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: public water systems, drinking water treatment facilities, local governments operating water utilities, and water treatment engineering contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2023 and $139,900 in FY 2024 to hire two contractual regulatory and compliance engineers at the Maryland Department of the Environment, with ongoing costs through FY 2028. State revenues are unaffected because there is no permit fee. Participating local governments incur potential indeterminate cost increases to construct, upgrade, and operate treatment facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program within MDE. MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing standards, reviewing and issuing potable reuse permits, conducting inspections, adopting regulations, and submitting a report on the program.

MDH's Laboratories Administration provides analytical support and water testing services for MDE, and the fiscal note notes potential workload and staffing impacts related to complex testing for PFAS and other contaminants under the pilot program.
The bill requires the Department of the Environment to submit a report to the Governor by December 31, 2024, regarding the status and recommendations for the pilot program.

Synopsis: Altering, from 60 days to 180 days, the time period after a medical examiner files findings and conclusions resulting from an autopsy during which a person in interest may request the medical examiner to correct findings and conclusions on the cause and manner of death recorded on a certificate of death.
Title: Public Health - Chief Medical Examiner - Corrections to Autopsy Findings and Conclusions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Extends the timeframe for a person in interest to request corrections to autopsy findings and conclusions. Increases the filing window from 60 days to 180 days after the medical examiner files the report. Covers findings and conclusions regarding the cause and manner of death on a death certificate. Excludes autopsy findings that result in a determination of homicide. Maintains the right of a person in interest to appeal any denial to the Secretary of Health.
responsible_party: Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; Maryland Department of Health; Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Persons in interest of a deceased individual (such as spouses, adult children, parents, adult siblings, grandparents, or legal guardians)
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Health and the Office of Administrative Hearings can absorb any minor increase in requests and hearings using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner is a unit within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). The bill directly modifies the timeline for persons of interest to request corrections to autopsy findings and conclusions from MDH's medical examiners and affects appeals directed to the Secretary of Health.

When the Chief Medical Examiner denies a request to correct cause and manner of death findings, appeals are referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings for a contested case hearing before an administrative law judge.
Decisions by the Secretary of Health that reject an administrative law judge's findings can be appealed to the circuit courts, which are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Requiring the Division of Rehabilitation Services in the State Department of Education and the Developmental Disabilities Administration in the Maryland Department of Health to enter into a memorandum of understanding, the terms of which shall include a data sharing agreement for the medical and psychological records of mutual clients in order to expedite decisions regarding eligibility for services.
Title: Division of Rehabilitation Services and Developmental Disabilities Administration - Memorandum of Understanding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Division of Rehabilitation Services and the Developmental Disabilities Administration to enter into a memorandum of understanding. Mandates that the agreement include data sharing of medical and psychological records for mutual clients. Specifies that the data sharing agreement must expedite decisions regarding eligibility for services. Defines covered records to include medical documentation, psychological information, school documentation, and other relevant information. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Division of Rehabilitation Services; Developmental Disabilities Administration
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities and developmental disabilities who are mutual clients of the Division of Rehabilitation Services and the Developmental Disabilities Administration
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the data sharing memorandum of understanding using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), a division within the Maryland State Department of Education, enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Developmental Disabilities Administration to share medical and psychological data of mutual clients.

The bill directly mandates that the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), a unit within the Maryland Department of Health, enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Division of Rehabilitation Services to share client records to expedite eligibility determinations.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission to contract for utility services to certain Prince George's County border properties. Permits the District of Columbia or the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority to provide water and sewer services. Requires contracts to allocate maintenance costs, assign billing duties, and mandate master meters for multifamily housing units. Establishes usage-based service rate setting procedures and mandates specific customer notices, including potential higher service rates. Limits the ability of the Commission and the District entities to reduce customer services. Terminates all provisions five years after the enactment date.
responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
stakeholders: Owners, developers, and residents of qualifying border properties in Prince George's County; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission; District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. The bill does not materially affect Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT was consulted as an information source during the legislative review process, as the legislation specifically targets transit-oriented border properties located within one-half mile of mass transit rail stations and regional transit districts.

The bill explicitly references the requirement to assess fees under the Environment Article, specifically the Bay Restoration Fee administered by MDE, for customer accounts served under the cross-border water and sewer contracts.

bill_summary: Establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General. Charges the unit with investigating and prosecuting violations of State criminal environmental and natural resources laws. Authorizes the unit to prosecute any other criminal offense discovered during an investigation. Grants the unit the full powers, rights, privileges, and duties of a State's Attorney. Authorizes designated attorneys to issue subpoenas for specific records to further criminal investigations. Requires the Attorney General to report annually by November 30 on the unit's activities.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Persons subject to investigation or prosecution for State criminal environmental and natural resources violations, and small businesses in resource-based industries.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $566,200 in FY 2024 to fund four new positions, start-up costs, and operating expenses, rising to $796,000 by FY 2028. State general and special fund revenues, as well as local revenues, may increase beginning in FY 2024 from criminal penalties and restitution, but the exact increase is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General to investigate and prosecute criminal violations of environmental and natural resources laws.

The new unit is tasked with prosecuting violations of State criminal environmental laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the unit.

The unit investigates and prosecutes violations of criminal natural resources laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings and recommendations of the unit.

The bill requires the Attorney General to cooperate with the Secretary of Budget and Management to establish minimum salaries, qualifications, and training and experience standards for positions within the unit.
The unit is granted authority to issue subpoenas enforceable in State circuit courts and to exercise grand jury powers across counties.
The Attorney General is mandated to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the unit's activities and any agency actions taken in response to its findings.

Synopsis: Authorizing Baltimore City to honor certificates of guarantee that are issued by certain associations or on behalf of certain contractors in order to satisfy certain county bond requirements; and providing that Baltimore City is not required under certain provisions of law to honor certain certificates of guarantee.

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City to honor certificates of guarantee issued by approved nonprofit contractor associations or their wholly owned subsidiaries. Permits contractors to use these certificates to satisfy county bond requirements for public improvements and other purposes. Clarifies that Baltimore City is not required under state insurance law to honor the certificates. Exempts these certificates of guarantee from the state Insurance Article. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Baltimore City; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Contractors bidding on or performing public improvements and construction in Baltimore City, nonprofit associations of contractors and their subsidiaries, and Baltimore City government
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce the provisions with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City finances are not affected because the authority to honor certificates of guarantee is permissive.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee. While these instruments are exempt from general insurance regulation, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees the Insurance Article and can implement or enforce the provision within existing budgeted resources.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the defined term "related event" as it applies to a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City includes events for which tickets are sold in advance or at the door or cover charges are imposed; reducing the number of days within which a person must apply for a permit, the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City must take certain actions relating to the permit, and alterations may be made to the permit; and altering the standards for determining the permit fee.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Related Event Promoter's Permit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Alters requirements governing related event promoter's permits for Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association Tournament events in Baltimore City. Expands the definition of related events to include events selling tickets at the door or imposing cover charges. Reduces the permit application deadline from 90 days to 30 days before a scheduled event. Requires the Board of License Commissioners to act on permit applications within 7 days instead of 14 days. Bases permit fee tiers on location capacity determined by the Baltimore City Fire Marshal rather than anticipated attendance. Extends the termination date of the permit program by two years to June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Baltimore City Fire Department, Fire Marshal; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, Executive Director
stakeholders: Related event promoters, participating alcoholic beverages license holders, and attendees of CIAA Basketball Tournament social events in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates the Alcoholic Beverages Article by striking an obsolete reference to the Comptroller's enforcement authority regarding State caterer's license violations and replacing it with the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area of the 40th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City to the holder of a Class C beer and light wine license under certain circumstances; prohibiting certain license holders in certain areas of the 40th alcoholic beverages district from selling alcoholic beverages at certain times of day; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - 40th District - Alcoholic Beverages
bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue specific alcoholic beverages licenses in the 40th district. Permits issuing a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 3600 block of Hickory Avenue. Authorizes a Class A-7 license in the 1200 block of West North Avenue under specified conditions. Exempts this Class A-7 license from the distance restriction near a place of worship or school. Prohibits sales before 10 a.m. or after 10 p.m. between the 1000 and 3200 blocks of West North Avenue.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Baltimore City's 40th legislative district, Penn North Community Association, and local consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license application and renewal fees to the extent new licenses are issued. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically authorizes local licensing actions administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverage regulation in Maryland.

Synopsis: Requiring the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission to obtain the approval from the Commissioners of St. Mary's County before submitting a loan application where the Commission seeks to incur debt upon the full faith and credit of the county; requiring the Commission to cause studies, plans, and estimates to be made for new facilities in certain portions of the county; requiring any excess revenue made by the Commission in the sale or transfer of certain debt to be exempt from taxation; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the St. Mary’s County Metropolitan Commission to obtain county approval before submitting loan applications backed by county credit. Exempts refinancing or refunding transactions with no additional debt liability from the county approval requirement. Mandates studies, public notices, and hearings for new water and sewerage facilities in the county. Authorizes the commission to pay in full or in part for moving structures that impede water or sewer projects. Exempts excess revenue from debt sales or transfers by the commission from state and local taxation.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission; Commissioners of St. Mary's County
stakeholders: Property owners, residents, and public service corporations in St. Mary's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect St. Mary's County operations or finances, as the provisions primarily codify and streamline existing procedural practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 887 pertains to the expansion, extension, and financing of local public water supply and sewerage systems governed by the St. Mary's County Comprehensive Water and Sewerage Plan. While the bill strictly alters St. Mary's County public local laws with no state fiscal effect, MDE oversees statewide water and sewerage planning and regulations and served as an information source on the bill.

Synopsis: Altering the application requirements for the homeowners' tax credit to allow homeowners with certain types of income to file an application every 3 years, subject to a certain certification requirement; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Homeowners' Property Tax Credit - Qualified Homeowner - Application and Certification Requirements
bill_summary: Alters application requirements for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for qualified homeowners. Defines a qualified homeowner as an individual receiving gross income solely from Social Security, a pension, or an annuity. Requires qualified homeowners to submit the full application only in their first year and every third year thereafter. Authorizes qualified homeowners to submit an abbreviated certification instead of the full application in intervening years. Prohibits the Department from requiring additional proof of income from homeowners who submit the certification.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners applying for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit whose gross income is derived solely from Social Security, a pension, or an annuity
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the altered application process with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding real property tax assessment matters, exemptions, and property tax credits administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Changes to the application, eligibility, and certification processes for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit under the bill may affect matters subject to appeal before the local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body reviewing appeals from final decisions of taxing authorities and the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, including disputes concerning eligibility for state property tax credits.

Synopsis: Establishing that a hernia caused as a result of repetitive trauma may be considered an occupational disease and be compensable subject to certain provisions of the workers' compensation law.
Title: Labor and Employment - Workers' Compensation - Hernia

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes that a hernia caused as a result of repetitive trauma may be considered an occupational disease. Authorizes workers' compensation benefits for these repetitive trauma hernias under statutory standards governing occupational diseases. Requires claimants to demonstrate that the condition arose out of and in the course of employment. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Covered employees experiencing repetitive trauma hernias, employers, and workers' compensation insurers (including Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company)
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local government finances or operations, as repetitive trauma hernias are relatively rare and existing statutory burden-of-proof standards still apply.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims. This bill directly amends the statutory requirements for compensable hernia claims, expanding coverage to include repetitive trauma as an occupational disease.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the agency is the state's largest workers' compensation insurer and acts as the third-party administrator handling claims for State of Maryland employees. It directly assesses and pays claims that may arise under this expanded hernia provision.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions that exacerbate an employee's disability and was consulted for the fiscal analysis of this bill.

Synopsis: Altering a certain condition under which the Board of License Commissioners of Garrett County may issue a certain alcoholic beverages license to a hotel or motel; authorizing a gift basket permit holder to purchase certain alcoholic beverages from a wholesaler; authorizing a holder of a Class C multiple day beer license, beer and wine license, or beer, wine, and liquor license to hold another license that is issued by the Board; etc.
Title: Garrett County Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2023
bill_summary: Establishes a statutory framework governing the expiration and extension of alcoholic beverages licenses in Garrett County. Causes an inactive license to expire six months after closing operations unless an extension or transfer applies. Reduces the minimum room requirement for hotel and motel Class B licenses from 25 to 10 rooms. Authorizes gift basket permit holders to purchase alcoholic beverages from a wholesaler or a retail license holder. Authorizes holders of multiple day or multiple event licenses to hold another license of a different class. Expands authorized Sunday on-premises sales hours for specified licenses to begin at 6:00 a.m. instead of 10:00 a.m.
responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license and permit holders, hotels, motels, clubs, and gift basket retailers in Garrett County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect, as the Judiciary can handle any workload increase within existing budgeted resources. Garrett County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill includes provisions regarding judicial review of decisions by the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners and references circuit court actions. The fiscal note confirms that the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts can handle any associated increase in workload using existing budgeted resources.

bill_summary: Converts the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Pilot Program into a permanent program. Requires newly constructed community solar systems to serve at least 40% of output to low- and moderate-income subscribers. Authorizes consolidated billing and limits residential subscription rates to the monetary value of the bill credit. Caps subscription rates for low- and moderate-income subscribers at 90% of the bill credit value. Mandates prevailing wage rates on projects exceeding one megawatt unless subject to a project labor agreement. Extends the personal property tax exemption application window for qualifying community solar systems.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: community solar developers, subscriber organizations, subscription coordinators, electric companies, electric utility ratepayers, and low- and moderate-income subscribers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures and revenues for the Public Service Commission increase by $264,900 in FY 2024, reflecting staffing and consultant costs funded by assessments on public service companies. Local personal property tax revenues potentially decrease beginning in FY 2026 due to the extended application window for community solar exemptions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Program. The bill mandates PSC to make the program permanent, adopt comprehensive revised and new regulations, approve electric company tariffs, establish a stakeholder workgroup, and create a new full-time position dedicated to administering the program.

OPC represents residential utility consumers before the PSC. The bill establishes new billing structures, rate limitations, consumer protections, and low- to moderate-income provisions that directly affect residential utility customers and require PSC proceedings in which OPC participates.

The bill requires developers of community solar systems with a capacity exceeding 1 megawatt to pay workers at least the prevailing wage rate determined under Title 17, Subtitle 2 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which is established and administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.
The bill defines and incorporates 'agrivoltaics' into project siting and co-location standards, referencing agricultural activities recognized by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

The bill requires community solar energy generating system developers to address critical area, climate resilience, and forest conservation concerns by complying with the Forest Conservation Act and Critical Area requirements overseen by DNR.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2026, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Commission; and requiring an independent evaluation of the Commission to be conducted in consultation with the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability in the Department of Legislative Services.

bill_summary: Continues the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors until July 1, 2026. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a consultant to evaluate the Commission. Assesses Commission adherence to diversity, equity, and inclusion guidelines under the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice. Requires conducting the evaluation in consultation with the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability. Directs the Department to submit the evaluation report to designated legislative committees by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors; Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability
stakeholders: Licensed real estate appraisers, appraisal management companies, and home inspectors in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by between $50,000 and $75,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire an independent consultant. Commission special fund revenues and expenditures are otherwise maintained from FY 2024 through FY 2026. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the Commission's termination date to July 1, 2026, and requires the Department to hire an independent consultant to evaluate the Commission's adherence to diversity, equity, and inclusion guidelines, resulting in special fund expenditures of $50,000 to $75,000 in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the statutory and regulatory authority and termination date of an ongoing state regulatory commission—the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors—through July 1, 2026, and mandates an independent evaluation of its regulatory practices.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to establish certain targets for the deployment of new energy storage devices in the State; requiring the Commission to establish and implement the Maryland Energy Storage Program to meet certain energy storage goals and develop a certain energy storage system in the State; and requiring the Commission to submit a certain report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2023, regarding the implementation of the Maryland Energy Storage Program and any needed statutory changes.
