bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to establish targets for deploying new energy storage devices in the State. Sets cumulative capacity goals of 750 megawatts by 2027, 1,500 megawatts by 2030, and 3,000 megawatts by 2033. Requires reducing any target that cannot be met cost-effectively to the maximum cost-effective deployable amount. Establishes the Maryland Energy Storage Program and mandates its implementation by July 1, 2025. Mandates competitive procurement mechanisms and authorizes energy storage credits and utility contracting requirements.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: investor-owned electric companies, electric customers and ratepayers, and energy storage project developers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $649,600 in FY 2025 to hire six staff, fully offset by assessments on public service companies. State and local government expenditures on electricity likely increase beginning as early as FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing deployment targets, administering and implementing the Maryland Energy Storage Program, conducting rulemakings, and reporting to the General Assembly.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in Public Service Commission proceedings, which will include the proceedings, rulemakings, and rate recovery mechanisms associated with the deployment of energy storage systems and related ratepayer impacts.

The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state energy policy and renewable energy initiatives, and collaborates on statewide energy storage planning and oversight connected to existing pilot storage programs.

Synopsis: Requiring student financing companies to register with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation before providing services in the State; requiring a student financing company to renew its registration on an annual basis; authorizing the Commissioner to adopt registration procedures for student financing companies, which may include certain fees; and requiring student financing companies to annually report certain information, to be made publicly accessible on a certain website, to the Commissioner beginning March 15, 2024.
Title: Financial Institutions - Student Financing Companies - Required Registration and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Requires student financing companies to register annually with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation starting March 15, 2024. Mandates annual reporting of detailed loan volume, default rates, and terms for Maryland borrowers by March 15 each year. Directs the Commissioner to publish reported information on a publicly accessible website by June 15 each year. Renders student financing products void and unenforceable if a company knowingly violates registration or reporting mandates. Authorizes the Commissioner, the Attorney General, and county State's Attorneys to enforce these requirements. Permits the Commissioner to bar individuals from student financing roles for up to 10 years for harmful violations.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Student financing companies, institutions of postsecondary education offering student financing, and Maryland consumers obtaining or holding student financing products
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances, as the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation can implement the bill with existing resources and registration fees are paid to a third-party licensing system. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, with registering student financing companies, receiving annual reports, creating and maintaining a public database, establishing regulations, and conducting investigations and enforcement.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General, alongside the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and local State's Attorneys, to enforce the requirements and exercise investigative and enforcement powers under the subtitle.

The bill makes certain noncompliant student financing contracts void and unenforceable in legal actions and references court enforcement of investigative subpoenas, potentially impacting judicial proceedings and court filings.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a certain proceeding for judicial review of a final decision or order by the Public Service Commission may be instituted in a circuit court for a county in which the public service company that is a party to the proceeding provides service or in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City.
Title: Public Service Commission – Judicial Review – Proceedings
bill_summary: Clarifies venue requirements for judicial review of a final decision or order of the Public Service Commission. Requires a proceeding to be instituted in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City or an authorized county circuit court. Restricts county venue to any county where the public service company that was a party provides service. Removes obsolete statutory references to circuit courts in equity. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Public service companies, parties to Public Service Commission proceedings, and litigants seeking judicial review of Commission decisions
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. Administrative expenditures for the Public Service Commission may decrease or be reallocated due to reduced travel for legal staff from limited judicial review venues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory venue provisions governing where proceedings for judicial review of the Public Service Commission's final decisions and orders must be filed, potentially reducing travel and administrative expenditures for PSC legal staff.

The Office of the People's Counsel frequently represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC and routinely exercises its statutory authority under § 3-202 to seek judicial review of PSC decisions, meaning this venue limitation directly applies to their appeals.
The bill alters the jurisdictional venue rules determining which county circuit courts or the Circuit Court for Baltimore City may hear judicial reviews of PSC decisions.
The Secretary of the Environment has specific statutory authority under § 3-202 to seek judicial review of PSC orders, which are governed by the venue provisions amended by this bill.

The Secretary of Natural Resources has specific statutory authority under § 3-202 to seek judicial review of PSC decisions regarding power plant siting, and any such proceedings are subject to the venue requirements set by this bill.
Section 3-202 specifically references actions where the Motor Vehicle Administration suspends or revokes vehicle carrier registrations pursuant to an order of the PSC.

Synopsis: Establishing procedures for the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City, in the case of an alleged complaint against a licensed establishment or license holder, to make an offer of a monetary penalty as a compromise in lieu of a hearing before the Board under certain circumstances; and altering the maximum penalty for certain alcoholic beverages violations.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Violation Procedures and Fines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to offer a monetary compromise in lieu of a hearing. Requires agreeing license holders to waive hearing rights, admit alleged facts, take prescribed corrective action, and accept the penalty. Directs the Board to maintain records, make safety findings, state accepted compromises on record, and publicly post decisions. Requires the Board to adopt regulations to implement the compromise process. Increases the maximum fine from $3,000 to $20,000 for subsequent offenses causing license suspension. Increases the maximum fine from $3,000 to $20,000 for unauthorized pub crawl promoter violations.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders and pub crawl promoters in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in Baltimore City revenues from monetary penalties collected via offers of compromise and higher maximum fines. Procedural requirements can be handled with existing Baltimore City resources, and there is no State fiscal effect.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to approve a license expansion to a noncontiguous property with a second separate use permit issued by the City if a certain condition is met; authorizing the establishment and conversion of various alcoholic beverages licenses in the 46th alcoholic beverages district; extending for 1 year the expiration of an alcoholic beverage licenses issued for  certain areas for certain transferal and renewal purposes; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - 46th Alcoholic Beverages District - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to approve specified license expansions and issuances in the 46th district. Permits qualifying Class D beer and light wine license holders to convert licenses upon paying a $15,000 fee. Authorizes new Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses for restaurants meeting specific investment standards. Alters seating capacity limits for license transfers within ward 3, precinct 3 to fewer than 200 individuals. Extends the expiration of specified licenses until July 1, 2024, to complete transfers or renewals.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages licensees, restaurant owners, and applicants in Baltimore City's 46th alcoholic beverages district
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Baltimore City revenues beginning in FY 2024 from additional license issuances, conversions, and transfer fees. No state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for collecting state alcohol and sales taxes and regulates the alcohol industry at the state level. While this bill specifically alters local retail alcoholic beverage licenses administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it pertains to the broader regulation and taxation of alcoholic beverages.

Synopsis: Establishing consumer protections related to the repair or replacement of motor vehicle glass on motor vehicles equipped with an advanced driver assistance system; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice.
Title: Consumer Protection - Motor Vehicle Glass Repair or Replacement - Advanced Driver Assistance System Recalibration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes consumer protections for motor vehicle glass repair or replacement on vehicles with advanced driver assistance systems. Requires motor vehicle safety glass facilities to inform customers if system recalibration is required before glass work. Requires facilities to provide a written statement that work will meet or exceed original equipment manufacturer specifications. Prohibits facilities from charging for services that are not performed or successfully completed. Requires facilities to inform customers if required recalibration is not performed or successfully completed. Makes violations an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners with vehicles equipped with advanced driver assistance systems; motor vehicle safety glass facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division, can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that violations by motor vehicle safety glass facilities are unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is directly enforced and investigated by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill references definitions in the Transportation Article and relates to motor vehicle safety systems; MDOT was consulted as an information source for the legislation, though it has no direct regulatory or enforcement mandate under the bill.

While the bill amends the Commercial Law Article, motor vehicle safety glass repairs and ADAS recalibrations commonly involve auto insurance claims, leading to MIA being consulted as an information source.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Department of Commerce from denying certain cannabis business entities conducting business in the State certain economic development program benefits under certain circumstances; clarifying the eligibility of certain cannabis business entities conducting business in the State under the Job Creation and One Maryland programs; authorizing certain cannabis business entities to reapply for benefits under certain economic development programs; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Program Participation - Cannabis Business Establishments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Cannabis Distribution -see also- Cannabis, Cannabis Prod.
Cannabis Production -see also- Cannabis, Cannabis Dist.
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Prohibits the Department of Commerce from denying economic development program benefits solely because an applicant is a licensed cannabis establishment. Applies this prohibition to programs under Title 5 of the Economic Development Article and the More Jobs for Marylanders Program. Requires the cannabis business entity to otherwise satisfy all program requirements, including industry sector-specific criteria. Authorizes cannabis establishments previously denied benefits or certification before July 1, 2023, solely on that basis to reapply. Adds the growth, processing, or dispensing of cannabis as eligible activities for Job Creation and One Maryland tax credits.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: licensed cannabis business entities, including medical cannabis growers, processors, and dispensaries
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2025 as newly eligible cannabis dispensaries claim Job Creation and One Maryland tax credits, largely driven by uncapped One Maryland credits. Transportation Trust Fund and Higher Education Investment Fund revenues, as well as local highway user revenues, decrease to the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering Title 5 economic development programs, certifying entities for the More Jobs for Marylanders Program, and administering the Job Creation and One Maryland tax credits to include licensed cannabis establishments.

The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state tax system, including processing and auditing the Job Creation and One Maryland tax credits claimed on income tax returns, which are expected to decrease general fund and special fund revenues.

The Maryland Cannabis Administration licenses and regulates the cannabis growers, processors, dispensaries, and other cannabis establishments that are granted eligibility for state economic development benefits and tax credits under the bill.
The Department of Transportation is minimally affected via a potential decrease in Transportation Trust Fund revenues resulting from tax credits claimed against the corporate income tax.

Synopsis: Providing that the Secretary of Higher Education is appointed by and serves at the pleasure of the Governor; requiring each institution of higher education to adopt a written policy that provides reasonable academic accommodations for students to practice sincerely held faith-based or religious beliefs; altering eligibility criteria for and the process for awards from the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Program of Educational Excellence Awards; altering the administration of the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Appointment of Secretary and Student Financial Assistance - Accommodations at Public Institutions for Religious Beliefs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: Provides that the Governor appoints the Secretary of Higher Education to serve at the Governor's pleasure. Requires each public institution of higher education to adopt a written policy providing reasonable academic accommodations for religious beliefs. Requires each public institution of higher education, except University of Maryland Global Campus, to provide campus space for religious practices. Alters eligibility criteria for the Guaranteed Access Grant and the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program. Transfers the administration and awarding of Maryland Community College Promise Scholarships from state financial aid staff to community colleges. Repeals statutory intent to reorganize the Office of Student Financial Assistance as a separate independent agency.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance; Governor; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: higher education students, public institutions of higher education, community colleges, and students observing religious beliefs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $278,200 in FY 2024 for contractual modifications to the Maryland College Aid Processing System. Baltimore City Community College and locally funded community colleges incur administrative expenditures beginning in FY 2024 to verify eligibility and award Promise Scholarships. Beginning in FY 2026, institutions incur administrative costs to process Guaranteed Access Grants, potentially offset by state funding. The State avoids indeterminate operational costs by repealing the planned independent agency spin-off of the Office of Student Financial Assistance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory agency impacted by the bill. The legislation alters the appointment and reporting structure of the Secretary of Higher Education, reforms the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards (EEA) and Guaranteed Access (GA) Grants, restructures the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship administration, and repeals the planned spin-off of the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA).

As the state's postsecondary coordinating board and administrator of state financial assistance, MHEC is directly responsible for implementing the financial aid reforms, auditing community college awards, and working with advisory councils on regulatory implementation.

The bill directly modifies the Governor's appointment power by removing the requirement to select the Secretary of Higher Education from a list of MHEC nominees and establishing that the Secretary serves at the pleasure of the Governor. It also expresses legislative intent regarding gubernatorial budget requests for financial aid administration funding.

USM institutions are public institutions of higher education that must adopt written religious accommodation policies, provide campus spaces for religious practices (with an exemption for UMGC), and implement new responsibilities for notifying students of Guaranteed Access Grant awards and calculating financial aid packages.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is required to establish religious accommodation policies and campus spaces, as well as take on financial aid notification and administration duties for the Guaranteed Access Grant program.

As a public four-year institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland must adopt faith-based academic accommodation policies, designate space on campus for religious practices, and administer Guaranteed Access Grant notifications and packaging for its students.

MSDE administers the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program in collaboration with MHEC. The bill alters student eligibility criteria for the program to include students who qualify for free or reduced-price lunch and allows continued participation for students who move to nonparticipating counties.

Synopsis: Altering the hours during which a licensee may sell alcoholic beverages on Sundays in Frederick County.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Sunday Sales
bill_summary: Alters Sunday hours of sale for specified alcoholic beverages licenses in Frederick County. Authorizes special Sunday opening permit holders for Class A licenses to sell starting at 6 a.m. Expands Sunday sales hours for Class B and Class C license holders to run from 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. Repeals prohibitions against Class B licensees selling alcoholic beverages at a bar or counter on Sunday. Aligns Sunday sales hours for conference centers, dinner theaters, entertainment centers, hotel lobbies, and municipal golf courses.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: holders of specified alcoholic beverages licenses in Frederick County and retail alcohol consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations, though small business license holders may realize increased sales revenue from expanded Sunday operating hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates Maryland's alcohol industry and issues state-level alcohol licenses referenced in related provisions (such as Class 7 micro-brewery licenses), although retail sales hours in Frederick County are administered primarily at the local level.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County to issue up to five Class B-DD (Development District) beer, wine, and liquor licenses for restaurants located within the Main Street Laurel development.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Main Street Laurel Development PG 404-23
bill_summary: Authorizes the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to issue up to five Class B–DD (Development District) licenses. Restricts eligibility to restaurants located within the Main Street Laurel development area. Defines the geographic boundaries from northbound Washington Boulevard to 7th Street, between the Patuxent River and Prince George Street. Permits license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption seven days per week. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurants located within the Main Street Laurel development area in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County revenues increase by $3,025 annually for each Class B-DD license issued, though the total number of licenses that will be issued cannot be reliably estimated. County enforcement can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating aspects of the alcoholic beverages industry and collecting state alcohol excise and sales taxes. While this bill specifically authorizes the local Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to issue local retail licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation of alcoholic beverages within the state.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Charles County to grant, by law, a  tax credit against the property tax imposed on the owner-occupied residence of certain emergency responders and their surviving spouses if the federal adjusted gross income of the emergency responder or the unmarried surviving spouse for the immediately preceding taxable years is $150,000 or less; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Charles County - Property Tax - Credit for Volunteer Emergency Responders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Charles County to grant a property tax credit against county property taxes. Applies to real property owned and occupied as the principal residence of an emergency responder or unmarried surviving spouse. Limits eligibility to individuals with a federal adjusted gross income of $150,000 or less for the preceding taxable year. Defines an emergency responder as an active or retired volunteer member of a Charles County fire, rescue, or emergency medical services company. Allows the county to determine the credit amount, duration, and additional eligibility criteria.
responsible_party: Governing Body of Charles County
stakeholders: Active and retired volunteer members of fire, rescue, and emergency medical services companies in Charles County and their unmarried surviving spouses
fiscal_impact_summary: Charles County property tax revenues decrease by $347,300 in FY 2024 and $375,900 in FY 2028 if the tax credit is granted. County expenditures increase by $115,900 in FY 2024 and $130,400 in FY 2028 for administrative staff in the County Treasurer's Office. No state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes Charles County to grant a local property tax credit on the principal residence of volunteer emergency responders. Although the credit is established and administered locally by Charles County with no state fiscal effect, the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board (through its local board in Charles County) serves as the appellate administrative body for disputes concerning property valuations, exemptions, and tax credits.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Native Plants Program to respond to the increasing demand for, use of, and sale of native plants at retail garden centers and wholesale nurseries and to educate the public on native plants; requiring the Department of Agriculture to administer the Program in coordination with the University of Maryland Extension and to establish the "Maryland Natives" marketing program; requiring the University of Maryland Extension to hire an extension agent to serve as a native plant specialist for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Maryland Native Plants Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Native Plants Program to promote the use and sale of Maryland native plants. Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture to administer the program and establish a voluntary certification program. Requires the University of Maryland Extension to hire a native plant specialist to direct educational components. Directs the Department to maintain a commercial native plant list and a Maryland Natives marketing program. Mandates annual state budget appropriations of $150,000 for the Extension and $100,000 for the Department starting in fiscal 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; University of Maryland Extension; Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial plant growers, retail nurseries, wholesale nurseries, garden centers, landscapers, and plant consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $285,100 in fiscal 2025 and ongoing years for personnel and operating costs. The bill mandates annual appropriations starting in fiscal 2025 of $150,000 for the University of Maryland Extension and $100,000 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Native Plants Program, including establishing a voluntary certification program for growers and retailers, developing the Commercial Maryland Native Plant List, operating the 'Maryland Natives' marketing program, and receiving a mandated annual appropriation of $100,000 to hire staff.

The University of Maryland Extension, an entity of USM, is tasked with co-administering the program, administering all educational components, creating and maintaining the 'Maryland Native Plants' webpage, and hiring an extension agent as a native plant specialist supported by a mandated annual appropriation of $150,000.

DNR is required to provide input into the creation and triennial update of the Commercial Maryland Native Plant List and cultivar evaluations, and must host a link to the program's webpage on its native plants website.
The bill mandates that the Governor include specific annual budget appropriations starting in FY 2025 of $150,000 for UME and $100,000 for MDA in the annual state budget.
DBM oversees the preparation and execution of the state budget and manages state personnel, requiring it to incorporate the bill's mandated funding and accommodate the new state positions.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from disbursing or authorizing the disbursement of certain funds to a county if the county has not provided certain information concerning its tax sales; altering the taxable year for which the Department is required to obtain certain information concerning county tax sales; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Tax Sales - Data Collection - County Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Prohibits the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from disbursing funds to any county that fails to provide required tax sale information. Alters the reporting period for county tax sale data to the second immediately preceding taxable year. Restricts homeowner-specific data collection to properties offered for sale, sold, or subject to foreclosure. Requires each county conducting tax sales to submit all specified information on department forms. Applies the funding prohibition prospectively to surveys conducted on or after June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland counties conducting tax sales and property owners subject to tax sales
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts collaborates with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and counties to provide data regarding properties for which the right of redemption has been foreclosed by private certificate holders, making it relevant to the data collection process addressed in the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim October 5 as Dashain Day, a festival originating in Nepal that celebrates and symbolizes victory of good over evil.
Title: General Provisions - Commemorative Days - Dashain Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Governor annually to proclaim October 5 as Dashain Day. Recognizes Dashain as a festival originating in Nepal that celebrates and symbolizes the victory of good over evil. Renumbers existing sections of the General Provisions Article to accommodate the new commemoration. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Governor
stakeholders: Nepalese and South Asian communities in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to annually issue a proclamation declaring October 5 as Dashain Day.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to include on its staff one or more employees that are experts in cybersecurity to perform certain duties; requiring the Commission to establish, in coordination with the Office of Security Management, cybersecurity standards and best practices for regulated entities; requiring each public service company to report a cybersecurity incident to certain entities; requiring the State Security Operations Center to immediately notify certain agencies of a certain reported cybersecurity incident; etc.
Title: Public Service Commission – Cybersecurity Staffing and Assessments (Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to employ cybersecurity experts to advise commissioners and support public service companies. Requires the Commission to collaborate with the Office of Security Management to establish cybersecurity standards and best practices. Requires public service companies, excluding common carriers and telephone companies, to adopt zero-trust cybersecurity approaches. Requires affected public service companies to engage third parties for biennial cybersecurity assessments beginning July 1, 2024. Requires public service companies to report cybersecurity incidents to the State Security Operations Center. Requires the Commission to submit biennial cybersecurity reports to the State Chief Information Security Officer beginning January 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of Information Technology; Office of Security Management; State Security Operations Center; State Chief Information Security Officer
stakeholders: Regulated public service companies, including investor-owned electric companies, electric cooperatives, municipal electric utilities, gas companies, and water companies (excluding common carriers and telephone companies), and Maryland utility customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures and offsetting revenues for the Public Service Commission increase by $364,400 in FY 2024 (and $446,200 in FY 2025) for three new staff positions funded through utility assessments. Local expenditures for municipal electric utilities increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 for biennial third-party assessments. The Department of Information Technology can implement requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 969 directly impacts the Public Service Commission (PSC) by requiring it to hire dedicated cybersecurity experts, collaborate on cybersecurity standards and best practices for regulated utilities, collect biennial compliance certifications, and submit biennial reports on utility cybersecurity posture to the State Chief Information Security Officer.

The bill assigns substantial responsibilities to DoIT and its units, including the Office of Security Management (OSM), the State Chief Information Security Officer (SCISO), and the State Security Operations Center. DoIT collaborates with the PSC to establish standards, establishes incident reporting processes for public service companies, receives incident notifications, and is authorized to receive transferred Dedicated Purpose Account funds for cybersecurity staffing and operational capacity.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation to study information on mold assessment and remediation to determine the best practices for identifying mold, preventing the development of mold within indoor environments, and remediating indoor molding conditions harmful to public health; and requiring the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by October 1, 2024.
Title: Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation to study mold assessment and remediation practices. Directs the workgroup to examine standards from specified industry organizations, state governments, international governments, and federal guidelines. Requires the workgroup to assess the extent to which climate change increases indoor mold development. Mandates recommending best practices for identifying, preventing, and remediating indoor mold harmful to public health. Requires the workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by October 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation
stakeholders: Maryland residents, building occupants, property owners, and mold assessment and remediation professionals
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are minimally affected as workgroup expense reimbursements and staffing costs are absorbable within existing Maryland Department of the Environment resources. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of the Environment or designee serves as the chair of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation, and the department is responsible for providing staff support and designating an accreditation representative.
The Secretary of General Services or designee is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation.
The Secretary of Health or designee is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation to evaluate health impacts and remediation standards.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development or designee is designated as a member of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation.
The Secretary of Labor or designee is designated as a member of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes a new temporary advisory body, the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation, to conduct a study and issue recommendations.
The Workgroup is statutorily mandated to submit its findings and recommended best practices to the Governor on or before October 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner in the Maryland Department of Health to advance forensic science and carry out other duties as provided by law; renaming the State Postmortem Examiners Commission to be the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee; requiring and authorizing the Department and the Office to perform certain duties and powers previously performed by the Commission; authorizing the Department to contract with a physician for employment with the Office on a per diem basis; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Office of the Chief Medical Examiner

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner as a unit within the Maryland Department of Health. Redesignates the State Postmortem Examiners Commission as the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to employ contractual physicians on a per diem basis. Prohibits the Department and the Advisory Committee from interfering with clinical autopsy findings and conclusions. Exempts certain reemployed Employees' Pension System retirees serving as health care practitioners from pension benefit offsets.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee
stakeholders: reemployed Employees' Pension System retirees serving as contractual health care practitioners, medical examiners and forensic staff, county medical societies, and the Maryland Department of Health
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or pension liabilities and contribution rates, as changes are primarily procedural.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner as a unit within the Department of Health, transfers administrative and staffing powers from the former commission to the Department and the Secretary of Health, and authorizes MDH to adopt rules and hire contract/per diem physicians.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to exempt Employees' Pension System retirees who are reemployed contractually by MDH as health care practitioners in the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner from standard retirement allowance reductions.
The bill requires the Department of Health to set compensation for designated medical examiner and forensic personnel with the approval of the Secretary of Budget and Management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and defines the duties of the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee, which advises the Secretary of Health and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.

The Secretary of State Police is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee, and State Police collaborate closely on medical examiner death investigations.
The head of the Pathology Department of the University of Maryland School of Medicine is designated by statute as a member of the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee.

The bill references and maintains the role of the Office of Administrative Hearings to conduct contested case hearings and submit findings of fact when an individual appeals a denial by the Chief Medical Examiner to correct autopsy findings.

Synopsis: Establishing the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers; altering the eligibility criteria for the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and the Maryland Police Officers Scholarship Program to include probation agents who work for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; establishing the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship; requiring the Maryland Higher Education Commission to make awards from the Human Services Careers Scholarship Pilot Program in fiscal year 2024; etc.
Title: State Employees – Programs and Scholarships for Human Services Careers and Probation Agents and State Contributions to Supplemental Retirement Plans

bill_summary: Establishes a human services career pilot program and companion scholarship in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County. Expands the police officer loan assistance repayment and scholarship programs to include parole and probation agents. Mandates annual budget appropriations of $5,000,000 each for the loan repayment and scholarship programs. Requires the State to match employee supplemental retirement contributions up to $600 per fiscal year. Authorizes an equivalent retirement match up to $600 for employees documenting higher education student loan payments.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State Board of Trustees of the Maryland Teachers and State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
stakeholders: State employees participating in supplemental retirement plans, parole and probation agents in the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, public school students and staff in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County, and Department of Human Services employees
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $21.8 million in FY 2024 ($13.5 million general funds, $4.1 million special funds, and $4.1 million federal funds) and by $21.7 million annually thereafter, driven primarily by State supplemental retirement matching contributions and new scholarships. Mandated annual appropriations shift $3.5 million from the police scholarship program to the loan assistance repayment program. Local school system expenditures in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County may increase to adjust required curricula.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers within the Department of Human Services (DHS), requiring DHS to collaborate with local school systems, prioritize program participants in hiring, pay stipends, assign and compensate employee mentors, and partner with MHEC to select scholarship recipients.

MHEC is responsible for administering the newly established Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship and administering the expanded Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and Scholarship Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents, requiring system updates to MDCAPS and additional personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates State matching contributions of up to $600 per fiscal year for participating employees in State supplemental retirement plans (including matches for higher education student loan repayments), increasing total assets under management and fee revenues for MSRP.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly benefits DPSCS by expanding eligibility for the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Maryland Police Officers Scholarship Program to include DPSCS parole and probation agents, supervisors, and regional administrators.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM is responsible for statewide personnel benefits, coordinating the implementation of the State supplemental retirement matching contributions across State agencies, and incorporating mandated appropriations in the state budget.

The bill requires local school systems to collaborate with DHS to identify students, create internships, add human services career competencies to curriculum, and integrate career opportunities into middle and high school career counseling programs under education law.

USM institutions serve as eligible public senior higher education institutions where scholarship recipients and participants in the police/probation and human services career programs will enroll and use state tuition assistance funds.

The bill establishes statutory mandated annual budget appropriations that the Governor must include in the annual state budget bill ($5,000,000 for the loan assistance repayment program and $5,000,000 for the scholarship program).

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the Heritage Conservation Fund to include acquiring interests in land that can be used by the general public for hunting; establishing the Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program to provide outreach and foster an interest in outdoor recreation and stewardship, hunting, and wildlife conservation; establishing a stamp for hunting sika deer; authorizing a nonresident attending a college or university in the State to purchase a resident hunting license; etc.
Title: Hunting, Wildlife Conservation, and Outdoor Recreation - Funding, Promotion, Management, Licenses, Permits, and Stamps

bill_summary: Establishes the Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program within the Department of Natural Resources to promote outdoor recreation and stewardship. Increases statutory fees for multiple hunting and trapping licenses, stamps, and permits, and codifies furbearer permit fees. Creates new resident and nonresident sika deer hunting stamps. Authorizes nonresident students attending a Maryland college or university to purchase a resident hunting license with proof of enrollment. Expands the Heritage Conservation Fund to include acquiring land usable by the general public for hunting. Requires the Department of Natural Resources, in consultation with the Department of Agriculture, to develop a deer overpopulation plan.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: hunters, trappers, nonresident college students attending Maryland institutions, farmers, and private landowners
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $2,271,600 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to increased license, stamp, and permit fees. Federal grant matching revenues increase by an estimated $6,814,900 annually beginning in fiscal 2025, which will fund staff and a farmer cost-share program. No direct local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including establishing the Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program, administering altered and new hunting/trapping license and stamp fees, managing the Heritage Conservation Fund and Wildlife Management and Protection Fund, creating eight new staff positions, and developing a statewide deer overpopulation plan.

DNR is required to consult with the Department of Agriculture to develop a plan addressing the overpopulation of deer in Maryland, and the bill establishes a farmer cost-share program to plant forage crops on agricultural land.
The bill mandates the creation of eight new Position Identification Numbers (PINs) for department personnel and involves significant ongoing state special and federal fund budgetary adjustments.
The bill codifies that the balance of migratory game bird stamp fees is paid over and accounted to the State Treasurer to be credited to the State Wildlife Management and Protection Fund.

Synopsis: Consolidating and altering certain laws governing collective bargaining for certain public employees, including laws related to the establishment of bargaining units, election and certification of exclusive representatives, employee and employer rights, unfair labor practices, and strikes and lockouts; establishing the Public Employee Relations Board to oversee collective bargaining activities for certain public employees; etc.
Title: Public Employee Relations Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Consolidates collective bargaining laws for State employees, public school employees, and community college employees into the State Government Article. Establishes the Public Employee Relations Board as an independent State agency to oversee collective bargaining activities. Repeals the State Labor Relations Board, State Higher Education Labor Relations Board, and Public School Labor Relations Board. Requires certification of an exclusive representative without an election if a petition is supported by a majority of unit employees. Prohibits public employers from engaging in lockouts and prohibits public employees from engaging in strikes.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board
stakeholders: State employees, public school employees, community college employees, public employers, and public employee labor organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $642,600 in FY 2024 to fund board member compensation, three deputy directors, legal counsel, and operational start-up costs for the new board, rising to $888,400 by FY 2028. Local expenditures are not anticipated to be materially affected, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 984 establishes the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) as an independent state agency responsible for overseeing and administering collective bargaining, union elections, and unfair labor practice disputes across Maryland public employers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: State Higher Education Labor Relations Board
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly repeals the State Higher Education Labor Relations Board and consolidates its responsibilities, functions, and pending matters into the newly established PERB.
The bill explicitly repeals the Public School Labor Relations Board and consolidates its powers, duties, and pending matters into the newly established PERB.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM represents the State in collective bargaining negotiations under Title 3 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, which is heavily amended and standardized under the bill.
The bill substantially modifies and restructures the statutory provisions in the Education Article governing collective bargaining for certificated and noncertificated public school personnel.
The bill explicitly authorizes hearings on unfair labor practice complaints to be conducted before the Office of Administrative Hearings.
The bill sets requirements for collective bargaining units, exclusive representative elections, and negotiation procedures covering employees at USM constituent institutions.
The bill specifically designates and structures collective bargaining units and bargaining procedures for employees and governing boards at Morgan State University.
The bill establishes specific statutory requirements governing bargaining unit composition and labor negotiations for Saint Mary's College of Maryland.
The bill specifically maintains and regulates a dedicated statutory collective bargaining unit for faculty at the Maryland School for the Deaf.
The bill explicitly maintains and regulates a separate statutory collective bargaining unit for MDTA police officers at the rank of first sergeant and below.
MES is explicitly referenced in collective bargaining statutory provisions regarding employer negotiating obligations under State Personnel and Pensions § 3-502.
The bill amends Health - General § 15-903 to update references for collective bargaining elections concerning independent home care providers under MDH programs to PERB.
The fiscal note identifies that additional Assistant Attorney General staffing is required to provide legal counsel, represent, and handle evidentiary/subpoena processes for the newly expanded PERB.
The Governor is tasked with appointing all five members and the full-time chair of the newly created Public Employee Relations Board with Senate advice and consent.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointments to state boards, including the newly established five-member PERB.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain students who are at least 18 years old and under the age of 21 years to taste certain alcoholic beverages while participating in a course or program in enology, fermenting, brewing, or hospitality and tourism offered by a qualified institution of higher education without criminal penalty to the student, instructor, or institution of higher education under certain circumstances.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages – Use of Alcoholic Beverages for Educational Purposes

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes qualified students aged 18 to 20 to taste alcoholic beverages in certain higher education courses without criminal penalty. Applies to students enrolled in enology, fermenting, brewing, or hospitality and tourism courses at qualified institutions of higher education. Requires students to spit out the beverage after tasting during scheduled class dates and times. Mandates that the alcoholic beverage remain under the control of an authorized instructor at least 21 years old. Exempts qualified institutions from obtaining an alcoholic beverages license if they charge no extra tasting fee. Protects participating students, instructors, and institutions from criminal penalties for furnishing, possessing, or tasting alcoholic beverages.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students aged 18 to 20 enrolled in enology, fermenting, brewing, or hospitality and tourism programs; authorized course instructors; and qualified Maryland institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates educational activities and curricula (enology, fermenting, brewing, and hospitality programs) at postsecondary institutions overseen and coordinated by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.

USM institutions offering courses and degree programs in hospitality, tourism, fermenting, or brewing are directly affected, allowing students aged 18 to 20 to taste alcohol under instructor supervision without criminal penalty or additional licensing requirements.

The Comptroller regulates aspects of the alcoholic beverage industry and enforcement in Maryland; the bill creates a specific statutory exception from alcoholic beverage licensing and permitting for qualified higher education institutions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates statutory exceptions to criminal penalties under the Criminal Law Article for underage alcohol possession/consumption and adult furnishing of alcohol, which OPD defends in criminal court.
The bill carves out exceptions to misdemeanor criminal charges related to underage alcohol possession and consumption, marginally affecting judicial caseloads and court proceedings.

Synopsis: Modifying the Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program by clarifying and altering certain provisions relating to the administration of the Program; establishing the employer and employee shares of the total rate of contribution; prohibiting the total rate of contribution from exceeding 1.2% of an employee's wages; requiring the State to pay for certain contributions for certain covered employees; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse certain community providers for certain employer contributions in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program - Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- Parents and Guardians
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
