Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Modifies the Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program by delaying required contributions to October 1, 2024, and benefit payments to January 1, 2026. Sets an even 50% employer and 50% employee cost-sharing split for employers with 15 or more employees. Caps the total contribution rate at 1.2% of employee wages up to the Social Security wage base. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse specified licensed or certified community service providers for employer contributions. Repeals the mandate that covered individuals exhaust employer-provided leave before receiving program benefits. Authorizes employers and covered individuals to agree to use employer-provided paid leave to replace up to 100% of average weekly wages during leave periods.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Covered employees, employers with 15 or more employees, participating self-employed individuals, and licensed or certified community service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds decrease by $28.7 million in FY 2024 and $10.0 million in FY 2025 due to the one-year delay in required employer contributions. General fund expenditures increase by $25.6 million in FY 2025 and by at least $35.5 million annually thereafter for Maryland Department of Health community provider reimbursements. FAMLI special fund contribution revenues and benefit expenditures are delayed by one year. Local government employer contributions are likewise deferred until October 1, 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing and regulatory agency responsible for administering the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program, establishing contribution rates, conducting annual cost analyses, processing claims and appeals, and issuing regulations.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse certain community-based behavioral health and developmental disability service providers for their required employer contributions on at least a quarterly basis, resulting in significant fiscal impact.

The bill assigns a statutory duty to the Board of Public Works to annually monitor state employment statistics and determine whether to temporarily suspend increases in the maximum weekly benefit amount.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM is impacted by the timeline changes and funding requirements for the State's share of employer contributions for state employees.
The bill specifies that private employer plans utilizing insurance must be provided through insurers holding a certificate of authority issued by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.
The bill statutorily references the Office of the Comptroller to report state revenue performance to the Board of Public Works when determining whether to suspend benefit increases.
The bill alters statutory provisions governing the issuance of benefit and refund checks by removing the requirement for the State Treasurer's signature.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B-MGC (miniature golf course) beer, wine, and liquor license to a miniature golf course under certain circumstances; authorizing a license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption under certain circumstances; requiring a license holder to submit an annual gross sales report for alcohol, golf games and food to the Board before a license may be renewed; and providing an annual license fee of $1,500.
Title: Frederick County – Alcoholic Beverages – Miniature Golf Course License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Establishes a Class B-MGC (miniature golf course) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County. Authorizes the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to qualifying miniature golf courses. Permits licensees to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption if food is offered at all times. Caps annual alcohol sales at 35% of gross sales, while requiring miniature golf and food sales of 50% and 15%. Sets an annual license fee of $1,500 and mandates an annual gross sales report for renewal.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
stakeholders: Miniature golf courses in Frederick County and their patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by $1,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to license fee collections. Additional county enforcement activities can be handled with existing resources. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a local miniature golf course alcoholic beverages license administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners. While the state fiscal effect is negligible, the Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcoholic beverage industry and collecting state sales and excise taxes on alcohol sales.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement in Frederick County that alcoholic beverages in a basket of cheer be produced in Maryland.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Basket of Cheer
bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that alcoholic beverages included in a basket of cheer in Frederick County be produced in Maryland. Applies to basket of cheer permits issued to holders of Class C per diem licenses. Retains authority to raffle up to 10 baskets of cheer as prizes at each benefit performance. Requires permit holders to obtain all alcoholic beverages for baskets from licensed retailers for off-premises consumption. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class C per diem alcoholic beverages license holders and benefit performance attendees in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Local operations and finances in Frederick County are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the regulation of the alcoholic beverage industry across the state. While this bill specifically addresses local 'basket of cheer' raffle permits administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages Article regarding rules on alcoholic beverage distribution and sourcing.

Synopsis: Altering the quantity of certain alcoholic beverages an individual may consume under certain consumption permits issued in Frederick County.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the quantity of alcoholic beverages an individual may consume under certain consumption permits in Frederick County. Authorizes individuals under a beer and wine consumption permit to consume three sample servings in any combination. Limits each sample to not more than two ounces of beer or one ounce of wine. Authorizes individuals under a beer, wine, and liquor consumption permit to consume three sample servings. Limits those samples to two ounces of beer, one ounce of wine, or 0.5 ounce of liquor. Maintains alternative single-serving consumption options and takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages license holders and patrons consuming alcoholic beverages on licensed premises in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Frederick County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. Although this legislation strictly alters allowable serving sizes under local consumption permits administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it falls within the general area of state alcoholic beverage law.

Synopsis: Repealing certain provisions of law applicable to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation that prohibit the acceptance of articles of dissolution and issuance of a certificate of termination for certain corporations unless certain reports on personal property are filed with the Department; etc.
Title: Corporations - Filing Requirements for Dissolution and Termination of Registration or Qualification - Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: Repeals the restriction prohibiting the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from accepting articles of dissolution without filed personal property reports. Repeals the requirement that the Department issue a certificate of termination to a foreign corporation upon filing required reports. Allows corporations to dissolve without first filing Title 11 personal property reports. Permits foreign corporations to terminate registration or qualification without prerequisite personal property report filings. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Corporations dissolving in Maryland and foreign corporations terminating Maryland registration or qualification
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by approximately $150,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 because an estimated 500 entities per year will no longer pay the $300 annual corporate report filing fee prior to dissolution or termination. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions related to the rates the Department of State Police sets for tow companies involved in certain police-initiated towing; establishing the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery; and requiring the Committee, on or before December 1, 2023, to recommend approved rates to the Department of State Police that should be charged for police-initiated towing and recovery services.
Title: Commercial Vehicles - Police-Initiated Towing - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery. Requires the Department of State Police to set maximum approved towing and recovery rates by January 1, 2024. Requires tow companies on the state tow list to ban per-pound billing by October 1, 2023. Prohibits authorized tow companies from charging more than Department-approved rates for police-initiated towing and recovery. Delays the disputed-fee release requirement to March 1, 2024, until approved rates take effect. Repeals the disputed-fee release mandate upon notification that the Department has adopted approved rates.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery
stakeholders: commercial vehicle owners and operators, commercial towing businesses providing medium-duty and heavy-duty towing services, and the Department of State Police
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $44,700 in FY 2024 for one part-time administrator, increasing to $58,000 by FY 2028. Revenues are unaffected. No material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of State Police with establishing approved rates for medium- and heavy-duty towing and recovery, maintaining the tow list, handling complaint resolution, and staffing the newly created Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes a new statutory committee, the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery.
The Administrator of the State Highway Administration is required to appoint a representative to serve on the newly created Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution.
The bill designates a seat on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for a representative of the Maryland Transportation Authority Police.

The Secretary of Transportation is responsible for appointing a representative of the MDTA Police to the Committee, and the Department oversees modal administrations involved in highway clearance and safety.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is required to appoint a representative of the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve on the new Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Wicomico County to create a sanitary district.
Title: Wicomico County - Sanitary District - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Sanitary Districts -see also- Wash Sub Sanitary District

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Wicomico County to create a sanitary district by ordinance or resolution. Removes Wicomico County from the list of counties exempt from State sanitary district laws. Grants created districts authority to oversee water and sewerage systems under a sanitary commission. Permits districts to issue bonds, set benefit assessments, and exercise eminent domain. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Council
stakeholders: Wicomico County residents, property owners with septic systems, and municipal water and sewer utilities in Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Wicomico County expenditures and revenues may increase if the county chooses to establish sanitary districts, but specific figures cannot currently be determined.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1004 amends Title 9, Subtitle 6 of the Environment Article to authorize Wicomico County to establish sanitary districts to address water, sewerage, and failing septic system issues. As the state's primary environmental regulatory agency, the Maryland Department of the Environment oversees public water and sewerage systems, county water and sewer plans, and related environmental infrastructure.

Synopsis: Reducing from 150 yards to 50 yards the size of the safety zone for archery hunters in Howard County who are under the authority of a deer management permit or who are actively participating in a hunting program administered by the county within which archery hunting may not take place except under certain circumstances; and requiring certain archery hunters in Howard County to be in an elevated position when hunting any wild bird or mammal within 50 to 150 yards of certain buildings.
Title: Howard County – Archery Hunting – Safety Zone and Position of Archery Hunter Ho. Co. 15–23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Decreases the archery hunting safety zone in Howard County from 150 yards to 50 yards for qualifying archery hunters. Applies this reduction to hunters operating under a deer management permit or participating in a county-administered hunting program. Requires these hunters to shoot from an elevated position with a downward trajectory within 50 to 150 yards of specified structures. Enforces the elevation requirement near dwelling houses, residences, churches, schools, and other human-occupied buildings or camps.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Archery hunters in Howard County hunting under a deer management permit or county-administered hunting program, as well as Howard County property owners and residents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article governing hunting safety zones and impacts hunters operating under Deer Management Permits, which are issued and regulated by the Department of Natural Resources' Wildlife and Heritage Service, and enforced by the Natural Resources Police.

Synopsis: Providing that, notwithstanding any other provision of law, except for regulations issued by the Department of the Environment, no provision of the State building code or other law or regulation may prohibit or otherwise limit the use of a refrigerant if the refrigerant is designated as acceptable for use under federal listing requirements and any appliance containing the refrigerant meets federal safety standards and use conditions.
Title: Public Safety – Refrigerants – Limitations on Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn

bill_summary: Prohibits the State building code or other laws and regulations from restricting the use of certain federally approved refrigerants. Exempts regulations issued by the Maryland Department of the Environment from this prohibition. Applies when the refrigerant is designated as acceptable for use under federal law. Requires appliances containing the refrigerant to be labeled, installed, serviced, repaired, and used under federal safety standards. Defines appliances to include household or commercial air conditioners, refrigerators, chillers, and freezers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Commercial and residential property owners, heating and cooling equipment manufacturers, HVAC and refrigeration service technicians, and local building code officials
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly provides an exception for regulations issued by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), preserving MDE's regulatory authority over refrigerants, greenhouse gas emissions, and stratospheric ozone protection.

The Maryland Department of Labor adopts and maintains the Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS) and the International Mechanical Code (IMC), both of which govern building HVAC/refrigeration requirements and are directly constrained by the bill's prohibition on limiting federally approved refrigerants.

Synopsis: Authorizing Prince George's County to exercise powers of eminent domain to acquire and develop or redevelop, for a public purpose, certain neglected property located in the county that has been designated as a transit-oriented development and is located within a business improvement district; and prohibiting land or property taken by the county through the use of eminent domain under the provisions of the Act to be taken without just compensation, as agreed on between the parties, or awarded by a jury.
Title: Prince George's County - Land Use - Development of Neglected Property PG 406-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to exercise eminent domain on certain neglected property. Applies to property designated as a transit-oriented development and located within a business improvement district. Excludes State-owned property from condemnation under this authority. Requires property takings to serve a public purpose, including private development consistent with a public purpose. Prohibits property takings without just compensation first paid or tendered to the entitled party. Defines transit-oriented development to include light rail stops located on the Purple Line in the county.
responsible_party: Prince George's County
stakeholders: Owners of abandoned, blighted, or condemned real property in Prince George's County transit-oriented development areas within business improvement districts; Prince George's County government; private developers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references transit-oriented developments designated under the Transportation Article as well as light rail stops along the Purple Line transit project managed within the state's transportation portfolio.
The department oversees state land use planning and smart growth initiatives, and it was consulted regarding the land use and redevelopment provisions authorized by the bill.
Eminent domain actions and contested just compensation proceedings authorized under the bill are adjudicated in Maryland's circuit courts, which are supported administratively by the agency.

Synopsis: Requiring educational professionals employed by a county board of education, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, or a county public library system who transfer to the Juvenile Services Education Program to be given credit as State employees for certain years of service for the purpose of establishing leave accrual rates; authorizing an individual who transfers to the Program to transfer leave balances in excess of a certain limit under certain circumstances; and applying the Act retroactively.
Title: Juvenile Services Education Program - Transfer of Locally Employed Educational Professionals

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Grants State service credit for leave accrual rates to locally employed educational professionals who transfer to the Juvenile Services Education Program. Requires transferring professionals to be placed in comparable positions compensated at the same hourly rate of their former positions. Directs the creation of a State classification position identification number matching the individual's former salary grade. Authorizes eligible professionals transferring directly without a lapse exceeding 90 days to retain uncompensated accumulated leave balances. Applies leave accumulation and carry-over requirements of State employees upon commencement of Program employment. Applies retroactively to qualifying transfers occurring on or after July 1, 2022.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Locally employed educational professionals from county boards of education, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, or county public library systems transferring to the Juvenile Services Education Program
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State operations or finances, as any operational impacts can be absorbed within existing Department of Juvenile Services resources. Local operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DJS oversees the Juvenile Services Education Program (JSEP) where these transferring educational professionals are employed, and DJS is directly responsible for operationalizing their employment, positions, and leave balances.

DBM serves as the state's central personnel agency and must assist with State classification, position numbers (PINs), and administering the special leave accrual and transfer rules established by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transit Administration to submit a report by December 1, 2023, and each year thereafter on assaults on public transit operators to each local executive authority, the State's Attorney for each county, and certain committees of the General Assembly; and requiring the report to include information on the nature of each assault, the mode of transit involved, the location of the assault, whether the police were involved, and the outcome of any investigation.
Title: Transportation – Assaults on Public Transit Operators – Report

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Harassment; Threats
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to submit an annual report on assaults on public transit operators. Mandates reporting to each local executive authority, county State's Attorneys, and specified General Assembly committees. Directs each report to detail assault incidents, compare multi-state data, and review transit industry best practices. Defines public transit operators to include bus, train, light rail, and subway workers, plus transit station managers. Requires the initial December 1, 2023 report to evaluate local safety policies and five-year assault data.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Public transit operators and transit station managers employed by the Maryland Transit Administration, the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority, or local political subdivisions; county and municipal local executive authorities; county State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for expert consultant costs to evaluate the feasibility of establishing a statewide local transit safety officer. Other reporting requirements are absorbed within existing resources. No effect on State revenues. Local governments can provide data and receive reports within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1049 directly mandates that the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) compile and submit an annual report detailing assaults on public transit operators, conduct multi-state comparative analyses, evaluate safety technologies, and examine the feasibility of establishing a statewide local transit safety officer, with an estimated $50,000 fiscal impact in FY 2024.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the modal administration's operations and finances the bill's implementation costs through the Transportation Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing an applicant to appeal a certain decision issued by the State Public Information Compliance Board; authorizing a party aggrieved by a final judgment of a circuit court in a proceeding for judicial review of a certain decision of the Board to appeal to the Appellate Court of Maryland.
Title: Public Information Act - Decisions of the State Public Information Act Compliance Board - Appeals

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Authorizes an applicant to appeal a decision issued by the State Public Information Act Compliance Board to the circuit court. Provides that an appeal automatically stays the Board's decision pending the circuit court's determination. Specifies venue in the county where the applicant resides or has a principal place of business for certain board decisions. Authorizes a party aggrieved by the circuit court's final judgment to appeal to the Appellate Court of Maryland.
responsible_party: State Public Information Act Compliance Board; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Public Information Act applicants, complainants, public record custodians, and state and local governmental units
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the decisions and appeals process of the State Public Information Act Compliance Board (PIACB), which is a state board established to review and resolve disputes under the Public Information Act.

The bill alters judicial review procedures by clarifying filing venues and authorizing applicants to appeal PIACB decisions to the circuit courts and further appeal final judgments to the Appellate Court of Maryland.

The Office of the Attorney General provides staff support and legal counsel to the Public Information Act Compliance Board, publishes the State's PIA Manual, and represents state agencies in litigation concerning public record disputes.

Synopsis: Establishing in Harford County a performing arts theater beer and wine license that authorizes the holder to sell or serve beer and wine in certain performing arts theaters at retail for on-premises consumption; and establishing an annual license fee of $500.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Performing Arts Theater License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Establishes a performing arts theater beer and wine license in Harford County. Authorizes the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to nonprofit-operated theaters. Allows license holders to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption during performances, intermissions, and designated receptions. Requires license holders to offer snacks for sale whenever beer and wine are sold. Mandates that license holders purchase beer and wine from authorized licensed wholesalers. Sets the annual license fee at $500 effective July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: nonprofit organizations operating performing arts theaters in Harford County, theater patrons, and licensed beer and wine wholesalers
fiscal_impact_summary: Harford County revenues increase by $500 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 from the issuance of one license. Additional county enforcement can be handled with existing resources. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry, including licensed alcohol wholesalers from whom licensees under this bill are required to purchase beer and wine, although direct licensing and local fee collection are handled by Harford County.

Synopsis: Altering the quota used to determine the maximum number of certain alcoholic beverages licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County may issue from one for every 3,000 individuals to one for every 4,000 individuals.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
bill_summary: Alters the population quota used to determine the maximum number of certain off-sale alcoholic beverages licenses in Harford County. Increases the population threshold from 3,000 individuals to 4,000 individuals per license. Prohibits issuing more than one Class A, Class A-1, or Class A-2 license per 4,000 county residents. Bars new license issuance when a class exceeds the quota until revocation or surrender creates a vacancy. Excludes the transfer, conversion, or renewal of an existing license from these quota restrictions.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A, Class A-1, and Class A-2 alcoholic beverages license applicants and license holders in Harford County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Harford County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references population metrics as specified by the Maryland Department of Health to determine the quota formula used for issuing certain alcoholic beverages licenses in Harford County.

Synopsis: Establishing a 6-day and a 7-day Class HC (health club) beer and wine license in Harford County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County to issue the license to a person who sells health club services; exempting the holder of the license from certain distance requirements related to places of worship and schools; establishing an annual fee of $1,300 for a 6-day license and $1,400 for a 7-day license; etc.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class HC (Health Club) License
bill_summary: Establishes 6-day and 7-day Class HC beer and wine licenses in Harford County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County to issue licenses to qualifying health club facilities. Requires qualifying clubs to have at least 150 dues-paying members and swimming pools or pickleball courts. Authorizes license holders to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption from 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. Requires license holders to provide prepackaged food or snacks whenever beer and wine are sold. Exempts Class HC licenses from distance restrictions regarding places of worship and schools.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Harford County
stakeholders: health clubs and health club members in Harford County
fiscal_impact_summary: Harford County revenues increase by an estimated $1,400 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 based on the issuance of one 7-day license. Local enforcement costs can be absorbed with existing resources, and State finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local licensing administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader regulation and distribution of alcoholic beverages from licensed wholesalers.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention to develop strategies to prevent and respond to hate crime activity and evaluate State laws and policies relating to hate crimes; and requiring the Commission to report to the General Assembly on or before December 1 each year, beginning in 2024, on legislative recommendations to address hate crimes in the State.
Title: Hate Crimes - Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention in the Office of the Attorney General. Requires the Attorney General to appoint commission members representing designated advocacy organizations, law enforcement, and the public. Directs the commission to develop prevention and response strategies and evaluate State hate crime laws and policies. Requires annual reports by December 1, beginning in 2024, to the State Department of Education and the General Assembly. Mandates annual State budget funding beginning in fiscal year 2025 for a full-time assistant Attorney General.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention
stakeholders: victims of hate crimes, community advocacy and civil rights organizations, law enforcement agencies, and Maryland public school students and educators
fiscal_impact_summary: Federal fund expenditures increase by $114,400 in FY 2024 for a contractual assistant Attorney General. General fund expenditures increase by $136,300 in FY 2025 for a permanent assistant Attorney General and ongoing operating costs under a mandated appropriation. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1066 establishes the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). The Attorney General appoints members, serves as chair (or designates a chair), and OAG provides staff for the commission, with direct fiscal impacts for personnel and operational costs.
The Maryland Center for School Safety is designated as a mandatory member of the newly established Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is statutorily designated to have a representative serve as a member of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

The Commission is required to report annually to the State Department of Education on policy recommendations to address hate crimes that occur in schools. Additionally, the Maryland Center for School Safety resides within MSDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new permanent state advisory and policy body, the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

The bill designates a representative of the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), which operates under the Maryland State Police as the state's intelligence fusion center, to serve as a commission member.
The bill creates a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include funding in the annual state budget starting in fiscal 2025 to support the commission and staff.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2025.

Synopsis: Altering the maximum fines for smoking cannabis in a public place; prohibiting a law enforcement officer from initiating a stop or a search of a person, a motor vehicle, or a vessel based solely on certain factors; prohibiting, under certain circumstances, a law enforcement officer from conducting a search of a certain area of a motor vehicle or vessel; providing that evidence obtained in violation of certain provisions of the Act is not admissible in certain proceedings; etc.
Title: Criminal Law and Procedure - Cannabis - Fines for Smoking in Public, Stops, and Searches
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 802

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Reduces maximum civil fines for smoking cannabis in a public place to $50 for first violations and $150 thereafter. Prohibits law enforcement officers from stopping or searching persons, vehicles, or vessels based solely on burnt or unburnt cannabis odor. Bars stops or searches based solely on personal use cannabis possession or nearby cash lacking distribution indicia. Limits vehicle and vessel searches during cannabis impairment investigations to readily accessible areas or those containing relevant evidence. Excludes evidence obtained in violation of these provisions, including consensual evidence, from admissibility in any trial or proceeding.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Department of Natural Resources Police; Maryland Transportation Authority Police; Maryland Transit Administration Police; Judiciary of Maryland
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, motor vehicle drivers, vessel operators, individuals possessing or using cannabis, criminal defendants, and prosecutors
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in State general fund revenues and incarceration expenditures due to lowered public smoking fines and fewer arrests and convictions. Local revenues and detention expenditures also decrease minimally from fewer fine collections and reduced local jail commitments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly governed by the bill's restrictions on initiating stops or searches based solely on the odor of cannabis, personal use possession, or the presence of cash, as well as the limitations on vehicle searches during impaired driving investigations.

The Judiciary and state courts are directly impacted by adjudicating suppression motions under the new statutory exclusionary rule, handling altered civil fine amounts for smoking cannabis in public, and managing associated court caseloads and fine revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent clients who will be directly affected by these search, seizure, and stop limitations, and its attorneys will litigate suppression issues under the bill's new evidentiary exclusion provisions.

The bill explicitly restricts searches of vessels and references violations under § 8-738 of the Natural Resources Article, directly affecting enforcement operations and vessel stops conducted by the Natural Resources Police.
The bill specifically references impaired driving under § 21-902 of the Transportation Article and governs search procedures during traffic stops conducted by MDOT modal law enforcement divisions.

The Maryland Transportation Authority operates its own sworn police force that conducts traffic stops and enforcement on state toll facilities and highways, directly subjecting its officers to the bill's stop and search limitations.

The Maryland Transit Administration maintains a sworn police force responsible for transit enforcement, directly impacting their procedures regarding pedestrian stops, vehicle searches, and enforcement of public smoking restrictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is anticipated to have a minimal fiscal impact on state incarceration expenditures by reducing the number of arrests, charges, and convictions leading to commitments in state correctional facilities.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in appellate litigation concerning Fourth Amendment questions, statutory search limitations, and evidentiary suppression disputes arising under this Act.

Synopsis: Allowing an individual or a business entity to claim a credit against the State income tax for the first $500 of the purchase price of an automated external defibrillator purchased for use at a restaurant location in the State with annual gross income of at least $400,000; prohibiting the credit from being claimed more than once by any individual or business entity for each restaurant location; and providing certain other limitations.
Title: Income Tax - Automated External Defibrillator Tax Credit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Authorizes a nonrefundable State income tax credit for an individual or business entity that owns a restaurant in Maryland. Sets the credit amount equal to the first $500 of the purchase price of an automated external defibrillator. Limits the credit to restaurant locations with annual gross income of at least $400,000. Restricts the credit to one automated external defibrillator per location, claimable only once per location. Caps the credit at the lesser of $1,500 or State income tax liability per taxable year. Prohibits carrying over unused credit amounts to any other taxable year.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Owners of restaurants in Maryland with annual gross income of at least $400,000
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by an estimated $1.12 million in FY 2024, $1.40 million in FY 2025, and $281,000 in FY 2026 across the general fund, Higher Education Investment Fund, and Transportation Trust Fund. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $63,000 in FY 2024 for tax system updates. Local highway user revenues decrease by an estimated $69,000 total from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for administering the state's income tax system, implementing and processing the new automated external defibrillator (AED) tax credit, and updating tax forms and software systems, incurring $63,000 in implementation expenditures in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the Maryland Public Access AED Program, under which facilities must register AEDs, assign coordinators, and maintain equipment, providing key regulatory oversight and operational context for the AED acquisitions incentivized by this bill.

The bill's corporate income tax credits reduce distributions to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), resulting in special fund revenue losses and reductions in local highway user revenue grants administered through MDOT.

Synopsis: Altering the duties and responsibilities of the Prince George's County Board of Education and certain officers of the county board; altering the voting authority of the student board member; requiring the county board to retain counsel and pay certain counsel fees and expenses incurred for defending a member in litigation involving a member's service in the member's official capacity on the county board under certain circumstances; altering certain procedures for the election of the student member of the county board; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Board of Education and School System Revisions PG 502-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Revises the governance, operations, and ethics requirements for the Prince George’s County Board of Education. Expands the voting rights of the student board member to include operating budgets and student discipline. Establishes annual retreats, self-evaluations, and professional development requirements for elected school board members. Mandates the county board retain legal counsel and cover defense costs for members acting without malice. Increases annual compensation for the board chair to $30,000 and elected members to $27,000 in 2026. Requires candidates for elected board seats to reside in their district for one year before the election.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education; Prince George's County Public Schools; Maryland State Board of Education
stakeholders: Prince George's County Board of Education members and candidates, Prince George's County Public Schools students, and Prince George's County Public Schools
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Prince George’s County Board of Education expenditures increase by $48,400 in FY 2027 and $83,000 annually thereafter for member compensation increases, alongside an indeterminate expenditure increase beginning in FY 2024 for member legal defense fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the authority and procedures of the State Board of Education regarding the removal of Prince George's County Board of Education members, allowing the State Board to remove a member for specified causes without requiring gubernatorial approval.
The bill eliminates the requirement that the Governor approve the removal of a member of the Prince George's County Board of Education by the State Board of Education.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of the inspection tax levied on marketable oysters shipped in the shell to any place outside the State from 30 cents to $1 per bushel; increasing the amount of the severance tax levied on oysters caught within certain natural oyster bars from $1 to $2 per bushel; repealing a certain requirement that a certain tax increase be used for the oyster seed program; and requiring that $1 of each $2 of the severance tax levied be used by certain county oyster committees for the repletion of natural oyster bars.
Title: Natural Resources - Oyster Inspection and Severance Taxes - Increase

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Increases the severance tax on oysters caught on Maryland natural oyster bars from $1 to $2 per bushel. Raises the inspection tax on marketable out-of-state oyster shell shipments from 30 cents to $1 per bushel. Requires $1 of each $2 severance tax collected to be used by designated county oyster committees for oyster bar repletion. Repeals an obsolete allocation requirement that dedicated a prior tax increase to the oyster seed program. Clarifies tax payment obligations when licensed harvesters sell oysters directly to consumers in the State.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: licensed oyster harvesters and sellers, oyster buyers and receivers, out-of-state oyster shippers, and county oyster committees in 11 specified counties
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Fisheries Research and Development Fund increase by approximately $580,900 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to increased tax collections and repletion expenditures. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1084 directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as it increases the oyster inspection tax and severance tax, which are collected by DNR and credited to the Fisheries Research and Development Fund. The department oversees these funds to support natural oyster bar repletion alongside county oyster committees, generating an estimated $580,900 annually in special fund revenues and expenditures.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow a person to hunt game birds and mammals on each Sunday of the game bird and game mammal seasons from 30 minutes before sunrise until 10:30 a.m. in Wicomico County; authorizing the Department to allow Sunday hunting in Wicomico County on public land, subject to certain time restrictions; and adding Wicomico County to the list of counties in which the safety zone for archery hunters extends 50 yards from certain structures occupied by human beings.
Title: Wicomico County - Sunday Hunting and Archery Hunting Safety Zones
bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to allow hunting of game birds and mammals on Sundays in Wicomico County. Applies this hunting authority to private property and designated public land from 30 minutes before sunrise until 10:30 a.m. Lifts the morning time restriction on specified Sundays during deer firearms and deer bow hunting seasons. Reduces the archery hunting safety zone in Wicomico County from 150 yards to 50 yards from occupied structures.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, archery hunters, property owners, and outdoor sports businesses in Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1087 directly authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to allow and regulate hunting on Sundays on private property and designated public lands in Wicomico County, and oversees enforcement of hunting regulations and safety zones.

Synopsis: Altering a certain exemption from property tax for real property that is located in Baltimore County that is owned by an incorporated, nonprofit fire company or rescue squad by providing that the exemption applies only if the property is used or will be used exclusively for the purposes of the fire company or rescue squad; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Baltimore County - Property Tax Exemption - Real Property Owned by Fire Company or Rescue Squad

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Alters the property tax exemption for real property owned by nonprofit fire companies or rescue squads in Baltimore County. Specifies that the exemption applies only under certain exclusive use criteria. Requires the real property to be actually used exclusively for fire company or rescue squad purposes. Alternatively covers real property not used for any purpose that will be used exclusively for squad purposes in the future. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Baltimore County
stakeholders: Incorporated, nonprofit fire companies and rescue squads in Baltimore County, and Baltimore County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and Baltimore County property tax revenues will not be significantly affected. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The board adjudicates appeals regarding real property tax assessments and exemptions, including disputes over eligibility for exemptions granted to nonprofit entities such as fire companies and rescue squads.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals from Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards concerning real property tax exemptions and assessments.
The Treasurer manages the Annuity Bond Fund, which receives state property tax revenue used for general obligation debt service and is referenced in the fiscal note regarding state revenue impacts.

Synopsis: Authorizing Prince George's County to create certain business improvement districts intended to promote the general welfare of the residents, employers, employees, property owners, tenants, consumers, and general public with the geographic area of the districts; requiring the county to adopt certain local laws to provide for the creation and organization of a district; removing Prince George's County from the scope of law governing the establishment of business improvement districts; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Economic Development - Business Improvement Districts PG 407-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to establish business improvement districts and exempts the county from statewide district law. Lowers the parcel owner petition threshold for establishing or expanding a district from 80% to 51%. Permits condominium and cooperative housing corporations within a proposed district to petition to join. Establishes a district board of at least nine members, retaining local state legislators as nonvoting members. Requires the county to impose a district tax on nonexempt property owners to fund district operations. Mandates a review of each district's effectiveness and desirability by the county every three years.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Government
stakeholders: Commercial property owners, commercial tenants, residential property owners, condominium and cooperative housing corporations, and small businesses in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Prince George's County expenditures may increase minimally to hold additional public hearings. Local revenues and expenditures will be affected depending on the number of districts established or expanded, though district administrative costs are recoverable through district taxes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland serves as the state's chief tax and financial officer and was consulted as an information source on the fiscal note regarding tax provisions. However, the business improvement district tax authorized by the bill is collected and administered locally by Prince George's County, resulting in no direct state fiscal or administrative impact.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article to establish a framework for business improvement districts in Prince George's County aimed at promoting business and economic vitality. While relevant to the Department of Commerce's overarching economic development mission, the bill grants local authority directly to Prince George's County and does not assign regulatory or administrative duties to the department.

Synopsis: Authorizing Baltimore County to honor certificates of guarantee that are issued by certain associations or on behalf of certain contractors in order to satisfy certain county bond requirements; and providing that Baltimore County is not required under certain provisions of law to honor certain certificates of guarantee.
Title: Baltimore County - Insurance - Certificates of Guarantee for County Bond Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore County to honor certificates of guarantee issued on behalf of contractors for county bond requirements. Applies to instruments issued by an approved nonprofit contractor association or its wholly owned subsidiary. Permits contractors to use certificates to satisfy bond requirements for public improvements or other county requirements. Specifies that Baltimore County is not required to honor any certificate of guarantee. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Baltimore County; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Baltimore County; contractors performing public works or improvements; nonprofit associations of contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact; the Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce the bill with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore County finances are expected to experience minimal impact because honoring the certificates is permissive rather than mandatory.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 1-203 of the Insurance Article to allow Baltimore County to accept certificates of guarantee from contractor associations for county bond requirements. The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance under this article and can handle oversight with existing resources.

Synopsis: Altering the requirements for governance of libraries designated as regional resource centers; and establishing a governing board for each regional resource center.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes a governing board for each library designated as a regional resource center. Reconstitutes the former board of advisors as a regional advisory council composed of member library system directors. Requires each governing board to appoint a center director, approve the annual budget, and determine center policies. Designates the Board of Trustees of the Washington County Free Library as the Western Maryland center governing board. Repeals requirements that a selected regional center be the strongest and most centrally located regional library.
responsible_party: State Library Board; Maryland State Library Agency; State Librarian
stakeholders: regional resource centers, participating public library systems, library trustees, regional library staff, and library patrons in Western Maryland, Southern Maryland, and the Eastern Shore
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. Any expense reimbursements for governing board members are expected to be covered with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency (through the State Library Board and State Librarian) provides direct oversight, standards, and regulatory approval for regional resource centers, including approving center establishment, approving independent auditors, and receiving annual financial and operational reports.
The bill explicitly subjects the regional resource centers and their governing boards to audits by the Office of Legislative Audits regarding any State funds received.

The bill stipulates that any selection of location and plans for the erection of regional resource center buildings by a governing board is subject to the approval of the Governor, as well as the State Library Board.

The bill requires that the appointed director of a regional resource center must be eligible for certification as a professional library director by the State Superintendent of Schools under MSDE regulations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program in the Department of Transportation; and authorizing program funds to be sourced from federal and State public transportation programs.
Title: Transit - Grant Funding for Local Service - Alterations
