Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation. Directs the program to provide funding to locally operated transit systems throughout the State. Authorizes transit systems to use grants for capital, operating, planning, and other eligible expenses determined by the department. Permits grant funds to be sourced from specified federal and State public transportation programs. Requires total program grants to exceed $107,997,575 adjusted for inflation beginning in fiscal year 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: locally operated transit systems in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill codifies an existing grant program within the Maryland Department of Transportation without affecting overall funding levels.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily establishes and requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to administer the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program, determining eligible expenses and sourcing funds from designated federal and State transportation programs.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for directing funding and technical assistance to locally operated transit systems throughout Maryland, the MTA is directly involved in the operational execution of grants to local transit providers.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Harford County to enact a local law providing for the membership and terms of the Harford County Advisory Plumbing Board.
Title: Harford County - Advisory Plumbing Board

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Harford County to enact a local law setting membership and terms for its Advisory Plumbing Board. Repeals statutory requirements that the board consist of a physician, a plumber, and one other individual. Repeals the specific four-year term requirement previously mandated in state law. Retains the requirement that the county governing body appoint an Advisory Plumbing Board upon adopting a plumbing code.
responsible_party: Governing Body of Harford County
stakeholders: Members of the Harford County Advisory Plumbing Board and Harford County officials administering the county plumbing code
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies current county appointment practices and does not affect Harford County finances.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with the Maryland Hospital Association, to conduct a survey of hospitals to identify the availability of hospital operating resources for dentist use; requiring the Department and the Maryland Health Care Commission, in consultation with the Maryland Hospital Association, to develop regional plans to ensure the availability of appropriate operating space for the performance of dental procedures for Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission - Dental Services - Survey and Regional Needs Assessment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to survey hospitals on operating room resource availability for dentist use. Directs both agencies to conduct a regional needs assessment for dental procedures that require anesthesia or moderate sedation. Requires both agencies to develop regional plans ensuring appropriate operating room space for Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients. Mandates consultation with the Maryland Hospital Association and the Maryland Ambulatory Surgery Association during the assessment. Requires the agencies to submit a joint final report to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, licensed dentists, anesthesiologists, acute care hospitals, and ambulatory surgery centers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission can complete the required survey, needs assessment, and regional plans using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1146 directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with conducting a hospital survey on operating room availability for dentists, co-conducting a regional needs assessment for dental procedures requiring anesthesia, co-developing regional access plans for Medicaid recipients, and submitting a joint report to the General Assembly.

HB 1146 directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission jointly conduct a regional needs assessment regarding dental procedures requiring anesthesia or sedation, jointly develop regional plans to ensure operating room space for Medicaid recipients, and jointly report findings to legislative committees.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to make recommendations to provide appropriate, accessible, and comprehensive behavioral health services that are available on demand to individuals in the State; establishing the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of Health; requiring the Department to apply for certain federal planning grant funds; requiring the Department to apply to participate in a certain demonstration program; etc.
Title: Behavioral Health Care - Treatment and Access (Behavioral Health Model for Maryland)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to recommend improvements across the behavioral health continuum. Creates a three-year value-based purchasing pilot program in the Maryland Department of Health for intensive care coordination. Mandates a $600,000 annual state appropriation for the pilot program in fiscal years 2025 through 2027. Extends telehealth payment parity and coverage for audio-only telephone conversations through June 30, 2025. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to apply for federal planning grants and certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration programs. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study telehealth delivery and payment parity by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
stakeholders: individuals with behavioral health conditions, specialty behavioral health care providers, Medicaid recipients, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $397,700 in FY 2024 for contractual staff and consultant costs, and by roughly $723,300 to $734,300 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027, reflecting a mandated $600,000 annual appropriation for the pilot program and ongoing staffing. Continued telehealth coverage has an indeterminate impact on overall Medicaid expenditures. Local health benefit expenditures may increase minimally to maintain telehealth reimbursement parity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill; it is required to staff the new Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, administer the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program, apply for federal CCBHC planning grants and demonstration programs, and maintain extended Medicaid telehealth coverage and payment parity.

The bill explicitly mandates MHCC to conduct an in-depth study and submit recommendations to the General Assembly regarding telehealth delivery and payment parity across audio-only and audiovisual services. MHCC's Executive Director is also a designated member of the newly formed commission.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, and MIA oversees commercial health insurers complying with the two-year extension of telehealth requirements and payment parity.

The Governor is required to jointly designate the chair of the new commission, appoint numerous stakeholder members, mandate an annual budget appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program for FY 2025–2027, and receive annual reports from the commission and MDH.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a significant new state body—the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access—along with four mandated specialized workgroups to develop long-term statewide behavioral health strategies.

The Executive Director of HSCRC is designated as an ex officio member of the commission, and the bill references HSCRC's rate-setting authority in relation to hospital facility fees for telehealth services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (identified in statute as Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) is named as a member of the commission to address criminal-justice and youth behavioral health challenges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of DPSCS is designated as a member of the commission to address the behavioral health needs of the state's forensic, court-ordered, and incarcerated populations.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is named as a commission member to provide expertise on youth behavioral health issues and juvenile justice-involved youth.
The Secretary of Disabilities is designated as a commission member to focus on behavioral health access for individuals with developmental and complex disabilities.
The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member of the commission to coordinate behavioral health access across social services and vulnerable populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: A representative of the Office of the Public Defender is designated as a member of the commission to advise on court-ordered treatment, forensic populations, and criminal justice-involved behavioral health.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in vetting and appointing the 22 gubernatorial appointees across diverse stakeholder categories to the newly created commission.
DBM is responsible for managing executive budget operations, which includes executing the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program in fiscal years 2025 through 2027.

Synopsis: Requiring certain Medicaid funding to be used to provide community services to individuals waiting for services through waiver programs; authorizing certain Medicaid funding to be used for expanding provider capacity in certain waiver programs; and altering the uses of certain funding appropriated to the Dedicated Purpose Account in the fiscal year 2023 budget bill.
Title: Medicaid Waiver Programs - Waitlist and Registry Reduction (End the Wait Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Alters the use of $30,000,000 appropriated to the Dedicated Purpose Account in the fiscal 2023 budget bill. Requires Medicaid funds to provide community services to individuals on waitlists for specified home- and community-based waiver programs. Authorizes funding to expand provider capacity, hire and retain staff, and increase reimbursement rates across these waivers. Extends provider capacity expansion provisions to include the Autism Waiver. Authorizes annual budget funding beginning in fiscal year 2024 to hire and retain waiver providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Individuals on waitlists or registries for Medicaid waiver programs and community-based service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State revenues or expenditures because the bill redirects existing appropriations rather than requiring new funding. Up to $20.0 million in fiscal 2023 Dedicated Purpose Account funds is repurposed to provide community services to individuals on waiver waitlists and expand provider capacity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the state's Medicaid program and the specified Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver programs, expanding provider capacity, and executing plans to reduce waiver waitlists.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) jointly develops plans with MDH regarding the Autism Waiver, applies to CMS for waiver expansions, and receives a dedicated transfer of at least $10 million for students with disabilities.
DBM is responsible for processing the budget amendments to transfer funds from the Dedicated Purpose Account and overseeing state budget allocations required to reduce waiver program waitlists.

The Governor's Office receives the waiver reduction plans developed by MDH and is statutorily directed to include sufficient funds in the annual state budget bill to carry out waitlist reduction and provider retention goals.

Synopsis: Making certain shared appreciation agreements subject to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and other provisions of law that regulate certain loans of single extensions of closed end credit and revolving credit plans; and authorizing the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt certain regulations regarding the enforcement of and compliance with provisions of law that regulate shared appreciation agreements.
Title: Commercial Law and Financial Institutions - Credit Regulation - Shared Appreciation Agreements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Subjects shared appreciation agreements to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and state credit regulations. Classifies funds advanced under a shared appreciation agreement as loans under revolving and closed end credit laws. Governs agreements that allow readvancing repaid funds under revolving credit provisions regardless of written election. Places agreements that do not allow readvancing under closed end credit provisions regardless of written election. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt regulations regarding enforcement and compliance.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Homeowners entering into shared appreciation agreements and credit grantors, lenders, or brokers offering or servicing them
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected because the bill generally codifies and clarifies existing practice. Certain small business lenders offering shared appreciation agreements may incur licensing and compliance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants regulatory and enforcement authority over shared appreciation agreements to the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR), which is a regulatory agency within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General advises on and enforces consumer protection laws concerning credit transactions and lending practices under the Commercial Law Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for all services rendered to an enrollee by a licensed pharmacist within the pharmacist's lawful scope of practice to the same extent as services rendered by any other health care practitioner; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed by January 1, 2024.
Title: Health Insurance - Reimbursement for Services Rendered by a Pharmacist

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and specified health insurance carriers to cover pharmacist services. Mandates coverage to the same extent as services rendered by any other licensed health care provider. Prohibits conditioning reimbursement on employment by a physician, pharmacy, or facility, or acting under physician orders. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to obtain any necessary federal program waivers by January 1, 2024. Applies to policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, pharmacies, Medicaid and Maryland Children's Health Program enrollees, covered insured individuals, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 (51% federal funds, 49% general funds) due to potential increased billing for covered services in Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program, with federal revenues increasing accordingly. Expenditures for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans may also increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program, both administered by the Department of Health, to cover services rendered by licensed pharmacists. The bill specifically directs the department to apply for and obtain any necessary federal waivers or state plan amendments, resulting in an indeterminate fiscal impact.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-716, requiring private insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to reimburse pharmacists for services within their lawful scope of practice. As the state's insurance regulator, the agency oversees carrier compliance with this coverage requirement.

The department oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and the overall state budget, including general fund expenditures associated with state health programs, although the fiscal impact on the state employee plan is determined to be non-material.

The agency regulates and offers individual and small group health benefit plans through Maryland Health Connection, which must conform to state insurance mandate revisions regarding pharmacist reimbursement parity.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations that establish certain food service facility standards that are appropriate to residential programs that have less than 17 residents.
Title: Behavioral Health Programs - Residential Programs - Food Service Facility Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing appropriate food service facility standards. Applies these standards to licensed residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents. Covers low-intensity, medium-intensity, high-intensity, and intensive residential substance-related disorder treatment programs. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Operators and residents of licensed residential behavioral health treatment programs with fewer than 17 residents
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and local finances experience no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing appropriate food service facility standards for residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents.

Synopsis: Providing that a therapy management contract may be entered into in writing or orally; requiring, if a therapy management contract is entered into orally, the parties to the therapy management contract to reduce the contract to writing within 30 days after entering into the therapy management contract; and providing that a therapy management contract may be in electronic form.
Title: Pharmacists - Therapy Management Contract - Form

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: Authorizes a therapy management contract to be entered into orally or in writing, including electronic form. Requires parties to reduce an oral therapy management contract to writing within 30 days after entering into it. Repeals the requirement that a therapy management contract be initially written. Replaces the requirement that parties sign the contract with a requirement that they agree on it. Applies to licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients under a prescriber-pharmacist agreement.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients entering into therapy management contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees health occupations and regulatory boards, including the State Board of Pharmacy under Title 12 of the Health Occupations Article, which regulates pharmacist practice, protocols, and therapy management contracts.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which a dentist who is a faculty member at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry and was trained at a foreign dental school must be qualified by the State Board of Dental Examiners to take an examination offered by the American Board of Dental Examiners, Inc., or its successor organization.
Title: State Board of Dental Examiners - University of Maryland School of Dentistry Faculty - Qualifying for Examination

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: Expands qualifications for foreign-trained faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry to take the ADEX examination. Qualifies general dentists who complete a general dental practice residency or an advanced education in general dentistry program. Qualifies general dentists who are board certified by the American Board of General Dentistry. Requires applicants to have completed at least seven consecutive years as full-time faculty members at the school. Requires applicants to submit a written letter of support from the University of Maryland School of Dentistry.
responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
stakeholders: foreign-trained dentist faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Dental Examiners special fund revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license fees, with expenditures absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Dental Examiners is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health responsible for qualifying applicants, administering licensing standards, and regulating dental professionals in Maryland.

The bill directly impacts full-time foreign-trained dental faculty at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) and requires the school to provide written letters of support for qualifying candidates.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to conduct a study on the utilization of the expedited licensing process for service members, veterans, and military spouses for certain occupational and professional licenses in the State; and requiring the Maryland Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by June 30, 2024.
Title: Study on the Utilization of the Expedited Licensing Process for Service Members, Veterans, and Military Spouses

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to study expedited occupational and professional licensing for service members, veterans, and military spouses. Directs the department to conduct the study in consultation with the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs. Examines the utilization of military experience, education, and training credit toward State licensing requirements. Evaluates outreach efforts, website visibility, and best practices compared to other states. Mandates reporting of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by June 30, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Service members, veterans, and military spouses seeking occupational and professional licenses in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Department of Labor and Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs can conduct the study and report using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the study on expedited licensing utilization for service members, veterans, and military spouses and reporting the findings.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families (referenced in statute as the Department of Veterans Affairs) is statutorily required to be consulted by the Department of Labor in conducting the study and preparing the report.
The bill requires the Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to submit the final report and recommendations of the study to the Governor by June 30, 2024.

Synopsis: Correcting certain references to the Comptroller of Maryland to be the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, as appropriate; and clarifying certain powers and duties of the Executive Director of the Commission relating to alcoholic beverages regulation and enforcement.
Title: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission – Technical Corrections and Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills

bill_summary: Updates statutory references from the Comptroller of Maryland to the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission. Clarifies the Executive Director's authority to issue licenses, conduct inspections, and enforce laws governing alcoholic beverages and tobacco. Grants concurrent enforcement, search, and seizure powers to the Commission and the Comptroller. Authorizes the Executive Director to seize contraband property and sell forfeited conveyances at public auction. Repeals obsolete provisions and penalties relating to alcoholic beverage tax stamps.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, common carriers, and tobacco product licensees and distributors in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practices and administrative responsibilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates numerous sections across the Maryland Code to remove obsolete references to the Comptroller and reassign regulatory and enforcement duties over alcohol and tobacco to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, while clarifying joint and retained tax administration and enforcement authorities of the Comptroller.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate and consult with the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, along with the Comptroller, to develop ongoing strategies for enforcing prohibitions on tobacco and cannabinoid sales to minors.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State's Attorney of Calvert County to designate county attorneys or assistant county attorneys to prosecute civil infractions; and authorizing the designated attorneys to exercise the powers of the State's Attorney when prosecuting civil infractions.
Title: Calvert County - Civil Infractions - Prosecutorial Designations
bill_summary: Authorizes the State's Attorney of Calvert County to designate the county attorney or an assistant county attorney to prosecute civil infractions. Requires the designation to receive the approval of the county commissioners. Allows a designated attorney to exercise the powers of the State's Attorney regarding civil infractions. Applies solely to civil infraction proceedings within Calvert County. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State's Attorney of Calvert County; County Commissioners of Calvert County; Calvert County Attorney's Office
stakeholders: individuals cited for civil infractions in Calvert County; State's Attorney of Calvert County; Calvert County Attorney and assistant county attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Any operational impact on Calvert County is not expected to materially affect local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Civil infractions prosecuted under this authority are adjudicated within the Maryland court system, for which the Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support. AOC was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of certain criminal records based on a conviction for certain hunting offenses.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Hunting Offenses - Expungement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a person convicted of specified misdemeanor hunting offenses to file a petition for record expungement. Applies to hunting without a license, failing to wear fluorescent clothing, and other specified natural resources violations. Prohibits filing a petition earlier than 10 years after satisfying all sentences imposed for the convictions. Requires courts and law enforcement agencies to remove eligible records from public inspection upon court order. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of specified misdemeanor hunting offenses under the Natural Resources Article
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase for the Judiciary through fiscal 2026 to process additional expungement petitions, though the exact cost cannot be reliably determined. General fund revenues increase minimally from expungement petition filing fees. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for expungement of convictions for specified hunting offenses, requiring the District Court and Circuit Court clerks to process new petitions for expungement and manage court record expungements, resulting in an operational and fiscal impact.

The bill authorizes expungement for specific misdemeanor hunting offenses regulated under Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article, impacting police and administrative enforcement records maintained by DNR and its Natural Resources Police.

Synopsis: Altering a certain benefit amount for certain fire and rescue volunteers; and authorizing the board of commissioners to approve an increase in benefit payment for certain fire and rescue volunteers.
Title: Calvert County - Length of Service Award Program - Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Increases death and burial benefits under the Calvert County Length of Service Award Program for volunteer emergency personnel. Raises the maximum death benefit for a qualified volunteer with 25 years of service from $6,000 to $10,000. Raises the maximum burial benefit for specified volunteers from $240 to $336 for each year of certified service. Increases the line-of-duty death benefit for a qualified volunteer from $6,000 to $10,000. Authorizes the Calvert County Board of County Commissioners to approve benefit increases matching cost-of-living increases for county employees.
responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Calvert County volunteer fire company, rescue squad, and rescue dive team members and their beneficiaries
fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures may increase by at least $450,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to potential cost-of-living benefit increases, along with minimal expenditure increases for higher death benefits. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the State Workers' Compensation Commission as the determining entity for whether a qualified volunteer's death occurred in the line of duty, which qualifies the individual's estate or beneficiary for an increased death benefit.

Synopsis: Defining "generating station" as it relates to the requirement to obtain a certificate of public convenience and necessity or approval from the Public Service Commission for a person who constructs a generating station that has the capacity to produce more than 2 but not more than 14 megawatts of electricity from a solar photovoltaic system; requiring an electric company to provide meter aggregation for certain eligible customer-generators under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity and Meter Aggregation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Excludes specified electric generating facilities and multi-unit combinations from the statutory definition of generating station. Authorizes construction of qualifying solar photovoltaic combinations up to 14 megawatts cumulative capacity without a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Requires each individual unit within an exempt combination to produce not more than 2 megawatts and be separately metered. Requires electric companies to provide meter aggregation upon written request to qualifying eligible customer-generators. Includes agricultural users, nonprofits, local governments, State units, and public senior higher education institutions as eligible entities. Mandates customer-generators provide written allocation instructions for excess generation credits before meter aggregation begins.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: electric companies, solar energy developers, agricultural electricity customers, nonprofit organizations, municipal and county governments, State agencies, and public senior higher education institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, though state agencies may review fewer Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity applications. Local government expenditures may increase significantly in some jurisdictions if local officials choose to study, regulate, or review projects that bypass the state certificate process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating electric utilities, issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN), processing CPCN exemptions, and overseeing net energy metering and meter aggregation regulations.

The Department of Natural Resources, through its Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), participates directly in reviewing CPCN applications and environmental impact evaluations, and may see a reduction in CPCN applications to review under the bill.

The Department of the Environment participates in environmental evaluations of CPCN applications and regulates brownfield and landfill sites referenced in the bill's definitions, and may have fewer CPCN applications to review.
The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in Public Service Commission proceedings related to utility rates, grid safety, and renewable generation regulations.
The Maryland Energy Administration manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which receives any unreturned or abandoned application deposits from escrow accounts under the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices relating to elder abuse and crimes commonly committed against older adults; and requiring the Task Force to submit a final report by December 31, 2024, to the Governor and the General Assembly with its findings and recommendations regarding changes to State law, policy, and practice that would aid in preventing elder abuse.
Title: Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Elder Abuse and Neglect -see also- Vulnerable Adults
Vulnerable Adults -see also- Developmental Disabilities; Eld

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse. Directs the Maryland Department of Aging to provide staff for the Task Force. Requires the Task Force to study existing laws, policies, and practices relating to elder abuse. Requires recommendations on statutory, policy, and practice changes regarding funding, oversight, and prosecution. Directs the Task Force to submit a preliminary report by December 31, 2023. Requires a final report by December 31, 2024, before the act terminates June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse
stakeholders: older adults in Maryland, victims of elder abuse, legal advocates, and elder care service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $26,500 in fiscal 2024 and $11,400 in fiscal 2025 for part-time contractual staff to assist the Task Force. State revenues are unaffected, and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary agency tasked with staffing the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse. The Secretary of Aging and the Maryland Long-Term Care Ombudsman serve on the task force, and the agency incurs a direct fiscal impact for hiring contractual staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes a temporary entity, the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse, to study laws and make recommendations on elder abuse prevention and prosecution.
The Governor is responsible for designating the chair of the Task Force, appointing 11 members, and receiving preliminary and final reports from the Task Force.
The Attorney General or their designee is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force, which will study laws and prosecution methods relating to elder abuse.
The Task Force includes the Maryland Chief Medical Examiner and a representative of the Office of Health Care Quality, both of which are units within the Maryland Department of Health.
The Task Force includes the Director of the Office of Adult Services (which oversees Adult Protective Services within the Department of Human Services).
The bill requires the Governor to appoint a representative of the Maryland Health Care Commission to serve as a member of the Task Force.
The bill mandates that a representative of the Maryland State Police be appointed by the Governor to serve on the Task Force.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees, which includes multiple members and the chair of the newly created Task Force.
The bill includes representation from the Circuit Court Guardianship program and discusses judicial and court recognition and adjudication of elder abuse crimes.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from parking certain vehicles in the Town of Sharpsburg, Washington County, subject to a certain exception.
Title: Town of Sharpsburg - Parking of Vehicles - Restrictions

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits parking certain trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses on streets or highways in Sharpsburg. Excludes Class A passenger vehicles and qualifying Class E trucks. Allows parking when essential to the immediate use of the vehicle. Imposes a separate fine for each vehicle in a combination tractor and trailer. Treats each day of a violation as a separate offense.
responsible_party: Town of Sharpsburg
stakeholders: Drivers and owners of commercial trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses in the Town of Sharpsburg
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. Local enforcement can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article to restrict the parking of specified vehicle classes on streets and highways in the Town of Sharpsburg.
The District Court and judicial system process citations and contested violations under the Maryland Vehicle Law, including statutory parking restrictions and fines.

Synopsis: Establishing a minimum training course compensation of $50 and minimum daily compensation of $250 for election judges for each election day and each early voting day actually served; requiring the State Board of Elections to reimburse each local board elections for $50 of the extra compensation that is paid to each returning election judge; and requiring the State Board to develop and implement a marketing campaign to assist in the recruitment of individuals to serve as election judges.
Title: Elections - Election Judges - Minimum Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Establishes minimum compensation rates for election judges across Maryland. Mandates daily pay of at least $250 for first-time election judges for each election day and early voting day served. Requires returning election judges to receive at least $100 more per day than first-time judges. Sets compensation at a minimum of $50 for completing each required course of instruction. Directs the State Board of Elections to reimburse local boards $50 per returning judge and to implement a recruitment marketing campaign.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
stakeholders: election judges, returning election judges, local boards of elections, and county governing bodies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.6 million to $2.1 million annually beginning in FY 2024 for returning judge reimbursements and marketing costs. Local government expenditures increase collectively by approximately $3.2 million to $3.8 million annually beginning in FY 2024 to fund higher compensation and marketing shares. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) to reimburse local boards of elections for $50 of the extra compensation paid to each returning election judge and to develop and provide a comprehensive marketing campaign to recruit election judges statewide, resulting in significant annual general fund expenditures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide coverage for biomarker testing that is supported by medical and scientific evidence; establishing requirements for deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for biomarker testing; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the impact of providing biomarker testing.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Biomarker Testing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide coverage for biomarker testing supported by medical and scientific evidence. Applies the mandate to commercial health benefit plans beginning January 1, 2024, and to Medicaid beginning July 1, 2025. Prohibits cost-sharing for biomarker testing from exceeding deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance required for similar coverages. Requires coverage to be provided in a manner that limits disruptions in care, including repeated biospecimen sampling. Directs the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit comprehensive evaluation reports by specified dates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees; commercial health insurance policyholders; health insurers; nonprofit health service plans; health maintenance organizations; managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount beginning in FY 2026 (60% federal funds, 40% general funds), matching federal fund revenue increases, potentially offset by indeterminate downstream treatment savings. Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from rate and form filing fees. Potential expenditure increases for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health, provide coverage for biomarker testing beginning July 1, 2025. The department is also required to submit a comprehensive report on the fiscal and access impacts to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

Section 3 of the bill specifically mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission study and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, on the impact of biomarker testing coverage across demographic groups and payer types.

The bill establishes an insurance coverage mandate for private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs delivering policies in the state, which the Maryland Insurance Administration regulates, reviews policy form filings for, and collects related filing fees from.
The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit its formal report regarding biomarker testing implementation, fiscal impact, and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for early childhood education teacher certification completed through an alternative teacher preparation program; requiring the State Department of Education, in consultation with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to establish specific goals for the recruitment and retention of teachers in teacher preparation programs; requiring that "high staff qualifications" for publicly funded eligible prekindergarten providers must be implemented by the 2027-2028 school year; etc.
Title: Maryland Educator Shortage Reduction Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Teacher Development and Retention Program as a pilot program to incentivize college students to pursue teaching careers. Delays high staff qualification requirements for eligible prekindergarten providers until the 2027–2028 school year. Expands the renamed Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award to include public school mental health professionals. Modifies eligibility criteria and service obligations for the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship program. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to maintain an educator recruitment, retention, and diversity dashboard.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: public school teachers, teacher candidates, public school mental health professionals, eligible prekindergarten providers, local school systems, and higher education institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $15.7 million in fiscal 2024, including $10.0 million to capitalize the Teacher Development and Retention Fund and $5.0 million for expanded loan assistance awards. General fund expenditures remain at $5.2 million annually in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Special fund expenditures from the new fund total an estimated $16.3 million through program termination in fiscal 2029. Local school boards can likely meet reporting mandates using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is a primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to establish teacher recruitment and retention goals in consultation with MHEC, create and maintain the Maryland Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Diversity Dashboard, identify high-needs schools and content shortages, and establish standards for early childhood alternative teacher preparation programs.

MHEC (and its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is a primary implementing agency responsible for administering the new Teacher Development and Retention Program and Fund, overseeing the expanded Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award within the Janet L. Hoffman LARP, modifying the Teaching Fellows for Maryland program, and commissioning an independent program evaluation.

USM institutions house teacher preparation programs directly affected by the bill's recruitment and retention goals, student reporting requirements, and practicum standards. Several USM constituent institutions meet the Pell Grant eligibility threshold for the new Teacher Development and Retention Program stipends.

As an HBCU with a teacher preparation program and an undergraduate population with over 40% Pell Grant recipients, Morgan State University is directly eligible and targeted for educator recruitment, retention initiatives, and student stipends under the bill.

Saint Mary's College operates educator preparation programs (such as its Master of Arts in Teaching) impacted by the bill's revisions to teacher preparation requirements, scholarships, and retention initiatives.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding separately and investing the moneys of the newly established Teacher Development and Retention Fund.
The bill specifies that the Comptroller must account for the newly established Teacher Development and Retention Fund.

DBM oversees the state budget and fiscal planning, which includes significant general fund expenditures ($15+ million in FY 2024) and ongoing out-year funding for the programs established or expanded under the bill.
This legislation is an Administration priority bill introduced by request to address statewide teacher shortages and requires executive reporting on program evaluation results.

Synopsis: Requiring an adult family member to submit a death certificate or evidence of disability to the State Real Estate Commission before the family member may carry on the business of a disabled or deceased licensed real estate broker; permitting a certain business to designate a licensed real estate broker to provide real estate brokerage services under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Disability or Death and Termination of Employment of a Broker

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers
Termination of Employment -see also- Work, Labor, and Employ

bill_summary: Requires an adult family member to provide a death certificate or disability evidence to the State Real Estate Commission. Prohibits the family member from carrying on the broker's business until submitting this documentation. Authorizes a business to designate another licensed broker if documentation is not provided within a reasonable time. Authorizes a business to designate another licensed broker if a broker is terminated for any reason. Requires the Commission to approve the designation under specified conditions regarding license surrender and broker standing.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: licensed real estate brokers, family members of disabled or deceased real estate brokers, and real estate brokerage businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: Does not materially affect State finances or operations; the State Real Estate Commission can implement the bill with existing resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Real Estate Brokers Act administered by the State Real Estate Commission, which is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Commission is responsible for receiving documentation and approving broker designations following death, disability, or termination.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs to the parent of a child with a disability who is the prevailing party in a certain special education proceeding; prohibiting a court from awarding attorney's fees and related costs to certain parents in a certain proceeding under certain circumstances; and authorizing an award of attorney's fees and related costs to a parent of a child with a disability who is a prevailing party under certain circumstances.
Title: Special Education - Judicial Actions - Attorney's Fees and Related Costs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Authorizes a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs to a prevailing parent of a child with a disability. Includes expert witness fees and costs within allowable judicial awards. Prohibits fee awards for services performed after a written settlement offer made over 14 days before proceedings. Applies this prohibition if the parent rejects the offer and achieves relief not more favorable than offered. Authorizes fee and cost awards if the prevailing parent was substantially justified in rejecting the settlement offer.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Maryland State Department of Education; local school systems
stakeholders: parents of children with disabilities, children with disabilities, local school systems, public education agencies, and attorneys and expert witnesses in special education proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: State agency expenditures are not significantly affected. Local school systems face an indeterminate increase in expenditures beginning in fiscal 2024 to pay awarded attorney's fees and related costs, expected in 10 or fewer cases annually. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees the state's public education system and special education programs under IDEA. It is explicitly identified as a public agency subject to due process proceedings and is responsible for making staff available for mediation and ensuring statewide compliance with special education dispute resolution.

The bill authorizes state circuit courts to award reasonable attorney's fees, expert witness fees, and related costs to prevailing parents in special education appeals, directly impacting court proceedings administered and supported by the Judiciary.

Due process complaints concerning special education are filed with OAH, and its administrative law judges preside over the underlying hearings that form the basis of the judicial actions and fee dispute rules addressed by the bill.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is explicitly defined as a 'public agency' under § 8-413, making it subject to special education due process complaints and potential judicial actions where attorney's fees and expert witness costs may be awarded.

The Juvenile Services Education Program is explicitly designated as a 'public agency' under the bill, exposing it to potential due process complaints and court-ordered awards of attorney's fees and related costs in special education disputes.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day; and requiring the proclamation to include a declaration of the purposes of Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day.
Title: Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day. Requires the proclamation to declare the day one of reflection, recollection, and determination. Calls on Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, and media to remember the Holocaust. Requires the proclamation to include a pledge spreading Holocaust lessons and realities to future generations. Seeks to ensure society never forgets and bears witness against prejudice, bigotry, ignorance, and hate.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, and media
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Commemorating Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to annually issue an official proclamation designating January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day, including specific declarations regarding reflection and education.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date by 2 years for certain provisions of law relating to Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforcement duties regarding administrative services organizations that administer a certain delivery system for specialty mental health services.
Title: Maryland Insurance Commissioner Enforcement - Specialty Mental Health Services and Payment of Claims - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Extends the termination date for laws governing Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforcement of clean claims requirements. Applies to administrative services organizations administering the delivery system for specialty mental health services. Continues subjecting administrative services organizations to interest on unpaid clean claims and specified fines and penalties. Prolongs the Insurance Commissioner's authority to investigate potential clean claims violations. Extends the statutory provisions for two additional years through May 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: administrative services organizations administering specialty mental health services under Medicaid, specialty mental health providers, and Medicaid managed care organization enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures, as the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle enforcement using existing budgeted resources. MIA special fund revenues may increase indeterminately from fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2025 if penalties or fines are assessed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the enforcement authority and regulatory duties of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner over administrative services organizations (ASOs) that process specialty mental health services claims, including conducting investigations and potentially assessing fines.

The Maryland Department of Health administers the Medicaid program and oversees the delivery system for specialty mental health services. Under the extended provisions, the Insurance Commissioner must provide findings of any investigated claims violations directly to MDH.

Synopsis: Exempting a certain retiree of the Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems from a certain earnings limitation when the retiree is reemployed by a certain previous employer for a certain time period to assist with the administration of federally funded grants or projects related to the COVID-19 pandemic; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act to January 1, 2020.
Title: Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems - Reemployment Earnings Limitation - COVID-19 Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Exempts certain State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health from statutory retirement allowance earnings limitations. Applies to retirees rehired for up to five years to administer federally funded COVID-19 grants. Extends the exemption to retirees serving on the COVID Unified Command for staffing support or contact tracing. Applies retroactively to January 1, 2020. Sunsets on December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health to support COVID-19 pandemic response projects and grants
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates. Any retirement benefit offsets already deducted in 2023 must be repaid to affected rehired retirees. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health to administer COVID-19 grants or serve on the COVID Unified Command, and was requested by the department.

The agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is responsible for implementing the earnings limitation exemption, waiving benefit offsets, and refunding any offsets previously deducted.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission is required to disqualify an applicant who committed a crime involving moral turpitude from holding a video lottery employee license.
Title: Video Lottery Employee Licenses - Crimes of Moral Turpitude - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Exempts certain applicants for video lottery employee licenses from mandatory disqualification due to criminal history or current prosecution. Applies when the conviction, active parole, probation, or prosecution involves a nonviolent misdemeanor offense other than a gambling crime. Requires the applicant to have participated in and completed a qualifying problem-solving court program. Defines problem-solving courts to include drug, DUI, veterans', mental health, or reentry courts. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Applicants for video lottery employee licenses who completed a problem-solving court program for a nonviolent misdemeanor and video lottery operation licensees
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Changes to licensing qualifications are not anticipated to significantly affect application volumes, licensing fee revenues, administrative expenses, or court caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1288 directly alters the licensing disqualification criteria enforced by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission for video lottery employee license applicants.

The bill references programs under the Judiciary's Office of Problem-Solving Courts, and the Administrative Office of the Courts evaluated the potential operational impact on requests to problem-solving courts and trial court caseloads.

Synopsis: Amending certain prior authorizations of State Debt to alter the requirement that certain grantees provide certain matching funds; extending the termination date of certain grants; altering the authorized uses of certain grants; and changing the names of certain grantees.
Title: Prior Authorizations of State Debt - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission

bill_summary: Modifies prior authorizations of State debt for various local and miscellaneous capital grant projects across Maryland. Extends expenditure and encumbrance termination dates for specified grants through June 1, 2030. Removes matching fund requirements and historic easement conveyance obligations for selected grantees. Alters authorized uses, project scopes, locations, and designated recipients for multiple capital grant awards. Conditions Baltimore City grant expenditures for the Reach Partnership Field on adopting a renaming resolution.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of General Services
stakeholders: Capital grant recipients, including local governments, nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, and healthcare facilities across Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the bill alters existing grant conditions, deadlines, and recipients rather than creating new debt authorizations. Local governments experience no fiscal impact unless acting as a designated grant recipient.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services administers and manages the State's capital grant programs and state-funded capital improvement projects, directly overseeing the implementation of capital budget debt authorizations modified by this bill.

The Board of Public Works oversees State capital expenditures and is the entity responsible under Maryland law for certifying matching funds and approving disbursements for authorizations of State debt altered by this legislation.
The State Treasurer manages State debt issuance, the State's bond funds, and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees authorizations and changes to general obligation bond-funded grants.

The Maryland Historical Trust is a unit within the Department of Planning; this bill specifically repeals a statutory requirement that a capital grantee grant and convey a historic easement to the Trust.

The bill amends capital grant authorizations specifically dedicated to the Historic St. Mary's City Fort to 400 Commission, modifying authorized uses, scope of work, and grant allocations for Phase 2 design and surveys.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to criminal background investigations for certain individuals who care for or supervise children; and requiring certain facilities to apply to the Central Repository for a national and State criminal history records check for each employee, employer, individual, or volunteer.
Title: Family Law - Child Care - Criminal Background Investigations
bill_summary: Alters provisions governing criminal background investigations for individuals who care for or supervise children. Requires covered child care facilities and schools to apply to the Central Repository for criminal history records checks. Directs the Central Repository to forward criminal history record information to the individual and authorized licensing agencies. Defines employees to include contractors and subcontractors with direct, unsupervised, and uncontrolled access to children. Requires immediate removal of a child from an emergency out-of-home placement if an individual refuses follow-up fingerprints.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State Department of Education
stakeholders: Child care centers, family child care homes, nonpublic and public schools, child care employees, contractors, volunteers, and individuals seeking adoption or guardianship
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations. The changes conform Maryland statute to federal requirements to allow continued access to national criminal history records checks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS requested this departmental legislation. The Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) is housed within DPSCS and is responsible for conducting the State and national criminal history records checks, collecting fees, and disseminating record information to authorized agencies in compliance with federal standards.

DHS oversees local departments of social services, foster care, adoptions, and child placement programs. The bill directly impacts procedures for criminal history checks and emergency out-of-home child placements managed by local departments.

MSDE regulates licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, informal child care providers, and schools. The bill dictates that the Central Repository forward criminal history records to MSDE and requires MSDE to conduct cross-reference checks against the central sex offender registry.

MDH licenses home health and residential service agencies providing services to minors, as well as day and residential camps, which are categorized as facilities whose employees and operators must obtain criminal history records checks under this subtitle.

Facilities under Title 9 of the Human Services Article (juvenile detention, correction, or treatment facilities) are listed among facilities requiring background checks, although direct employees of DJS are explicitly exempted under the definition of employee in this subtitle.

Synopsis: Urging the U.S. General Services Administration to select for the new Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters one of the two finalist sites located in Maryland.
Title: Locating the New Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters in Maryland
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Joint Resolution 1
bill_summary: Urges the U.S. General Services Administration to select Greenbelt or Landover, Maryland, for the new Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters. Highlights Maryland's established role in national defense and cybersecurity infrastructure. Notes that locating the facility in Prince George's County promotes equity and workforce diversity. Commits the General Assembly to supporting employee relocation and necessary transportation infrastructure improvements. Directs the Department of Legislative Services to transmit copies of the resolution to federal and state officials.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Prince George's County, Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel, and federal contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Compliance with the joint resolution does not directly affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution designates Governor Wes Moore as an official recipient of the joint resolution and directly concerns intergovernmental coordination and federal relations regarding the location of a major federal facility in Maryland.

The joint resolution advocates for bringing the consolidated Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters to Maryland, which directly intersects with the Department of Commerce's core mission of attracting major employers, stimulating economic development, and job growth.

The resolution emphasizes Maryland's commitment to supporting the FBI headquarters through mass transit access and infrastructure improvements at the Greenbelt and Landover finalist sites, aligning with MDOT's responsibilities for state transit and roadway infrastructure.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly wearing, carrying, or transporting a firearm in certain locations; prohibiting a person from wearing, carrying, or transporting a firearm onto certain property unless the owner or owner's agent has given certain permission; altering certain provisions of law relating to the authority of the Secretary of State Police to limit the wearing, carrying, or transporting of a handgun at certain times and locations; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Wearing, Carrying, or Transporting Firearms - Restrictions (Gun Safety Act of 2023)
