bill_summary: Prohibits wearing, carrying, or transporting firearms in areas for children and vulnerable individuals, government areas, and special purpose areas. Requires government buildings to display conspicuous signage at main entrances indicating firearms are prohibited. Prohibits carrying a firearm into another person's dwelling or onto private property without express permission or posted authorization. Restricts handgun permit holders to carrying concealed from view under clothing or within an enclosed case. Repeals the authority of the Secretary of State Police to limit handgun permit times and geographic areas. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to one year of imprisonment, a fine up to $1,000, or both.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Secretary of State Police
stakeholders: firearm owners, handgun permit holders, private property owners, and operators of restricted sensitive facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues and expenditures from misdemeanor penalty provisions. Potential minimal one-time increase in State and local expenditures in FY 2024 to post required signage at owned or leased government buildings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police oversees handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. The bill directly alters the authority of the Secretary of State Police regarding handgun permits, eliminating certain discretionary limitations and mandating statutory concealed carry restrictions.

The bill establishes new criminal misdemeanor prohibitions on carrying firearms in sensitive areas and on private property, which will be adjudicated in the state court system. It also explicitly preserves the authority of court administrative heads to adopt rules prohibiting weapons in court facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor crimes subject to imprisonment for up to one year, directly impacting OPD's caseload for defending indigent individuals charged under these new provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor penalties carrying potential incarceration, which could have an impact on detention and correctional facilities and supervision managed by the department.

As the primary manager of state-owned and leased facilities, DGS is affected by the requirement that government-owned or leased buildings post clear and conspicuous signage prohibiting firearms at main entrances.

Synopsis: Expanding the requirement that the Department of Natural Resources make available and issue certain licenses and stamps in a digital or electronic format; and providing that, if the Department cannot issue certain licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, or certificates in a digital or electronic format because of federal restrictions, it is the intent of the General Assembly that the Department issue certain licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, or certificates in a digital or electronic format whenever the federal restrictions are eliminated.
Title: Department of Natural Resources – Documents – Digital or Electronic Issuance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Expands the requirement that the Department of Natural Resources make available and issue documents in a digital or electronic format. Applies this mandate to all licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates authorized under the Natural Resources Article, subject to specified exceptions. Exempts thirteen specific items, including charter boat licenses, vessel certificates of title, and various registration decals and stickers. Authorizes individuals to satisfy possession or display requirements by presenting qualifying documents in a digital or electronic format. Retains requirements to attach, affix, or display associated numbers, stickers, or decals on a vehicle, vessel, dock, or gear.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Holders and applicants of Department of Natural Resources licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates, including hunters, anglers, boaters, and commercial harvesters
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 10 directly expands the requirement for the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to issue nearly all licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates in a digital or electronic format upon request, and allows individuals to satisfy possession or display requirements via electronic format.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that the Capital Debt Affordability Committee include certain debt that is secured by future federal aid within its review of State tax supported debt; altering the calculation of the maximum amount of debt secured by future federal aid that the Department of Transportation may issue; providing that the maximum amount of debt that may be issued is calculated as of June 30; establishing the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs; etc.
Title: Department of Transportation - Financing and Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs (State and Federal Transportation Funding Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Alters the maximum outstanding debt secured by future federal aid that the Department of Transportation may issue to $1,000,000,000. Restricts bond proceeds to six specified transit and highway infrastructure projects. Extends the maximum maturity of these bonds from 12 years to 15 years after issue. Repeals the secondary pledge of State tax revenue and excludes these bonds from State tax supported debt. Establishes the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs to recommend sustainable transportation funding options.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Transportation, transit riders, motorists, local governments, and transportation construction contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 and $50,000 in FY 2025 for contractual staff support for the commission. The bill expands MDOT's authority to issue up to $1.0 billion in debt backed by future federal aid for specified capital projects. There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency. The bill expands MDOT's bonding authority for debt backed by future federal aid up to $1.0 billion for specific projects, alters bond terms, and requires MDOT to provide staff support and funding for the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs to study and recommend changes to the state's transportation funding and revenue structure.

MTA transit projects, including the Baltimore Red Line and procurement of zero-emission buses and related infrastructure, are specifically authorized for financing under the expanded federal aid bond proceeds, and the Commission membership includes a representative from the MTA core service area.

SHA highway corridor projects, including improvements to MD Route 2/Route 4 (Thomas Johnson Bridge), MD Route 90, and Interstate 81, are specifically authorized to receive financing from the bond proceeds under the bill.

The Treasurer chairs the Capital Debt Affordability Committee (CDAC). The bill amends State Finance and Procurement Section 8-104 to alter the definition of State tax-supported debt reviewed by CDAC by removing certain debt backed by future federal aid.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.
The Secretary of Planning is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members and designating the chair of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs, and receives interim and final reports from the Commission.
MDTA debt backed by federal aid under Title 4, Subtitle 3 is included in the statutory debt limits and provisions amended under the bill.
The Board of Public Works is required under existing statutory provisions to approve the issuance of transportation debt and bonds backed by federal aid prior to their issuance.

Synopsis: Altering the application requirements for a certain property tax exemption for a dwelling house owned by a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran by adding a rating decision of the disabled veteran's disability from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to the type of supporting documents that may be included with application.
Title: Property Tax - Exemption for Dwellings of Disabled Veterans - Application
bill_summary: Alters application requirements for a real property tax exemption on dwellings owned by disabled veterans or surviving spouses. Permits applicants to submit a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs rating decision showing its effective date. Provides this rating decision as an alternative to the department-issued disability certification form. Prohibits unauthorized inspection of the submitted rating decision. Restricts inspection solely to the disabled veteran and appropriate state, county, or municipal employees. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Disabled veterans, surviving spouses of disabled veterans, and county and municipal tax assessment offices
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the changes with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the documentation requirements for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses to apply for a 100% property tax exemption on their dwelling house. DVMF is responsible for assisting and advocating for Maryland veterans and their families regarding state benefits and housing-related programs.

PTAAB hears appeals regarding disputes over real property tax exemptions and credits following decisions made by local supervisors of assessments. Changes to acceptable documentation for granting exemptions may indirectly affect appeals brought before the board.

Synopsis: Providing that any unpaid court fees or costs are not a bar to a certain expungement; requiring a court to waive certain court fees and costs when ordering or effecting a certain expungement; adding malicious destruction of property to the list of misdemeanor convictions that may be expunged; and altering the waiting periods applicable to the filing of petitions for expungement of convictions of certain crimes.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement of Records (REDEEM Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Shortens waiting periods for filing petitions to expunge records of certain misdemeanor and felony convictions. Adds misdemeanor malicious destruction of property to the list of convictions eligible for expungement. Reduces general waiting periods to 5 years for eligible misdemeanors and 7 years for eligible felonies. Sets waiting periods at 10 years for first-degree burglary, second-degree burglary, and felony theft. Specifies that unpaid court fees or costs do not bar an individual from receiving an expungement. Requires courts to waive all court fees and costs associated with an expunged charge.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of State Police
stakeholders: individuals seeking criminal record expungements; crime victim compensation funds; state courts; law enforcement record custodians
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in special fund revenues from waived court costs and fees, with no material impact on general fund revenues. Potential minimal increase in general fund expenditures for the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to process an initial influx of expungement petitions. No material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary and trial courts are directly responsible for processing petitions for expungement, modifying waiting periods under the Maryland Electronic Courts (MDEC) system, and implementing the requirement to waive outstanding court fees and costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) acts as the central repository for criminal records and must execute expungement orders, while the Division of Parole and Probation tracks sentence completion dates and related fee collections.
As the primary state law enforcement agency holding criminal history and arrest records, the department receives, processes, and complies with court-issued expungement orders.
DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which handles collection of delinquent court costs and fees that are now subject to mandatory waiver upon expungement.
The State Archives serves as the custodian of permanent judicial and government records and must comply with court expungement orders for archived records.
MDOT agencies and police units maintain transportation-related law enforcement and licensing records that may be subject to expungement orders under the expanded and accelerated provisions.
The Natural Resources Police maintain citation and arrest records for specific Natural Resources Article violations eligible for expungement under § 10-110.

Synopsis: Adding certain State employees to certain provisions of law authorizing disaster service leave with pay; authorizing certain appointing authorities to waive certain requirements for disaster service leave and to increase the number of days of disaster service leave under certain circumstances; defining "uniformed services" for the purpose of adding certain individuals to certain provisions of law relating to certain paid leave and military administrative leave; etc.
Title: Disaster Service and Uniformed Services Leave Modernization Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Expands paid disaster service leave eligibility for State employees belonging to qualifying volunteer emergency and disaster organizations. Authorizes appointing authorities to waive approval requirements and increase leave days during prolonged or recurrent disasters. Retains State employee status under workers' compensation and tort claims for Maryland Incident Management Team members on disaster leave. Replaces military leave provisions with uniformed services leave under federal definitions. Defines emergency manager within State emergency management law.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: State employees serving in uniformed services or volunteer disaster response organizations, including the Civil Air Patrol, Coast Guard Auxiliary, volunteer fire and rescue companies, and community emergency response teams
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances or operations. Expenditures may increase minimally in limited situations if agencies incur overtime or temporary coverage costs for employees on disaster leave during emergencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency, DBM is directly tasked with adopting regulations for paid uniformed services leave and maintaining records of State employees' use of uniformed services administrative leave.

The bill amends the Public Safety Article governing MDEM by defining 'emergency manager' and modifies disaster service leave provisions for State employees engaging in emergency response organizations, including the Maryland Incident Management Team.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2024 or fiscal year 2025 an appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund to be used for loans under the Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan (NIMBL) Account; and repealing a requirement that 5% of proceeds from video lottery terminals go to the NIMBL Account.
Title: Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program - Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan (NIMBL) Account - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $1,000,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund. Mandates this funding in fiscal year 2024 or alternatively in fiscal year 2025. Dedicates the appropriation to loans issued under the Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan Account. Repeals the transfer of video lottery terminal proceeds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the loan account.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: Nonprofit entities in Maryland seeking bridge loans, and small, minority, and women-owned businesses eligible for investment capital from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2025 due to a mandated appropriation for the Maryland Department of Commerce. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund increase correspondingly by $1.0 million in FY 2025 to provide micro bridge loans, with further special fund activity beginning as early as FY 2026 as loans are repaid and reissued. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and the NIMBL Account are administered by the Department of Commerce, which experiences a direct fiscal impact of a $1.0 million general fund increase in FY 2025 to fund interest-free micro bridge loans.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and this bill establishes a statutory mandated appropriation of $1.0 million for FY 2025.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific $1.0 million appropriation in the annual state budget bill for the NIMBL Account.

The bill amends the statute governing distributions by the Comptroller of video lottery terminal proceeds by repealing the requirement to divert funds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the NIMBL Account.

Synopsis: Repealing the definition of "public safety officer" for purposes of a certain credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on a dwelling owned by a public safety officer; repealing a certain limitation on the amount of the credit; requiring the governing body of a county or municipal corporation that authorizes the credit to establish, by law, the definition of "public safety officer" for purposes of eligibility for the credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Public Safety Officer

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Repeals the statutory definition of public safety officer for local property tax credits on qualifying dwellings. Repeals the $2,500 cap on the maximum property tax credit local jurisdictions may grant. Requires county and municipal governing bodies that grant the credit to define public safety officer by law. Authorizes local governing bodies to establish the credit's amount, duration, and additional eligibility requirements. Applies the changes to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Public safety officers who own qualifying dwellings and Maryland county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in county and municipal property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent local jurisdictions authorize the credit, expand eligibility, or increase credit amounts. State revenues and expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters eligibility criteria and local authority regarding property tax credits under the Tax - Property Article. While the fiscal impact is local and administrative execution falls to local jurisdictions, the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears disputes and appeals regarding property tax exemptions and credits.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body for tax disputes, hearing appeals from final decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property assessments and tax credits.

Synopsis: Requiring an appointee for a civil commission to contact the clerk of the circuit court to which the commission was delivered by the Governor to coordinate a time and place for the administration of the oath of office and presentation of the commission; altering the frequency with which the clerk of a circuit court must report to the Secretary of State the name and office of each officer who has taken the oath of office; etc.
Title: Clerks of the Circuit Courts - Civil Commissions - Presentation and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires an appointee for a civil commission to contact the circuit court clerk to coordinate oath administration. Directs the clerk to administer the oath of office and present the commission. Alters the required reporting frequency from monthly to regularly when clerks notify the Secretary of State of qualifying officers. Repeals obsolete statutory provisions regarding the collection and payment of taxes on commissions.
responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Courts; Secretary of State
stakeholders: Appointees for civil commissions; clerks of the circuit courts; public officers taking oaths of office
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirements to the Secretary of State, requiring clerks of the circuit court to regularly report names and offices of individuals taking oaths of office under civil commissions, which the Secretary of State must preserve and certify.

The bill alters statutory duties and procedures for the clerks of the circuit courts regarding the presentation of civil commissions, scheduling oaths of office with appointees, and reporting to the Secretary of State.
The bill repeals an obsolete statutory requirement that required circuit court clerks to remit taxes collected on civil commissions to the State Treasurer.
The bill involves the administration and presentation of civil commissions issued by the Governor for gubernatorial appointees.

Synopsis: Requiring that the Apprenticeship and Training Council and consultants to the Council include representation by individuals who are Asian, Black, and Latino; establishing the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine and make recommendations to expand access to apprenticeships to reduce skill shortages in high-demand occupations and provide affordable training for career pathways for young people; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Labor and Employment - Apprenticeship 2030 Commission and Representation on the Apprenticeship and Training Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Apprenticeship and Training Council and its consultants to include representation by individuals who are Asian, Black, and Latino. Establishes the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine and recommend strategies to expand registered apprenticeships. Directs the Commission to target growing registered apprenticeships to at least 60,000 by 2030. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023. Abrogates the Commission on December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Apprenticeship 2030 Commission; Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: high school students, unemployed and underemployed adults seeking apprenticeships, employers, labor organizations, and members of the Apprenticeship and Training Council
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $36,900 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire contractual staff to support the commission. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the membership and diversity requirements for the Apprenticeship and Training Council housed within MD Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. Additionally, the Secretary of Labor serves on the newly established Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, and MD Labor incurs direct general fund expenditures to staff and support the commission.

The chair of the Governor's Workforce Development Board and the chair of the board's Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee both serve on the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission. The bill also establishes legislative intent regarding policies between the commission and the CTE Committee.

The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a member of the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, which is tasked with achieving the Blueprint for Maryland's Future target of having 45% of high school graduates complete an apprenticeship.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a member of the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine high-demand industry sectors with skill shortages and business needs for workforce development.

The Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) serves on the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine postsecondary pathways and explore degree apprenticeships in fields requiring higher education credentials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary statutory study and advisory body, the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, which is required to evaluate apprenticeship targets and report findings to state leadership before sunsetting.

The Governor appoints members to the Apprenticeship and Training Council, appoints employer representatives to the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, jointly selects the commission chair, and receives the commission's final report.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the Apprenticeship and Training Council and the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring certain notices relating to increases in property assessments; altering certain notice requirements relating to the intention of a county or municipal corporation to set a certain real property tax rate that exceeds the constant yield tax rate and requiring instead certain notice when a county or municipal corporation intends to increase its real property tax rate.
Title: Property Tax - Real Property Tax Assessment and Tax Rate Increases - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Repeals public notice requirements for taxing authorities setting a real property tax rate exceeding the constant yield rate. Requires taxing authorities intending to increase real property tax rates above current rates to provide public notice and hold a hearing. Mandates publishing the notice in a general-circulation newspaper and on the taxing authority's website or an accessible public posting. Requires assessment notices to state that property taxes owed may increase if assessments increase without a tax rate increase. Requires counties to display prior and current taxable year property tax rates on annual property tax bills.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Real property owners and county and municipal taxing authorities in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local expenditures may decrease due to fewer required public notices of tax rate increases, though county expenditures may increase in FY 2023 to update information on annual property tax bills. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 6-308(I) of the bill, the Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation is required to report any taxing authority that appears to violate the property tax rate notice requirements to the Attorney General. The Office of the Attorney General is mandated to investigate these reports and institute legal action to compel compliance.

Synopsis: Altering a reporting requirement to require the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to report certain student Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) data to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 15 each year, beginning in 2023 and ending in 2028; and requiring the Maryland Higher Education Commission to provide the Center with access to student FAFSA data.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - Student FAFSA Data - Reporting Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Alters reporting requirements for student Free Application for Federal Student Aid data. Repeals the requirement for county boards of education to report high school FAFSA completion data. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to provide student FAFSA data access to the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center. Requires the Center to report annual FAFSA submission data to specified legislative committees by December 15 from 2023 through 2028. Requires the Center to disaggregate the reported information by county and other student subgroups.
responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland high school students submitting financial aid applications and local boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances, as the MLDS Center and MHEC can implement the requirements using existing resources. Local school system expenditures may decrease minimally due to the elimination of reporting mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to receive FAFSA data, disaggregate it by county and student subgroups, and submit an annual report to legislative committees through 2028.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to provide the MLDS Center with access to student FAFSA data from the Federal Student Aid Internet Gateway and the Office of Student Financial Aid.
The bill requires the commission to provide the MLDS Center with access to student FAFSA data collected via the Federal Student Aid Internet Gateway and the Office of Student Financial Aid.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding high school student FAFSA reporting and repeals the requirement for local school boards under MSDE's purview to collect and report this data directly.

Synopsis: Increasing the maximum number of years of eligibility service that certain members of the State Police Retirement System or Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System may have to participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) from 30 to 32; increasing the number of years that certain members of the State Police Retirement System or Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System may participate in the DROP from 5 to 7; and authorizing certain individuals to elect to extend their participation in the DROP.
Title: State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Deferred Retirement Option Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Increases the maximum Deferred Retirement Option Program participation period from 5 to 7 years for eligible law enforcement retirement systems. Expands eligibility for State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System members with less than 32 years of service. Authorizes active program participants as of July 1, 2023, to elect to extend their participation. Requires members seeking an extension to submit an election form on or before December 31, 2023. Prohibits any extension that results in a member participating in the program past age 60.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System; local law enforcement agencies participating as governmental units
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension contributions decrease by $400,000 in FY 2025 ($220,000 for SPRS and $180,000 for LEOPS), with out-year savings reflecting actuarial assumptions. Local pension contributions for participating governmental units decrease by approximately $150,000 beginning in FY 2025. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes both the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The agency is directly responsible for implementing the alterations to the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP), processing DROP applications and extension elections, and managing pension liability and contribution calculations.

The bill directly impacts Maryland State Police officers participating in the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) by expanding DROP eligibility and participation limits from 5 to 7 years. Additionally, the Maryland State Police Secretary and Director of Human Resources are required to review and sign off on binding letters of resignation and DROP extension agreements.

As the State's central budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and monitors statewide employer pension contribution rates, which are projected to decrease by $400,000 in FY 2025 and similar amounts in out-years due to the actuarial impact of the DROP extension.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain eligible customer-generator to accrue net excess generation for an indefinite period; requiring the Public Service Commission to establish a method for calculating the value of certain accrued net excess generation; and requiring that a subscriber of a community solar energy generating system accrue virtual net excess generation in the same manner as a certain eligible customer-generator.
Title: Electricity - Net Energy Metering and Virtual Net Energy Metering - Accrual of Net Excess Generation (Net Metering Flexibility Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Authorizes eligible customer-generators to accrue net excess generation indefinitely instead of only for up to 12 months. Excludes eligible customer-generators served by a municipal electric utility or an electric cooperative from indefinite accrual. Shifts the end of the standard 12-month net excess generation accrual cycle from April to August. Requires electric companies to pay customer-generators for remaining indefinitely accrued generation within 15 days of account closure. Directs the Public Service Commission to establish a valuation method for indefinitely accrued net excess generation. Allows community solar subscribers to accrue virtual net excess generation indefinitely and repeals the 200% baseline usage cap.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: eligible customer-generators, community solar energy generating system subscribers, electric companies, municipal electric utilities, and electric cooperatives
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues. The Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Public Service Commission with establishing a method to calculate the value of accrued net excess generation for customer-generators electing indefinite accrual, and oversees electric company net metering and community solar regulations.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility customers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding electric utility rates, billing rules, and net metering tariffs.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Social Work Examiners, under certain circumstances, to issue a conditional license to practice social work to an applicant who, except for passing a required examination, has met the appropriate education and experience requirements for a certain license if the required examination was unavailable to the applicant for a period of at least 15 business days; providing that a conditional license is valid until 180 days after the examination becomes readily available to the applicant; etc.
Title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Conditional Licenses to Practice Social Work

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Social Work Examiners to issue conditional licenses for bachelor or master social work. Applies when administrative delays or unforeseen circumstances prevent examination availability for at least 15 business days. Limits eligibility to applicants who meet all education and experience requirements except passing the examination. Requires conditional licensees to practice exclusively under the supervision of a Board-approved supervisor. Establishes that a conditional license remains valid until 180 days after the examination becomes readily available. Mandates annual reports to the General Assembly on examination availability and conditional licensing beginning December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Applicants for bachelor social work and master social work licenses, board-approved social work supervisors, and social work clients
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund revenues and expenditures beginning as early as fiscal 2024 if conditional licenses are issued. The FY 2024 state budget included $75,000 in general funds for board operations contingent on enactment of this bill or other legislation. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. MDH and the Board are directly responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, issuing conditional licenses to bachelor and master social workers during exam delays, and submitting required annual reports.

As the state's primary social services agency, DHS employs a large workforce of bachelor- and master-level social workers across local departments; provisions allowing conditional licensure during examination delays directly affect the onboarding and practice eligibility of DHS caseworkers and staff.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign to encourage the use of mental health advance directives in the State; and requiring the Behavioral Health Administration and the Maryland Health Care Commission jointly to study how first responders and behavioral health crisis providers can access a certain advanced directive database when responding to a behavioral health crisis and to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on their findings on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Public Health - Mental Health Advance Directives - Awareness and Statewide Database

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign encouraging mental health advance directives. Mandates outreach initiatives supporting state agencies, local health authorities, health care facilities, academic institutions, and religious organizations. Requires the Behavioral Health Administration and Maryland Health Care Commission jointly to study database access for crisis responders. Directs both entities to report their study findings to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: individuals receiving or seeking mental health services and their families, behavioral health providers, and emergency first responders
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $140,700 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one program manager and procure campaign materials. Ongoing expenditures range between $87,400 and $100,400 annually. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing and executing the statewide public awareness campaign regarding mental health advance directives. Additionally, its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) must jointly conduct a study and report on database access for first responders.

MHCC is required to collaborate jointly with the Behavioral Health Administration to study how first responders and crisis providers can access the advance directives database and submit a report of findings to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is specifically designated in the bill to participate in outreach and awareness initiatives for mental health advance directives, and has potential operational adjustments regarding mental health services in correctional facilities.
The Maryland State Police is specifically enumerated in the statute to support and engage in outreach initiatives to inform individuals about mental health advance directives.

The department (referenced in the bill as the Department of Veterans Affairs) is specifically designated to take part in outreach efforts to inform veterans and their families about mental health advance directives.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor, for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2028, to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $500,000 to the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive to be used for the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program; and requiring that funds made available by the Act are supplemental to, and may not supplant, funds otherwise available for the reentry employment incentives in Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $500,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028. Directs these funds to the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive. Mandates that the funding support the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program. Prohibits these funds from supplanting other funding available for reentry employment incentives in the county. Terminates the statutory funding mandate on June 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Governor; Prince George's County Office of the County Executive
stakeholders: Prince George's County government, formerly incarcerated county residents seeking employment, and employers participating in the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 for the mandated appropriation. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures increase by matching amounts of $500,000 annually over the same period as grant funds are received and distributed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to include an appropriation of $500,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 for the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program.

As the agency responsible for preparing and supervising the annual state budget on behalf of the Governor, DBM must incorporate and manage this $500,000 statutory mandated appropriation from FY 2025 through FY 2028.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Aviation Commission to consider information and advice from certain additional stakeholders when carrying out the Commission's duties; requiring the Commission to consider the aviation, economic, business, environmental, health, and community-related impacts or any other impacts the Commission finds relevant; requiring that certain members of the Commission appointed by the Governor are to be recommended by the Anne Arundel County and Howard County Senate delegations; etc.
Title: Maryland Aviation Commission - Duties, Composition, and Member Orientation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the Maryland Aviation Commission from nine to 13 voting members. Requires two gubernatorial appointees recommended by the Anne Arundel County Senate delegation and two by Howard County. Directs the Commission to establish policies mitigating negative impacts of local aviation and airport industries. Requires the Commission to consider advice from airport employees, local governments, and nearby communities. Mandates member orientation and subjects the Commission to enhanced Open Meetings Act livestreaming requirements. Expands the annual report to include community health impacts and mitigation initiatives.
responsible_party: Maryland Aviation Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Communities near State-owned airports, airport workers and their representatives, local governments in Anne Arundel and Howard counties, and aviation industry stakeholders
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures may increase minimally for the Maryland Aviation Commission to comply with enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements. Special fund revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Aviation Commission directly oversees and directs the Maryland Aviation Administration in developing airport management policy, approving regulations, and establishing policies for State-owned airports such as BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport.

The Maryland Secretary of Transportation serves as the Chairman of the Maryland Aviation Commission, and MAA is a modal administration under MDOT. The fiscal note also notes potential minimal expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 12 members to the Maryland Aviation Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, subject to newly specified recommendation and experience criteria.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for state boards and commissions, which includes the four additional seats and specific delegation recommendations for the Maryland Aviation Commission.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated by statute to serve as an ex officio, nonvoting member of the Maryland Aviation Commission.
The Commission's annual estimate of operating expenditures included in its report to the General Assembly is subject to review by the Department of Budget and Management.

Synopsis: Clarifying the calculation for certain funding for the Maryland State Arts Council for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter; repealing a certain requirement for certain funds distributed to the Maryland State Arts Council to be included in the Council's prior fiscal year appropriation; etc.
Title: Maryland State Arts Council - Funding

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Clarifies the statutory General Fund mandate calculation for the Maryland State Arts Council beginning in fiscal year 2025. Requires the Governor to include a mandated General Fund appropriation in the annual budget bill using a specified formula. Calculates the appropriation using prior-year admissions and amusement tax distributions increased by the General Fund growth adjustment. Adds the prior-year General Fund appropriation adjusted for growth and subtracts the prior-year tax distributions. Repeals an uncodified requirement that previously included those tax distributions in the prior fiscal year appropriation.
responsible_party: Governor; Department of Budget and Management; Maryland State Arts Council
stakeholders: Maryland State Arts Council, arts organizations, and individual artist grant recipients
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State expenditures or revenues, assuming the Department of Budget and Management continues its current interpretation and calculation methodology. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) operates within the Department of Commerce, and this bill directly alters and clarifies the statutory formula governing MSAC's annual mandated General Fund appropriation.

DBM is responsible for calculating and preparing the Governor's annual budget bill, and the bill codifies and clarifies DBM's interpretation and methodology for calculating MSAC's mandated funding appropriation.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific calculated General Fund appropriation for the Maryland State Arts Council in the annual state budget bill.
The Comptroller collects and distributes the admissions and amusement tax revenues under § 2-202 of the Tax - General Article that are integrated into MSAC's statutory funding formula.
The bill reaffirms statutory authority for the Legislative Auditor to conduct audits and reviews of grant recipients from the Maryland State Arts Council.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Crime Classification to study and make recommendations regarding a method for classifying crimes and civil offenses under State law and to identify and logically categorize all crimes and civil offenses that exist under State law; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 31, 2023.
Title: Task Force to Study Crime Classification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Crime Classification. Requires the task force to study and recommend a method for classifying crimes and civil offenses under State law. Directs the task force to identify and logically categorize all existing State crimes and civil offenses. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide staff for the task force. Mandates reporting of findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Task Force to Study Crime Classification
stakeholders: individuals charged with civil or criminal offenses in Maryland, crime victims, criminal justice practitioners, and legal professionals
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $177,400 in FY 2024 only for contractual staffing within the Office of the Attorney General. Task force expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Revenues and local governments are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is named as a member of the Task Force, is required to provide primary staff support, and incurs a direct fiscal impact of at least $177,400 in FY 2024 to hire contractual personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender, or the Public Defender's designee, is designated as a formal voting member of the Task Force to Study Crime Classification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state body, the Task Force to Study Crime Classification, tasked with studying and making recommendations regarding the classification and categorization of crimes and civil offenses in Maryland.
The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding crime and civil offense classification directly to the Governor on or before December 31, 2023.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "organics recycling" to include the processing of certain compostable packaging materials in a certain manner; requiring the Department of the Environment to approve a single producer responsibility organization to represent the interests of producers by October 1, 2023; establishing a producer responsibility advisory council to provide advice and make recommendations regarding establishing and implementing a producer responsibility program in the State for packaging materials; etc.
Title: Environment - Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment and Producer Responsibility for Packaging Materials

Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment's Office of Recycling to hire an independent consultant for a statewide recycling needs assessment. Directs the Office of Recycling to report the assessment results to the Governor and the General Assembly by July 30, 2024. Requires the Department to approve a single producer responsibility organization to represent producers by October 1, 2023. Establishes a Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council to recommend policies for a packaging materials producer responsibility program. Requires the Advisory Council to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and specified legislative committees by December 1, 2024. Alters the definition of organics recycling to include processing compostable packaging materials.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Office of Recycling
stakeholders: producers of packaging materials, local governments, recycling and composting processors, solid waste collectors, and Maryland residents
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $532,100 in FY 2024 and $12,100 in FY 2025 to fund an independent consultant and a part-time contractual employee. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of the Environment's Office of Recycling with procuring an independent consultant to conduct a statewide recycling needs assessment, approving a single producer responsibility organization, providing staff support to the newly established advisory council, and submitting required reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new state advisory body, the Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council, charged with providing advice, evaluating policies, and reporting recommendations on establishing an extended producer responsibility program for packaging materials in Maryland.

The Governor's Office receives the required reports on the results of the statewide recycling needs assessment by July 30, 2024, and the findings and recommendations of the Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council by December 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly or intentionally accessing and intentionally viewing a certain visual representation of a child under the age of 16 years.
Title: Criminal Law - Child Pornography - Accessing and Intentionally Viewing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Pornography -see also- Nudity and Sexual Displays; Obscenity

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from knowingly or intentionally accessing and intentionally viewing certain visual representations of child pornography. Covers depictions of actual children or indistinguishable computer-generated images of children under 16 years of age. Applies to depictions involving sadomasochistic abuse, sexual conduct, or sexual excitement. Establishes a misdemeanor penalty of up to five years imprisonment, a $2,500 fine, or both for first offenses. Classifies repeat offenses as a felony punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both. Maintains existing affirmative defenses for individuals who promptly destroy representations or report them to law enforcement.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: individuals charged with or convicted of child pornography offenses; victims of child sexual exploitation; state and local law enforcement agencies; state and local correctional facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures resulting from expanded application of existing criminal fines and incarceration penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal offenses under child pornography laws, subjecting convicted individuals to imprisonment in State correctional facilities for up to 5 years (misdemeanor) or 10 years (subsequent felony), resulting in a fiscal and operational impact on state incarceration resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of criminal acts related to viewing and accessing child pornography, which will require OPD to provide legal representation for indigent individuals charged under this statute.
The bill introduces new punishable misdemeanor and felony offenses to be adjudicated in the District Court and Circuit Courts, affecting judicial caseloads and court fee/fine administration.

As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations and digital crimes, MSP investigates child exploitation offenses and receives reports referenced under the statute's affirmative defense provisions.
The OAG represents the State in civil and criminal appeals resulting from convictions under Maryland's criminal laws, including prosecutions brought under expanded child exploitation statutes.

Synopsis: Establishing that the terms "spouse", "family", "immediate family", "dependent", and any other terms that denote a spousal relationship shall be construed to include a party to a domestic partnership for purposes of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; and establishing that the provisions of the Program that apply to spouses shall apply to parties who have entered into a domestic partnership.
Title: State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program – Domestic Partnerships
bill_summary: Extends State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program coverage to domestic partners. Construes statutory terms denoting spousal relationships to include a party to a domestic partnership. Applies all Program provisions that govern spouses to individuals in domestic partnerships. Requires domestic partnerships to satisfy defined statutory criteria under the Health – General Article. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State employees, State retirees, and their domestic partners and dependents
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State expenditures for the Department of Budget and Management beginning in FY 2024 to provide health and welfare benefits for additional enrollees and update administrative and payroll systems; local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program through its Employee Benefits Division. The bill directly requires DBM to extend health and welfare benefits to domestic partners of state employees and retirees, necessitating system updates for eligibility and payroll deductions and resulting in increased state benefit expenditures.

As the agency that pays state employees and administers state payroll via the Central Payroll Bureau, the Comptroller may coordinate with DBM on post-tax payroll deductions and imputed income reporting on W-2 forms for domestic partner health benefits.

Synopsis: Providing, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, an addition modification under the Maryland income tax for the amount of a certain tax credit claimed for certain taxes paid to another state by a pass-through entity under certain circumstances.
Title: Income Tax – Out–of–State Taxes Paid by Pass–Through Entities – Addition Modification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: Requires resident taxpayers to add back certain tax credits when calculating Maryland adjusted gross income. Applies the addition modification to credits claimed for income taxes imposed on pass-through entities by other states. Covers out-of-state taxes that are deductible in determining the entity's income under the Internal Revenue Code. Takes effect July 1, 2023, and applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland resident members of pass-through entities paying income taxes to other states
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 due to added tax liability; specific estimates are unavailable. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Office of the Comptroller and directly impacts the administration, collection, and enforcement of state income taxes by creating an addition modification for certain credits claimed for taxes paid by pass-through entities to other states.

Synopsis: Requiring the Comptroller, as Administrator of abandoned property in the State, to determine the value of certain nonmonetary abandoned property; and authorizing the Administrator, if it is determined the property has no commercial value and need not be offered for sale, to return the property to the holder, destroy the property, or dispose of the property.
Title: Commercial Law – Abandoned Property – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to determine within one year of delivery whether nonmonetary abandoned property has commercial value. Authorizes the Comptroller to decline offering property for sale if it lacks commercial value. Permits the Comptroller to return, destroy, or otherwise dispose of property not offered for sale. Repeals the requirement to publish advance notice of sales in a local newspaper. Requires the Comptroller to give reasonable notice to the public before any sale.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Holders of abandoned property, previous owners of unclaimed property, auction purchasers, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, though the Comptroller may realize operational efficiencies and savings from reduced property storage costs. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller serves as the Administrator of abandoned and unclaimed property in Maryland. The bill directly alters the Comptroller's statutory duties by establishing procedures to assess the commercial value of nonmonetary abandoned property, authorize its disposal or destruction if it lacks commercial value, and update public notice requirements for auctions.

Synopsis: Correcting a certain incorrect cross-reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code relating to the federal work opportunity credit.
Title: Income Tax - Work Opportunity Tax Credit - Technical Correction
bill_summary: Corrects an erroneous statutory cross-reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code regarding the federal work opportunity credit. Updates the cross-reference within the definition from Section 51 to Section 38 of the Internal Revenue Code. Clarifies eligibility for employers and not-for-profit entities claiming the State income tax credit. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Employers and not-for-profit entities claiming the Maryland Work Opportunity Tax Credit for qualified employees
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances because the bill makes only technical corrections.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the Office of the Comptroller to correct a technical cross-reference to the Internal Revenue Code regarding the Maryland Work Opportunity Tax Credit, which the Comptroller administers as the state's chief tax collection authority.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for the State child and dependent care tax credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit - Alterations
bill_summary: Limits eligibility for the State child and dependent care tax credit to resident taxpayers. Defines a taxpayer as an individual or married couple filing a joint income tax return. Prohibits nonresident taxpayers from claiming the credit for qualifying dependent care expenses. Applies the restriction to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
stakeholders: Nonresident income tax filers who incur qualifying child and dependent care expenses
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by an estimated $332,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to the elimination of the credit for nonresident taxpayers. Expenditures are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill introduced at the request of the Office of the Comptroller. As the state's tax administration and revenue collection agency, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing the altered eligibility criteria for the child and dependent care income tax credit, adjusting tax forms and filing instructions, and processing returns.

Synopsis: Altering the amount of a certain appropriation the Governor is required to make for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund; and repealing a provision of law requiring 100% of the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund to be used for community enhancement projects in sustainable communities located, at least in part, within the boundary created by Interstate 495 in the State and the District of Columbia beginning in fiscal year 2024.
Title: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund - Annual Appropriation and Authorized Uses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Increases the mandated annual appropriation for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund to $12,000,000 beginning in fiscal 2025. Requires the Governor to include this appropriation in the annual operating or capital budget. Restricts fund use to community enhancement projects within specified sustainable communities in Montgomery and Prince George's counties. Repeals a scheduled requirement limiting fund use starting in fiscal 2024 to areas inside Interstate 495. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: community development organizations, local governments, housing authority entities, and small businesses in designated sustainable communities in Montgomery County and Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State pay-as-you-go general fund or general obligation bond expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to meet the increased mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase commensurately by $5.0 million annually. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent eligible local jurisdictions receive additional program funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is the primary implementing agency that administers the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Program and Fund, overseeing the disbursement of funds for community enhancement projects in eligible sustainable communities.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing and supervising the execution of the annual state budget, which must accommodate the bill's increased statutory mandated annual appropriation of $12 million starting in fiscal year 2025.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an increased annual appropriation of $12 million in the operating or capital budget for the fund beginning in fiscal year 2025.

Synopsis: Establishing that a sheriff's sale of real property extinguishes subordinate liens on the land being sold; providing that certain provisions of the Act do not impair a lien on land affected by a judgment in favor of a local government for real property maintenance violations or nuisance condition violations that is indexed and recorded in accordance with the Maryland Rules; and authorizing the Judiciary to transfer up to $12,000,000 of a General Fund appropriation to a certain special fund on or before June 30, 2023.
Title: Real Property - Sheriff's Sales - Procedures and Subordinate Interests

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes that a sheriff's sale of real property extinguishes any subordinate lien or interest on the land sold. Requires judgment creditors to send notice of execution sales to property owners, occupants, and subordinate interest holders. Permits sheriffs to use assessment records instead of appraisals when levying on certain real property. Protects local government judgment liens for property maintenance or nuisance violations from debtor exemption claims. Authorizes the Judiciary to transfer up to $12,000,000 to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund.
responsible_party: Judiciary; county sheriffs
stakeholders: judgment creditors, judgment debtors, real property owners, subordinate lienholders, occupants of levied properties, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund increase by up to $12.0 million in fiscal 2023, offset by an equivalent general fund revenue decrease from the authorized transfer of Judiciary appropriations. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary and the Administrative Office of the Courts by altering statutory court procedures for money judgments and sheriff's sales of real property (including required court filings and affidavits). Additionally, it specifically authorizes the Judiciary to transfer up to $12.0 million of its FY 2023 General Fund appropriation to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund, which is managed and supervised by the State Court Administrator.

Synopsis: Expanding the investigative jurisdiction of the Independent Investigations Division of the Office of the Attorney General to include a police-involved incident resulting in serious bodily injury to an individual that is not otherwise within the jurisdiction of the Division; requiring the Division to submit an annual report on its activities in the prior calendar year to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before January 31; authorizing the Attorney General to prosecute certain criminal matters under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Office of the Attorney General - Independent Investigations Division - Authority to Prosecute

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Expands the investigative jurisdiction of the Independent Investigations Division within the Office of the Attorney General. Grants the Attorney General exclusive authority to prosecute criminal offenses discovered during Division investigations. Permits a State's Attorney to prosecute only if requested by the Attorney General. Authorizes State's Attorneys to refer police-involved incidents causing serious bodily injury to the Division. Repeals the requirement that the Division submit investigative reports to local State's Attorneys. Requires the Division to submit an annual activity report to the Governor and General Assembly by January 31.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Independent Investigations Division
stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies; police officers; individuals involved in police-involved incidents; State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $548,900 in FY 2024 to hire four personnel, increasing to $729,700 by FY 2028. State revenues are not affected. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the Independent Investigations Division (IID) within the Office of the Attorney General, expanding its investigative jurisdiction and granting the Attorney General exclusive prosecutorial authority over certain police-involved incidents. It also carries a direct fiscal impact requiring additional staff and funding for the agency.

The statute explicitly authorizes the IID to detail police officers employed by the Department of State Police to investigate alleged criminal offenses committed by police officers, and MSP is also subject to the mandatory incident reporting and investigation cooperation requirements.

The bill requires the IID to submit an annual report of its activities to the Governor by January 31 each year and mandates that the Governor include sufficient funding in the State budget for the operation of the Division.

The bill involves judicial procedures including the issuance and enforcement of subpoenas in circuit courts, applications for injunctive relief, grand jury utilization, and court prosecutions handled by the Attorney General.

Synopsis: Altering the term "inmate" to be "incarcerated individual" meaning an individual who is actually or constructively detained or confined in a correctional facility.
Title: Corrections - Incarcerated Individuals
bill_summary: Replaces the statutory term "inmate" with "incarcerated individual" throughout the Annotated Code of Maryland. Renames inmates as incarcerated individuals in every State law, executive order, rule, regulation, policy, and document. Directs code publishers to correct cross-references and terminology rendered incorrect by the Act. Requires publishers to consult with and receive approval from the Department of Legislative Services. Mandates that publishers describe any correction in an editor's note following the affected section.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
stakeholders: individuals confined in State and local correctional facilities; State officials, employees, and units
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary state department administering correctional facilities and supervising justice-involved individuals. The bill directly alters the statutory definition of an individual confined in a correctional facility from 'inmate' to 'incarcerated individual' in the Correctional Services Article and requires state correctional policies, regulations, and documents to adopt this terminology.
