Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow not more than $65,600,000 in order to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public facilities in Carroll County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds; etc.
Title: Carroll County - Public Facilities Bond

NarrowSubjects.Name: Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $65,600,000 by issuing general obligation bonds. Directs bond proceeds to finance public facilities, water and sewer projects, and loans to volunteer fire departments. Permits borrowing via installment purchase obligations to acquire agricultural land and woodland preservation easements. Requires bond maturities not to exceed 30 years from the date of issue. Mandates the county levy sufficient annual ad valorem property taxes to pay bond principal and interest. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
stakeholders: Carroll County residents, property owners in Carroll County, and volunteer fire departments in Carroll County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Carroll County bond revenues increase by up to $65.6 million, with county debt service expenditures increasing by an estimated $4.4 million annually over a 20-year period.

Synopsis: Altering the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to authorize grants from the Fund to be made for projects that prevent damages caused by black bears and reduce conflicts between black bears and humans; renaming the Fund to be the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund; increasing the maximum amount of reimbursement from the Fund per person annually authorized for damage caused by black bears to $5,000; authorizing the Governor to include at least $50,000 in the annual budget bill for the Fund; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund - Uses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Renames the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to award grants for projects preventing black bear damage through nonlethal methods. Caps grant funding to leave at least 10% of annual appropriations available for damage reimbursements. Increases the maximum annual black bear damage reimbursement per person from $3,000 to $5,000. Prohibits grant awards for lethal bear removal, stand-alone research, or direct revenue generation. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual budget bill appropriation of at least $50,000 to the fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Farmers, landowners, local governments, parks and recreation departments, businesses, tribes, institutions of higher education, and nonprofit organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $145,600 in FY 2024, which includes $95,637 for Department of Natural Resources personnel and administrative costs alongside $50,000 in discretionary fund capitalization. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $50,000 annually. Local governments and higher education institutions may experience indeterminate increases in grant revenues and operational expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for administering the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund, establishing and managing the new nonlethal conflict prevention grant program, verifying bear damage claims, and issuing reimbursements.

Statute requires damage amounts to be determined by extension agents of the University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Service before reimbursements can be made. Additionally, institutions of higher education are eligible grant recipients under the fund.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Comptroller shall account for the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $50,000 to the fund in the annual state budget bill.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive project grant funding under the expanded fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the holder of a Class 4 limited winery license to prepare, sell, or serve any food under certain conditions; altering certain requirements for off-premises and on-premises consumption at a limited winery; and removing the 14-day notice requirement for certain planned promotional events at a limited winery.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 4 Limited Winery License - Food Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Authorizes Class 4 limited winery license holders to prepare, sell, or serve sandwiches and other ready-to-eat light fare. Permits wineries licensed as food establishments to serve additional foods under specified gross receipt ratios. Extends daily operating hours for on-premises consumption and food sales until 10:00 p.m. each day. Repeals the requirement to give the Comptroller advance notice before holding planned promotional events.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; local licensing boards
stakeholders: Class 4 limited winery license holders and winery patrons in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government finances. Small business revenues for Class 4 limited winery licensees may increase due to expanded food service allowances and extended operating hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. The bill directly alters regulatory requirements for Class 4 limited wineries, including repealing the requirement that licensees submit advance notice of certain promotional events to the Comptroller and referencing the Comptroller's oversight of wine storage and reporting.

Class 4 limited wineries must produce wine from Maryland agricultural products and meet fruit cultivation requirements under § 2-206 of the Alcoholic Beverages Article, which authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to grant percentage exemptions and adopt regulations governing exemptions.

The bill allows wineries to serve and prepare expanded food menus if they obtain a food establishment license under Title 21, Subtitle 3 of the Health - General Article, which is overseen and regulated by the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments.

Synopsis: Altering the salary of the Washington County Sheriff to be 90% of the salary of the State's Attorney of Washington County; and repealing the requirement for the Washington County Salary Study Commission to study and issue a report that contains recommendations relating to the salary of the Sheriff of Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Sheriff's Salary - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Sets the salary of the Washington County Sheriff at 90% of the salary of the county State's Attorney. Repeals the requirement for the Washington County Salary Study Commission to study and recommend the sheriff's salary. Applies the compensation alteration to the next term of office following the effective date. Allows an individual appointed or elected to fill an unexpired term after the effective date to receive the salary. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Washington County Commissioners; Washington County Salary Study Commission
stakeholders: Sheriff of Washington County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Washington County expenditures increase by a minimum of $21,100 in fiscal 2027 and $36,200 annually thereafter to fund the sheriff's increased salary.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services, in coordination with the Department of Information Technology, to negotiate certain contracts with third parties for the acquisition or maintenance of body-worn cameras, equipment, or technology for certain law enforcement agencies; requiring the Department of Information Technology, in coordination with the Department of General Services, to study the cost and feasibility of implementing a statewide uniform storage and access system for law enforcement body-worn camera data; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement - Body-Worn Cameras (Body-Worn Camera Appropriation and Financing Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to negotiate third-party body-worn camera contracts upon law enforcement agency request. Requires the Department of General Services to coordinate these contract negotiations with the Department of Information Technology. Requires the Department of General Services to notify law enforcement agencies by posting contracts on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage. Prohibits restricting any law enforcement agency from receiving third-party services to view, edit, redact, or transfer camera data. Requires the Department of Information Technology to study a statewide uniform camera data storage and access system. Requires the Department of Information Technology to report study findings to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies; third-party vendors of body-worn cameras and related technology
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by between $200,000 and $400,000 in FY 2024 only for the Department of Information Technology to hire a consultant for the feasibility study, though costs may be mitigated by relevant prior studies. The Department of General Services and the Department of Information Technology can otherwise implement the bill with existing resources. State and local law enforcement agencies may achieve indeterminate administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is a primary implementing agency tasked with negotiating third-party contracts for body-worn cameras, equipment, and technology on behalf of law enforcement agencies, posting them on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage, and coordinating with DoIT on the statewide data storage and access feasibility study.

DoIT is directly tasked with conducting a feasibility and cost study regarding a statewide uniform storage and access system for body-worn camera data, reporting findings to legislative committees, and coordinating contract negotiations with DGS, resulting in a direct fiscal impact of up to $400,000.

As the primary state law enforcement agency subject to body-worn camera mandates, MSP is directly impacted as a beneficiary that can request and utilize contracts negotiated by DGS and will be affected by statewide storage and access systems.
DNR operates the Natural Resources Police, an authorized state law enforcement agency that may request DGS to negotiate contracts for body-worn camera acquisition and maintenance.

MDOT oversees state transportation police forces (such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and Maryland Transit Administration Police) that qualify as law enforcement agencies eligible to utilize the negotiated procurement contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs law enforcement and correctional security personnel and is an affected state agency that can benefit from administrative efficiencies under the negotiated body-worn camera contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP previously commissioned a relevant feasibility study on body-worn camera costs and data storage, which may provide data to mitigate DoIT study costs and align with the office's criminal justice coordination role.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority; exempting the Authority from certain provisions of State procurement law; and altering the report on the Authority's comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy the Authority is required to submit to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly to be due by December 15, 2023, to include any procurement activities undertaken by the Authority, and to be also submitted to the House Health and Government Operations Committee.
Title: Baltimore City – West North Avenue Development Authority – Membership and Procurement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Alters the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority in Baltimore City. Adds state economic officials and authority-appointed members to the governing body. Delays the reporting deadline for the comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to December 15, 2023. Requires the revitalization report to include procurement activities undertaken by the authority. Exempts the authority from general state procurement law while retaining minority business enterprise requirements. Terminates the procurement exemption on September 30, 2026.
responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents and business owners in the West North Avenue target area and buffer zone in Baltimore City, minority business enterprises, and state contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The authority will use existing funds to cover an estimated $250,000 expedited contract to complete the revitalization strategy.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of Commerce (or the Secretary's designee) as a voting member of the West North Avenue Development Authority.
The bill explicitly adds the Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or the Executive Director's designee) as a member of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development serves on the West North Avenue Development Authority, which is charged with developing a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan and housing strategies.
The Secretary of Transportation serves on the Authority, and MDOT serves as the certifying agency for the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program to which the Authority remains subject.
The President of Coppin State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, serves as the Chair of the Authority and is granted authority to appoint two additional members.
As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is impacted by the provision granting the Authority an exemption from Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
Exempting the Authority from Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article removes standard procurement oversight and approval mechanisms normally required under the Board of Public Works.
The Governor appoints a member to the Authority and receives the required comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Authority remains specifically subject to the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program under Title 14, Subtitle 3, which is coordinated and monitored by this office.

Synopsis: Establishing certain procedures regarding the persons who may establish or receive distributions from an ABLE account in the Maryland ABLE Program for a certain eligible individual; and requiring the Maryland 529 Board to adopt certain procedures regarding the establishment and operation of an ABLE account by a person other than a certain designated beneficiary.
Title: Maryland Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) Program - Account Establishment - Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc

bill_summary: Establishes procedures for who may open an ABLE account and request distributions on behalf of an eligible individual. Permits an account to be established by the eligible individual, a selected representative, or designated family members and fiduciaries in a specific priority order. Excludes minors, individuals subject to protective or no-contact orders, and individuals liable for financial exploitation from opening accounts. Authorizes authorized account establishers to request distributions alongside designated beneficiaries. Requires the Maryland 529 Board to adopt procedures for account establishment and operation by authorized third parties.
responsible_party: Maryland 529 Board
stakeholders: Eligible individuals with disabilities, their families, legal guardians, and authorized representatives under the Maryland ABLE Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local revenues may decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2024 due to additional income tax subtraction modifications. Maryland 529 nonbudgeted fee revenues and distribution expenditures increase with new accounts. State general fund expenditures may decrease if fee revenues offset the existing $300,000 annual State grant to the Maryland ABLE Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the governing statutes of the Maryland ABLE Program, which is administered by Maryland 529, establishing procedures and regulatory authority regarding who may establish accounts and receive distributions.
The State Treasurer's Office oversees the Maryland 529 program and its components, including the Maryland ABLE program, making it directly responsible for administrative oversight and implementation.

The bill is projected to impact State personal income tax revenues collected by the Comptroller due to additional subtraction modifications claimed for contributions to and distributions from newly opened ABLE accounts.
The Department of Disabilities works in consultation with Maryland 529 to administer and promote the ABLE program to eligible Maryland residents with disabilities.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees Medicaid and means-tested health programs, for which assets held in ABLE accounts are protected from eligibility determinations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide eligible seniors access to affordable civil law-related services; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation of $225,000 in the annual budget for the Program.
Title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program
bill_summary: Establishes the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. Serves clients at least 65 years old with family incomes up to 75% of State median family income. Requires an intake method, outreach mechanisms, and grants to fund legal representation, particularly in rural communities. Primarily covers last will and testaments, powers of attorney, special needs trusts, advance health care directives, and life estate deeds. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $225,000 for the program.
responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
stakeholders: Maryland seniors aged 65 and older with family incomes up to 75% of the State median family income, and civil legal service grantees
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,000 annually beginning in FY 2024, with funding in FY 2024 being discretionary and reflecting a mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2025. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a $225,000 appropriation for the program in the annual state budget and requires the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the program's implementation and utilization.
As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal management, DBM must account for and execute the mandated annual general fund appropriation of $225,000 established by the bill.

The program is specifically targeted at Maryland residents aged 65 and older, directly intersecting with the Department of Aging's mission to support older adults' legal advocacy, rights, and access to essential life-planning services.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Center for Mental Health Services for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds related to certified community behavioral health clinics for fiscal year 2025; and requiring the Department to apply to the Administration for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program for fiscal year 2026.
Title: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics - Planning Grant Funds and Demonstration Application

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply for federal grant funds for certified community behavioral health clinics. Directs the department to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Center for Mental Health Services. Mandates submitting the planning, development, and implementation grant application for fiscal year 2025. Requires applying for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program for fiscal year 2026. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Certified community behavioral health clinics, community behavioral health care providers, and individuals seeking mental health or substance use treatment services
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on state or local finances. The Maryland Department of Health can apply for federal grant funds and demonstration program inclusion using existing budgeted resources. Federal planning grant revenues in fiscal 2025 were already anticipated under current operations, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 362 specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of Health apply to SAMHSA for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds for FY 2025 and for inclusion in the federal CCBHC demonstration program for FY 2026.

Synopsis: Defining "commercial use" in Baltimore City to include multifamily residential development if the development is located within a waterfront commercial zoning district and within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station.
Title: Baltimore City - Commercial Use - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Defines "commercial use" under Baltimore City zoning law to include certain multifamily residential developments. Applies this classification to multifamily residential development located within a waterfront commercial zoning district. Requires the development to also be located within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; Baltimore City Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals
stakeholders: Commercial and residential property developers, landowners, and residents in Baltimore City within waterfront commercial zoning districts near commuter rail stations
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 371 amends Title 10 of the Land Use Article regarding Baltimore City zoning definitions to classify certain transit-oriented, waterfront multifamily residential developments as commercial use. The Maryland Department of Planning oversees state land use policy and assists local jurisdictions with comprehensive planning.

The bill alters land use definitions to facilitate multifamily residential development in waterfront commercial zoning districts near commuter rail stations, directly interacting with housing development patterns and community revitalization policies overseen by DHCD.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Physicians to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, under certain circumstances, to reinstate the license of an individual who is on inactive or emeritus status; exempting licensees who are on inactive status or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements; repealing the requirement that the Board issue a license to an individual who is on inactive status under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Board of Physicians – Inactive and Emeritus Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Physicians to place a qualifying licensee on emeritus status upon application and fee payment. Exempts physicians on inactive or emeritus status from license expiration terms and continuing medical education requirements. Prohibits licensees on inactive or emeritus status from practicing medicine or delegating medical acts. Permits emeritus status licensees to use titles such as doctor or physician without representing authorization to practice. Requires the Board to reinstate an inactive or emeritus license upon satisfaction of renewal conditions and fee payment.
responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Maryland-licensed physicians, retired physicians seeking emeritus status, and physicians on inactive status
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Physicians workload can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Any net impact on special fund revenues from emeritus or inactive status licensee fees is anticipated to be minimal, with no effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians (MBP) is an operating unit and health occupations licensing board within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts MDH/MBP operations by establishing rules, fee structures, and application procedures for physician emeritus and inactive status.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the payment of a benefit by a governmental unit or quasi-public corporation to a covered employee offsets the liability for benefits under the workers' compensation law; and stating that it is the intent of the General Assembly that the Maryland Association of Counties and the Professional Fire Fighters of Maryland jointly research and report data and analysis on the effects of the Act by December 1, 2024, to interested parties and certain committees of the General Assembly.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Benefits - Offset and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Limits workers' compensation benefit offsets for covered employees of governmental units or quasi-public corporations. Applies the offset only when employer-paid benefits and workers' compensation benefits cover the same body part. Abrogates the Maryland Supreme Court holding in Spevak v. Montgomery County. Requires application of the offset consistent with Reger v. Washington County Board of Education. Directs local government and firefighter associations to jointly research and report findings by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Covered employees of Maryland governmental units and quasi-public corporations, local governments, the Subsequent Injury Fund, and Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances or operations. Local government expenditures likely increase due to higher workers' compensation payouts from narrowed benefit offsets, but specific figures cannot be reliably estimated. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures and premium revenues increase correspondingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the independent state agency responsible for administering the Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims, and the bill directly governs its authority under Section 9-610 to determine benefit offsets and make awards.

The Subsequent Injury Fund is explicitly amended in Section 9-610, which alters the circumstances under which municipal or quasi-public benefit payments satisfy the fund's statutory liability for workers' compensation benefits.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity is directly impacted fiscally as an insurer of local government entities, resulting in increased benefit payouts and adjusted premiums.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of certain voting and nonvoting members of the Upper Shore Regional Council.
Title: Economic Development - Upper Shore Regional Council - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Alters the voting and nonvoting membership of the Upper Shore Regional Council. Removes the requirement that three Cecil County commissioners serve as voting members. Designates the Cecil County Executive and two Cecil County Council members as voting members. Requires the Cecil County Council to appoint the two voting council members. Adds unappointed regional county council members as nonvoting members of the council.
responsible_party: Upper Shore Regional Council
stakeholders: Cecil County Executive, Cecil County Council members, and the Upper Shore Regional Council
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Minimal local fiscal impact, as the bill alters county representation without changing overall voting membership numbers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory composition and membership of the Upper Shore Regional Council, an entity encompassed under state regional councils and advisory bodies.

The Upper Shore Regional Council is established under the Economic Development Article to foster regional economic development and coordinate with the Department of Commerce, which was consulted as an information source for the bill.
The Upper Shore Regional Council is one of the five rural regional planning and development councils that partner with and receive support through the Rural Maryland Council.

Synopsis: Authorizing the County Executive and County Council of Prince George's County to determine the compensation for the judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Judges of the Orphans' Court - Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Executive and County Council of Prince George’s County to determine annual compensation for judges of the Orphans’ Court. Repeals fixed statutory salaries of $50,000 for associate judges and $55,000 for the Chief Judge. Prohibits applying compensation changes during a term of office that began before October 1, 2023. Permits compensation changes to take effect at the beginning of a judge’s subsequent term of office. Authorizes salary changes for judges appointed or elected after the effective date to fill an unexpired term.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Executive; Prince George's County Council
stakeholders: Judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County; Prince George's County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Potential indeterminate increase or decrease in Prince George's County expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 depending on salary determinations by local officials. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judicial Branch, of which the county Orphans' Courts are a specialized component.

The Register of Wills serves as the clerk to the Orphans' Court in each county, maintaining probate proceedings and working directly with the Orphans' Court judges whose compensation is affected by this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland to study and make recommendations regarding the effectiveness and viability of certain incentives, offerings, or practices employed in other states to attract, support, and retain individuals in fire fighting and emergency medical services roles; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Recruitment and Hiring -see also- Work, Labor, and Emp.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland. Directs the Commission to study practices and incentives used in other states to attract and retain personnel. Requires the Commission to evaluate the suitability of those practices for Maryland. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff support for the Commission. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland
stakeholders: Career and volunteer firefighters, emergency medical services personnel, and local fire companies in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 only for one part-time contractual employee at the Maryland Department of Labor. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is directly responsible for staffing the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland, has a representative appointed by the Secretary of Labor serving on the Commission, and incurs a fiscal impact of approximately $25,000 to hire staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), or their designee, is designated as a mandatory member of the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study body—the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland—to evaluate recruitment and retention policies and report recommendations.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI), which is a branch of the University of Maryland, is designated as a member of the Commission.

The newly created Commission is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding fire fighting and emergency medical services incentives and retention directly to the Governor by December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to make transfers of not more than $150,000,000 subject to certain conditions to establish quasi-endowment funds; and authorizing the Board to use investment income produced by quasi-endowment funds in accordance with the University System of Maryland Policy on Endowment Fund Spending Rule to provide need-based student financial aid.
Title: University System of Maryland - Board of Regents - Quasi-Endowment Funds

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland Board of Regents to transfer up to $150,000,000 to establish a quasi-endowment fund. Requires the transferred funds to come from balances held and invested by the State Treasurer. Authorizes the Board to use investment income from the fund for need-based student financial aid. Requires financial aid spending to follow the University System of Maryland Policy on Endowment Fund Spending Rule.
responsible_party: Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: University System of Maryland students with financial need; University System of Maryland constituent institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming transfers of $150.0 million occur in FY 2024, University System of Maryland fund balances decrease by $150.0 million with an offsetting increase in quasi-endowment funds. Higher education revenues may increase by an estimated $1.6 million annually beginning in FY 2025 from higher investment yields, and scholarship expenditures may increase by about $6.4 million annually, though returns will vary with market conditions. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the University System of Maryland (USM) Board of Regents, authorizing the transfer of up to $150 million from fund balances to establish a quasi-endowment fund and directing the use of investment proceeds for need-based student financial aid.

The authorized transfers of up to $150 million come directly from fund balances held and invested by the State Treasurer, impacting Treasurer-held investment balances. The agency also receives an annual investment performance report.
The Comptroller of Maryland is designated by statute to receive an annual investment performance report on the university's gift, endowment, and quasi-endowment investment portfolio.
The Governor's Office receives the required annual investment performance report submitted by the USM Board of Regents.

Synopsis: Increasing the funding level of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund that is administered by the Home Improvement Commission from $250,000 to $1,000,000; increasing a certain Fund threshold that determines whether a fee is assessed to each contractor; and increasing the limit, from $100,000 to $250,000, on the amount of money the Commission may award from the Fund to all claimants for the acts or omissions of a single contractor, subject to a certain reimbursement to the Fund.
Title: Business Regulation - Home Improvement Commission - Guaranty Fund and Award Limits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Increases the minimum balance of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund from $250,000 to $1,000,000. Raises the maximum award to all claimants for a single contractor's acts or omissions from $100,000 to $250,000. Requires the Maryland Home Improvement Commission to assess each contractor $50 if pending claims threaten that $1,000,000 threshold. Requires the Commission to submit a restoration report to legislative committees within 30 days of projecting a balance under $1,000,000. Authorizes proportionate claim payments when approved claims against a contractor exceed $250,000 less prior unreimbursed payments.
responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission
stakeholders: licensed home improvement contractors and residential property owners seeking compensation for actual losses from contractor acts or omissions
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund increase by an indeterminate, but likely significant amount due to higher minimum fund balance requirements and increased claim payout limits. Commission operations can be implemented with existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters the statutory minimum balance of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund administered by MHIC, raises the threshold for mandatory contractor assessments, and increases the maximum award limit payable from the fund per contractor.
The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund special account and the expert witness account, and is responsible for investing the fund's increased balances.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to establish a Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program to provide financial incentives to holders of aquaculture leases who maintain the lease in accordance with certain criteria, maintain the restorative conditions for at least 4 years, and meet certain other criteria the Department considers necessary; authorizing a holder of an aquaculture lease who is participating in the Pilot Program to meet certain requirements by shellfish seed planting only; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to establish and implement a Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program. Directs the program to provide financial incentives to aquaculture leaseholders who maintain restorative conditions for at least four years. Authorizes participating leaseholders to satisfy active use lease requirements through shellfish seed planting only. Requires the department to identify restorative metrics considering oyster density, biomass, and habitat complexity. Mandates the adoption of program regulations by October 1, 2024. Terminates the pilot program on September 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Maryland aquaculture leaseholders
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $144,631 in FY 2024 to hire two staff members to administer the program, increasing to $196,800 by FY 2028. Total expenditures exclude the cost of financial incentive payments, which are indeterminate and dependent on program design and participation. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, managing, and adopting regulations for the Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program, as well as administering financial incentives to qualifying leaseholders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires DNR to consult and coordinate with the statutory Aquaculture Coordinating Council to develop program criteria, metrics, and financial incentive payment rates.
The bill specifies coordination with the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES), a USM institution, to identify and develop metrics and criteria for restorative aquaculture.

Synopsis: Altering the amount of taxable or tax exempt bonds that the Maryland Stadium Authority may issue for certain sports entertainment facilities from $200,000,000 to $220,000,000; altering the entities from which the Authority is required to have received a request for financing and construction management services concerning a sports entertainment facility; altering the entities with which the Authority is required to enter into an agreement before issuing bonds to finance a sports entertainment facility; etc.
Title: Economic Development – Sports Entertainment Facilities – Financing and Construction

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds

bill_summary: Increases the maximum bond issuance by the Maryland Stadium Authority for sports entertainment facilities from $200,000,000 to $220,000,000. Authorizes a nonprofit organization that will own or operate a facility to request financing and construction management services. Requires the Authority to secure an agreement with the nonprofit organization or local jurisdiction before issuing bonds. Requires participating entities to maintain, repair, market, and operate the facility in first-class operating condition. Mandates an annual maintenance assessment report to legislative committees on or before December 31 each year.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: nonprofit organizations that own or operate sports entertainment facilities, local governments, and sports facility contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Sports Entertainment Facilities Financing Fund increase by $15.0 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million in FY 2025 from bond proceeds. General fund revenues decrease by $1.1 million in FY 2026 and $1.5 million annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 to cover debt service payments from State Lottery revenues. Local revenues and expenditures may increase for related facility construction and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory bonding capacity of the Maryland Stadium Authority for sports entertainment facilities, increasing it from $200 million to $220 million, and authorizes the Authority to receive financing requests and enter into facility agreements with nonprofit organizations.

The Board of Public Works is statutorily required to approve bond issuances by the Maryland Stadium Authority under the altered bond cap, as well as review and approve the financing plans and written agreements established with eligible entities (now including nonprofit organizations).

Synopsis: Extending the termination date, to June 30, 2024, for provisions relating to the authorization of holders of certain manufacturer's licenses to sell and deliver and to directly ship their own alcoholic beverages products to certain individuals under certain circumstances; establishing the maximum amount of beer and liquor that holders of certain manufacturer's licenses may directly ship to consumers in a calendar year; delaying the effective date for the authorization of certain manufacturer off-site permits to July 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages – Manufacturer’s Licenses and Off–Site Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: Extends through June 30, 2024, the authority of certain alcoholic beverages manufacturers to sell, deliver, and directly ship products. Limits direct shipment authority to manufacturers authorized by the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission on or before April 6, 2023. Restricts annual direct shipments per consumer to 3,456 ounces of beer or 18 standard 750-milliliter bottles of liquor. Requires reporting of shipped and delivered amounts to the Commission by December 1, 2023, and June 1, 2024. Delays until July 1, 2024, authorization for specified manufacturers to sell up to 288 ounces of beer off-site.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: licensed alcoholic beverages manufacturers in Maryland (including breweries, wineries, and distilleries) and Maryland consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal State general fund revenues and expenditures for the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission are maintained through fiscal 2024 due to the extension of authorizations. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates the direct shipment, delivery, and reporting of alcoholic beverages by manufacturers, which requires verification that all applicable sales and excise taxes are paid. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller is responsible for collecting state sales taxes and regulating the alcohol industry.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for the credit against the State income tax for certain film production activities to include documentaries and talk, reality, and game shows; increasing the percentage of total direct costs that qualify for the tax credit; increasing the aggregate amount of tax credit certificates that the Secretary of Commerce may issue for fiscal years 2024 through 2026; establishing the Maryland Entertainment Council to study and make recommendations regarding Maryland's film, television, and entertainment industry; etc.
Title: Film Production Activity Income Tax Credit - Alterations and Maryland Entertainment Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the film production activity income tax credit to include documentaries and talk, reality, or game shows. Includes compensation for Maryland-domiciled writers, directors, or producers within qualifying direct costs. Increases credit percentages to 28% of qualified direct costs, or 30% for a television series. Increases the annual tax credit cap to $15 million in fiscal 2024, $17.5 million in 2025, and $20 million in 2026. Establishes the Maryland Entertainment Council to study the entertainment industry and submit strategic recommendations by September 2024.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Entertainment Council
stakeholders: Qualified film production entities, Maryland small or independent film entities, in-state writers, directors, and producers, and Maryland film industry workers and support businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $3.0 million in FY 2024, $5.5 million in FY 2025, and $8.0 million in FY 2026 across the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund due to expanded tax credit caps. State general fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2024 and FY 2025 for council study and evaluation costs. Local highway user revenues decrease by $0.1 million to $0.3 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency administering the Film Production Activity Income Tax Credit program, determining project eligibility, issuing tax credit certificates, and providing staff support and funding for the newly created Maryland Entertainment Council.

The Comptroller of Maryland jointly adopts regulations with the Department of Commerce to administer the credit, receives notifications of estimated direct costs, and processes the income tax credits and refunds claimed by qualifying production entities.

The bill requires the Governor to appoint multiple members and honorary cochairs to the Maryland Entertainment Council, tasks the Governor's Senior Advisor on Film, Television, and Entertainment with chairing the Council, and directs the Council to submit preliminary and final reports to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Maryland Entertainment Council as a temporary advisory body tasked with studying Maryland's film and entertainment industry and providing strategic recommendations to state leaders.

The fiscal note identifies a notable direct fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), projecting revenue reductions of $0.5 million to $1.5 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026, which correspondingly reduces TTF expenditures for local highway user revenue grants.

Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County, from time to time, to borrow not more than $56,000,000 in order to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public facilities in St. Mary's County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds; etc.
Title: St. Mary's County - Public Facilities Bond

NarrowSubjects.Name: Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Piers and Docks -see also- Marinas; Ports
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to borrow up to $56,000,000 through general obligation bonds. Requires bond proceeds to fund the construction, improvement, or development of specified public facilities. Limits bond maturities to no later than 30 years from their date of issue. Directs the county to levy annual ad valorem property taxes sufficient to pay bond principal and interest. Exempts all issued bonds, refunding bonds, and associated income from Maryland state and local taxation.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
stakeholders: Taxpayers and residents of St. Mary's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. St. Mary’s County bond proceeds increase county revenues by up to $56.0 million, and county debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $3.8 million annually over a 20-year period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 457 exempts the principal, interest, and income derived from St. Mary's County's public facilities bonds from state taxation. As Maryland's principal tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the administration of state tax exemptions, although the bill has no direct state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives to study the types and impact of solar energy incentives and make recommendations regarding measures and incentives needed to ensure that the State meets the solar energy goals established in the State's renewable energy portfolio standard, minority business participation, the creation of good quality jobs, equitable access to renewable energy, and efficient use of land; and requiring the Task Force to submit its report to the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2023.
Title: Task Force to Study Solar Incentives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives to examine solar development and financial incentives. Requires the Maryland Energy Administration to staff the task force and designate the chair. Directs the task force to study state and federal solar incentives and compliance fee calculations. Requires recommendations regarding renewable energy goals, workforce development, minority business enterprise participation, and efficient land use. Mandates a report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Solar energy developers, minority business enterprises in solar development, electric utilities, electricity customers, and environmental advocacy organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues or local government finances. The Maryland Energy Administration can staff the task force and provide member expense reimbursements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary implementing agency for the bill; its Director serves on the Task Force and designates the chair, and MEA is required to provide staff support and absorb travel reimbursement costs for the Task Force.

The Chairman of the Public Service Commission (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which is tasked with studying solar renewable energy credits and alternative compliance fees under the Public Utilities Article overseen by the PSC.
The People's Counsel is designated to appoint a representative of the Office of People's Counsel to serve as a member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state body, the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives, to study solar policies and incentives and report findings to the General Assembly.
The Governor is responsible for appointing six members to the Task Force: four representatives of the solar energy industry and two representatives of environmental advocacy groups.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for the six gubernatorial appointments to the Task Force.

Synopsis: Establishing certain goals and programs related to land conservation; establishing the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program to provide loans to land trusts to purchase land for conservation purposes; authorizing the Maryland Environmental Trust to exercise certain remedies under certain circumstances; prohibiting a person from making any false statements affecting a Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program loan; establishing the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program to support land conservation goals; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Land Conservation - Establishment of Goals and Programs (Maryland the Beautiful Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Smart Growth -see also- Zoning and Planning

bill_summary: Establishes State land conservation goals to conserve 30% of Maryland land by 2030 and 40% by 2040. Requires the Smart Growth Subcabinet to publish an implementation plan by July 1, 2024, and report annually. Creates the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program and Fund to finance property acquisitions for conservation. Establishes the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program administered by the Maryland Environmental Trust. Authorizes the Governor to include annual budget appropriations for competitive conservation grants and local stewardship capacity building.
responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Trust; Smart Growth Subcabinet; Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: local land trusts, private landowners, local governments, schools, and nonprofit conservation organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6,747,711 in FY 2025, by $738,573 in FY 2026, and by ongoing amounts in future years for personnel, fund capitalization, and grants. Special fund revenues increase by $6.0 million in FY 2025 from fund capitalization, with special fund expenditures of $3.0 million annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026 for revolving loans. Local revenues and expenditures likely increase beginning in FY 2025 from participation in conservation grants and partnerships.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) is a unit of the Department of Natural Resources. The bill tasks MET with administering the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund, the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program, and stewardship grants, requiring additional staff and managing multi-million dollar funds. A DNR representative also sits on the new advisory committee.

The Department of Planning plays a central role in the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which the bill tasks with developing, publishing, and updating a plan to meet statewide land conservation goals (30% by 2030 and 40% by 2040) and submitting annual progress reports to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes ambitious land conservation goals that encompass agricultural land preservation, affects transfer tax revenue allocations that support the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), and includes the department as a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Land Preservation Rapid Response Advisory Committee to review, prioritize, and make recommendations on program loan applications.
The bill specifically directs the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Comptroller account for the newly established Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include annual appropriations in the state budget bill for grant and loan programs and involves executive subcabinet coordination.
The bill authorizes significant new appropriations and special fund structures that impact state budget planning and execution, and the Secretary sits on the Smart Growth Subcabinet.
The department is part of the Smart Growth Subcabinet tasked with implementing state conservation goals, which include carbon and greenhouse gas sequestration and ecological preservation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to review and update specifications for sediment control plans in a certain manner on or before December 1, 2025, and every 5 years thereafter; prohibiting the Department from authorizing the discharge of stormwater associated with construction activity under a general discharge permit unless certain requirements are satisfied; and requiring the Department to take certain public notice and comment actions if a person makes a written request within the public notification period of the permit.
Title: Sediment Control Plans, Discharge Permits for Stormwater Associated With Construction Activity, and Notice and Comment Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Erosion -see also- Sediment Control; Shore Erosion
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to update sediment control plan specifications by December 1, 2025, and every five years thereafter. Requires the Department to revise water quantity control standards using the most recent precipitation data available. Prohibits applying updates retroactively to active, unexpired projects where construction has commenced. Prohibits authorizing general discharge permits for construction disturbing five or more acres in specified sensitive areas until public notice requirements are met. Requires the Department to extend the public comment period to 60 days upon receiving a timely written request.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: construction permit applicants, land developers, engineering firms, local soil conservation districts, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $83,303 in FY 2024 and at least $100,000 annually thereafter for one staff engineer. MDE anticipates additional costs exceeding $500,000 beginning in FY 2024 to update specifications, which may be offset by federal grants. Local government expenditures may increase starting in FY 2026 for training and enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary regulatory agency tasked with administering the bill. MDE must review and update specifications for sediment control plans every five years, report to the General Assembly, and implement enhanced public notice and comment requirements for construction stormwater discharge permits.

MDOT SHA holds an NPDES Phase I MS4 permit requiring compliance with state erosion and sediment control programs and conducts substantial roadway construction activities that require sediment control plans and stormwater discharge permits.

MDOT oversees large-scale transportation and infrastructure construction projects that require compliance with sediment control specifications and stormwater discharge permits, potentially experiencing project timeline and compliance cost impacts.

DGS manages planning, design, and construction of state-owned facilities, making it an affected permit holder subject to updated sediment control plan specifications and potential public review delays for capital projects.

MDA oversees soil conservation programs and works closely with local soil conservation districts, which serve as statutory approval authorities for erosion and sediment control plans under the affected statutes.

DNR manages state lands and waterways, interfaces with Critical Area Buffer protections referenced in the bill, and undertakes environmental restoration projects that may interact with the bill's permitting exemptions and water quality standards.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County; requiring the Task Force to study issues related to student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts for bus contractors in Charles County and to research best practices in surrounding jurisdictions related to the facilitation of student transportation; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the members of the Charles County Delegation to the General Assembly on or before September 1, 2023.
Title: Charles County - Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to study student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts for bus contractors. Requires the Task Force to research best practices in surrounding jurisdictions regarding student transportation facilitation. Mandates a report of findings and recommendations to the Charles County Delegation by September 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: school bus contractors and school bus drivers in Charles County, Charles County Public Schools, and the Amalgamated Transit Union Local 689
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Maryland Department of Labor can staff the task force with existing resources, and member travel expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. The bill does not materially affect Charles County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff and administrative support for the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary statutory task force—the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County—to study student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts.

Synopsis: Requiring that a county or municipality that operates a minority business enterprise utilization program for county or municipal procurements and has a process for the certification of minority business enterprises shall accept as certified a person that holds a certification as a minority business enterprise by the State certification agency.
Title: Local Procurements - Minority Business Enterprise Utilization Programs - Certification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires counties and municipalities operating minority business enterprise utilization programs to accept State-certified minority business enterprises. Applies to local jurisdictions that maintain their own certification process for procurement programs. Mandates acceptance of any entity certified by the designated State certification agency. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: certified minority business enterprises and county and municipal procurement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State certification requests for the Maryland Department of Transportation may increase minimally, absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local governments experience no material fiscal impact, though some may realize indeterminate administrative savings if they discontinue separate certification processes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the designated State certification agency under § 14-303(b) of the State Finance and Procurement Article. The bill requires local governments to accept MDOT's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) certifications, which could result in an increase in certification applications submitted to MDOT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office oversees and coordinates the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program and policies across Maryland, making changes to how state MBE certifications are recognized at the local level relevant to its mission.

Synopsis: Altering composition of the stakeholder advisory committee to advise the Department of Natural Resources on the scope and management of Port of Deposit State Historical Park; requiring the Department to make a certain report to the General Assembly on or before September 1, 2024; extending the deadline for the Bainbridge Development Corporation to transfer certain property to the Department to June 1, 2025; authorizing the Governor to include in the State budget an appropriation of at least $400,000 for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Port of Deposit State Historical Park - Planning

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees

bill_summary: Alters planning requirements, advisory committee membership, and property transfer deadlines for the Port of Deposit State Historical Park. Authorizes the Bainbridge Development Corporation to transfer up to 150 acres to the Department of Natural Resources by June 1, 2025. Removes the historic Tome School from required transfer parcels while retaining the Snow Hill archaeological site. Requires transferred property excluded from the park to be preserved in perpetuity based on stakeholder advisory committee recommendations. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to report on park property and funding needs by September 1, 2024. Authorizes the Governor to appropriate at least $400,000 in fiscal year 2025 for archaeological and soil studies.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Bainbridge Development Corporation
stakeholders: Bainbridge Development Corporation, residents of Cecil County and Port Deposit, and visitors to Port of Deposit State Historical Park
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by at least $400,000 in fiscal year 2025 if the Governor includes the authorized appropriation for a Phase 1 Archaeological Survey and Soil Study. Revenues are not affected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for administering the Port of Deposit State Historical Park, establishing the stakeholder advisory committee, managing property transferred from the Bainbridge Development Corporation, submitting the required study/report to the General Assembly, and conducting the archaeological survey and soil study.

The Secretary of Planning (or designee) and the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (which is administratively housed within the Department of Planning) are designated as ex officio members of the stakeholder advisory committee for the historical park.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and modifies the composition and reporting duties of the Port of Deposit State Historical Park Stakeholder Advisory Committee.
The Chief Archaeologist of MDOT SHA (or their designee) is designated as a voting member of the stakeholder advisory committee to advise DNR on the scope and management of the park.
The Chief Archaeologist of the Maryland Department of Transportation, State Highway Administration, is appointed as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $400,000 in the annual State budget for fiscal year 2025 to DNR for an archaeological survey and soil study.

Synopsis: Altering the defined term "peer support counseling program" for peer services offered to fire, rescue, or emergency medical services members to be "peer support program"; and requiring peer support programs to be evidence-based.
Title: Fire, Rescue, or Emergency Medical Services Entities - Peer Support Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Alters terminology and standards for peer support programs serving fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel. Requires peer support programs, services, and specialist training to be evidence-based. Replaces references to counseling sessions with interactions regarding confidentiality protections and disclosures. Directs the Behavioral Health Administration to focus its best-practices report on evidence-based peer support programs. Mandates the administration publish a list of evidence-based training programs on its website following report completion.
responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
stakeholders: members of fire, rescue, or emergency medical services entities; peer support specialists; International Association of Fire Fighters
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact as the changes are technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Behavioral Health Administration, a division within the Maryland Department of Health, develop a report on best practices and professional standards for evidence-based peer support programs and publish the report and a list of training programs on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Behavioral Health Administration to consult with the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems in developing the report on best practices, professional standards, and guidelines for peer support programs for fire, rescue, and EMS personnel.

Synopsis: Altering the formula for the calculation of certain assessments by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; requiring the Board of Trustees of the Fund, under certain circumstances, to authorize the Fund to withdraw certain amounts from the money held by the Fund from a prior overassessment; prohibiting members of the Industry Automobile Insurance Association from being subject to an annual assessment under certain circumstances; requiring in a certain fiscal year that additional funds be allocated to the Fund; etc.
Title: Insurance – Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund – Assessments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Alters the assessment calculation and collection process for the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund. Authorizes the Fund on June 1, 2023, to withdraw money held from prior overassessments into Fund surplus. Prohibits annual assessments on Industry Automobile Insurance Association members when prior overassessment money equals or exceeds the assessment. Requires Association members to refund excess surcharges to policyholders or apply them as expense reductions in subsequent rate filings. Increases the Fund's statutory distribution of uninsured motorist penalty revenue by $2,000,000 for fiscal year 2024. Requires the Fund to report to the General Assembly by July 1, 2023, regarding fund balances and withdrawn money.
responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; Industry Automobile Insurance Association; Maryland Insurance Administration; Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; motor vehicle insurers licensed in Maryland (Industry Automobile Insurance Association members); motor vehicle policyholders; uninsured vehicle owners assessed penalties
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $2.0 million in FY 2024 due to a temporary $2.0 million reallocation of uninsured motorist penalty collections to the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF). Nonbudgeted MAIF revenues increase by $10.2 million in FY 2023 from accessing prior overassessment reserve balances and by $2.0 million in FY 2024 from the penalty reallocation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the assessment formula, overassessment withdrawal procedures, and funding allocations for the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), resulting in an increase of nonbudgeted revenues of $10.2 million in FY 2023 and $2.0 million in FY 2024.
