The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is tasked with receiving notification of assessment certifications, verifying Board of Trustees calculations, and determining aggregate net direct written premiums for private passenger and commercial auto insurers.

The Motor Vehicle Administration collects vehicle lapsed-security penalties under Section 17-106 of the Transportation Article, and the bill alters the distribution formula for these penalties in FY 2024 to reallocate $2.0 million from the General Fund to MAIF.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the administration of the Transportation Article provisions amended by the bill regarding vehicle security penalties and their statutorily designated fund distributions.

Synopsis: Extending to June 30, 2025, the inclusion of certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of "telehealth" for the purpose of certain provisions of law relating to reimbursement and coverage of telehealth by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; requiring the Maryland Medical Health Care Commission to study and make recommendations regarding the delivery of health care services through telehealth by December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Preserve Telehealth Access Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Extends the inclusion of certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of telehealth through June 30, 2025. Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and private health insurers to provide reimbursement parity through June 30, 2025. Excludes clinic facility fees and room and board fees from required telehealth reimbursement. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study telehealth service delivery and payment parity. Requires the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health care providers, Medicaid recipients, commercial health insurance enrollees, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures and federal matching fund revenues continue through fiscal 2025, with an indeterminate net impact on total Medicaid spending. Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration from form filing fees in fiscal 2024. Potential expenditure increases for certain local governments to continue reimbursing specified telehealth services under local health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a comprehensive study on the delivery of health care services through telehealth—including payment parity, clinical effort, and behavioral health reimbursement—and submit a report with recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is directly required under the bill to extend coverage of audio-only telehealth and maintain payment parity with in-person care through June 30, 2025.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs in the state, which are required under the bill to continue reimbursing covered telehealth services at parity with in-person rates through June 30, 2025, resulting in rate and form filings reviewed by the agency.

The bill explicitly references the Health Services Cost Review Commission, clarifying that the telehealth reimbursement requirements do not supersede the commission's authority to set hospital rates and facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

bill_summary: Extends the renewal term for a video lottery operation license from 10 years to 15 years. Requires a licensee to file a notice of intent to renew between two and five years before expiration. Requires the licensee to apply for renewal within one year after filing that notice. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to renew the license unless finding the licensee unqualified. Requires licensees to pay renewal fees into the Education Trust Fund in equal installments across each five-year period. Distributes 20% of paid renewal fees back to licensees for marketing and promotions exclusively targeting out-of-state audiences.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency and its governing Commission are the primary regulators responsible for administering video lottery operation license renewals, establishing application procedures and renewal fees by regulation, reviewing licensee qualifications, providing hearings, and collecting and remitting renewal fees to the Education Trust Fund.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to disburse funds from the proceeds of video lottery terminals according to the updated distribution formulas upon transmittals from the Commission, including the newly added allocations for out-of-state marketing.

The State Treasurer is statutorily responsible for investing and reinvesting moneys credited to the Education Trust Fund, which will receive increased revenue from the video lottery operation license renewal fees.
License renewal fees are deposited into the Education Trust Fund, which supports public school programs and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund administered in conjunction with MSDE.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations on behalf of State residents. Prohibits civil rights actions by the Attorney General against political subdivisions, government units, or their employees. Allows the Attorney General to obtain injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $25,000. Establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund to support enforcement activities, education, and community outreach. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase from civil penalties deposited into the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund. General fund revenues increase minimally from fund interest earnings. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 540 directly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, seek injunctions and civil penalties, enter into conciliation agreements, and adopt implementing regulations in coordination with the Commission on Civil Rights, requiring dedicated staff and substantial operational resources.

The bill explicitly preserves the authority of the Commission on Civil Rights and requires the Attorney General to coordinate and make referrals with the Commission in areas of overlapping jurisdiction to eliminate duplication of effort, while also allowing the Commission to receive reimbursements from the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund.
The bill establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund and explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund and explicitly mandates that the Comptroller account for the fund.

The bill requires civil enforcement actions initiated by the Attorney General to be filed in the circuit courts, which are supported operationally and administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Replaces the prior mandate requiring reclamation opportunities 24 hours per day. Alters parking lot signage requirements to state the revised statutory hours for reclamation. As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law, the Maryland State Police regulates and responds to motor vehicle, towing, and property disputes, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

bill_summary: Establishes the Department of Service and Civic Innovation as a principal department of State government. Transfers administration and management of the Maryland Corps Program to the Department. Creates the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and Maryland Service Year Option Pathway. Requires participating corps members to be paid at least fifteen dollars per hour or State minimum wage. Authorizes six thousand dollar program completion awards as cash stipends or Maryland 529 account deposits. Mandates annual State budget appropriations to the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund through fiscal 2027.

stakeholders: young adults within three years of high school graduation, Maryland residents pursuing community service, participating employers, and host organizations

Mandated annual funding for the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund begins at $5.0 million in FY 2024 and increases to $20.0 million by FY 2027. Local expenditures may increase if local governments voluntarily host corps participants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 551 codifies the Department of Service and Civic Innovation as a principal department in state government and charges it with administering the Maryland Corps Program and the two newly created service pathways.

The bill establishes the Secretary as a member of the Governor's Executive Council, authorizes the Governor to appoint the Secretary and members of the Advisory Board, and transfers programs from executive offices.
The bill designates the Attorney General as legal adviser to the Department and requires the assignment of Assistant Attorneys General, including a designated Counsel to the Department.
The State Treasurer is tasked with holding and investing moneys for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund.
The Comptroller is required to separately account for each revenue source of the newly established pathway special funds and handle fund reversions.
DBM oversees the state budget allocations, mandated appropriations, staffing positions, and the handling and reversions of Dedicated Purpose Account (DPA) funds associated with the bill.

The bill amends the $6,000 program completion award provisions, allowing participants the choice of receiving cash stipends rather than solely requiring deposits into Maryland 529 accounts, potentially reducing Maryland 529 deposits.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund are subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

The Department of Service and Civic Innovation is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Labor to assess awarding corps participants credit for prior learning experience toward trade or vocational certifications and registered apprenticeships.
The bill requires consultation with MHEC regarding the awarding of academic credit for corps participants' service at postsecondary institutions.
The bill and related budget transfers reassign the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism and associated funding from GOCI to the Department of Service and Civic Innovation.
The bill authorizes funds to expand the Maryland Conservation Corps and the Chesapeake Conservation Corps, and expand service opportunities in state and local parks.

Public senior higher education institutions must waive in-state residency requirements for individuals who complete a Maryland Corps service program, and institutions may participate in awarding academic credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program within the Military Department, which is headed by the Adjutant General, requiring the department to adopt regulations, hire staff, and administer premium reimbursement grants.
Members of the Maryland National Guard and their immediate families are the direct beneficiaries of the health and dental insurance premium reimbursement grants established by the bill.
The bill effectuates $1.0 million in contingent general fund appropriations and necessitates the addition of three permanent state positions to administer the new grant program.

Repeals the authority of the Board of Public Works to temporarily suspend scheduled minimum wage increases. Repeals required 4% annual provider reimbursement rate increases for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.

fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $206.7 million in both FY 2024 and FY 2025 ($109.1 million general funds, $97.6 million federal funds) for provider reimbursements, with modest increases in state and higher education payroll costs. Federal revenues increase by $97.6 million in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to match the federal share. Local government personnel expenditures increase significantly in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to meet the accelerated wage threshold.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the Maryland Wage and Hour Law, which sets the state minimum wage accelerated by this bill.

The bill amends the Health - General Article concerning reimbursement rates for community service providers under the Developmental Disabilities Administration, Behavioral Health Administration, and Medicaid, generating a substantial fiscal expenditure impact of over $200 million across FY 2024 and FY 2025.
The bill specifically repeals statutory provisions granting the Board of Public Works the authority to temporarily suspend scheduled increases in the State minimum wage rate.

DBM oversees the state budget and state personnel management. The bill impacts state budget mandates regarding provider rate increases and has potential fiscal implications for state service contracts.
USM institutions experience direct expenditure increases to raise wages for certain exempt, hourly, and undergraduate student workers to meet the accelerated $15.00 per hour minimum wage.
The bill was introduced on behalf of the Administration and directly alters statutory mandates governing the rate increases that must be included in future executive budget proposals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH is responsible for administering the program, establishing application and award procedures, issuing competitive grants, and reporting annually on grant distribution and outcomes.
The bill mandates a $500,000 appropriation in the annual State budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027, directly impacting DBM's budget development and fiscal planning responsibilities.

The bill requires an annual mandated appropriation of $500,000 to be included in the Governor's budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027 and mandates that MDH submit an annual report on the grant program to the Governor.

Establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties for improper recording submissions, including fines up to $1,000 and imprisonment. responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division; Clerks of the Circuit Courts

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a violation of the prohibited residential property service agreement provisions is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill directly involves the Judicial Branch by authorizing Clerks of the Circuit Court to deny recording of prohibited service agreements, establishing a civil cause of action in circuit courts to void unlawful agreements and recover damages, and creating a misdemeanor offense punishable in court.

The Department of Labor licenses and regulates real estate professionals through the State Real Estate Commission; although specific annual reporting amendments in earlier drafts were struck, the bill directly regulates agreements commonly used in real estate transactions.

Establishes operational standards, enrollment caps, and staffing rules for public virtual schools. Prohibits approving any new elementary grade band virtual school on or before December 1, 2024. Mandates that county boards adopt virtual education plans by June 1, 2024, for prolonged states of emergency.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland State Board of Education; county boards of education
stakeholders: Maryland public school students and their families, public school teachers and educational support personnel, local school systems and county boards of education, and teacher preparation programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 in FY 2024 and $500,000 in FY 2025 for the Maryland State Department of Education to upgrade computer and internet security infrastructure. Local school systems are anticipated to implement the bill's requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing standards, approving and overseeing virtual schools, developing training standards, expanding cybersecurity infrastructure, and convening the virtual education study group.

The bill mandates an expansion of computer and Internet security infrastructure for virtual education, which the fiscal note indicates requires direct collaboration and an in-depth needs assessment with DoIT.

The bill alters mandatory curriculum components for teacher preparation programs to include teaching effectively in virtual learning environments and includes higher education institutions in the study group.
USM institutions offer public teacher preparation programs that must incorporate the bill's new virtual instruction training requirements into their educator curriculum.
Morgan State University operates teacher education and preparation programs that must update coursework to meet the new requirement for instruction in virtual learning environments.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to identify and license certain independent evaluators to evaluate and rate certain sports wagering content provided by sports wagering experts, sports wagering influencers, and content partners; authorizing the Commission and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission to consider a request to amend a Class B-2 sports wagering facility license application for the purpose of altering the proposed location of the facility under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Gaming - Sports Wagering - Independent Evaluation of Sports Wagering Content and Sports Wagering Facility Application Amendments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State

bill_summary: Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to license independent evaluators of sports wagering content by December 31, 2023. Establishes qualification criteria, conflict-of-interest prohibitions, and betting restrictions for licensed independent evaluators and their personnel. Authorizes sports wagering licensees and sports wagering operators advertising in Maryland to contract with licensed independent evaluators. Prohibits evaluators from being compensated by entities utilizing their services solely for marketing materials. Authorizes state gaming commissions to consider certain Class B-2 license location amendments requested by December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; Sports Wagering Application Review Commission
stakeholders: Independent evaluators of sports wagering content, sports wagering licensees, sports wagering operators, sports wagering experts, sports wagering influencers, content partners, and Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applicants
fiscal_impact_summary: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency administrative expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to license independent evaluators of sports wagering content, but a precise dollar estimate is currently unavailable. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with licensing independent evaluators of sports wagering content, adopting implementing regulations, and considering location amendment requests for Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), an independent statutory commission, to consider requests to amend certain Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applications.

Synopsis: Requiring that the members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission be appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate of Maryland.
Title: Health Services Cost Review Commission - Members - Appointment

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Requires members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission to be appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate. Maintains the composition of the Commission at seven members appointed by the Governor. Preserves the requirement that four members have no connection with the management or policy of any facility. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Governor; Senate of Maryland; Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: members and prospective nominees of the Health Services Cost Review Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the appointment change is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the appointment process for members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission by requiring that their appointments by the Governor receive the advice and consent of the Senate.
The Governor is the appointing authority for members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission; this bill subjects those gubernatorial appointments to Senate advice and consent.
The Office of Appointments vets and manages gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, including coordinating nominations through the Senate confirmation process.
The Health Services Cost Review Commission is an independent commission established within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law governing the Historic St. Mary's City Commission, including laws relating to membership of the Commission, appointment of certain officers, Commission meeting times, and duties; and specifying the process for the Commission to collaborate with an affiliated nonprofit organization.
Title: Historic St. Mary's City Commission Reform Act of 2023

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Alters the governance, membership composition, and operational duties of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission. Adds a Native American community representative and two legislative-appointed public members to the Commission. Requires the Commission to publish written operational policies and update a comprehensive maintenance plan every three years. Establishes rules for collaborating with affiliated nonprofit organizations, including ethics reviews and mandatory annual audits. Subjects the Historic St. Mary's City Fund to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits. Mandates an audit-progress report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Historic St. Mary's City Commission; Office of the Attorney General; State Ethics Commission; Office of Legislative Audits
stakeholders: Historic St. Mary's City Commission members and staff, affiliated nonprofit organizations including the Historic St. Mary's City Foundation, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Maryland's Native American community
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reforms the governance, membership, operating procedures, reporting requirements, and nonprofit collaboration rules of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission.

The Board of Trustees chair (or designee) serves as an ex officio voting member, and the bill establishes specific statutory standards for operating agreements, collaborative programs, and administrative services between the College and the Commission.

The bill requires the State Ethics Commission to review and approve policies governing conflicts of interest for officials/employees serving on affiliated nonprofits, receive notifications and issue objections regarding dual service, and receive annual implementation reports.

The bill requires the Attorney General to review and approve the Commission's operating agreements with other units or nonprofits, as well as its nonprofit collaboration policies, for form and legal sufficiency.
The bill explicitly establishes that the Historic St. Mary's City Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits pursuant to state law.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 14 voting members of the Commission with Senate advice and consent, and receives annual activity and nonprofit collaboration reports from the Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing a transfer of service credit to, and a purchase of service credit in, the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for local law enforcement officers of the City of Bowie Police Department hired on or after January 1, 2007, and not later than December 31, 2015, under certain circumstances.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System – City of Bowie Police Department – Transfers and Purchases of Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes certain City of Bowie Police Department officers to transfer or purchase service credit in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. Applies to officers hired between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2015, who satisfy specified documentation requirements. Requires eligible officers to submit verification by December 31, 2023. Waives statutory one-year transfer deadlines and five-year retirement benefit limitations for eligible transferring members. Permits officers who withdrew prior contributions to purchase service credit through a single payment with regular interest. Terminates all provisions on December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; City of Bowie Police Department
stakeholders: City of Bowie Police Department officers hired between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2015; participating governmental units in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Creates a minimal increase in pension liabilities for participating governmental units in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, with no discernible effect on employer contribution rates and no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The bill directly tasks the system and its Board of Trustees with providing forms, receiving documentation and payments, and processing the service credit transfers and purchases for eligible City of Bowie police officers.

Synopsis: Requiring certain health care providers and health care facilities to provide to the local team, on request of the chair, prompt access to all relevant medical records associated with a case under review by the Maternal Mortality Review Program without undue delay; and providing that certain provisions of law related to the confidentiality of medical records do not apply to certain disclosures made to a local team.
Title: Maternal Mortality Review Program - Local Teams - Access to Records

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires health care providers and health care facilities to provide a local maternal mortality review team prompt access to certain medical records. Mandates access without undue delay on request of the local team chair. Applies the requirement to all relevant medical records associated with a case under review by the Maternal Mortality Review Program. Exempts disclosures made to a local team from state medical record confidentiality provisions. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Local Maternal Mortality Review Teams
stakeholders: Health care providers, health care facilities, and local maternal mortality review teams
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the change is procedural in nature and does not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maternal Mortality Review Program and coordinates with local health departments and local maternal mortality review teams, which are granted direct and prompt access to relevant medical records under the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing a nursing home that contracts with or uses an electronic health information network or electronic medical record vendor to direct the network or vendor to release electronic medical records and electronic health care transactions to a business associate of the nursing home.
Title: Electronic Health Networks and Electronic Medical Records - Nursing Homes - Release of Records

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes a nursing home to direct an electronic health network or electronic medical record vendor to release records. Permits release of patient medical records or electronic health care transactions to a business associate with patient consent. Requires networks and vendors to release information timely in an electronic format conforming to specified health information standards. Prohibits networks and vendors from restricting, limiting, or charging a fee for the release of the records. Prohibits fees to exchange-contracted business associates unless approved by the State-designated health information exchange.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: nursing homes, electronic health network vendors, electronic medical record vendors, nursing home patients, and health care business associates
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is responsible for certifying electronic health networks (EHNs) and overseeing the State-designated health information exchange (CRISP), which the bill directly references regarding record format standards and fee approval for quality-improvement business associates.

The Maryland Department of Health regulates and licenses nursing homes across the state and oversees the statutory provisions governing medical records and health transactions under the Health - General Article.

Synopsis: Establishing the State Disaster Recovery Fund to provide disaster recovery assistance to units of local government for individuals and families and for the repair, restoration, reconstruction, or replacement of public facilities, low-interest or no-interest loans to businesses and nonprofits when a federal disaster declaration is not received, and disaster-related assistance for the unmet needs of individuals and families after a federal disaster declaration or in the event of a certain denial of federal assistance; etc.
Title: Public Safety - State Disaster Recovery Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the State Disaster Recovery Fund to provide disaster recovery assistance to individuals, families, businesses, nonprofits, and local governments. Requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to administer the special, nonlapsing fund. Authorizes assistance when a federal disaster declaration is not received or for unmet needs. Permits fund expenditures only if the Governor declares an emergency or a local emergency organization requests aid. Requires the Secretary of Emergency Management to report annually on fund usage by December 31.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Individuals, families, businesses, and nonprofits affected by disasters; local governments and local emergency management organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2024 to capitalize the fund, with special fund revenues increasing correspondingly. Special fund expenditures increase by at least $344,442 in FY 2024 for MDEM administration (3.5 positions), growing to $473,915 by FY 2028. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local governments receive and spend disaster assistance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly created State Disaster Recovery Fund, adopting regulations, determining eligibility criteria, and submitting annual reports.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account, which this bill directly amends to allow local governments to receive funding directly, and oversees state budget and expenditure accounts.

The bill allows the Governor to include appropriations for the fund in the annual budget bill, requires a gubernatorial state of emergency declaration for certain fund uses, and authorizes the Governor to transfer funds via budget amendments.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the fund separately, invest its money, and ensure interest earnings are credited directly to the fund pursuant to the amendment to Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the State Disaster Recovery Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring a real estate broker or an escrow agent, if a purchaser terminates a certain transaction under certain circumstances, to distribute trust money to the purchaser within 30 days after a certain written notice of the termination is sent; requiring a holder of trust money who makes a certain distribution to notify the seller and purchaser of the distribution within a certain period of time, subject to a certain exception; etc.
Title: Real Estate - Real Estate Brokerage Services and Termination of Residential Real Estate Contracts (The Anthony Moorman Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Requires a real estate broker or escrow agent to distribute trust money to a residential real estate purchaser after contingency termination. Allows a purchaser who terminates a contract under a contingency clause to request trust money in writing. Requires the seller to provide a copy of a District Court complaint or notarized mediation request within 10 days. Requires the holder to distribute trust money within 30 days if no complaint or mediation request is received. Protects trust money holders from liability for distributing funds under these statutory procedures. Authorizes any aggrieved claimant to file an action in the District Court.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: residential real estate purchasers, sellers, licensed real estate brokers, and escrow agents in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation and licensing of real estate brokers and salespersons through the State Real Estate Commission. The bill directly amends Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article concerning real estate broker duties and the handling of trust money.

The bill explicitly establishes procedural remedies in the District Court, authorizing sellers to file complaints, holders of trust money to initiate interpleader actions, and aggrieved claimants to file actions in District Court.

The Office of the Attorney General houses the Consumer Protection Division, which monitors residential real estate practices and consumer disputes, and provides legal counsel to state licensing boards within the Department of Labor.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that this Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.
Title: Annual Corrective Bill
bill_summary: Corrects technical errors, omissions, and obsolete references across various articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Clarifies statutory language and reorganizes select provisions without intending substantive legal changes. Authorizes the publishers of the Annotated Code to make approved nonsubstantive corrections to codification and style. Requires the publishers to describe any such corrections in editor's notes following affected sections. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: users of the Annotated Code of Maryland, legal practitioners, state agencies, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill is technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Updates statutory references in the Public Safety Article regarding the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council to reflect the agency's cabinet-level status, replacing obsolete references to the 'Director of the Maryland Emergency Management Agency' with 'Secretary of Emergency Management' and 'Maryland Department of Emergency Management'.

Contains numerous technical, grammatical, and typographical corrections to Title 13A of the Public Safety Article (Maryland Code of Military Justice), which governs military justice administration under the Adjutant General.
Technical corrections throughout Title 13A of the Public Safety Article directly pertain to members of the Maryland National Guard and court-martial/nonjudicial punishment procedures.

Enacts various technical, grammatical, and cross-reference corrections across multiple sections of the Education Article governing public school operations, educator pay plans, career ladders, and student health standards.

Includes technical clarifications and obsolete reference updates in the Health - General Article and Health Occupations Article, including terminology regarding the state-designated health information exchange and loan assistance repayment programs.
Makes minor technical and cross-reference corrections to provisions in the Natural Resources Article concerning Program Open Space, regulated shooting grounds, and local water fishing regulations.
Corrects statutory cross-references and minor phrasing in Education Article provisions relating to school construction priority grant awards and maintenance tracking systems.
Corrects technical phrasing and cross-references in the Tax - General and State Government Articles concerning tax filings and the distribution of video lottery terminal proceeds.
Corrects obsolete cross-references in the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding the reemployment of disability retirees as law enforcement officers.

Synopsis: Applying the sales and use tax to a sale or use of certain home amenity rentals; and authorizing a county or municipality to impose a certain home amenity rental tax under certain circumstances and subject to certain limitations.
Title: Home Amenity Rentals - Sales and Use Tax Imposed and Local Tax Authorized
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 805

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Applies the State sales and use tax to home amenity rentals facilitated by an intermediary or platform. Defines a home amenity as residential property rented by the hour for up to 15 consecutive hours, excluding sleeping quarters. Classifies home amenity rental intermediaries and platforms as vendors required to collect and remit sales and use tax. Authorizes eligible counties to impose a local home amenity rental tax by resolution subject to statutory rate caps. Authorizes municipalities to levy a home amenity rental tax up to 1% if the underlying county imposes one.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: home amenity rental platforms and intermediaries, residential property owners offering home amenity rentals, consumers renting home amenities, and Maryland county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues increase by a potentially significant indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2025, with potential increases in general fund administrative expenses. County and municipal revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent local home amenity rental taxes are imposed, with potential increases in local administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Maryland sales and use tax to include home amenity rentals and home amenity rental intermediaries/platforms. As Maryland's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for collecting the sales and use tax revenue and will incur administrative costs to implement and enforce the new tax provisions.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State to exchange real property owned by the State for the use and benefit of the Department of Natural Resources with private real property under certain circumstances.
Title: Department of Natural Resources' Real Property - Exchange With Private Real Property
bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to exchange certain State-owned real property for adjacent privately owned real property. Limits eligible State-owned real property to parcels not exceeding five acres in size. Requires the private property owner requesting the exchange to pay all related costs, including legal fees and surveying. Requires the Department to notify adjacent property owners, local General Assembly members, and the county governing body in writing. Requires the Department to refer the proposed exchange to the Board of Public Works for final disposition.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Private landowners seeking land exchanges with the Department of Natural Resources; owners of real property adjacent to exchanged private land; county governing bodies
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State operations or finances because the bill is authorizing in nature, and the requesting private landowner pays all transaction costs. Local fiscal effect is minimal or none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency authorized under the bill to exchange up to 5 acres of State-owned real property with adjacent privately owned land under an expedited process and is responsible for providing the required notices.
All proposed real property exchanges under the bill must be referred by DNR to the Board of Public Works for final review and disposition.

Exchanges authorized by the bill bypass the standard excess real property review and disposition study procedures conducted by the Department of Planning under Title 5, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

DGS oversees State real estate transactions and standard property disposition procedures under Title 10, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which are exempted for eligible DNR property exchanges under this bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing members of the State Retirement and Pension System to receive service credit at the rate of 4 months for each full year of attendance at a United States service academy that interrupts the member's employment, not to exceed a total of 16 months.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Military Service Credit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes members of the State Retirement and Pension System to receive credit for attending a United States service academy. Grants service credit at the rate of four months per full year of attendance, up to 16 months total. Applies to academy attendance that preceded employment or attendance that interrupts public employment. Maintains the existing overall limit of five years on total military service credit. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members and former members of the State Retirement and Pension System and members of local retirement systems who attended a United States service academy
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2026; the average state employer cost per member claiming the maximum 16 months of credit ranges from $1,200 to $3,600 depending on the plan. There is no effect on revenues, and no discernible effect on local government pension liabilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill amends state pension law to allow SRPS members to receive retirement service credit for attendance at a U.S. service academy, requiring the agency to process these applications and calculate benefit adjustments.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and budgets for employer pension contributions, which will be fiscally impacted by the additional service credit liabilities beginning in FY 2026.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a fee for the issuance of a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse under certain circumstances.
Title: Vehicle Laws – Certificate of Title – Surviving Spouse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Prohibits the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a fee for a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse. Applies upon the death of a sole vehicle owner when ownership transfers under statutory estate procedures. Eliminates the standard $100 titling fee previously charged to a surviving spouse not listed as a joint owner. Requires vehicle ownership transfer to comply with testamentary disposition or intestate devolution requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of deceased sole vehicle owners in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by approximately $375,000 in FY 2024 and by $500,000 annually in subsequent years due to foregone titling fee revenues. Expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly prohibits the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a $100 fee for issuing a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse of a deceased sole vehicle owner.
As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund experiences an estimated revenue decrease of approximately $500,000 annually due to the fee exemption.
The Register of Wills issues certificates of letters testamentary or administration referenced in statutory vehicle transfers upon an owner's death, and was consulted as an information source.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain deputy State fire marshal to be on probation for a period of 2 years after the date of appointment to the Office of the State Fire Marshal under certain circumstances; and specifying the pay that a certain deputy State fire marshal is entitled to on promotion.
Title: Public Safety - Deputy State Fire Marshal - Probationary Status and Promotion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires each deputy State fire marshal to remain in probationary status for two years after appointment. Applies the two-year probationary requirement to individuals appointed for training before regular assignment. Entitles a deputy State fire marshal upon promotion to pay specified for the new rank at their prior step. Restricts promotional pay to the next lower step under specific conditions based on peer service time. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Office of the State Fire Marshal
stakeholders: Deputy State fire marshals and individuals appointed for training at the Office of the State Fire Marshal
fiscal_impact_summary: None. The bill codifies existing Department of State Police practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This was a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. The Office of the State Fire Marshal operates within the department, and the bill directly governs the probationary period and promotional pay structure for deputy State fire marshals.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee compensation rules, probationary standards, and the approval of departmental pay plans specified in the statute.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository for criminal history records checks for certain youth camp applicants; requiring that the Department issue a certain written determination to a youth camp within 3 business days; repealing the authority of youth development organizations and programs to request from the Department a determination of whether the results of a criminal history records check would prohibit the hiring of a job applicant; etc.
Title: Public Health - Youth Camps, Development Organizations, and Programs - Criminal History Records Checks

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to obtain State and national criminal history records checks for youth camp applicants. Applies to individuals seeking to become a youth camp owner, operator, employee, or volunteer with access to a camper. Requires the Department to issue a written hiring determination within three business days after receiving an operator's request. Repeals the authority of youth development organizations and programs to request hiring determinations from the Department. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: youth camp owners, operators, employees, and volunteers; youth camps; youth development organizations and programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $172,030 in FY 2024 to hire one full-time administrator, temporary contractual staff, and cover operating expenses, increasing to $207,200 by FY 2028. General fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount from authorized background check fees. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply for State and national criminal history records checks for youth camp personnel applicants, review records, issue binding written hiring determinations within three business days, and set fees to cover associated costs, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directs the department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository to process fingerprint submissions and fees, disseminate criminal history record information to the applicant and MDH, and provide revised records if subsequent criminal information is reported.

Synopsis: Altering the expiration date for a commercial driver's instructional permit held by certain individuals; and exempting a holder of a commercial driver's license who applies for renewal from the requirement to pass a vision test if the holder has a current certificate of physical examination on file with the Motor Vehicle Administration.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Commercial Driver's Licenses and Instructional Permits - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the expiration term of a commercial driver's instructional permit from 180 days to one year. Applies this extension to licensed drivers seeking a different class of license. Exempts commercial driver's license renewal applicants from the vision test requirement under specific conditions. Requires renewal applicants to have a current certificate of physical examination on file with the Motor Vehicle Administration. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Commercial driver's license holders and applicants for commercial driver's instructional permits
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by approximately $263,300 in fiscal 2024 and $351,000 annually thereafter due to fewer permit reissuances. Expenditures are not materially affected, though the Motor Vehicle Administration may realize operational efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency directly responsible for issuing commercial driver's instructional permits, administering CDL renewals, verifying federal medical certificates for vision test exemptions, and managing the associated licensing fee collections.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation. MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) will experience a special fund revenue decrease of approximately $351,000 annually due to fewer commercial permit reissuances.

SponsorPrimary: Chair, Education, Energy, and the Environment Committee

Sponsors.Name: Chair, Education, Energy, and the Environment Committee

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Architects in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2028, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Architects - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Extends the termination date for statutory and regulatory provisions governing the State Board of Architects to July 1, 2028. Continues the board in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Authorizes the board to continue qualifying and licensing architects in the State. fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 due to the redirected unclaimed property proceeds. Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $14.0 million annually across FY 2025 through FY 2027 to fund legal representation through the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Comptroller distribute $14.0 million annually from net abandoned property proceeds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal year 2027 and account for the fund.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $14.0 million from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the state budget bill for each fiscal year through 2027.

As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal planning, DBM must implement the $14.0 million annual mandated appropriation and manage the associated impact on General Fund and special fund revenues and expenditures through fiscal year 2027.
Under the provisions of the bill and underlying statute, the State Treasurer holds the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and is responsible for investing the fund's assets.

bill_summary: Regulates security guard employers and requires individuals who provide security guard services to an employer to be certified. Mandates completion of initial and continuing security training identified or established by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission. Prohibits security guards from carrying handguns on duty without employer approval and State Police verification. Requires security guards and employers to report use-of-force incidents within 48 hours. Mandates that security guard agencies and employers maintain specified commercial general liability insurance coverage.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: security guards, security guard agencies, and security guard employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $476,900 in FY 2024 for the Department of State Police to hire two administrative specialists and complete technical systems upgrades, with ongoing operating costs in future years. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (through the Secretary of State Police) is the primary regulatory and implementing body under the bill, responsible for certifying security guards, regulating security guard employers, tracking handgun authorizations, and collecting use-of-force incident reports. The bill also requires general fund expenditures of over $476,000 for personnel and system upgrades within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which operates under DPSCS, identify or establish 12-hour initial and 8-hour continuing training programs for security guard certification. In addition, background checks and fingerprinting run through the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository.

The Department of General Services directly employs security personnel to protect state facilities and Capitol Police property, making it an employer subject to the standards, although fiscal impact on the agency is anticipated to be absorbed within existing operations.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council, to publish a model policy on or before January 1, 2024, concerning the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in procurement contracts; requiring a unit of State government to adopt a written policy that is substantially similar to the Board's policy; requiring a unit that decides not to include a liquidated damages clause under certain circumstances to obtain the approval of the head of unit; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Liquidated Damages - Policies and Requirements

bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works to publish a model liquidated damages policy by January 1, 2024. Requires each unit of State government to adopt a substantially similar written policy by July 1, 2024. Authorizes primary procurement units to adopt policies applicable to procurements within their control authority. Requires a unit to obtain unit head approval when deciding not to include a liquidated damages clause. Requires unit head approval and documentation if not pursuing liquidated damages on contracts valued at $5,000,000 or more.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Procurement Improvement Council
stakeholders: State procurement units; State contractors and vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: The Board of Public Works and State procuring agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary implementing agency under the bill, required to publish a model policy regarding the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in State procurement contracts by January 1, 2024, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council.

As the State's central procurement authority and a designated primary procurement unit controlling most executive branch procurements, DGS is authorized and required to establish a liquidated damages policy for units within its control and adhere to unit-head approval and documentation requirements.

MDOT is a designated primary procurement unit with independent procurement authority and must adopt and implement a liquidated damages policy substantially similar to BPW's model policy for transportation contracts under its control authority.

The State Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works, acts as a primary procurement unit for banking and insurance services, and oversees Maryland 529, whose contracts are explicitly brought under the bill's liquidated damages requirements.

USM is a primary procurement unit and the bill explicitly amends § 11-203(e) to subject its procurements to the liquidated damages requirements under § 15-113, despite its general exemption from State procurement law.
Morgan State University is a designated primary procurement unit and is explicitly subjected to § 15-113 liquidated damages policies and documentation rules under § 11-203(e).
St. Mary's College of Maryland is a designated primary procurement unit and is explicitly subjected to § 15-113 liquidated damages requirements under the amended § 11-203(e).
The Maryland Port Administration is a designated primary procurement unit authorized to conduct its own procurements and must adopt a liquidated damages policy governing port-related contracts.
The bill explicitly amends § 11-203(c) to apply the liquidated damages requirements of § 15-113 to the Maryland Stadium Authority, an entity otherwise largely exempt from State procurement law.

The bill amends § 11-203(d) to specifically subject contracts executed for the State Retirement and Pension System (for investment management, asset maintenance, and administration) to § 15-113 liquidated damages rules.
The bill explicitly amends § 11-203(f) to make investment and asset management contracts for the Maryland Prepaid College Trust subject to the liquidated damages provisions in § 15-113.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency administers the Maryland Corps Program, which is explicitly amended in § 11-203(i) to be subject to the liquidated damages requirements of § 15-113.

bill_summary: Establishes a State offshore wind energy goal of reaching 8,500 megawatts of capacity by 2031. Requires the Public Service Commission to request transmission system analyses and solicit offshore wind transmission proposals. Directs the Department of General Services to competitively procure up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours of offshore wind annually. Authorizes offshore wind developers meeting specified labor standards to request exemptions from remitting certain federal tax credits. Mandates that approved offshore wind projects and selected transmission projects enter into binding community benefit agreements.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of General Services
stakeholders: Offshore wind developers, electric transmission owners, electricity ratepayers, labor organizations and craft workers, and small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2024, Public Service Commission special fund expenditures increase by $635,256, offset by public service company assessments. Department of General Services general fund expenditures increase by $213,905 in FY 2024 for procurement personnel. Future state and local electricity costs under resulting power purchase agreements are indeterminate but potentially significant.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is a primary implementing agency tasked with coordinating with PJM Interconnection to study transmission upgrades, issuing competitive solicitations for offshore wind transmission facilities, selecting proposals, adjudicating federal tax credit remittance exemptions, and submitting annual reports on supplier diversity.

DGS is designated to issue a major competitive sealed procurement and enter into power purchase agreements (PPAs) for up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours annually of offshore wind energy and associated renewable energy credits, and manage associated labor peace agreement attestations.

MEA is statutorily required to be consulted by the Public Service Commission regarding the transmission system expansion analysis and to coordinate with PSC and stakeholders following the selection of transmission proposals.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is authorized to propose conditions on transmission project proposals selected by the PSC, and DNR experiences operational impacts associated with environmental and siting evaluations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is charged with assisting potential offshore wind applicants and minority investors, and collaborating with applicants to establish clear plans for minority business enterprise participation goals and procedures.

OPC advocates for residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC, which is directly relevant given the bill's significant provisions regarding ratepayer impacts, transmission cost allocations, and OREC exemptions.

The bill establishes community benefit agreement terms requiring payment of prevailing wage rates set by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and utilization of registered apprenticeship programs overseen by MD Labor.
OAG is consulted alongside GOSBA to assist applicants and minority investors and to provide legal counsel for the State's complex regulatory and procurement requirements under the Act.

The Governor's Office receives annual reporting on minority business enterprise participation in offshore wind projects, receives statements of determination if transmission proposals are not selected, and is authorized to provide funding appropriations in the state budget for PSC studies.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for phased catalytic revitalization projects. Permits original recipients to transfer initial tax credit certificates under specified written consent requirements. Limits each phased final credit certificate to not more than 20% of eligible project expenses to date. Requires the Smart Growth Subcabinet to study and recommend an implementation plan for preserving and reusing historic complexes. Mandates that the Subcabinet report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Smart Growth Subcabinet
stakeholders: individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities undertaking catalytic revitalization projects or developing historic properties in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential acceleration and extension of the timing of credits claimed against the State income tax, which may significantly affect State general fund revenues in any given year. Corporate income tax impacts may also affect local highway user revenues and the Transportation Trust Fund. The Smart Growth Subcabinet can complete the required study and report with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) administers the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit. The bill directly alters DHCD's authority by allowing the Secretary to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for phased projects and establishing specific conditions for the transfer of initial tax credit certificates.

The Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) staffs the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which is mandated by the bill to conduct a study and develop recommendations for an implementation plan addressing the preservation and reuse of historic complexes in Maryland.

The Comptroller administers State income tax collections and tax credit claims. The bill's changes to the catalytic revitalization tax credit structure may alter the timing and claiming of income tax credits and refunds.

The Smart Growth Subcabinet operates under the Executive Branch, and the bill requires the Subcabinet to report its findings and recommendations regarding historic complexes directly to the Governor by December 31, 2023.

bill_summary: Authorizes individuals to register and terminate domestic partnerships with the local register of wills. Grants surviving registered domestic partners intestate inheritance rights, family allowances, priority of administration, and inheritance tax exemptions. Prohibits a surviving registered domestic partner from claiming an elective share against a decedent's will. Removes statutory references to child legitimacy and clarifies parentage for children of registered domestic partners. Increases the surviving partner or spousal intestate share to $100,000 plus half the residue when non-joint surviving issue exist.
responsible_party: Register of Wills
stakeholders: couples in domestic partnerships, surviving registered domestic partners, estate heirs, and personal representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease annually by an indeterminate amount due to the new inheritance tax exemption for registered domestic partners, partially offset by filing fees of up to $25. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including receiving and recording declarations of domestic partnership and termination, maintaining public records with appropriate address redactions, establishing and maintaining a certified list of reciprocal jurisdictions, and applying domestic partner intestate succession rules and inheritance tax exemptions during estate administration.

The Comptroller oversees state tax revenue collection, including the inheritance tax. The bill expands the inheritance tax exemption for surviving registered domestic partners, which impacts state general fund tax revenues.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judiciary, including the Orphans' Courts and Circuit Courts that oversee contested probate, estate administration proceedings, and parentage determinations modified by the bill.

Creates the Cyber Maryland Fund to administer grants to elementary and secondary schools, higher education institutions, for-profit corporations, and non-profits. Establishes the Cyber Maryland Board to provide strategic input, stakeholder engagement, and advisory support. Requires the Governor to appropriate sufficient annual budget funds beginning in fiscal year 2025 for program personnel. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to expand the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program to accommodate emerging certification trends. Directs unexpended Cyber Warrior Diversity Program allocations to revert to the Commission for reallocation in the upcoming fiscal year.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Cyber Maryland Board; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: cybersecurity employers, information technology workers, elementary and secondary schools, public and private higher education institutions, community colleges, and participating workforce non-profits
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $690,000 in FY 2024, with ongoing mandated and discretionary funding projected between $669,300 and $705,400 annually through FY 2028. Cyber Maryland Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly. Local revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local school systems and community colleges receive program grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, housing, and administering the Cyber Maryland Program and the Cyber Maryland Fund, appointing the program's executive director, and supporting the Cyber Maryland Board.

MHEC is directly tasked with expanding the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program annually based on industry certification trends identified under the bill, and managing the reallocation of unexpended program funds.
MHEC is directly tasked with expanding the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program annually based on cybersecurity certification trends and administering grant funding and reallocations under the program.

The Cyber Maryland Program is specifically charged with supporting DoIT's efforts to improve the state's cybersecurity posture, and the Secretary of Information Technology serves as an ex officio member of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a designated member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board is mandated to coordinate cybersecurity workforce development efforts with the Department.

The Secretary of Labor serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, the board must coordinate workforce development efforts with MD Labor, and the program considers synergies with MD Labor programs like EARN and Maryland Apprenticeship.
Morgan State University is a statutory participating institution and grant recipient under the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program, which is expanded and restructured by the bill.
Multiple USM institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, UMES, and UMBC Training Centers) participate in and receive funding from the expanded Cyber Warrior Diversity Program.
The Maryland Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Veterans and Military Families) or their designee is designated as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Governor is required to include mandated appropriations in the state budget beginning in FY 2025 for program personnel, appoints nine members to the Cyber Maryland Board, and receives annual reports from the program.
DBM is responsible for state budget oversight and must implement the mandated state general fund appropriations required beginning in FY 2025 to fund program staffing.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the newly established Cyber Maryland Fund separately from other funds.
The Comptroller is required by statute to account for the newly established Cyber Maryland Fund.
The Cyber Maryland Fund authorizes grants to elementary and secondary schools to operate cybersecurity programs aligned with the statewide strategic plan.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Cyber Maryland Board as a new advisory body to provide strategic guidance, assist with stakeholder outreach, and advise the program.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the nine required non-ex-officio members of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The board focuses on statewide workforce strategy and oversees Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs in IT and cybersecurity that intersect with the program's talent pipeline goals.

Requires evaluating State costs, impacts on the uninsured, potential benefit designs, and implementation considerations. Mandates analysis across Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and qualified Exchange health and dental plans. Requires study of specific groups, including low-income individuals, residents under 21, and adults aged 65 and older. Requires reporting findings and recommendations to designated General Assembly committees by October 31, 2023.

stakeholders: undocumented immigrants in Maryland ineligible for Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, or Exchange plans due to immigration status
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health can develop the report and submit findings with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, alongside the Maryland Department of Health, to develop and submit a report comparing options, costs, potential benefit designs, and implementation considerations for offering affordable health care and dental care coverage to undocumented immigrants.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health, in conjunction with the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, to study and report on options and costs for expanding coverage through Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) to individuals currently ineligible due to immigration status.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health to study local environmental health specialist staffing needs. Mandates that the study examine educational requirements, wage competitiveness, and the feasibility of establishing an apprenticeship program. Requires both departments to report their staffing findings and recommendations by December 1, 2023.
